I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so this derivation is from the usual rules rather than from a source.

1. In जाहच्, the initial ज् is an indicatory letter (इत्) by 1.3.7 (चुटू), since 1.3.8 does not exempt the च-वर्ग. The final च् is also an इत्. The affix that remains is आह.
2. Before this vowel-initial taddhita affix, शौनकिन् takes भ status. The final टि (इन्) is dropped by 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते), leaving शौनक्.
3. जित् would normally trigger vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the first syllable शौ already has it.
4. Adding आह gives शौनक् + आह = शौनकाह.

<answer>शौनकाह</answer>
<answer>बजस्तात्</answer>

The rule that licenses this is not one I could pin down, so this form is a best guess from the general mechanics of ṭhan.

The affix ठन् (ṭhan) is replaced by इक (ṭh → ik). Before इक, the final -य of बाध्य is dropped by यस्येति च. The initial vowel already has vṛddhi (बा), so nothing else changes. This gives बाध् + इक = बाधिक.

<answer>बाधिक</answer>

This is the affix दघ्नच् (daGnac) taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37, which is added to a word denoting measure. I am working from memory of that rule and have not checked it against the text. The affix is added directly to the stem भृत. Its final च् is only an indicatory marker, and the affix has no ञित् or णित् marker that would trigger vṛddhi. The stem therefore takes no vowel strengthening and simply becomes भृत + दघ्न.

<answer>भृतदघ्न</answer>

I could not fully confirm a rule for this specific case, so this form is my best derivation rather than a certain one.

The affix चरट् is the one taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Pāṇini 5.3.53), meaning "formerly was that". The final ट् is only a marker, so the affix is added as चर.

I assumed the feminine stem सुम्न्या is kept whole and no shortening of its final ā applies before the affix, so सुम्न्या + चर gives सुम्न्याचर.

<answer>सुम्न्याचर</answer>

The stem सर्वान्नीन takes the कन् affix, whose ककार is only an indicatory letter (it drops out). Nothing else in the stem changes, so the result is सर्वान्नीन + क = सर्वान्नीनक. I did not trace which specific rule licenses कन् here (for example the sense of contempt or of an unknown referent); the task accepts any licensed meaning.

<answer>सर्वान्नीनक</answer>

Here बहुच् is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.69 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is added optionally to a subanta in the sense of "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it is placed before the base. Prefixing बहु to मरणात्मक gives the stem below, which I have not verified against a source.

<answer>बहुमरणात्मक</answer>

This is a form built from the taddhita affix शस् (P. 5.4.43 ff.), which yields an indeclinable.

- Initial श् of a taddhita affix is not an it-letter, because 1.3.8 (लशक्वतद्धिते) excludes taddhita affixes. The affix therefore stays as "शस्", beginning with a consonant.
- Since the affix does not begin with a vowel, the final आ of the stem is not dropped under 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). I also assumed no other rule shortens or alters it here.
- The result is तुल्यावस्था + शस् = तुल्यावस्थाशस्, and the final स् becomes visarga in the complete indeclinable.

I could not tie the stem तुल्यावस्था to a specific licensed meaning with certainty, so the form rests on the general affixation rules above.

<answer>तुल्यावस्थाशः</answer>

I formed this from the affix साति (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.52, विभाषा साति कार्त्स्न्ये), which attaches to a nominal stem and gives an indeclinable. I did not verify the exact sense or conditions against the commentary, and I assumed no sandhi or stem-final change applies. On that basis the affix is simply added to the stem लोकाधिका.

<answer>लोकाधिकासाति</answer>

Taking रीढ as an ordinary basic stem, I apply the comparative affix ईयसुन्. By the rule भस्य टेर्लोपः (6.4.155), the last vowel and any consonants after it (the "ṭi" portion) drop before ईयसुन्. Here the final अ is dropped, giving रीढ्. Adding ईयस् (the ु and न् are markers and do not remain) gives रीढ् + ईयस् = रीढीयस्.

<answer>रीढीयस्</answer>
<answer>यौषिण्यरूप</answer>

This is the possessive use of इनि (by अत इनिठनौ, 5.2.115, which applies after stems ending in short अ). The final अ of पटक drops before the affix, giving पटक् + इनि = पटकिन्, "one who has a पटक". I am assuming this rule is the one intended; I did not check for any other rule that licenses इनि on this stem.

<answer>पटकिन्</answer>
<answer>ब्राह्मणादातरा</answer>

Here the affix चरट् (caraw) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, भूतपूर्वे चरट्, which means "formerly such". It is added to the stem मल्लि with no vowel change. The final ट् is only an indicatory marker and drops out, leaving the stem मल्लिचर, meaning "formerly Malli".

<answer>मल्लिचर</answer>
<answer>बाहुलात्व</answer>

Taking the stem काण्वक with the affix इञ् in its patronymic sense ("descendant of …"), the final अ of the stem drops before इ (अत इञ्, 4.1.95). The initial vowel is already आ, so the vṛddhi triggered by the ञ् marker changes nothing. This gives काण्वक् + इ = काण्वकि.

<answer>काण्वकि</answer>

The affix *tasi* (as in Pāṇini 5.4.44, *pratiyoge pañcamyās tasiḥ*) adds *-tas* to the stem, giving an indeclinable. Adding it to गृत्स gives गृत्स + तस् = गृत्सतः. I formed this from the rule and did not check it against an attested example.

<answer>गृत्सतः</answer>

The affix बहुच् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.68, in the sense of "somewhat" or "nearly") is placed before the word, as in बहुपटुः. Added to खाण्डिक, it gives बहुखाण्डिक. I did not find any further change to the stem.

<answer>बहुखाण्डिक</answer>
<answer>सादकता</answer>
<answer>चिञ्चोटकमय</answer>
<answer>याजनपाश</answer>

Applying the affix इष्ठन् (the superlative, atiśāyane) to वरेन्द्री, the final ई of the stem is dropped before the taddhita affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This leaves वरेन्द्र् + इष्ठ, which gives वरेन्द्रिष्ठ. I did not check whether this stem can take इष्ठन् at all, so the form rests on the ई-deletion rule alone.

<answer>वरेन्द्रिष्ठ</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is introduced by Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*. It applies after a stem in the third-case sense and means "known by that", as in विद्याचुञ्चुः. The final प् is only a marker and drops out, leaving चुञ्चु. The stem कासारि takes the affix without any change to its final इ, so the derived stem is कासारिचुञ्चु.

<answer>कासारिचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>घनेतरतम</answer>
<answer>संस्कारोद्द्योतमात्र</answer>

This is a mechanical derivation, since the stem पुक्लक is not a stem on which Pāṇini's rules actually license थमु. The rule that gives थमु (इदमस्थमुः, 5.3.24) is restricted to इदम्, so I applied the affix to the supplied stem as the table asks.

The final उ of थमु is an indicatory letter (इत्) and drops, leaving the operative affix थम्. The stem ends in अ and the affix begins with a consonant, so no sandhi or stem change applies. Taddhita forms of this kind are indeclinable, so no case ending is added.

पुक्लक + थम् = पुक्लकथम्

<answer>पुक्लकथम्</answer>

The affix यत् leaves the first syllable unchanged, since it has no ञ् or ण् marker to trigger vṛddhi. Its final त् is only an indicatory letter and drops out. Before the initial य of the affix, the final अ of रजताचल is elided by "यस्येति च". This gives रजताचल + य = रजताचल्य, which can mean "relating to or located on the silver mountain". I did not identify which specific sūtra licenses यत् for this stem, so the choice of affix rests on the task statement.

<answer>रजताचल्य</answer>
<answer>पारणवत्</answer>
<answer>मान्धात्रत्रा</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (P. 5.3.67, "ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः") is added to the stem. I am working from memory of the rules, and I am not fully certain of the shortening point below. The meaning is "slightly short of being अतीन्द्रिया", that is, nearly so.

I took the long ā of अतीन्द्रिया as staying long. The shortening rule for feminine endings (P. 6.3.43) lists कल्पप् but, as I remember it, not देशीयर्, and it covers only ङी, not ā. The final अ of the affix is the stem-final vowel of the result.

अतीन्द्रिया + देशीय → अतीन्द्रियादेशीय

<answer>अतीन्द्रियादेशीय</answer>

Taking तसि as the Pāṇinian affix तसि (तस्) added to the stem, the form is अधिव्रत + तस् = अधिव्रततः. The result is an indeclinable (अव्यय). I have not tied this to a specific sūtra; I applied the affix directly to the given stem.

<answer>अधिव्रततः</answer>
<answer>चान्द्रात्रेय</answer>
<answer>कालियक</answer>
<answer>श्वेतातपत्रीय</answer>

I derived this from general rules and did not identify a specific Aṣṭādhyāyī sūtra that licenses यत् after this stem, so the result is less certain than usual.

The stem is बुधेय (बुध + एय), ending in short अ. The affix यत् has the initial य, and its final त् is an indicatory letter that drops. Attaching it gives बुधेय + य.

The final अ of the stem is then elided before the taddhita affix by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), leaving बुधेय् + य, which joins as बुधेय्य. The ए inside the stem is not at the end of the stem, so it is not affected. Since यत् is neither ṇit nor ñit, no vṛddhi applies.

<answer>बुधेय्य</answer>

The stem दम्भन ends in short अ. Before इष्ठन्, the rule *ṭeḥ* (6.4.155) deletes the stem's ṭi, which here is just that final अ. This leaves दम्भन्, and adding इष्ठ gives दम्भनिष्ठ.

<answer>दम्भनिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>पेषणीयिका</answer>
<answer>शिलारम्भाचणः</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (the final र् is only a marker) is taught in P. 5.3.67, with the sense "slightly short of being complete", so जटिन् gives "a person who is somewhat of a जटी".

The affix begins with द, so it is neither a vowel nor य. The base therefore counts as a pada (not bha), and the final न् drops by 8.2.7. Adding देशीय to जटि gives जटिदेशीय.

<answer>जटिदेशीय</answer>

The affix कुणप् has प् as its only marker (it), so what is added is कुण. I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule for this affix, so I formed the word by general rules rather than from the sūtra.

Because कुण begins with a consonant, the final अ of वैदल is not elided. The result is वैदल + कुण = वैदलकुण.

<answer>वैदलकुण</answer>
<answer>हिममय</answer>

This is a rule-based guess, not a form I could match to a specific attested derivative. I did not identify a sūtra that licenses वलच् after वालूका.

I simply attached the affix to the stem. The affix वलच् begins with a consonant, so the stem's final -ा is not dropped before it. After the indicatory च् is removed, the affix is -वल, giving वालूका + वल.

<answer>वालूकावल</answer>
<answer>ढक्किष्ठ</answer>

The affix रूपप् (rūpap) is the one taught by Pāṇini 5.3.66, "praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap", which is added in the sense of praise. Adding it to गुल gives गुलरूप, meaning "excellent jaggery". This is the same pattern as वैयाकरणरूप, "an excellent grammarian". I am giving the stem form, as asked.

<answer>गुलरूप</answer>

Taking the affix `थमु` (Tamu) with the stem `भाव्य`: the final `उ` of `थमु` is only a marker (`इत्`) and drops, leaving `थम्`.

`यस्येति च` (6.4.148) does not apply, because `थम्` begins with a consonant. The stem is therefore not shortened, and the form is `भाव्य` + `थम्` = `भाव्यथम्`, which is indeclinable.

In Pāṇini's grammar `थमु` is licensed only after `इदम्` and `किम्`, as in `इत्थम्` and `कथम्`. I did not find a rule licensing it after `भाव्य`, so this form comes from joining the stem and affix as the prompt describes, not from a rule that attests it.

<answer>भाव्यथम्</answer>

The affix तरप् is added directly to the stem क्षम्य with no change to the stem, which gives क्षम्य + तर = क्षम्यतर ("more patient" or "more able to forgive").

<answer>क्षम्यतर</answer>

Adding अञ् to घाटाल leaves the stem unchanged on the surface. I could not tie घाटाल to a specific rule or गण, so this follows only the general mechanics of the affix.

- The initial syllable घा already has long आ, so the आदिवृद्धि required before a ञित् affix changes nothing.
- The final अ of the stem is elided before the अ of the affix.
- Joining the affix अ then gives घाटाल again.

<answer>घाटाल</answer>

This is the affix बहुच् taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It means "almost, not quite" (ईषदसमाप्ति) and is placed before the base rather than after it. Applied to हुण, it gives बहुहुण, with the final च् serving only as an accent marker.

<answer>बहुहुण</answer>

जिजीविषा में आकार (टाप्) है। तद्धित अण् परे होने पर "यस्येति च" से यह आकार लुप्त हो जाता है। फिर "तद्धितेष्वचामादेः" से आदि अच् में वृद्धि होती है, जिससे जि → जै। इस प्रकार जिजीविष + अ से जैजीविष बनता है।

<answer>जैजीविष</answer>
<answer>ध्मापितिक</answer>
<answer>गौपवनता</answer>

Here the affix वलच् (SLP1 *valac*) is added to the stem वेष्टक. The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter (it marks accent), so the affix is just व + ल, giving वल. Since वल begins with a consonant, the final अ of the stem is not dropped (the rule यस्येति च needs a vowel-initial or ई-initial affix). The result is वेष्टक + वल.

I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule licensing this affix after वेष्टक, so the form follows from the stated stem and affix alone.

<answer>वेष्टकवल</answer>
<answer>वैष्णवागमिन्</answer>

The affix कुणप् (kuṇap) comes from Pāṇini 5.2.24, "तस्य पाकमूले पील्वादिकर्णादिभ्यः कुणब्जाहचौ". The stem वाच्य is not in the गण lists for that rule, but the task says any licensed meaning is acceptable, so I attached the affix anyway.

The affix is effectively कुण, with the final प् as an इत् letter that drops out. It begins with क, so it is not ञित् or णित् and triggers no वृद्धि. It also does not begin with a vowel or य, so the stem is not treated as भ and the final अ of वाच्य is not deleted. The stem and affix simply join.

वाच्य + कुण = वाच्यकुण

<answer>वाच्यकुण</answer>

This is a derivation under the general ṭhak rules (P. 4.4.1 ff.). I did not tie it to one specific meaning.

1. The affix ठक् (ṭhak) has its initial ठ् replaced by इक (P. 7.3.50, ठस्येकः). So the affix becomes -इक.
2. The first vowel of गर्दभिल्ल takes vṛddhi because of the ṭhak-type affix with ञ्/ट्/ण् markers (P. 7.2.117), so ग becomes गा.
3. The final अ of गर्दभिल्ल is dropped before the -इक affix (P. 6.4.148).

Result: गार्दभिल्ल + इक → गार्दभिल्लिक.

<answer>गार्दभिल्लिक</answer>

This is formed by 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), where द्वयसच् is added to a word denoting measure, as in ऊरुद्वयसम्. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -a of the stem is not dropped. The affix is simply appended to the stem मशकार्थ.

<answer>मशकार्थद्वयस</answer>
<answer>पुण्यकदेशीय</answer>

I applied the superlative affix इष्ठन् (atiśayane tamabiṣṭhanau, 5.3.55) to रोपणीय.

Before इष्ठन्, the stem loses its टि, the final vowel together with any consonant after it (टेः, 6.4.155). In रोपणीय the final अ of the last syllable य is the टि, so it drops, leaving रोपणीय्. Adding इष्ठ gives रोपणीयिष्ठ.

I did not apply 6.4.150 (halastaddhitasya), because the य is preceded by the vowel ी, not a consonant.

<answer>रोपणीयिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>शङ्कान्वितदेशीय</answer>

Under the rule अत इञ् (4.1.95), the affix इञ् is added to a stem ending in अ to give the meaning "descendant". I take that as the licensed meaning here.

1. The stem is कुमुदाकर, ending in अ, so the affix इञ् (here just इ) is added.
2. The first vowel takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि), so कु becomes कौ.
3. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix.

This gives कौमुदाकरि.

<answer>कौमुदाकरि</answer>

भानु + क gives भानुक. The stem already ends in a short उ, so the short-vowel substitution before क (7.4.13) changes nothing. Since the stem is a basic nominal stem and not one ending in the टाप् suffix (the "nyap" note in the table), I did not apply the rule that changes the final आ before क to इ. I did not add the feminine suffix टाप्, so the stem stays as भानुक. The affix can carry meanings such as contempt, smallness or unknownness, and any of these is acceptable.

<answer>भानुक</answer>

Here तल् (which becomes -ता) is added in the sense of "state or quality" (भावे त्वतलौ, 5.1.119). The final -ā of the feminine stem सायासा is dropped before the taddhita affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This gives सायास + ता = सायासता. I derived this from the rules and did not check it against a source.

<answer>सायासता</answer>
<answer>नभस्यीयस्</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rules for the affix ṭhak, applied mechanically to the stem as given.

1. The affix ठक् has ṭ and k as markers, and its ठ is replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50).
2. The ṭ-marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so ऊ becomes औ.
3. The final अ of ऊतीक is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148).

This gives औतीक् + इक = औतीकिक.

<answer>औतीकिक</answer>
<answer>मारीचोपपुराणत्रा</answer>

The affix is *astāti* (Pāṇini 5.3.27), which gives forms like *purastāt*. I applied it formally to the stem मृजित, since the table does not require the stem to be a direction word.

The stem's final अ drops before the vowel-initial affix (*yasyeti ca*, 6.4.148). That gives मृजित् + अस्तात्, which joins as मृजितस्तात्.

<answer>मृजितस्तात्</answer>

I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix त्रा, so this form is a plain concatenation, not a derivation checked against a rule. The affix is added directly to the stem, with no change to the stem, and the result is an indeclinable.

<answer>साम्प्रयोगिकत्रा</answer>

This is the affix रूप्य taught in Pāṇini 4.3.81 (हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यः), used in the sense "come from that" (ततः आगतः). The stem दिलीर takes it directly. रूप्य is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi. It begins with र, not with य or a vowel, so the stem does not take the भ-designation and its final अ is not dropped. The result is simply the stem followed by the affix.

<answer>दिलीररूप्य</answer>

The affix त्व is added in the sense of "state or quality of that" (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ, A. 5.1.119). Nothing in the stem changes before it, so विथुर + त्व gives विथुरत्व, a neuter abstract noun meaning "the state of being विथुर".

<answer>विथुरत्व</answer>

I could not fully verify this derivation, so the answer is a best judgement. The affix साति is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.4.52 (विभाषा साति कार्त्स्न्ये), added after a nominal stem in the sense of "entirety". I attach it directly to the stem सादक and keep the final इ of the affix. The result is an indeclinable. I am not certain whether the final इ is retained or dropped.

<answer>सादकसाति</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that licenses जाहच् for this stem, so the form below comes from the general rules for the affix rather than from a verified source.

The initial ज् and the final च् of जाहच् are इत् markers, so the affix that is actually added is आह.

The stem आश्मायन ends in अ. Before a taddhita affix that begins with a vowel, that final अ is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148). Joining आश्मायन् with आह gives आश्मायनाह.

<answer>आश्मायनाह</answer>

I derived this from P. 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which gives दघ्नच् in the sense of measure. The ending is च्-it, so it leaves the affix अ-final as दघ्न. The affix begins with a consonant (द), so the stem does not take the "bha" designation and the final अ of कफान्तिक is not elided under 6.4.148. I did not check whether this particular stem is attested; the form follows from the rule alone.

<answer>कफान्तिकदघ्न</answer>
<answer>वासन्तकीन</answer>

Applying च्वि to the stem पौत्रिक्य, which ends in short अ, triggers the rule "अस्य च्वौ" (7.4.32): the final अ becomes ई, and च्वि itself leaves no trace. This gives पौत्रिक्य → पौत्रिक्यी, used as in "पौत्रिक्यी भवति". I did not use the neuter gender or the "without nyap" note, since neither affects this stem.

<answer>पौत्रिक्यी</answer>

The affix देश्य is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It is added to a subanta in the sense of "almost, but not quite" (ईषदसमाप्ति).

The shortening of a final ई/ऊ or आ before the affix (6.3.43) is taught only for कल्पप् and certain others, not for देश्य. So the ई of यवासिनी stays long, and the derived stem is यवासिनीदेश्य ("almost a यवासिनी").

<answer>यवासिनीदेश्य</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātracaḥ), which gives a measure-sense derivative. I assumed that sense applies to जूर्णि, since the stem is otherwise unusual.

The final च् of द्वयसच् is only a marker (it), so the affix added to the stem is द्वयस.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as bha. The final इ of जूर्णि therefore does not drop, as it would before a vowel-initial affix under 6.4.148. This matches ऊरु → ऊरुद्वयस.

जूर्णि + द्वयस gives जूर्णिद्वयस.

<answer>जूर्णिद्वयस</answer>

This is the affix पाशप् (pāśap), taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (*yāpye pāśap*), used for something "despicable" or "kept going only by palliatives". It is added to the stem रद्धा, and the final ā is not shortened, since 6.3.43 does not list pāśap among the affixes that shorten a feminine stem. I have not checked this derivation against a source beyond my recollection of these sūtras.

Adding पाश to रद्धा gives रद्धापाश.

<answer>रद्धापाश</answer>

Applying देशीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ, "slightly short of complete") to the feminine stem ष्ठ्यूता, the feminine ending is replaced by the masculine form before देशीय. This is the rule पुंवत्कर्मधारयजातीयदेशीयेषु (6.3.42, with 6.3.34). So ष्ठ्यूता becomes ष्ठ्यूत, and adding देशीय gives ष्ठ्यूतदेशीय. I worked this out from memory of the sūtras, so the rule numbers are not checked against a text.

<answer>ष्ठ्यूतदेशीय</answer>

The affix वलच् leaves the stem form वल (the च् is only a marker), and this is added directly to जङ्घिल. Because वल begins with a consonant, nothing triggers deletion of the stem-final अ, so it is retained. This gives जङ्घिलवल. This formation was worked out from the affix rules rather than checked against an attested word.

<answer>जङ्घिलवल</answer>
<answer>तारलीय</answer>
<answer>तर्षितथा</answer>

This is a derivation from the affix's technical name, not from a source I could confirm. I could not recall the sūtra that teaches jAhac, so I worked only from the general rules.

1. In जाहच्, the initial ज् is an it-marker by 1.3.7 (चुटू), and the final च् is an it-marker by 1.3.3. The affix that actually attaches is therefore आह.
2. Because the affix is jit, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi by 7.2.117 (तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). The first vowel of स्परण is the अ in प, so it becomes आ, giving स्पारण.
3. The stem-final अ is dropped before the vowel-initial affix by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), giving स्पारण् + आह.

The result is स्पारणाह.

<answer>स्पारणाह</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that introduces this affix, so this form is my best reconstruction and I am not certain of it.

I read कुणप् as the affix कुण with a final इत् प्. The initial क् is not an इत् here, because the rule that drops an initial क् as इत् applies only to non-taddhita affixes. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem शौर्पी is a pada before it. That means the final ई is not elided by the rule यस्येति च, and I assume no shortening rule applies. This gives शौर्पी + कुण.

<answer>शौर्पीकुण</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so this form is a best guess rather than a derivation I could check.

The final च् of जाहच् is only an indicatory letter (it), so the affix that attaches is जाह. It begins with a consonant, so the stem-final ई of वृषणी is not dropped. Adding जाह directly gives वृषणीजाह. I did not apply any shortening of the ई, since I could not identify a rule that requires it here.

<answer>वृषणीजाह</answer>

I treated this as the comparative formation. The affix ईयसुन् is added to the stem शुभित. Before इष्ठन्, इमनिच् and ईयसुन्, the ṭi (the last vowel and any consonants after it) of the stem is dropped (टेः, 6.4.155). Here the ṭi is "इत", so शुभित becomes शुभ. Adding ईयसुन् with its उन् marker removed gives शुभ + ईयस्, which is शुभीयस्.

<answer>शुभीयस्</answer>

Before the affix, the final -a of the stem is replaced by long ī by the rule अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32). The affix च्वि is then dropped entirely, which gives the indeclinable-type stem used with कृ, भू or अस्. So कंवूल becomes कंवूली.

<answer>कंवूली</answer>
<answer>मालवकतः</answer>

Applying the affix छ (SLP1 `Ca`) to the stem रुद्राह्व:

1. By the rule that छ is replaced by ईय (आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्), the affix becomes ईय.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before ईय (यस्येति च), giving रुद्राह्व् + ईय.
3. छ is not a ṇit affix, so there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel.

I did not trace which specific sūtra licenses छ for this stem, so that part is assumed rather than checked.

<answer>रुद्राह्वीय</answer>

The affix cvi (च्वि) is added to a nominal stem when something becomes what it was not before (abhūtatadbhāva), typically in combination with kṛ, bhū or as. The affix itself disappears entirely, leaving only the "ī" substitution. The stem-final "a" of पृष्ठानुग is replaced by "ī" (Pāṇini 7.4.32, *asya cvau*), giving पृष्ठानुगी, as in पृष्ठानुगीभवति.

<answer>पृष्ठानुगी</answer>
<answer>जलाभिषेकस्तात्</answer>
<answer>संघावशेषद्वयस</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् is added to the stem सांकृत्यायन. The initial ण्-like markers drop, leaving the affix इष्ठ. Before इष्ठन्, the rule टेः (6.4.155) removes the "ṭi" of the stem, which is its last vowel together with any consonant after it. In सांकृत्यायन that is the final -अन. This leaves सांकृत्याय, and adding इष्ठ gives सांकृत्यायिष्ठ.

<answer>सांकृत्यायिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>रैषण</answer>

The affix रूपप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap), "in the sense of praise". It is added to the stem तीव्रान्ता, whose final -ā is a feminine suffix. Because रूपप् falls among the affixes before which a feminine stem takes its masculine form (puṁvat) or is shortened, the final ā is replaced by a. This gives तीव्रान्त + रूप. I am reconstructing the puṁvat/shortening step from memory of the rules rather than from a checked source, so that step is the less certain part. I have given the bare derived stem, without the optional feminine ending.

<answer>तीव्रान्तरूप</answer>

Applying अण् to घर्घर्य gives घार्घर्य, assuming the standard rules apply to this stem.

1. अण् is a ञित्/णित् affix, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117). The अ of घ becomes आ, giving घा-.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the taddhita affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This leaves घार्घर्य् + अ.
3. The affix then joins the remaining य्, giving घार्घर्य.

I have not confirmed that घर्घर्य is an attested word, so this follows the general rules rather than a documented example.

<answer>घार्घर्य</answer>

The affix sāti (Pāṇini 5.4.52 ff.) gives indeclinables in -sāt, as in अग्निसात् and राजसात्. I recalled the final form from the tradition, not from a full derivation. I did not settle whether the final -i is dropped by a ḍit-type rule or whether the affix is really सात् with the sūtra using its locative. Either account gives -sāt.

The stem कालियक ends in -a. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not altered. Adding sāti to कालियक gives कालियकसात्.

<answer>कालियकसात्</answer>

I recalled this from Pāṇini's rule 5.2.26, "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ", and did not check it against a text. The affix चणप् is added to a nominal stem in the sense "known by that" (as in विद्याचण). The final प् is only an accent marker and drops. The initial च् stays, because 1.3.7 does not apply to taddhita affixes (1.3.8). The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ of गण्डुल is not elided, and the affix is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi. Adding चण to गण्डुल gives गण्डुलचण.

<answer>गण्डुलचण</answer>

This is derived by working through the ṭhak rules from memory, without confirming which specific sūtra licenses ṭhak after this stem.

1. ṭhak has the final ṭh replaced by इक (ṭh → ik), and the initial ṭh's marker k is dropped, so the affix is added as -इक.
2. Before the affix, the final ई of पटोली is dropped (यस्येति च), leaving पटोल्+इक.
3. The first vowel takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि, because ṭhak carries the ṭ marker that triggers it), so प → पा.

The result is पाटोलिक.

<answer>पाटोलिक</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses ञ्यट् here, so this derivation rests on the general taddhita rules for a ñit affix, not on a located sūtra.

1. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the base य after dropping the markers ञ् and ट्. The ञ् is an indicatory letter that triggers vṛddhi of the stem's first vowel.
2. In योक्तृ, the first vowel ओ becomes औ, giving यौक्तृ.
3. The final ऋ of the stem becomes the semivowel र् before the affix य, giving यौक्त्र्य.

<answer>यौक्त्र्य</answer>

I could not identify which specific sūtra licenses यत् on this stem, so this is a derivation from the general rules rather than a confirmed attested form.

The stem स्नातव्य ends in अ. Before the affix य, that final अ is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), leaving स्नातव्य्. Adding य gives स्नातव्य्य. No vṛddhi applies, because यत् is not ṇit or ñit.

<answer>स्नातव्य्य</answer>
<answer>अङ्गूषदेश्य</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule that licenses थाल्. Pāṇini's थाल् (5.3.23, 5.3.111) is normally taught after pronominal or similar bases such as तथा, यथा, सर्वथा and the Vedic विश्वथा. I therefore simply attached the affix to the stem as given, which is an assumption rather than a derivation I could verify.

The affix थाल् loses its final ल् as an indicatory letter, leaving था. Added to पृषित, this gives an indeclinable form.

<answer>पृषितथा</answer>
<answer>भीषणवत्</answer>

The affix रूप्य begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of फलोद्देश is not elided and the affix is simply added to the stem. I could not identify the exact Pāṇinian rule behind this affix label. The form below is an assumption: it adds the affix directly, with no vowel change.

<answer>फलोद्देशरूप्य</answer>
<answer>छर्दितदेशीय</answer>

The affix रूपप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्). It is added after a subanta word to express praise. Adding it to स्फरक gives the stem स्फरकरूप, meaning a praiseworthy स्फरक.

<answer>स्फरकरूप</answer>

This is the affix रूपप् of Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशस्ते रूपप्), which is added to a nominal base to mean "praiseworthy X". The affix is added to रिफित without any other change to the base, so the derived stem is रिफितरूप.

<answer>रिफितरूप</answer>

This is reasoned from my recollection of the Pāṇinian rules, and I did not check it against the text. The stem ऊषी ends in the feminine ī, and the taddhita affix कन् is added to it.

1. The affix कन् leaves the stem ऊषी + क.
2. Before क, the long vowel of a stem like this shortens by the rule *ke 'ṇaḥ* (7.4.13), giving ऊषि + क.
3. The result takes the feminine ending ā, giving ऊषिका.

I am less sure of the shortening in step 2 than of the other steps. If it did not apply, the form would instead be ऊषीका.

<answer>ऊषिका</answer>

The affix अस्ताति begins with a vowel, so the stem counts as *bha* before it (1.4.18). The final आ of प्रकुब्रता is then deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), leaving प्रकुब्रत्. Joining the affix gives प्रकुब्रत् + अस्ताति = प्रकुब्रतस्ताति. This is my own derivation from the rules, not a form I could check against an attested example.

<answer>प्रकुब्रतस्ताति</answer>

This is the taddhita affix *pāśap* (SLP1 `pASap`), taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 "याप्ये पाशप्". It is added to a nominal stem to mean a contemptible or barely acceptable version of what the stem denotes. The final *p* is only an indicatory letter, so the affix that remains is पाश.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of हर्म्य is not elided (the elision of 6.4.148 applies only before vowel-initial affixes or ones beginning with य). The stem therefore stays whole and takes the affix directly: हर्म्य + पाश = हर्म्यपाश.

<answer>हर्म्यपाश</answer>

गावेधुक ("Coix barbata") takes तमप् in the sense of "most" (अतिशायन). The affix is added directly to the stem. The stem ends in a short अ, with no ṭāp-type feminine ending that would need shortening. The neuter source gender also causes no change. The result is गावेधुकतम.

<answer>गावेधुकतम</answer>

The affix अञ् carries an ञ् marker, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (आदि-वृद्धि) of टङ्कण. The initial अ of the stem becomes आ, and the final अ drops before the affix's अ. I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् after टङ्कण, so this form rests on the general vṛddhi rule for ञित् affixes.

<answer>टाङ्कण</answer>

Here तल् is the भाव (abstract-quality) affix, which gives a feminine stem in -ता (the तल् affix takes टाप्). I found no rule that would shorten or otherwise alter the final आ of कङ्कतिका before it, so I join the stem to ता unchanged, giving कङ्कतिका + ता. I did not look up a source form for this word.

<answer>कङ्कतिकाता</answer>

The affix खञ् (KaY) is added to रसोनक. Its initial ख् is replaced by ईन (खस्य ईन, 7.1.2). The final अ of the stem drops before the affix. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (तद्धितेष्वचामादेः, 7.2.117), and र becomes रा.

रसोनक + ईन → रासोनकीन

I derived this from the general rules for खञ्. I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses khañ after this stem.

<answer>रासोनकीन</answer>
<answer>वरूथिनीमय</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् (cuñcup) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), with the sense "known by that". It is added to a stem in the instrumental sense, as in विद्याचुञ्चुः ("known for learning").

I did not trace the derivation in detail. I recalled the rule and the pattern of the example, and I assumed the long ā of the feminine stem stays unchanged, as it does in विद्या. Dropping the markers (ञ् and प्) leaves the affix as चुञ्चु, so the result is ओषिष्ठा + चुञ्चु.

<answer>ओषिष्ठाचुञ्चु</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces ञ्यङ् (YyaN), so this derivation is a best guess from the general rules rather than from a confirmed source.

The ending -आ of the feminine stem वैयाघ्रा is dropped before a taddhita affix (6.4.148, यस्येति च). That leaves वैयाघ्र, which already has the vṛddhi vowel ऐ. Adding the affix's remaining part -य gives वैयाघ्र्य. I take this as the stem form and have not added a further feminine ending such as टाप्, which would give वैयाघ्र्या.

<answer>वैयाघ्र्य</answer>

The affix pāśap (pASap) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47, *yāpye pāśap*. It is added to a nominal stem to mean "a poor or contemptible example of that kind". The affix is simply added to the stem बडाह with no change to the base, giving बडाहपाश.

<answer>बडाहपाश</answer>

This is a derivation by rule application; I did not identify a specific sūtra that licenses यत् after this stem, so only the sandhi steps below are grounded in rules.

1. The stem is पृतनायु, ending in -u, and the taddhita affix यत् (य) is added: पृतनायु + य.
2. Before a taddhita affix, a stem-final उ takes guṇa by ओर्गुणः (6.4.146), giving पृतनायो + य.
3. The ओ then becomes अव् before the vowel-less affix by एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78), giving पृतनायव्य.

This parallels शङ्कु + यत् → शङ्कव्य.

<answer>पृतनायव्य</answer>

Adding अण् (aṆ) to अहीन्द्र follows the usual two steps. The first vowel takes vṛddhi, so अ becomes आ (by the rule that a Ṇ-marked affix triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel). The final अ of the stem is then dropped before the affix (यस्येति च). This gives आहीन्द्र, which can mean "descendant of Ahīndra". I did this from the general rules rather than checking for a special rule on this word.

<answer>आहीन्द्र</answer>

The affix ञ्यट् is not one I could place in a specific Pāṇinian rule, so I derived the form from the affix's markers alone.

1. The stem सानला ends in आ. The affix, once its markers are dropped, is य, so the final आ of the stem is elided (यस्येति च). This gives सानल् + य.
2. The ञ् marker calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The first vowel, सा, is already vṛddhi, so nothing changes.
3. The ट् marker means the derivative takes the feminine suffix ङीप् (टिड्ढाणञ्…). Adding ई to सानल्य, the final अ of य is dropped before ई (यस्येति च again). This gives सानल्य् + ई = सानल्यी.

This form depends on my reading of the markers rather than on a confirmed rule for ञ्यट्.

<answer>सानल्यी</answer>

Reasoning from the affix markers rather than from a located Pāṇinian rule: the affix ञ्यट् leaves the suffix -य, with ञ् and ट् as indicatory letters. The ञ् makes the affix ञित्, which triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the base, so ज becomes जा. The final अ of जलेश्वर drops before the suffix. This gives जालेश्वर्य. I did not confirm which rule licenses this affix, so the form rests on that derivation.

<answer>जालेश्वर्य</answer>
<answer>भाषान्तरि</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), which is added to a nominal base to express something contemptible or hardly worth the name. I am recalling the sūtra from memory. The final -a of अदृष्टार्थ is dropped before the taddhita affix (6.4.148), and पाश is then added. The result is a stem ending in -a.

<answer>अदृष्टार्थपाश</answer>

The stem द्राह्यायणीया takes the superlative affix इष्ठन्. Before इष्ठन् the final आ of the stem is dropped (ṭi-lopa, टेः 6.4.155), leaving द्राह्यायणीय्. Adding इष्ठ gives द्राह्यायणीयिष्ठ. I did not check whether a puṃvadbhāva rule applies first, but it would give the same result here.

<answer>द्राह्यायणीयिष्ठ</answer>

पार्श्वल से तृतीयान्त अर्थ में "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ" (५.२.२६) के अनुसार चणप् लगता है। यहाँ अर्थ है "उससे जाना गया"। चणप् में कोई ञित्, णित् या किदंश नहीं है, इसलिए वृद्धि नहीं होती। प् केवल स्वर-विधान के लिए है। चण का आदि वर्ण व्यंजन है, इसलिए पार्श्वल के अन्तिम अ का लोप भी नहीं होता। इस प्रकार पार्श्वल + चण = पार्श्वलचण बनता है।

यह रूप सूत्र के अनुसार बनाया गया है; "पार्श्वलचण" का कोई प्रमाणित प्रयोग मैंने नहीं देखा।

<answer>पार्श्वलचण</answer>
<answer>शङ्कान्वितिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>लब्धव्यत्व</answer>

The derivation starts from the feminine stem औपवसथिका. Before the taddhita affix अण्, the final feminine ā is dropped by "yasyeti ca" (6.4.148). That leaves औपवसथिक्, and adding अ gives औपवसथिक. The affix is ṇit, so it calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. That vowel is already औ, a vṛddhi vowel, so nothing changes. I did not identify the specific rule that licenses अण् here, so the result rests on these general steps.

<answer>औपवसथिक</answer>
<answer>नन्दात्मजात्व</answer>

I could not pin down the exact Pāṇinian sūtra for this derivation, so the form rests on the general pattern. The affix त्रा attaches to the stem without changing it. This gives तलित + त्रा = तलितत्रा, an indeclinable.

<answer>तलितत्रा</answer>

I did not trace this to a specific Pāṇinian rule, so this is a best guess. The affix क (ka) is added directly to the stem शेव, with no vowel change needed. This gives the stem शेवक.

The affix ठन् (Wan) takes the substitute ठ → इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50). I assume the sense "lives by that" (e.g. 4.4.12, वेतनादिभ्यो जीवति), though I did not confirm that स्वरोपघात belongs to that group.

1. Because ठन् has no ञ or ण marker, the stem takes no vṛddhi.
2. The final अ of स्वरोपघात drops before the affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148).
3. Adding इक gives स्वरोपघातिक.

<answer>स्वरोपघातिक</answer>

I applied the rule स्त्रीभ्यो ढक् (4.1.120), which adds ढक् to feminine stems.

1. The stem हरिद्राक्ता ends in the feminine suffix टाप् (ā).
2. In ढक्, the initial ढ् is replaced by एय (आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्, 7.1.2), and क् is only a marker.
3. The stem's final ā is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This leaves हरिद्राक्त.
4. The first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi because the affix is ञित्/णित्/तद्धित-type (आदिवृद्धि, 7.2.117): ह → हा.
5. Adding एय gives हारिद्राक्त + एय = हारिद्राक्तेयः.

<answer>हारिद्राक्तेयः</answer>

The stem एष्टव्या ends in the feminine suffix ā, and I could not identify the specific rule licensing यत् on it, so this derivation rests on the general taddhita process. Before the taddhita affix य (from यत्, with the final त् as an indicatory letter), the final ā is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). That leaves एष्टव्य्, and adding य gives एष्टव्य्य.

<answer>एष्टव्य्य</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) lets the affix देश्य attach to a nominal stem to mean "almost, not quite" the thing named. Added to आभ्यन्तरिक, it gives "nearly आभ्यन्तरिक". The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final -अ stays unchanged and no sandhi applies.

<answer>आभ्यन्तरिकदेश्य</answer>

I could not match this stem to the usual rule for this affix, so I formed it by direct addition. Pāṇini's थमु (5.3.24–25) normally applies only to इदम् (इत्थम्) and किम् (कथम्).

Here the stem गमथ ends in a consonant plus अ. The affix थमु loses its final उ as an इत् marker, leaving थम्. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not deleted. Joining the two gives गमथ + थम् = गमथथम्. A taddhita ending that takes no case endings is an indeclinable (अव्यय).

<answer>गमथथम्</answer>

I formed this by rule 5.2.115 (*ata iniṭhanau*), which adds *ini* in the sense "having that" to a stem ending in -a. The stem ल ends in -a, and the final -a drops before the affix (इन्). So ल् + इन् gives लिन्, meaning "one who has ल".

<answer>लिन्</answer>
<answer>गमिष्णुता</answer>

I could not recall the rule that introduces जाहच् with confidence, so this form is a best guess rather than a derivation I could verify.

The affix is जाह, since the final च् is only a marker (it) and drops. I assumed the affix begins with a consonant (ज), so the stem is not treated as bha (the stem-class that triggers dropping of a final आ). On that assumption the final -ā of नमना is not elided, and the form is नमना + जाह.

<answer>नमनाजाह</answer>

The affix वलच् is added to the stem कृतावधान. Dropping the final अ of the stem (by यस्येति च) does not apply here, because वलच् begins with a consonant (व), not a vowel or ईकार. The stem therefore stays whole, and the चकार (the इत् marker in वलच्) drops, leaving the ending -वल. This gives कृतावधान + वल = कृतावधानवल.

I did not match this to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for वलच् (the one I recall, 5.2.112, covers only a fixed list of stems that does not include this one). I formed the word by the general rules for a consonant-initial taddhita affix.

<answer>कृतावधानवल</answer>

This is a derivation from memory. I could not recall the exact rule that introduces जाहच्, so I assumed it behaves like the other affixes that take पुंवद्भाव.

1. The affix जाहच् loses its इत् letter च्, leaving the affix जाह.
2. The stem पलायका ends in the feminine suffix टाप्. I assumed पुंवद्भाव applies before this affix, so the stem is treated as masculine, पलायक.
3. Adding जाह to पलायक gives पलायकजाह.

I am not fully certain of step 2. If पुंवद्भाव did not apply, the form would instead be पलायकाजाह.

<answer>पलायकजाह</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses कुणप् for this stem, so this form comes from the general rules of suffixation rather than from a confirmed source.

The final प् of कुणप् is an indicatory letter (it), so what is actually added is कुण. This suffix begins with a consonant, so the stem माध्विक keeps its final अ. The derivative is therefore माध्विक + कुण, with no vowel elision.

<answer>माध्विककुण</answer>

I treated अण् as added to तैजस (taijasa) with the usual sense "relating to / belonging to that". The first vowel of तैजस is already ऐ, which is vṛddhi, so the initial-vowel strengthening changes nothing. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the suffix, and the suffix's own अ takes its place. The result is the same spelling as the input.

<answer>तैजस</answer>

Before the affix च्वि (cvi), a final अ becomes ई by the rule "अस्य च्वौ" (7.4.32), and the affix itself is then wholly deleted. This affix is used with the verbs कृ, भू and अस् to mean becoming what one was not before. So सुख + cvi gives सुखी, as in सुखीकरोति or सुखीभवति.

<answer>सुखी</answer>

Taking the affix खञ् (KaY) on the stem काह्लार: the initial ख् is replaced by ईन् (by the rule that substitutes ईन for ख), and the stem-final अ is dropped before it. The affix carries ञ्, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel. That vowel, ā, is already long, so nothing changes there. This gives काह्लार + ईन = काह्लारीण. I derived this from the general rules for खञ् and did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses it for this stem, so the result is a best-fit formation.

<answer>काह्लारीण</answer>

The affix ईयसुन् is added to शुक्त. Its उन् part is only a marker (the indicatory letters उ and न्) and drops out, leaving the affix as ईयस्. Before ईयस्, the final अ of शुक्त is deleted by the rule "ṭeḥ" (6.4.155). Joining शुक्त् with ईयस् gives शुक्तीयस्.

<answer>शुक्तीयस्</answer>

The affix बहुच् (Pāṇini 5.3.68, in the sense of ईषदसमाप्ति, "almost / not quite complete") is placed before the subanta, not after it. Prefixing बहु to छेदक gives बहु + छेदक.

Because a short vowel (उ) precedes छ, the augment तुक् is added by 6.1.73 (छे च), giving बहुच्छेदक. I applied तुक् on the assumption that the prefixed affix and the stem form a single pada. I did not confirm this against a worked example.

<answer>बहुच्छेदक</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau* ("known by that"). In चणप्, the final प् is an indicatory letter (it drops), so the affix that remains is चण. The ण is not an indicatory letter here, so there is no vṛddhi or other change to the base. Because चण begins with a consonant, the final -अ of मन्दक is not elided, and the two simply join.

मन्दक + चण = मन्दकचण

<answer>मन्दकचण</answer>

This is a derivation from the ṭhak rules, not a form I could match to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for मोरण. The steps below follow the general ṭhak mechanics.

1. The affix ठक् (ṭhak) has ṭh as its operative consonant, and ṭh is replaced by इक (ika) by ṭhasyekaḥ (7.3.50).
2. The final क् of ṭhak is an indicatory marker, so the affix counts as kit. By kiti ca (7.2.118) the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi.
3. The first vowel of मोरण is ओ, and its vṛddhi is औ, giving मौरण-.
4. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving मौरण् + इक.

Result: मौरणिक.

<answer>मौरणिक</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), in the sense "known by that". It is added to the stem, as in विद्याचुञ्चु (known for learning). Since the affix begins with a consonant, the stem's final अ is not dropped. The final -p only marks the affix, so the derived stem is करुणार्द्र + चुञ्चु.

<answer>करुणार्द्रचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>तावकीनि</answer>

Before the taddhita affix मयट् (whose vowel is "a" once ट् is dropped), the final -ā of the feminine stem सौमित्रीया is deleted by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). That leaves सौमित्रीय, and adding मय gives सौमित्रीयमय.

<answer>सौमित्रीयमय</answer>

Formed by 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which adds चणप् after a word in the instrumental sense "known by". I did not check why this particular stem appears in the table, so I took it as given and applied the rule directly.

The final प् of चणप् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix that is actually added is चण. It has no ṇit marker that would trigger vṛddhi. It begins with a consonant, so the stem is a pada before it and its final अ is not elided (यस्येति च does not apply). The stem therefore stays unchanged: करन्थ + चण = करन्थचण.

<answer>करन्थचण</answer>

Taking the affix as the matvartha (possessive) इनि, which attaches to a stem ending in अ (अत इनिठनौ, 5.2.115), the final अ of ज्येष्ठेश्वर drops and इन् is added. This gives ज्येष्ठेश्वरिन्, "one possessing Jyeṣṭheśvara". The neuter gender of the source stem does not change the result.

<answer>ज्येष्ठेश्वरिन्</answer>

Following the standard rule for the comparative affix, तरप् (tarap) is added directly to the nominal stem. The stem ends in -a and takes no special changes. The neuter gender is not triggered here, so there is no shortening or other alteration. The result is a stem ending in -a.

<answer>शाकुन्तलोपाख्यानतर</answer>
<answer>प्लुष्टत्व</answer>

Here रूपप् is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), which is added in the sense of praise. As I recall it, 6.3.43 shortens a stem ending in the feminine suffix ई before this affix, so शुची becomes शुचि. Adding रूप gives शुचिरूप. I have not added the feminine टाप् (which would give शुचिरूपा), since you asked for the derived stem only. I applied Pāṇini's rule for the taddhita affix शस् (5.4.42–43). The stem मलना ends in the feminine -ā, and the affix begins with the consonant श, so it is not a vowel-initial affix. The elision of -ā by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148) therefore does not apply, and the stem keeps its long ā: मलना + शस् → मलनाशस्. The result is an indeclinable (1.1.38), and in pausa its final -s appears as visarga. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that introduces ञ्यट् after कम्र, so this form rests on the affix's marker letters alone.

- ट् is also indicatory. It would mark the feminine with ङीप्, but it does not change the stem here.
- The final अ of कम्र is dropped before the affix -य, giving काम्र्य.

The affix रूपप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), where it conveys praise. It is added directly to the stem, as in वैयाकरणरूपः, so no change is needed to the base. This gives the derived stem श्रेष्ठान्वयरूप, meaning roughly "praiseworthy one of excellent lineage".

Applying कन् to the stem gives गाङ्गामहिकक. This assumes a sense of कन् that applies to any nominal stem, such as the diminutive or pejorative use. I did not identify the exact rule behind this stem.

1. कन् is a taddhita affix, and its final न् is only an indicator, so what is added is क.
2. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped under 6.4.148 (यस्येति च लोपः), which applies only before an affix beginning with a vowel or य.
3. The stem therefore keeps its final अ and takes क directly, giving गाङ्गामहिक + क = गाङ्गामहिकक.
4. The ‑इक‑ substitution before क under 7.3.44 applies only when a feminine आप् follows, so it does not apply to this neuter stem.

<answer>गाङ्गामहिकक</answer>

Taking the stem आशिन् with the affix क (ka), which Pāṇini allows after any nominal stem in senses such as "unknown" or "contemptible" (5.3.73–74), the derivation runs as follows.

2. The form is the stem आशिक, which is neuter, the same gender as the source.

The final प् is only a marker and drops. The ञ् belongs to the syllable चुञ्चु and is not an indicatory letter, so it causes no vṛddhi. The stem is therefore unchanged and takes चुञ्चु directly.

I applied the iÑ suffix (A.4.1.95 "ata iñ", in the descendant sense) to the stem ऐकभौतिक, which ends in अ. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the suffix (A.6.4.148). The first vowel ऐ is already vṛddhi, so it stays unchanged. This gives ऐकभौतिक + इ = ऐकभौतिकि.

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule behind this affix, so this form is a best guess from the affix's shape and standard sandhi, not a derivation I could confirm.

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (*pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātracaḥ*), which gives forms like *ūrudaghna*. The final -c is only an indicatory letter and drops. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -a of the base is not elided. The affix has no ṇit or ñit marker, so there is no vṛddhi. The result is simply the base followed by -daghna.

Applying ञ्यङ् to the stem औत्सर्गिक is a mechanical derivation. I could not tie this stem to a specific rule licensing ञ्यङ्, so I formed it by the general rules.

1. The initial vowel औ is already vṛddhi, so the ञित् marker leaves it unchanged.
2. The affix is -य once its indicatory letters ञ् and ङ् are dropped.
3. The final -अ of the stem is deleted before the affix by "यस्येति च", so औत्सर्गिक becomes औत्सर्गिक्.
4. Adding -य gives औत्सर्गिक्य.

<answer>औत्सर्गिक्य</answer>

This is a derivation by the general rules; I did not identify a specific sūtra that licenses अञ् after this stem.

1. Start with समवायिन् + अ.
2. The affix has a ñit marker (ञ्), so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (अ → आ), giving सामवायिन् + अ.
3. Before a taddhita affix, the final टि of a stem in -न् is deleted (6.4.144 नस्तद्धिते), so the final -इन् drops. The exception इनण्यनपत्ये (6.4.164) names only the affix अण्, so it does not apply to अञ्.
4. The result is सामवाय.

<answer>सामवाय</answer>

This is the taddhita affix चरट् taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, *bhūtapūrve caraṭ* ("formerly was X"). It is added to the stem माषक without changing it, and the affix's ट् and र् are dropped as markers, leaving -चर. This gives माषकचर, "one who formerly was a māṣaka" (or who formerly had it). I recalled the rule from memory and did not check it against a source.

<answer>माषकचर</answer>

The affix चणप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, and it is added to a word in the instrumental sense "known by". For example, विद्यया वित्तः gives विद्याचणः.

Since चणप् is neither ñit nor ṇit, there is no vṛddhi. Its initial च is a consonant, so the final अ of सूक्ष्म is not elided. Adding the affix to the stem gives सूक्ष्म + चण = सूक्ष्मचण, which is a masculine a-stem.

<answer>सूक्ष्मचण</answer>

This gives शौचिष्ठ. I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् for this base, so the result rests on the general taddhita process.

<answer>शौचिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>व्यालमय</answer>

As I recall it, the final -ति is dropped, leaving अस्तात्. The stem's final अ is then elided before the affix (6.4.148), giving वाराटकीय + अस्तात् → वाराटकीयस्तात्.

<answer>वाराटकीयस्तात्</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यङ् for this stem, so this form comes from general derivation rules and is a best guess.

- The affix ञ्यङ् reduces to the suffix **-य**. Its ञ् marker calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the stem's initial vowel पा is already long.
- The stem पात्त्रिक्य ends in -अ. The ending -अ is dropped before a taddhita by यस्येति च, leaving पात्त्रिक्य्.
- Adding -य gives पात्त्रिक्य्य.

The affix देशीयर् (P. 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) is added after a subanta to express "almost, but not quite." The final र् is only a marker (इत्) and drops, leaving the affix देशीय.

Because देशीय begins with a consonant (द), the stem before it counts as a pada. The final न् of सहायार्थिन् is therefore deleted (P. 8.2.7, नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य). This gives सहायार्थि + देशीय.

The derivative means "almost a seeker of help."

<answer>सहायार्थिदेशीय</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*) for the sense "known by that". Here the ञ् is a real letter of the affix, and the final प् is only an indicatory marker. The affix therefore added is चुञ्चु, with no vṛddhi.

Before a consonant-initial taddhita affix other than य, the stem counts as a *pada* (1.4.17). The final न् of चुक्रिमन् therefore drops by 8.2.7 (*nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya*), giving चुक्रिम + चुञ्चु.

<answer>चुक्रिमचुञ्चु</answer>

<answer>दोषलसात्</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् after श्रेयस्, so this form rests on the general mechanism for an अञ् taddhita. Such an affix triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (आदिवृद्धि), and the final अ of the affix remains after the stem's final consonant.

1. श्रेयस् + अञ्: the indicatory ञ् marks vṛddhi of the first vowel, so ए of श्रे becomes ऐ, giving श्रै.
2. The stem then takes the affix's अ directly, so श्रैयस् + अ gives श्रैयस.

<answer>श्रैयस</answer>

Taking the affix शस् (Sas) as the one taught in Pāṇini 5.4.43 (*saṅkhyaikavacanāc ca vīpsāyām*), I add it to the stem सिध्मल in the distributive sense. This gives the indeclinable सिध्मलशः, "each sidhmala in turn". I chose this sūtra from recall and did not check it against a source. Pāṇini 5.4.42 (*bahvalpārthāc chas*) is the other sūtra that teaches शस्, but it applies only to stems meaning "many" or "few", which सिध्मल is not.

<answer>सिध्मलशः</answer>

The affix has no letters left, but it still affects the stem, since cvi itself lengthens a final stem vowel (च्वौ च, 7.4.26).

The stem बल्लवी already ends in a long ई. Nothing changes in this step, because the vowel is already long. The final form is therefore the same as the input, and it would appear before कृ, भू or अस्, as in बल्लवीभवति.

<answer>एकादशोत्तमदेश्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses ञ्यट् here, so this derivation follows the general mechanics of taddhita affixes.

2. The affix is ञ्यट्. Its ञ् and ट् are indicatory letters (*it*), so what is added is य. The ञ् marks vṛddhi of the first vowel, which here is already आ.
3. Before an affix beginning with य, the base counts as *bha* (भ). Its final आ is therefore dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), giving आश्वलक्षणिक् + य = आश्वलक्षणिक्य.
4. The ट् makes the affix *ṭit*, which would add feminine ङीप् (ई) only if a feminine output were wanted. The table does not ask for one, so I give the stem without it.

<answer>नाष्टिकचण</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् here, so this form is derived from the general taddhita mechanics rather than from a named rule.

1. The affix अञ् is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117 तद्धितेषु अचामादेः). This turns नि into नै.
2. The final अ of the affix is added, giving a stem in -अ.
3. The स् of आयुस् follows उ and is no longer pada-final before the vowel-initial affix, so it becomes ष् (8.3.59 आदेशप्रत्यययोः).

This gives नैमित्तायुष.

<answer>नैमित्तायुष</answer>

I could not identify the rule that introduces जाहच्, so this form rests on a general derivation and is not confirmed against Pāṇini's text.

1. In जाहच्, the initial ज् and the final च् are indicatory letters (it), which leaves the operative affix आह.
2. The stem सर्वानुक्रमणिका ends in the feminine suffix आ (टाप्).
3. By 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), the stem-final आ is dropped before an affix that begins with a vowel, giving सर्वानुक्रमणिक्.
4. Adding आह gives सर्वानुक्रमणिकाह.

<answer>सर्वानुक्रमणिकाह</answer>

The affix रूपप् (rūpap) is added by Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्) to a subanta to express praise. The affix reduces to the form रूप. The base मटक is a neuter stem and nothing in it needs to change. The derived stem is therefore मटक + रूप.

<answer>मटकरूप</answer>

I could not confirm which rule this "rUpya" affix comes from, so this form is a best guess. I took it to be the affix यप् added to रूप, as in "रूपादाहतप्रशंसयोर्यप्" (P. 5.2.120). That rule does not obviously apply to a stem like वाताहता, so I simply attached रूप्य to the stem.

For the feminine आ-ending stem, I assumed the final आ is shortened before the affix, following P. 6.3.43. That sūtra covers a feminine stem before रूप and similar words, and its application to this affix is an assumption. This gives वाताहतरूप्य rather than वाताहतारूप्य.

<answer>वाताहतरूप्य</answer>
<answer>क्षैत्रज्ञ्यतर</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so the meaning and exact conditions of the affix are assumed here. The affix is जाह with the final च् as an indicatory letter.

1. The stem सूरिन् ends in न् and is followed by a taddhita affix beginning with the consonant ज्.
2. Because the affix begins with a consonant other than य, the stem keeps the pada status of a stem before a consonant-initial affix and is not treated as a भ-stem. So the rule नस्तद्धिते (6.4.144), which drops the टि of a भ-stem, does not apply.
3. Instead, the final न् of the pada stem is dropped by नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (8.2.7), giving सूरि + जाह.

<answer>सूरिजाह</answer>
<answer>माङ्गलिकतर</answer>

This is an application of P. 4.1.120 (स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्), which adds ढक् to a feminine stem. I did not check ध्रौव्या against a source, so the result rests on the rule itself.

1. ढक् begins with ढ्, which is replaced by एय (P. 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The affix therefore becomes एय.
2. Because ढक् is marked ड्, the टि-part of the stem is deleted before it (P. 6.4.143). Here that is the final आ of ध्रौव्या, leaving ध्रौव्य्.
3. Adding एय to ध्रौव्य् gives ध्रौव्येय. I am treating ढक् as having no vṛddhi effect on the stem, since the stem already has the vowel औ.

<answer>ध्रौव्येय</answer>

The stem डुली is a feminine stem in ई, and इष्ठन् is a taddhita affix, so the final ई is dropped before it by "yasyeti ca" (6.4.148). The ष्ठ comes from the affix after its ‑न् marker is dropped. I did not check this rule's scope for stems in ई against a source, so the result rests on that reading.

डुल् + इष्ठ → डुलिष्ठ

<answer>डुलिष्ठ</answer>

This is a direct formation: the affix त्रा (Pāṇini 5.4.55, which gives it after certain nouns in the second and seventh case relations) is added to the stem. I did not verify the rule against the text, and काम्पिल्य is not one of the stems that rule lists, so this rests on the table naming the affix. The stem is not changed before the affix, so the result is काम्पिल्य + त्रा = काम्पिल्यत्रा, with the sense "in Kāmpilya".

<answer>काम्पिल्यत्रा</answer>
<answer>वान्दनेय</answer>

This is an application of the rule तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ (Pāṇini 5.2.26), which gives चुञ्चु and चण after a stem to mean "known by that". I formed it from memory and did not check it against a commentary.

1. The affix चुञ्चुप् leaves चुञ्चु once the final प् is dropped as an indicatory letter.
2. चुञ्चु begins with a consonant other than य, so it does not trigger the भ-designation (1.4.18). The stem therefore keeps पद status (1.4.17).
3. As a पद, वराकाङ्क्षिन् loses its final न् by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), giving वराकाङ्क्षि.
4. Adding चुञ्चु gives वराकाङ्क्षिचुञ्चु.

<answer>वराकाङ्क्षिचुञ्चु</answer>

Taking the stem as ending in the feminine suffix -ā, the affix ईयसुन् reduces to ईयस् after dropping its indicatory letters उ and न्. The final आ of सूर्योढा is then deleted before the ई-initial taddhita affix, by the rule यस्येति च, giving सूर्योढ् + ईयस् = सूर्योढीयस्. I did not check this against a source, so the treatment of the feminine -ā (no पुंवद्भाव assumed) rests on my recollection of the rules.

<answer>सूर्योढीयस्</answer>
<answer>मूटकी</answer>

I could not tie सप्तिक to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for वलच् (the usual ones are 5.2.112 and 5.2.113, which take other bases), so this form rests only on the general rule for adding the affix. The affix वलच् leaves the stem unchanged, and its final च् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix is added as -वल. Because वल begins with a consonant, the final अ of सप्तिक is not elided by "yasyeti ca", and no other rule applies. The result is सप्तिक + वल = सप्तिकवल.

<answer>सप्तिकवल</answer>

This is based on my recollection of Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, which I did not check against the text. The affix चणप् is added to the stem, and the final प् is only a marker, so the actual affix is चण. The form begins with च, so no vowel sandhi occurs and the stem's final vowel is kept. Examples I recall from the commentary are केशचणः and विद्याचणः. Following the same pattern, द्वीरावतीक + चण gives द्वीरावतीकचण.

I could not match द्वीरावतीक to the usual examples for this sutra, so the formation follows the affix pattern rather than a specific attested word.

<answer>द्वीरावतीकचण</answer>

This is a formation under Pāṇini 5.2.37 (pramāṇe dvayasac-daghnañ-mātracaḥ), where the affix attaches to a word that gives a measure. I did not check that मौञ्जकायन works as a measure word, so I applied the affix as the table asks.

The final च् of द्वयसच् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the affix द्वयस. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not altered and takes no vṛddhi. The derived stem is therefore मौञ्जकायन + द्वयस.

<answer>मौञ्जकायनद्वयस</answer>

I derived this by the usual rules rather than from a specific sūtra, so the form is my best reconstruction, not a verified attestation.

The stem गार्ह्या ends in the feminine suffix -ā (गार्ह् + य + आ). Before a taddhita beginning with य, the final -ā of the bha-aṅga is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). That leaves गार्ह्य्, and adding यत् (-ya) gives गार्ह्य्य. No vṛddhi applies, because यत् is neither ñit nor ṇit and the initial vowel is already long.

<answer>गार्ह्य्य</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them, not checked against the text of the sūtras.

1. The affix ठक् (ṭhak) has ठ् replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50). This gives the ending -ika.
2. The stem लवका ends in the feminine suffix ā, and that final आ is dropped before a taddhita affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148). This leaves लवक्.
3. ठक् is only ṭit, not ñit or ṇit, so there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel.
4. Joining लवक् and इक gives लवकिक.

<answer>लवकिक</answer>
<answer>मुग्धालोकतर</answer>

Here, *astāti* is the Pāṇinian affix of 5.3.27, which gives forms like *purastāt*. I took it as applying to the stem कूर्चल as given.

1. कूर्चल + अस्ताति: the affix is a taddhita, so the stem-final अ drops before it (*yasyeti ca*, 6.4.148). This gives कूर्चल् + अस्ताति.
2. The final ि of the affix, the *ṭi* part, is elided (6.4.143), leaving the form अस्तात्.
3. Joining them gives कूर्चलस्तात्, which is indeclinable.

<answer>कूर्चलस्तात्</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) is added to a nominal stem in the sense of "becoming what it was not", and it is used together with कृ, भू or अस् (अभूततद्भावे, Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.50). The whole affix is then elided, and the stem-final अ becomes ई by अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32). So तीराट (tīrāṭa) becomes तीराटी, which is indeclinable, as in तीराटीकरोति.

<answer>तीराटी</answer>
<answer>स्तम्भोत्कीर्णाथा</answer>
<answer>वर्ष्मतम</answer>

बद्धानुशया में आबन्त स्त्रीलिंग शब्द है। उसके बाद घ-संज्ञक तरप् आने पर, "ह्रस्वः" (६.३.४३) के अनुसार ङ्याप्-अन्त शब्द का अन्तिम दीर्घ स्वर ह्रस्व हो जाता है, इसलिए बद्धानुशया का अन्तिम आ ह्रस्व अ बनता है। तब प्रातिपदिक बद्धानुशय + तर बनता है, और स्त्रीलिंग में टाप् जुड़ने से बद्धानुशयतरा बनता है। इस नियम के आबन्त शब्दों पर लागू होने की बात मैंने स्मृति से मानी है, उसकी पुष्टि नहीं की है।

<answer>बद्धानुशयतरा</answer>

I could not tie this to one specific sūtra, so the derivation below is the generic one for a ख-type affix.

1. The affix खञ् takes ख → ईन (by "आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्").
2. The final -ा of the टाप् feminine ending in शास्त्रोक्ता is elided before the affix by "यस्येति च", leaving शास्त्रोक्त्.
3. The ञ् marker would normally trigger vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the first vowel शा is already vṛddhi, so nothing changes.
4. Adding ईन gives शास्त्रोक्तीन.

<answer>शास्त्रोक्तीन</answer>
<answer>वैतनीयस्</answer>

Following P. 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, "known by that"), the affix चणप् is added to the stem चरणोदक. The final प् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix becomes चण. Its initial च is retained, because in a taddhita affix the initial च is not an indicatory letter. The stem ends in अ and the affix begins with a consonant, so there is no elision of the stem's final vowel. The result follows the pattern of the textbook examples विद्याचणः and अक्षरचणः.

<answer>चरणोदकचण</answer>
<answer>सांतपनतम</answer>
<answer>धितववल</answer>

This is a reasoned derivation; I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् on this stem.

The affix अञ् is ñit, so it normally triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel. The stem ऐकशतिक already begins with ऐ, which is the vṛddhi vowel, so there is no further change there. The final अ of the stem is then dropped before the affix (यस्येति च), and the affix अ is added. This gives ऐकशतिक् + अ, which returns the same surface form.

<answer>ऐकशतिक</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.37, which gives द्वयसच्, दघ्नच् and मात्रच् in the sense of "measure" (प्रमाणे). The affix is added directly to the stem वैमत्तायन. It begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not dropped, and the final च् is only an accent marker. This gives the stem वैमत्तायनदघ्न.

<answer>वैमत्तायनदघ्न</answer>

Applying the affix छ (Ca), which is replaced by ईय, to the stem शटि gives the form below. I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses छ for this stem, so I assumed the general substitution छ → ईय. The final इ of the stem is then dropped before the affix (यस्येति च): शट् + ईय = शटीय.

<answer>शटीय</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rules for the affix, not a form I could tie to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for this stem.

1. The affix खञ् has the final ञ् as an indicatory letter, and the initial ख् is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, by 7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).
2. Because the affix carries ञ्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117): शु → शौ.
3. The stem-final आ is dropped before the affix, which begins with a vowel (6.4.148 यस्येति च).
4. This gives शौष्काङ्ग + ईन = शौष्काङ्गीन.

<answer>शौष्काङ्गीन</answer>

This is derived by rule recall; I could not pin down which meaning-rule licenses छ for this stem, though the question accepts any licensed meaning.

The affix छ is replaced by ईय (by आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्, 7.1.2). The stem शुभार्थिन् ends in न्, so before the taddhita ईय it takes the भ-designation. The rule नस्तद्धिते (6.4.144) then drops its टि, which here is इन्. That leaves शुभार्थ. The final अ is then dropped before ईय (यस्येति च), and the result is शुभार्थ् + ईय = शुभार्थीय.

<answer>शुभार्थीय</answer>

I formed this from the affix साति (Pāṇini 5.4.52–54) without checking it against a source for a feminine base. Attached to a base, the affix gives an indeclinable ending in -सात्, as in अग्निसात् and राजसात्. I took the final इ of साति to be only for pronunciation, so the working affix is सात्. I also assumed that the feminine ending ई of कर्षिणी is kept unchanged before the taddhita, so the result is कर्षिणीसात्.

<answer>कर्षिणीसात्</answer>

Adding तमप् (the superlative affix) to पेचकिन् gives a stem before an affix beginning with a consonant, so the stem counts as a pada (1.4.17). The final न् is therefore dropped by नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (8.2.7). Likewise तपस्विन् gives तपस्वितम. The result is पेचकि + तम.

<answer>पेचकितम</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशस्ते रूपप्) allows the affix रूपप् after a nominal stem to express "praiseworthy". The final प् is only a marker and drops out. The stem वैकर्णेय takes the affix unchanged, giving वैकर्णेयरूप. I recalled the rule from memory and did not check it against a source.

<answer>वैकर्णेयरूप</answer>
<answer>नेत्रौषधीत्व</answer>
<answer>औरसिकजातीय</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), the affix चरट् means "formerly was". Its ट् only marks the feminine (ṅīp), and the initial च is not replaced. So the affix attaches directly to the stem: पुलोम + चर = पुलोमचर, "formerly Puloma".

<answer>पुलोमचर</answer>
<answer>झिण्टिकात्रा</answer>

The affix रूपप् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), which gives the sense "praiseworthy …". Adding it to आष्टकीय gives the stem आष्टकीयरूप. I did not check this against a source beyond recalling that rule. The stem is neuter, so no feminine-to-masculine (पुंवत्) change applies.

<answer>आष्टकीयरूप</answer>

The affix रूपप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), which expresses praise, as in पटुरूप. The final प् is only a marker and drops out. Adding रूप to the stem gives:

<answer>दन्ताग्रीयरूप</answer>

ईर्ष्यिन् takes the affix साति (for example अग्निसात्, राजसात्). Before this affix the stem counts as a pada, so the final न् is dropped, as in राजन् → राजसात्. The affix's final इ is also lost, so the result is an indeclinable ending in -सात्. This is from my recollection of the sūtras and the standard examples, not a step-by-step derivation.

<answer>ईर्ष्यिसात्</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठन् after हल्लक, so this derivation rests on the general rules for the affix rather than on a located rule.

1. The affix ठन् has its initial ठ् replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50). The markers ट् and न् do not trigger vṛddhi, so the stem vowels stay unchanged.
2. The final अ of हल्लक is dropped before the affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148). This gives हल्लक् + इक = हल्लकिक.

<answer>हल्लकिक</answer>
<answer>वैश्यातः</answer>

The affix ञ्यट् loses its markers: ञ् and ट् are both indicatory and drop, leaving the suffix -य. Because ञ् makes it ñit, the first vowel of the stem takes ādi-vṛddhi (7.2.117).

1. Start with stem रेच्य and add the suffix य.
2. The final -अ of the stem (the अ of -य) is elided before a taddhita suffix by 6.4.148, giving रेच्य्.
3. Ādi-vṛddhi turns the initial ए into ऐ, giving रैच्य्.
4. Adding the suffix य gives रैच्य्य.

I could not identify which Pāṇinian rule introduces ञ्यट्, so the steps above assume the usual treatment of ñit taddhita suffixes.

<answer>रैच्य्य</answer>

This is a straightforward formation: the affix क is added to the stem कृशित, which ends in -a, with no further change. The result is कृशितक. This is reasoned from the table rather than tied to a specific sūtra. The neuter gender of the source does not alter the stem, and the -ikā substitution applies only to feminine stems in -ā.

<answer>कृशितक</answer>

I could not confirm which sūtra licenses this exact case. I assumed the affix त्रा attaches directly to the stem, in the pattern of forms like देवत्रा. Under that assumption, the final -ā of पुला is not elided before त्रा, so the result is पुला + त्रा = पुलात्रा.

<answer>पुलात्रा</answer>

This is my best reading of the table, not a rule I could pin down with certainty. I took तसि as the Pāṇinian ablative-sense affix (as in 5.4.44–45), which has the form -तस् and gives an indeclinable. I could not pin down the specific rule that licenses छ after रणैषिन्, so this derivation rests on the general mechanics of the affix rather than a cited sūtra.

The affix द्वयसच् (dvayasac) is added to the stem मवर directly. I did not derive this from a specific rule application; I only checked that nothing alters the stem.

I derived this by working through the rules from memory and did not check them against the text of the Aṣṭādhyāyī.

1. Adding कन् to सान्तःस्था leaves क, because the न् is only an indicatory letter.

3. The result is feminine, so the feminine suffix टाप् is added: सान्तःस्थका.
4. Under 7.3.44, a non-final अ before the क of a pratyaya, followed by a feminine आप्, becomes इ. This gives सान्तःस्थिका.

<answer>सान्तःस्थिका</answer>

I could not confirm the exact derivation, so this form rests on partial reasoning.

I took दघ्नच् to be the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.37, which gives the sense "as much as" a measured extent. Its initial द is a consonant, so the stem is not treated as bha before it. That means the final आ of काण्ठेविद्ध्या is not dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving a stem in -अ.

This gives काण्ठेविद्ध्या + दघ्न = काण्ठेविद्ध्यादघ्न.

<answer>काण्ठेविद्ध्यादघ्न</answer>
<answer>साधावल</answer>

Taddhita मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) begins with a consonant, so the stem-final आ of शिशया is not dropped. Adding मात्र gives the neuter stem शिशयामात्र. I derived this from the rules as I recall them and did not check it against a source.

<answer>शिशयामात्र</answer>
<answer>लोकाभिलाषिष्ठ</answer>

This derivation is a formal one: I did not trace वास्तव to a specific sūtra or meaning, and the form below is the one I derived.

The affix वलच् has the final अच् as a marker only, so what is added is -वल. It begins with a consonant (व्), and the stem before such an affix counts as a pada, not as a bha-stem. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148), which would delete a final अ, therefore does not apply. This is the same pattern as in रजस्वल and कृषीवल. The final अ of वास्तव stays, giving वास्तव + वल = वास्तववल.

<answer>वास्तववल</answer>

Rule 5.3.23 (*prakāravacane thāl*) provides the affix थाल्, which means "in that manner". It is added to the stem हीरक, and the final ल् is only a marker (it fixes the accent) and drops. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem is not elided. The result is हीरक + था = हीरकथा, which is indeclinable (an avyaya), so it takes no case or number endings.

This is a mechanical formation: the rule is taught for pronominal stems, and I applied it to हीरक as the table directs.

<answer>हीरकथा</answer>
<answer>षोडशांशुमत्</answer>
<answer>खननीयवत्</answer>

I could not identify the Aṣṭādhyāyī rule that prescribes ञ्यट् for this stem, so this form is derived from general principles rather than from a located sūtra.

1. The final ā of the feminine stem त्वचा is dropped before the taddhita affix, giving त्वच्.
2. The affix ञ्यट् leaves ञ्य, since ञ् and ट् are indicatory letters. Because ञ् marks the affix as ñit, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi, so त्वच् becomes त्वाच्.
3. Adding ञ्य gives त्वाच्य.

The affix's ṭ would normally call for a feminine ṅīp, but I have left the stem in its basic form without it. I am not certain this is the form intended.

<answer>त्वाच्य</answer>
<answer>वेल्लिताग्रकल्प</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68–69 in the sense of "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is placed before the subanta, so बहु is prefixed to the stem, and the feminine ending -ā of अर्द्यमाना is left unchanged. Since the result is a single word, sandhi applies: बहु + अर्द्यमाना → बह्वर्द्यमाना.

I have not checked this against a source for feminine stems specifically, so the retention of -ā (no puṃvadbhāva or shortening) rests on my reading of the rules.

<answer>बह्वर्द्यमाना</answer>

श्मश्रुल is a masculine stem ending in -अ, so the patronymic affix इञ् applies by "अत इञ्" (Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.95), meaning "descendant of श्मश्रुल". The final -अ of the stem is dropped before the affix. The first vowel takes vṛddhi, so श्म → श्मा. This gives श्माश्रुलि.

<answer>श्माश्रुलि</answer>

The stem सात्म ends in -a and the affix अञ् is ञित्, so two rules apply:

1. The first vowel takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि). Here it is already ā in सा, so nothing changes.
2. The final -a of the stem is deleted before the affix (यस्येति च). That gives सात्म् + अ.

The result is spelled the same as the input stem. I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra licensing अञ् on this stem, so I derived the form from the general rules for ञित् affixes.

<answer>सात्म</answer>

I could not confirm the exact Pāṇinian rule licensing त्रा on this stem, so I added the affix directly; it should be the one in 5.4.55 (देये त्रा च). The affix त्रा is added to the stem षाड्विध्य without further change. The result is an indeclinable, so no case or number ending follows.

<answer>षाड्विध्यत्रा</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), in the sense "known by that". Examples are विद्याचुञ्चुः and केशचुञ्चुः. The final प् is only an indicatory letter and drops out. चुञ्चु carries no ṇit or ṅit marker, so the stem-final इ is not elided. The affix is simply added to भद्राकृति.
