The affix इञ् is added in the sense of "descendant" (अत इञ्, A.4.1.95).

1. The stem मेय ends in अ, so that final अ is dropped before the affix (A.6.4.148), leaving मेय् + इ.
2. Because the affix has the marker ञ्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (A.7.2.117), so ए becomes ऐ.
3. The result is मैय् + इ = मैयि.

<answer>मैयि</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), the affix रूपप् is added to a subanta word to express praise. The final प् is only an indicatory marker and drops out. The case ending of the base is elided, so रूप attaches directly to कैरातक. This gives कैरातकरूप, meaning "an excellent कैरातक". No other change applies here.

<answer>कैरातकरूप</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.2.37, the affix दघ्नच् (daghnac) is added to the stem रात्री. Its initial द is a consonant, so the stem ending ई is not dropped. The final च् is only an indicatory letter and disappears, leaving the affix as दघ्न. This gives the stem रात्रीदघ्न. I did not check this against an attested example, so it rests on the rule reasoning alone.

<answer>रात्रीदघ्न</answer>

Here the affix छ (SLP1 Ca) is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṁ pratyayādīnām"). I assumed the vṛddha-initial rule 4.2.114 ("vṛddhāc chaḥ") as the licensing rule, since सासूया begins with the vṛddhi vowel ā. I did not check this against a specific source. The final ā of the stem is dropped before the affix by 6.4.148 ("yasyeti ca"), which gives सासूयीय.

<answer>सासूयीय</answer>

This is an application of मयट् to the stem वारेण्यायनि, which ends in -इ. The affix is licensed, for example, in the sense "abundant" (तत्प्रकृतवचने मयट्, 5.4.21).

मयट् begins with the consonant म, so the stem takes pada status and its final इ is not elided. The affix is neither ञित् nor णित्, so there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel. The final ट् is only a marker, and the affix reduces to मय. The result is the stem वारेण्यायनि + मय.

<answer>वारेण्यायनिमय</answer>

The stem कर्बुरी already ends in the long ई (a ङीप् feminine). The affix वलच् begins with the consonant व, so the stem takes it as a pada-stem and the long ई stays unchanged, as in कृषीवल. The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops out, leaving the derived stem कर्बुरीवल. I reasoned this by analogy with कृषीवल rather than from a specific rule licensing वलच् after कर्बुरी, so the match is by pattern.

<answer>कर्बुरीवल</answer>

I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप् here, so this form is derived from the affix's mechanics rather than from a located sūtra.

The affix is कुणप् (kuṇap). Its ण् marker calls for ādi-vṛddhi, but the first vowel of द्वादशाक्ष is already the vṛddhi vowel आ (in द्वा), so nothing changes there. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix's initial vowel, and the form then ends in -a.

द्वादशाक्ष + कुण → द्वादशाक्ष् + कुण → द्वादशाक्षकुण

<answer>द्वादशाक्षकुण</answer>

I did not match this to a specific Pāṇinian rule giving यत् after this stem, so the derivation below covers only the stem change before the affix.

The stem शिरोपस्थायिन् ends in -इन्, which counts as a bha stem before the taddhita affix यत्. By 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते), the ṭi part (the last vowel together with what follows it, here -इन्) of a stem ending in न् is dropped before a taddhita affix.

- शिरोपस्थायिन् + य → शिरोपस्थाय् + य
- Result: शिरोपस्थाय्य

<answer>शिरोपस्थाय्य</answer>

I am not certain of this form. The affix तल् (tal) is the bhāva-affix of "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (5.1.119). It surfaces as ता and makes a feminine stem in -ā.

The usual पुंवद्भाव rule (6.3.35) does not seem to reach तल्, since तल् is not among the तसिल्-type affixes it covers. So the feminine stem गौष्ठी should keep its long ई, and adding ता gives गौष्ठीता.

<answer>गौष्ठीता</answer>

I could not identify a specific rule that applies this affix to this stem. I formed the derivative by simple attachment.

The affix is वलच्. Its final च् is only a marker and drops, leaving the suffix -वल. The suffix begins with व, which is neither a vowel nor य, so the stem's final ā is not elided. The feminine stem श्लाघिता therefore keeps its form, and adding -वल gives श्लाघितावल.

<answer>श्लाघितावल</answer>

<answer>कोमलदेशीय</answer>
<answer>विश्वावर्तत्रा</answer>

This is a derivation by the rules as I recall them, not a form I could confirm in a source. The affix थमु loses its marker उ and becomes थम्, giving an indeclinable (avyaya). Since थम् begins with a consonant, the stem प्रेयस् takes pada status. Its final स् passes through ru and visarga, and visarga before the aspirate थ becomes स् again. The result is प्रेयस्थम्.

<answer>प्रेयस्थम्</answer>

Using P.5.3.57 (द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ), the affix ईयसुन् is added to the stem अप्रमाणाभ. Before ईयसुन्, the टि (the final vowel with any following consonant) of the stem is deleted by P.6.4.155 (टेः). So अप्रमाणाभ → अप्रमाणाभ्, which with ईयस् gives अप्रमाणाभीयस्.

<answer>अप्रमाणाभीयस्</answer>

The affix थमु (Tamu) leaves the मु as an it-marker, so the affix that is actually added is -थम्. The form below follows from my reading of the rules, not from an attested example.

2. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem stands as a pada before it. The final न् is therefore dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), leaving चित्रि.
3. Adding the affix gives चित्रि + थम् = चित्रिथम्. This is an indeclinable, since a taddhita ending of this kind takes no case endings.

<answer>चित्रिथम्</answer>

Taking the affix ṭhan (SLP1 `Wan`) in the sense "possessing", by "ata iniṭhanau" (5.2.115), which applies to stems ending in short a:

1. The stem is बलक, and the affix is ठन्.
2. The final ṭhan loses its markers ṭ and n, leaving ठ.
3. By "ṭhasyekaḥ" (7.3.50), ठ is replaced by इक.
4. The stem-final अ of बलक drops before the vowel of इक, which gives बलक् + इक = बलकिक.
5. ṭhan carries no ñ or ṇ marker, so there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel.

<answer>बलकिक</answer>

The stem शौल्किक ends in short अ. The affix इनि is added in the sense of possession by the rule अत इनिठनौ (5.2.115), which allows इनि after a-ending stems. Before the vowel-initial affix, the final अ of the stem is dropped (यस्येति च), giving शौल्किक् + इन्. Since इनि is neither ञित् nor णित्, no vṛddhi or other change applies. The resulting stem is शौल्किकिन्, "possessing a शौल्किक".

<answer>शौल्किकिन्</answer>

The affix क (ka) is added directly to the stem नैवाकवीय. The stem already ends in अ, so no other change applies. This gives the stem नैवाकवीयक, which I formed from general knowledge of the ka affix without checking a specific sūtra.

<answer>मेघास्थिजाह</answer>

This is my best reconstruction. I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that teaches ञ्यट्, so the derivation rests on the general taddhita procedure.

1. The stem अशितव्या ends in the feminine suffix टाप् (आ). Before the taddhita affix, its final आ is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), leaving अशितव्.

The affix अञ् is added to शैखण्ड, and the form is worked out as follows. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule behind this pairing, so I derived the form from the general mechanics of the affix.

The affix चणप् (caRap) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, with the sense "known or famous by that". The final प् is only an indicatory marker (it affects accent), so the affix that remains is चण. The stem उपलब्धार्थ ends in -अ, but चण begins with a consonant, so the stem is not truncated by *yasyeti ca*. The affix is simply added after the stem, as in केश + चण → केशचण.

This is the affix चणप् of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which I am recalling from memory rather than checking. I did not derive this from a confirmed rule. I assumed the affix is *deśya* of Pāṇini 5.3.67, which means "slightly incomplete" (*īṣad-asamāpti*), and attached it to the stem भूमिका. This is the affix देशीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, in the sense of "not quite complete") added to the stem पुत्रेज्या.

Sanskrit has no standard rule I could confirm for this exact form, so this derivation rests on my reading of the rules. The affix जातीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added to the stem कूचिका, giving the sense "of the kind of a कूचिका".

Adding the affix अण् (aṇ) triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (ओ → औ), and the final अ of the stem drops before the affix's अ. This gives दोलान्दोलन → दौलान्दोलन, "relating to swinging to and fro".

The stem उपजल्पिन् ends in -इन्. When a taddhita affix such as यत् is added, the final टि (the last vowel and the consonant after it, here इन्) is dropped by 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते). यत् has no ञ् or ण् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. The result is उपजल्प् + य.

I treated the ण् as part of the affix, which leaves the base's initial vowel unchanged (no vṛddhi). The feminine ending -ā of हतेक्षणा drops before the affix, so हतेक्षण + कुण gives हतेक्षणकुण.

<answer>हतेक्षणकुण</answer>
<answer>लौहायस</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses कुणप् for this stem, so this form is derived by the general rules rather than from a located sūtra.

The affix कुणप् leaves the pieces कुण (the प् is only a marker). Before it, the final आ of सैंहिका is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), leaving सैंहिक्. The ण् marker would call for vṛddhi of the first vowel, but it is already vṛddhi (सै), so nothing changes. Joining सैंहिक् and कुण gives सैंहिककुण.

<answer>सैंहिककुण</answer>

This is a recollection, not a verified derivation. I believe the affix जाहच् is taught in a Kāśikā vārttika for "kind or manner of" (प्रकारवचने) senses, alongside जातीयर्.

The final च् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix is added as जाह. It carries no ञ, ण or क that would trigger vṛddhi or other changes, so the stem कैट stays unchanged. This gives कैट + जाह = कैटजाह, a masculine stem ending in -a.

<answer>कैटजाह</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule or meaning for the affix कुणप् with any confidence, so this form is a best guess.

I read the affix as कुण, taking the final प् as the only indicatory letter. Since it begins with a consonant, the final -अ of सेधनीय is not elided. Nothing in the affix's markers calls for vṛddhi, so the stem is unchanged and the affix is added directly.

<answer>सेधनीयकुण</answer>
<answer>चरितार्थचर</answer>

I recall that चरट् is the affix of "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Pāṇini 5.3.53), meaning "formerly such". I formed the stem by adding चर to the full stem वगला, and I did not recall a rule that shortens the final ā of वगला before this affix, so I kept it long. I am not certain of this last point.

<answer>वगलाचर</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् (izWan) is the superlative suffix, added to the stem मिषि.

Before इष्ठन् the stem loses its final vowel together with any consonants after it (the "ṭi" part, by the rule टेः, 6.4.155). Here that is only the final इ, so मिषि becomes मिष्.

Adding इष्ठ gives मिष् + इष्ठ = मिषिष्ठ. No further sandhi applies.

I derived this from the general rules and did not check it against a stated example.

<answer>मिषिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>खण्डिताशंसमय</answer>

उत्क से अञ् (अण्-प्रकार) लगाने पर आदि स्वर की वृद्धि होती है: उ → औ। अन्तिम अ का लोप होता है और अञ् का अ जुड़ता है। इससे औत्क बनता है। यह रूप सामान्य अञ्/अण् नियम पर आधारित है। मैंने इस प्रत्यय के लिए कोई विशिष्ट सूत्र सत्यापित नहीं किया।

<answer>औत्क</answer>
<answer>ज्वालिता</answer>

Following Pāṇini 7.4.13, "ke ṇaḥ" (an अण् vowel of the stem is shortened before क), I shorten the stem-final आ of अनन्तरीया before क. This gives अनन्तरीय + क, which is अनन्तरीयक.

I am giving the taddhita stem itself, without adding a feminine ending. If the feminine were formed again, 7.3.44 would change the preceding अ to इ and give अनन्तरीयिका, but that is a separate step.

<answer>अनन्तरीयक</answer>

I could not recall the Pāṇinian rule that introduces this affix, so this form is derived by general principles, not checked against the rule.

The affix जाहच् has च् as an indicatory letter, which is dropped, leaving जाह. The affix has no ञ् or ण् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. It begins with the consonant ज्, not a vowel or य्, so the final उ of अदब्धायु is not elided. The stem and affix therefore join directly.

<answer>अदब्धायुजाह</answer>
<answer>मड्डुस्तात्</answer>

Here शस् is the distributive affix (as in बहुशः, एकैकशः). It is added to the stem गार्गा, which stays unchanged, and the result is an indeclinable ending in visarga: गार्गा + शस् → गार्गाशस् → गार्गाशः. I applied the affix by analogy with बहुशः and did not check this specific form against a source.

<answer>गार्गाशः</answer>
<answer>एकाश्रितचर</answer>
<answer>ऊढमय</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् is taught in the sense of measure (प्रमाणे, A. 5.2.37), as in ऊरुदघ्न. The final च् is only an marker and drops, so the affix is दघ्न.

The stem मन्दानुसारिन् ends in -न्. Before an affix beginning with द, the stem keeps the status of a pada (A. 1.4.17). So its final न् is deleted by नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (A. 8.2.7), leaving मन्दानुसारि. Adding दघ्न gives मन्दानुसारिदघ्न.

<answer>मन्दानुसारिदघ्न</answer>

The affix ईयसुन् (ईयस् after the इत् letters are dropped) is added to देवतानुक्रमणी. The stem ends in the feminine ई, and ईयस् begins with ई. By "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), the final ई of the stem is deleted, giving देवतानुक्रमण् + ईयस्. I did not check this against a source. The derived stem is therefore देवतानुक्रमणीयस्.

<answer>देवतानुक्रमणीयस्</answer>

I could not recall the rule that introduces जाहच् with certainty, so this form is a best guess. I treated जाहच् as adding the affix जाह, with the final च् as an indicatory letter. Because the affix begins with a consonant, I assumed the stem-final आ is neither dropped nor shortened.

<answer>मदिरोत्कटाजाह</answer>
<answer>हृदयेशशः</answer>

Following the taddhita rule तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ (Pāṇini 5.2.26), the affix चुञ्चु ("known by that") is added to the stem पञ्चाक्षरा. This is the same pattern as विद्याचुञ्चुः from विद्या, where the final आ is kept. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem takes pada status and the final आ is not dropped. I did not verify the form against a source for this exact stem. The result is the masculine stem पञ्चाक्षराचुञ्चु.

<answer>पञ्चाक्षराचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47, याप्ये पाशप्, and is added to a nominal word to mean "bad" or "despicable". The affix leaves the stem ending in -पाश. The feminine stem दुवसना is kept unchanged before it, because the rule that shortens a stem ending in ṅī or āp (6.3.43) does not list पाशप्. This gives दुवसनापाश. I chose the plain stem here and did not add the feminine ending ā (दुवसनापाशा), which would also be arguable.

<answer>दुवसनापाश</answer>

The affix तसि (तसिल्) is added to the stem क्रौड. It takes the ablative sense, as in प्रतियोगे पञ्चम्यास्तसिः (5.4.44). The stem ends in -अ, so the affix is attached directly and no further change applies. This gives the indeclinable क्रौडतः. The neuter gender of the source stem does not affect the result.

<answer>क्रौडतः</answer>

Applying तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ (Pāṇini 5.2.26), the affix चुञ्चुप् is added to the stem वैद्यका, giving a taddhita meaning "known/famous by that".

The affix begins with च, so the stem takes the pada designation and its final आ is kept unchanged. The final प् is only an indicatory marker and drops out. This gives the derived stem वैद्यका + चुञ्चु. I derived this by applying the rule directly, without checking it against a worked example.

<answer>वैद्यकाचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to the stem. The final च् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix द्वयस.

The stem काटयवेम ends in -अ and the affix begins with a consonant, so there is no vowel replacement or other change at the junction. The stem and affix simply join.

<answer>काटयवेमद्वयस</answer>

I did not derive this from a specific rule application; it rests on one assumption about how the stem-final ā behaves before the affix.

The affix वलच् (valac) is a taddhita, so its final च् is only an indicatory letter and the affix itself is वल. Because वल begins with the consonant व्, the stem does not count as भ (rule 1.4.18, यचि भम्, covers only affixes beginning with य् or a vowel). It is therefore a पद (1.4.17), and the rule that deletes a final अ/आ before a taddhita (6.4.148, यस्येति च) does not apply. The stem-final आ of चैत्रभानवा stays, giving चैत्रभानवा + वल = चैत्रभानवावल, a stem ending in -a.

<answer>चैत्रभानवावल</answer>

I could not match ञ्यट् to a known Pāṇinian rule for this stem, so this is a derivation from the general rules.

1. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the suffix य after the markers are dropped. Because it carries ञ्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117), so अ becomes आ.
2. The stem ends in -न्, and the टि part (अन्) is deleted before a taddhita affix (6.4.144), leaving अग्राद्व् before the affix.
3. Adding य gives आग्राद्व्य.

<answer>आग्राद्व्य</answer>
<answer>शाब्दानुशिष्टिक</answer>
<answer>तार्क्ष्यायणशः</answer>
<answer>लस्तता</answer>

This is an application of Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, which adds the affixes cuñcup and caṇap to a word to mean "known by that". The word-final p in caṇap is only a marker, so the affix that is actually added is -caṇa.

The affix begins with a consonant and is not marked ṇit, so the stem undergoes no vṛddhi and no final-a deletion. The stem जाप्य therefore stays intact, and the result is जाप्यचण. I did not check this against a source that attests this exact form; it follows the pattern of the standard examples विद्याचण and केशचण.

<answer>जाप्यचण</answer>

Following the rule ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः (P. 5.3.67), the affix देशीयर् is added to a subanta stem to mean "slightly short of complete". The final र् is only an indicatory marker (it), so the affix reads देशीय. Its initial consonant is not a vowel, so the final -अ of षिड्ग is not elided. The stem takes the affix directly and ends in -a, giving षिड्गदेशीय, meaning "somewhat like a षिड्ग".

<answer>षिड्गदेशीय</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation. I could not tie it to a specific rule for थाल् applying after a non-pronoun stem, so the answer rests on the general mechanics.

By 4.1.1 (ṅyāp-prātipadikāt), a taddhita affix may be added after a stem ending in the feminine suffix ā (āp). Since थाल् begins with a consonant, the stem's final ā is not elided (यस्येति च 6.4.148 applies only before vowel- or ya-initial affixes). The final ल् of थाल् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the affix as -था. This gives पुरुषादका + था.

<answer>पुरुषादकाथा</answer>

Applying the affix मयट् to किण्व gives, after dropping the marker ट्, the ending मय. The result is the stem किण्वमय. I am not certain which sūtra licenses मयट् here, but the combination itself is straightforward.

<answer>किण्वमय</answer>

Under the rule for the affix च्वि (अभूततद्भावे, कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि), the base's final अ becomes ई (अस्य च्वौ, 7.4.32). Then उलप्य + च्वि gives उलप्यी, as in उलप्यी भवति ("becomes ulapya").

<answer>उलप्यी</answer>

Working from the affix as given, I take जाहच् to be आह, with ज् and च् as markers that drop out. The ज् marker (जित्) calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, and the stem already has आ in its first syllable (का). The final अ of the stem is then dropped before the vowel-initial affix आह (6.4.148 यस्येति च), giving काण्डाग्नक् + आह → काण्डाग्नकाह. I could not recall the specific rule that licenses this affix on this stem, so the form rests on this reasoning rather than a verified source.

<answer>काण्डाग्नकाह</answer>

This is a mechanical derivation. The stem सौवीरिका does not obviously take this affix meaningfully, since अस्ताति normally follows direction words.

1. The affix अस्ताति (taught in Pāṇini 5.3.27) surfaces as अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्.
2. The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem counts as a *bha* stem (1.4.18).
3. The stem's final आ is therefore dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), leaving सौवीरिक्.
4. Adding अस्तात् gives सौवीरिकस्तात्.

I did not verify this against a grammar tool, so the dropping of the final आ rests on my reading of 6.4.148.

<answer>सौवीरिकस्तात्</answer>

Applying यत् to वेष्य, I take the only rule that changes the stem to be 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), which deletes the final अ of the stem before a taddhita affix beginning with य. यत् has no ञित् or णित् marker, so there is no vṛddhi.

1. वेष्य + य
2. The final अ of वेष्य is deleted, leaving वेष्य्
3. Joining the affix gives वेष्य्य

This follows from applying the rule mechanically to the stem as given, and I did not check the form against an attested example.

<answer>वेष्य्य</answer>
<answer>निपुणदेशीय</answer>

The affix cvi is added to a nominal stem to express "becoming what it was not", and it is used with kṛ, bhū or as. Before cvi, a final a of the stem becomes ī (rule 7.4.32, *asya cvau*). The cvi affix itself disappears completely, so the stem अटन becomes अटनी, as in अटनीभवति or अटनीकरोति.

<answer>अटनी</answer>

This is a best-reasoned form, not one I could check against a source.

The affix जातीयर् is added in the sense of "a kind of" (P. 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्). The input stem प्रातस्त्या is the feminine of प्रातस्त्य, which is also used as a masculine. Before affixes in the range तसिल् onward, which includes जातीयर्, a feminine stem of this kind is treated like its masculine (P. 6.3.35, पुंवद्भाव). The feminine ending आ is therefore dropped, giving प्रातस्त्य + जातीय.

<answer>प्रातस्त्यजातीय</answer>

Here the affix देशीयर् is added to the feminine stem प्रत्ययितव्या, meaning "slightly short of complete" (ईषदसमाप्तौ, Pāṇini 5.3.67).

Before जातीय and देशीय, a feminine stem whose masculine counterpart exists takes masculine form (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.42). So प्रत्ययितव्या reverts to प्रत्ययितव्य, and adding देशीय gives प्रत्ययितव्यदेशीय. I give the stem form without the feminine ending, since the question asks for the derived stem. I am recalling the sūtra numbers from memory and am not fully certain of them.

<answer>प्रत्ययितव्यदेशीय</answer>

I could not trace this exact derivation with certainty. I take the affix to be the one taught in A. 5.2.96, which attaches लच् to a stem ending in आ, and the stem तावतिथा does end in आ. The Kāśikā's examples there, such as चूडाल, keep the long आ, so I apply the same pattern and add ल directly: तावतिथा + ल = तावतिथाल. The "any meaning is acceptable" note in the question is what lets me ignore the rule's usual restriction to words for parts of the body.

<answer>तावतिथाल</answer>

The affix is *sāti* (Pāṇini 5.4.52–54), which forms indeclinables that end in *-sāt*, like *agnisāt*. I attached it directly to the stem सखी. I know of no rule that changes the long ī, so it stays. I did not check this against a grammar text.

<answer>सखीसात्</answer>
<answer>सौदायिकावत्</answer>

Panini's ञ्यट् rule is not one I could recall, so this form rests on the general behaviour of the affix.

The affix is ञ्य with the markers ञ् and ट्.

1. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (7.2.117). The first vowel of बाणेश्वर is बा, which is already long ā, so nothing changes.
2. The final अ of बाणेश्वर is dropped before the affix beginning with य (6.4.148).
3. Adding ्य gives बाणेश्वर्य.

The marker ट् only matters for forming the feminine, so it does not affect this form.

<answer>बाणेश्वर्य</answer>
<answer>हलीमकिक</answer>

Applying the affix वलच् to the stem gives भस्मावशेष + वल. The final च् of the affix is only a marker (it drops), and the stem takes the affix as it stands. The result is the stem भस्मावशेषवल, meaning "possessing the remains of ashes." I could not match this stem to a sūtra that licenses वलच् (the one I recall is रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच्, 5.2.112, for other bases), so this form follows the general pattern rather than a specific rule.

<answer>भस्मावशेषवल</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses कुणप्, so this form is a best guess based on the general rules rather than on a rule I could cite.

In कुणप्, the final प् is only an indicatory marker (it), so the affix that is actually added is कुण. It begins with a consonant, so the final इ of भव्याकृति is not dropped by यस्येति च. The affix is also not ञित् or णित्, so no vṛddhi applies. The stem therefore stays whole and takes the affix: भव्याकृति + कुण = भव्याकृतिकुण.

<answer>भव्याकृतिकुण</answer>

The affix क (ka) added to the stem धनिष्ठ gives धनिष्ठक. I did not match this to a specific Pāṇinian rule. I assumed one of the senses licensed for क, such as कुत्सित (contempt), अनुकम्पा (compassion) or अज्ञात (unknown). Because the source stem is a neuter basic stem with no feminine ā-suffix, the i-substitution (as in -ikā) does not apply.

<answer>धनिष्ठक</answer>

This is a derivation by the rules as I recall them, not checked against the Aṣṭādhyāyī text. The affix फिञ् is replaced by आयन् (फ् → आयन्), and it is ञित्, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi.

1. The stem त्रैगुण्या loses its final आ before the taddhita affix (यस्येति च), leaving त्रैगुण्य्.
2. The first vowel ऐ is already vṛddhi, so the ञित् rule changes nothing.
3. Adding आयन् gives त्रैगुण्यायन्. The masculine patronymic ends in इ, so the stem is त्रैगुण्यायनि.

<answer>त्रैगुण्यायनि</answer>

Following the rule अत इनिठनौ (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.115), the affix इनि is added to a stem ending in अ to mean "possessing". Here मौक्तिक ("pearl") takes इनि, and its final अ is dropped by यस्येति च. This gives मौक्तिक् + इन् = मौक्तिकिन्, "one who has pearls".

<answer>मौक्तिकिन्</answer>

I could not identify a Pāṇinian rule that prescribes an affix named रूप्य for this stem. I treated रूप्य as a plain affix and joined it directly to the stem. The affix begins with र, so the stem is not treated as a bha-stem and its final अ stays unchanged. That gives the result below.

<answer>छान्दोविचितरूप्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् after साम्बि, so this derivation rests on the general mechanics of the affix.

1. The affix खञ् has ख as its operative part, which is replaced by ईन (7.1.2).
2. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel. Here the first vowel is already ā in सा, so nothing changes.
3. The final इ of साम्बि is deleted before the ईन ending (6.4.148).

So साम्ब् + ईन gives साम्बीन.

<answer>साम्बीन</answer>

Adding the affix त्व (rule तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ, 5.1.119, giving "the state of being X") to वैमात्रेय yields वैमात्रेयत्व. त्व begins with त, not with य or a vowel. So the stem does not get the bha designation (1.4.18). The final अ of the stem is therefore not elided, as in ब्राह्मणत्व.

<answer>वैमात्रेयत्व</answer>

This is the affix बहुच् taught in P. 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is placed before the subanta, as in बहुपटु, in the sense of "slightly" or "almost" (ईषदसमाप्ति). The indicatory च् drops out, leaving बहु.

Attaching it before उदयादित्य gives बहु + उदयादित्य. The two u-vowels then merge by savarṇa-dīrgha sandhi into ऊ, giving बहूदयादित्य. I derived this from memory of the sūtra and did not check it against a source.

<answer>बहूदयादित्य</answer>

I did not trace the specific rule for this affix. Adding the affix क (ka) to the stem नडिल gives नडिलक, which would be the same form if the affix were कन्.

<answer>नडिलक</answer>

Tamap (P. 5.3.55, in the sense of "most") is added directly to the stem करालक. The stem ends in short -a and has no nyap suffix, so nothing is shortened. No ām-type augment applies either, because that applies only to tiṅ-endings and indeclinables. The result is करालक + तम = करालकतम.

<answer>करालकतम</answer>
<answer>शासित्व</answer>

Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ) gives the affix चुञ्चुप् after a stem in the sense "known by that" (as in विद्याचुञ्चुः). The ञ् is a real nasal letter in the affix, which is actually चुञ्चु; the प् is only a marker. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as भ and the final अ of अर्जनीय is not elided. So अर्जनीय + चुञ्चु gives:

<answer>अर्जनीयचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>वर्षैकथा</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcupcaṇapau*), meaning "known by or famous for that". The affix is चुञ्चु, and the final प् is only an indicatory marker. It is added directly to the stem सैसक with no further change, giving a stem ending in -उ. I recalled the rule and the adjoining of the affix from memory rather than checking a source, and I did not verify any special treatment of the stem सैसक.

<answer>सैसकचुञ्चु</answer>

I did not locate the specific rule that licenses थाल् after इक्कट, so I formed the derivative mechanically from the affix. The affix थाल् loses its marker ल् and leaves था. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of इक्कट is not elided, and the result is इक्कट + था.

<answer>इक्कटथा</answer>

बहुच् का प्रयोग "विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु" (५.३.६८) के अनुसार सुबन्त के पहले होता है, और इसका अर्थ ईषदसमाप्ति (कुछ कम होना) है। इसलिए "वत्सिका" के आगे "बहु" जुड़ता है और स्त्रीलिंग रूप वैसा ही रहता है। मैंने यह रूप सूत्र की स्मृति से बनाया है, कोई ग्रंथ देखकर पुष्टि नहीं की।

<answer>बहुवत्सिका</answer>

I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses this affix, so the form rests on the affix's markers rather than a located sūtra.

In कुणप्, the final प् is the only marker (it). The ṇ sits inside the affix, so the affix is कुण (kuṇa). Because ṇ is not a marker here, there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem.

The affix begins with क्, so the final अ of शक्राशन is not elided (elision of a-final stems before an affix applies only if the affix begins with ī, i or y). The affix is therefore simply added to the stem. The न् of the stem does not become ण् because the palatal ś intervenes after the preceding र्.

शक्राशन + कुण → शक्राशनकुण

<answer>शक्राशनकुण</answer>

I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule licensing वलच् on this particular stem. I assumed the generic rule that a taddhita affix attaches to a stem that already ends in the feminine ā (ṭāp, which falls under the nyap suffixes in 4.1.1).

The affix वलच् loses its indicatory च् and becomes -वल. It begins with a consonant, so nothing changes at the joining point. The stem ह्वानीया therefore keeps its final ā and takes -वल.

<answer>ह्वानीयावल</answer>
<answer>भविष्यत्व</answer>

The affix च्वि is added to औपवस्त्र with the sense "becoming what it was not before". Under the rule अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32), a final अ of the stem becomes ई before च्वि. So औपवस्त्र becomes औपवस्त्री. The च्वि affix itself leaves no trace, and the form is used with कृ, भू or अस्.

<answer>औपवस्त्री</answer>

Here the affix दघ्नच् is added to the stem रमाधिप without any change to the stem. The च् is only an indicatory letter and drops away. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not elided. I took the licensing rule to be Pāṇini 5.2.37 (the measure sense), and I did not check whether the stem is semantically suited to it. This gives the stem रमाधिपदघ्न.

<answer>रमाधिपदघ्न</answer>

I did not trace this to a specific Pāṇinian rule, so this is a derivation by the general rules for the affix.

1. The affix खञ् (KaY) leaves the ending ख, which is replaced by ईन (by 7.1.2, "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām"). The ञ् is only a marker.
2. Because the affix carries the ञ् marker, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (by 7.2.117, "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ"). So ए becomes ऐ.
3. The final ा of हेक्का is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (by 6.4.148, "yasyeti ca").
4. Joining the pieces gives हैक्क + ईन = हैक्कीन. The retroflex ण rule (8.4.2) does not apply, since the stem has no ऋ, र or ष.

<answer>हैक्कीन</answer>

The affix वलच् is added to the stem केनिप. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, and the final च् of the affix is an indicatory letter and is dropped too, leaving the ending -वल. This gives केनिपवल. I did not trace a specific Pāṇinian rule for the affix on this particular stem; I am relying on the general pattern for वलच्.

<answer>केनिपवल</answer>
<answer>नाशयित्र</answer>

I applied the affix kalpap (Pāṇini 5.3.67, "slightly incomplete"). Before kalpap, a feminine stem in -ī shortens its final vowel (6.3.43), so ईशिनी becomes ईशिनि. Adding kalpap then gives the stem ईशिनिकल्प, without case endings. I have not checked the exact wording of the shortening rule against a text. I also gave the stem form rather than a feminine form in -ā.

<answer>ईशिनिकल्प</answer>
<answer>योगावापिक</answer>

The affix साति (SLP1 sAti) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.4.52–54. It forms indeclinables meaning "entirely turned into" or "dependent on", as in अग्निसात् and भस्मसात्. I am recalling the usage from memory and have not checked the sūtras. In that usage the final -ि is not kept, so the form ends in -सात्, and I follow that pattern here. Adding it to the stem समुद्रीय, which ends in -a and is unchanged, gives the indeclinable below.

<answer>समुद्रीयसात्</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so this form rests on an assumption about its initial ज्.

The final च् of जाहच् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the suffix -जाह. I assumed the initial ज् is retained, as it is in the comparable affix जातीयर्. I could not confirm this. If the ज् were instead treated as an indicatory letter, the form would be ग्रहणीयाह.

Adding -जाह to ग्रहणीय needs no further sandhi or vowel change, so the result is:

<answer>ग्रहणीयजाह</answer>
<answer>आटाजातीय</answer>
<answer>बीजोपनयनशः</answer>

This is a derivation by the general rules; I did not identify a specific sūtra for this affix on this stem.

The affix अञ् has a ञ् marker, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (ādyaco ñiti). The final आ of the stem (the feminine suffix) is dropped before the vowel-initial affix.

1. Start with सव्यापग्रहणा.
2. Drop the final आ to get सव्यापग्रहण्.
3. Add अ (the affix without its markers): सव्यापग्रहण + अ.
4. Apply vṛddhi to the first vowel, so स (with short अ) becomes सा.

The result is साव्यापग्रहण.

<answer>साव्यापग्रहण</answer>

The stem गल्या ends in the feminine suffix आ. Before the affix कन्, whose ending क is a "ka" suffix, the final long आ is shortened by the rule केऽणः (7.4.13). This gives गल्य + क = गल्यक.

I chose the bare derived stem गल्यक. If the feminine were then formed with टाप्, the form would become गल्यिका by 7.3.44, but that step is not part of the taddhita derivation itself.

<answer>गल्यक</answer>
<answer>कूर्चलदेश्य</answer>

I could not find a rule that applies थमु (thamu) to लोकाचार specifically. Pāṇini's थमु rules, as I recall them, cover इदम् and किम्, so this pairing looks synthetic. I formed the derivative by simple addition. थमु carries no marker that would trigger vṛddhi or another change in the stem, so लोकाचार + थम् gives an indeclinable ending in -म्.

<answer>लोकाचारथम्</answer>

I derived this from the general rules; I could not tie the stem घनाञ्जनी to a specific sūtra, so the result is not checked against one.

1. ठक् is replaced by its substitute: ठ becomes इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50), and the indicatory ट् and क् drop. This gives the affix -इक.
2. The final ई of the stem is deleted before the taddhita affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This leaves घनाञ्जन + इक.
3. ठक् carries no ञ्, ण् or ण्-marker, so there is no vṛद्धि of the first vowel.
4. The result is घनाञ्जनिक.

<answer>घनाञ्जनिक</answer>
<answer>सौवीरकतः</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses this affix on this base, so the form below rests on the general rules for फिञ् rather than a rule I could cite.

The affix फिञ् replaces फ् with आयन् and keeps the vowel इ, so it surfaces as -आयनि. The ञ् marker calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel of the base. The base already begins with long आ, so that step changes nothing.

Before a taddhita affix the feminine suffix ई of आवसानिकी drops (यस्येति च). That leaves आवसानिक.

Adding आयनि gives आवसानिक + आयनि, where the final अ and the initial आ merge into आ. The result is आवसानिकायनि.

<answer>आवसानिकायनि</answer>

The stem ध्वस्रा ends in the feminine suffix ṭāp (ā). Before the affix क, the final long ā is shortened (ke 'ṇaḥ, 7.4.13), giving ध्वस्रक. The feminine suffix is then added again, giving ध्वस्रका. The a before the ka-affix, when āp follows, becomes i (pratyayasthāt kāt pūrvasyāta idāpy asupaḥ, 7.3.44). So ध्वस्रका becomes ध्वस्रिका. I worked this out from memory of the rules and did not check it against a source.

<answer>ध्वस्रिका</answer>

The affix मात्रच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नमात्रचः), where it is added to a word to express measure. Nothing in the feminine-stem rules (such as puṃvadbhāva) applies before this affix, so the final ā of ग्रीष्मा is retained and मात्र is added. I did not find an attested example for this exact stem, so the form is built from the rule.

<answer>ग्रीष्मामात्र</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् on this stem, so this derivation rests on the general taddhita rules, not on a cited sūtra.

1. The final -ā of कृच्छ्रा is dropped before the taddhita affix, which leaves कृच्छ्र् + य.
2. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi: कृ becomes कार्, giving कार्च्छ्र्य.
3. The affix is also टित्, which would add the feminine ङीप् (कार्च्छ्र्यी) only if a feminine is wanted. The question asks for the stem, so I give the base form without it.

<answer>कार्च्छ्र्य</answer>
<answer>आरटिष्ठ</answer>

The affix अण् is ṇit, so the stem's first vowel would take vṛddhi. Here the first vowel, ā in सां-, is already vṛddhi, so it does not change. The final अ of सांकेतिक is dropped before the affix's अ (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). The result is सांकेतिक्+अ, which is spelled the same as the input stem.

<answer>सांकेतिक</answer>

This is a formation with the taddhita affix चणप् (5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, "known by it"). The affix is added to the stem as चण, with the प् as an inert marker. The Kāśikā's example is विद्याचणः, built on the feminine stem विद्या, where the final आ of the stem is kept. The initial च of the affix is not य or ई, so यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not delete the stem-final vowel. By analogy I keep the ā-ending of अक्षर्या, giving अक्षर्या + चण. I did not find अक्षर्याचण itself attested, so this form is derived by that analogy.

<answer>अक्षर्याचण</answer>

I took this to be the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*), where caṇap is added to a third-case word to mean "known by".

The affix is c-a-ṇ-a-p. The final p is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the suffix चण (caṇa). The suffix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as a *bha* stem. The final -अ of मांसाद is therefore not elided by 6.4.148. This gives मांसाद + चण = मांसादचण.

I did not check that this particular stem is attested with this affix. The form follows from the general rule.

<answer>मांसादचण</answer>

I formed this by joining the base to the comparative suffix ईयसुन्, whose operative form is ईयस्. I did not check whether कपिलाश्रम qualifies as a guṇavacana base for this suffix; I took the pairing as given.

1. The base is कपिलाश्रम, ending in short अ.
2. Before ईयसुन्, the final vowel अ of the base is dropped, either by ṭi-lopa (6.4.155) or by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This gives कपिलाश्रम्.
3. Adding ईयस् gives कपिलाश्रमीयस्.

<answer>कपिलाश्रमीयस्</answer>
<answer>चोलकचण</answer>
<answer>छेदकतर</answer>

I applied the ठक् rules mechanically. I did not identify the specific sūtra or meaning that licenses this affix on शङ्कव्य, so the result rests on the general rules below.

1. The affix ठक् has ठ् replaced by इक (ṭha → ika), so the affix becomes इक.
2. The initial vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi because the affix carries the indicatory क् (kit): श → शा, giving शाङ्कव्य.
3. The final अ of the stem is deleted before the इक affix (यस्येति च), giving शाङ्कव्य् + इक.
4. Joining the parts gives शाङ्कव्यिक.

<answer>शाङ्कव्यिक</answer>

This is a tentative answer: I could not identify the specific Aṣṭādhyāyī rule that licenses अञ् after this stem, so I reasoned from the affix mechanics alone.

The affix अञ् is added after ऐन्द्रमारुत. The stem's final अ is dropped before the affix (ordinary a-lopa before a vowel-initial taddhita). Because अञ् is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem would take vṛddhi, but it is already ऐ, so nothing changes. The result is spelled the same as the input stem.

<answer>ऐन्द्रमारुत</answer>

I formed this by adding the affix कन् (kan) to the stem बुध्निय. The final न् is only a marker (it drops), so the affix is just क. It is added after the stem's final अ.

The source gender is neuter, so no feminine ending (the 7.3.44 इ-substitution, as in बुध्नियिका) applies. The stem is simply extended with क, giving बुध्नियक.

<answer>बुध्नियक</answer>
<answer>शाशकर्णितर</answer>

The affix मतुप् is added to the feminine stem सट्वा, since a stem ending in a feminine suffix can take a taddhita affix (P. 4.1.1). The affix's initial म् becomes व् after a stem ending in अ/आ (P. 8.2.9, as I recall it), so मतुप् becomes वत्. This gives सट्वा + वत् = सट्वावत्, parallel to the standard example खट्वावत् (nominative खट्वावान्).

<answer>सट्वावत्</answer>

I took the affix क (ka) to be the one introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.70 (प्रागिवात् कः), which is added to a nominal stem. I could not tie it to a more specific rule for ओजस्, so this is my best reading.

The affix is not an अजादि or य-initial affix, and it falls within the range of affixes before which the stem counts as a pada. The final स् of ओजस् therefore stays unchanged, and no vowel shortening applies (7.4.13 concerns only a stem-final अण् vowel before ka).

ओजस् + क → ओजस्क

<answer>ओजस्क</answer>

नखर + जातीयर् (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्, "of the kind of …") gives नखरजातीय. The final र् of the affix is only a marker and drops out, so the stem ends in -a, and the full nominative would be नखरजातीयः.

<answer>नखरजातीय</answer>

The affix मात्रच् (A. 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) has an indicatory च्, which drops, leaving the ending -मात्र. The affix is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi, and the stem कपृथ stays unchanged. Adding the affix gives कपृथमात्र.

<answer>कपृथमात्र</answer>

Rule 5.4.52 (*vibhāṣā sāti kārtsnye*) allows the affix *sāti* to be added to a nominal stem in the sense of "totality".

The affix falls within the 1.4.17 range (*sU* to *kap*), so the stem रेपस् takes pada status. Its final *s* becomes *ru*, giving a visarga (8.2.66). The following *s* is a sibilant followed by a vowel, so 8.3.36 (*vā śari*) lets the visarga stay, or optionally become a sibilant. I chose the visarga form, though the sibilant form रेपस्साति would also be valid.

<answer>रेपःसाति</answer>

Pāṇini 5.2.37 (*pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātracaḥ*) licenses द्वयसच् in the sense of measure. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of जानुक is not elided. The च् is only an accent marker and drops, leaving the affix as द्वयस. Adding it directly to the stem gives जानुकद्वयस. I could not confirm that जानुक is an attested stem, so this form follows the stated rule applied mechanically to the stem as supplied.

<answer>जानुकद्वयस</answer>

I take the ञ्यङ् here to be the affix of Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.171, added to a stem for the descendant (apatya) sense. I could not confirm that this rule applies to a stem in -क like यौवनाश्वक, so the derivation below is a best reading rather than a checked one.

1. यौवनाश्वक + ञ्यङ् gives यौवनाश्वक + य, since ञ् and ङ् are indicatory letters that drop out.
2. The ञित् marker would call for vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the initial vowel is already औ, so nothing changes.
3. The final अ of the stem is elided before the affix by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), giving यौवनाश्वक्य.

<answer>यौवनाश्वक्य</answer>
<answer>जायिक</answer>

Applying the affix मयट् (4.3.82) to the stem मयु gives मयुमय. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem counts as a pada before it. The final उ therefore takes no guṇa. मयट् is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi either. The टकार is only a marker, and it would call for the feminine suffix ङीप् in the feminine.

<answer>मयुमय</answer>

This is a derivation by the rules as I recall them, not checked against a source. कातल is a basic masculine stem, and इष्ठन् is added to it with a superlative sense.

1. Before इष्ठन्, the stem counts as a भ-अङ्ग.
2. Rule 6.4.155 (टेः) deletes the टि, the last vowel together with any consonant after it. In कातल that is "अल", leaving कात्.
3. Adding इष्ठ (the final न् of इष्ठन् is only a marker) gives कात् + इष्ठ = कातिष्ठ.

<answer>कातिष्ठ</answer>

I derived this from the rule तिकादिभ्यः फिञ् (4.1.154), assuming रावन् is treated as belonging to that class; I did not confirm it against the गण list.

1. The affix फिञ् takes the form फ् → आयन् with the इ retained, so it is added as -आयनि.
2. The stem रावन् ends in न्, so before a taddhita affix its final टि (the vowel with what follows it, अन्) is dropped by नस्तद्धिते (6.4.144). This leaves राव्.
3. The first vowel of राव् is already long, so the ञ् marker's vṛddhi changes nothing.
4. Adding the affix gives राव् + आयनि = रावायनि.

<answer>रावायनि</answer>

This is a mechanical application of the affix rather than a worked derivation. The affix द्वयसच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to the feminine stem दण्डापूपायिता. The final -ā of the stem is not elided because द्वयस begins with a consonant, so the rule that deletes a stem-final vowel before affixes with an initial vowel or य (6.4.148) does not apply. The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops out. The result is the stem दण्डापूपायिताद्वयस. I did not check this against any attested form.

<answer>दण्डापूपायिताद्वयस</answer>
<answer>कोङ्कणकत्व</answer>

पटल (a-ending stem) + इनि, the possessive affix taught in "अत इनिठनौ" (5.2.115), meaning "one who has a पटल". The final अ of पटल drops before the affix, giving पटलिन्.

<answer>पटलिन्</answer>
<answer>आञ्जलिक</answer>
<answer>तात्कर्म्यतर</answer>

This looks like the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which gives words like विद्याचुञ्चुः "known by learning". I am recalling that rule from memory rather than checking it.

Here the affix is चुञ्चु, and the final प् is only a marker that drops out. The ञ् in चुञ्चु is a real consonant, not a marker, so nothing in the affix triggers a stem change. The affix is simply added to the stem मुरवार.

<answer>मुरवारचुञ्चु</answer>

I derived this by rule recall and did not check it against a source text.

The stem पेया ends in the feminine suffix ā. Before the affix क, this long ā is shortened by 7.4.13 (केऽणः), giving पेय + क, then the feminine ā is added again: पेयका.

The rule 7.3.44 would normally turn the a before क into i, as in कारिका. It does not apply here, because पेया is never used as a masculine word (7.3.47, अभाषितपुंस्काच्च). So the form stays with a, as in खट्वका and मालका. I am reciting 7.3.47 from memory, so this step is the least certain.

<answer>पेयका</answer>
<answer>शापत्व</answer>

बहुच् (अष्टाध्यायी ५.३.६८, "विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु") is added to a subanta in the sense of "somewhat, almost, not completely" (ईषदसमाप्ति). The affix is placed before the word, as in बहुपटुः. Applied to पर्णाश, this gives बहुपर्णाश, meaning "somewhat of a पर्णाश". The masculine stem takes no further change.

<answer>बहुपर्णाश</answer>

The affix मतुप् (matup) becomes वतुप् after a stem ending in अ that follows a झय् consonant, by 8.2.9–10 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः, झयः). In सूच्छ्रित the final अ follows त्, which is a झय्, so म becomes व. This works like वृक्ष → वृक्षवत्. The result is the stem सूच्छ्रितवत्.

<answer>सूच्छ्रितवत्</answer>
<answer>लालसकपाश</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of "measure") is added directly to the stem. The final च् is only an indicatory marker and is dropped. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not deleted. The result is महान्वय + दघ्न.

<answer>महान्वयदघ्न</answer>

Here the affix इष्ठन् (SLP1 izWan) is the superlative affix of 5.3.55, added to the stem ऋजीति.

1. Before इष्ठन्, the टि part of the stem is dropped (6.4.155). The टि is the last vowel with whatever follows it, so the final इ of ऋजीति is removed, leaving ऋजीत्.
2. The ऋ → र् substitution (6.4.161) does not apply. It requires the stem to begin with a consonant, and this stem begins with the vowel ऋ.
3. Adding इष्ठ to ऋजीत् gives ऋजीतिष्ठ.

<answer>ऋजीतिष्ठ</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to the stem अञ्जनाम्भस्, and the final च् is only an accent marker, so the added affix is द्वयस.

The affix begins with a consonant (द्), so the stem takes pada status (1.4.17). The final स् of अम्भस् then becomes रु (8.2.66), and रु becomes उ after अ before a voiced consonant (6.1.114). The अ and उ combine to ओ, giving अञ्जनाम्भोद्वयस.

<answer>अञ्जनाम्भोद्वयस</answer>
<answer>धौन्धुमारीमत्</answer>

The affix चणप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), with the sense "known or famous by that". The final प् is only a marker. The ण is part of the affix, so the added element is -चण.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as भ and its final अ is not dropped. No आदिवृद्धि applies either, because the affix has no ञ or ण marker. The result is simply stem + चण.

<answer>रुक्माङ्गदचण</answer>
<answer>यामिनीशतर</answer>
<answer>व्रताचारजातीय</answer>

The stem राजादनी is feminine and ends in a ṅī-type suffix, and रूपप् is added to it to express praise (Pāṇini 5.3.66, प्रशंसायां रूपप्). Before रूप, a polysyllabic stem ending in ṅī takes a short final vowel (Pāṇini 6.3.43, घरूपकल्प…ङ्योऽनेकाचो ह्रस्वः), so राजादनी becomes राजादनि. I recalled both rules from memory rather than checking them.

Adding रूप gives राजादनिरूप. Puṃvadbhāva (6.3.35) might instead give राजादनरूप, but I took 6.3.43 to apply because the stem is ṅī-final and polysyllabic. I stopped at the taddhita stem and did not add the feminine ending -ā.

<answer>राजादनिरूप</answer>
<answer>प्रियासुक</answer>

Per Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), the affix चुञ्चुप् means "known by (that)". I am recalling this rule from memory rather than checking it. In the affix, ञ् and प् are only marker letters, so what is actually added is चुञ्चु.

Since चुञ्चु begins with a consonant, the final -अ of पुल्य is not elided. The stem and affix simply join, giving पुल्य + चुञ्चु = पुल्यचुञ्चु.

<answer>पुल्यचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>पदान्तरचण</answer>

This is a derivation I reasoned out from memory of the rules, not one I checked against a source. I take the affix शस् to be the one taught in Pāṇini 5.4.43 (संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायाम्), used here in the distributive sense "one … after another".

1. The stem वर्ग्य is singular, so it can take शस् in the distributive sense.
2. The ś of a taddhita affix is not an indicatory letter (1.3.8 excludes taddhitas), so the affix keeps its ś.
3. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final -अ is not elided (6.4.148 does not apply).
4. This gives वर्ग्य + शस् = वर्ग्यशस्, which is indeclinable (1.1.38). In its final form the स् becomes visarga: वर्ग्यशः.

<answer>वर्ग्यशः</answer>

I did not derive this step by step. I took पिपासित ("thirsty") and added the affix क (ka) directly, giving पिपासितक. The rule that changes a preceding अ to इ before ka applies only when the feminine suffix आप् follows. The stem here is neuter and has no आप्, so no such change applies.

<answer>पिपासितक</answer>

जित (अकारान्त) + इञ् (अत इञ्, अपत्य-अर्थ में) में अन्तिम अ का लोप होता है। ञित् होने से आदि अच् को वृद्धि होती है, यानी ज के इ को ऐ होता है। इससे जैत् + इ = जैति बनता है, अर्थ "जित का अपत्य"।

<answer>जैति</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this derivation rests on the general taddhita rules and is not confirmed against a specific sūtra.

1. The affix खञ् reduces to ईन. The initial ख् is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, 7.1.2), and the ञ् is only a marker.
2. The feminine ending -ā (ṭāp) is deleted before a taddhita affix (6.4.148, यस्येति च). This leaves the base सहक.
3. Because ञ् marks the affix as ञित्, the first vowel of the base takes vṛddhi (7.2.117, तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). So स's अ becomes आ, giving साहक.
4. Adding ईन gives साहकीन.

<answer>साहकीन</answer>

Only a partial derivation is possible here, because I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् after this stem.

The rest follows from the affix markers:

- The ञ् in ञ्यट् is an it-marker, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi. In साप्ति the first vowel is already आ, so nothing changes.
- The final इ of the stem is dropped before the affix, by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). This gives साप्त् + य.
- The ट् marker only serves to form the feminine with ङीप्, so it does not affect the masculine stem.

The resulting masculine stem is साप्त्य.

<answer>साप्त्य</answer>

I am not certain this is a licensed formation, so this answer rests on a mechanical derivation.

The affix शस् (Sas) is introduced in rules such as 5.4.43, for words of plurality or smallness and for numerals in a distributive sense. I could not tie the stem अङ्क्रि to any of those conditions, so I simply attached the affix to the stem as given. The stem ends in इ and takes no feminine suffix here, so it has no further change. The result is an indeclinable (avyaya). Its final स् appears as visarga when the form is written as a complete word.

<answer>अङ्क्रिशः</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठन् on हतक, so this form rests on the general rules for ठन्, not on a cited rule.

1. The affix ठन् (Wan) has initial ठ, which is replaced by इक by "ठस्येकः" (7.3.50), giving हतक + इक.
2. The final अ of हतक is dropped before the taddhita affix by "यस्येति च", giving हतक् + इक.
3. ठन् has the indicatory letter न्, not ञ् or ण्, so it does not cause vṛddhi of the first vowel. The first vowel therefore stays short.

The result is हतकिक.

<answer>हतकिक</answer>
<answer>सामुदायिकचर</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ, "almost complete") is added to a full word (subanta) and gives the sense "almost X". Before it, a feminine stem ending in a long ī or ā is shortened (the rule I am recalling for this is 6.3.43, though I am not certain of its number or exact wording). So तलिका becomes तलिक, and adding देशीय gives तलिकदेशीय, meaning "somewhat like a तलिका".

<answer>तलिकदेशीय</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses कुणप् for this stem, so this form rests on a partial derivation and a guess.

1. The affix is कुणप्. Its final प् is only a marker (it-letter), so what attaches is कुण.
2. The stem पीयूक्षिला ends in the feminine suffix आ and is added directly before कुण.
3. I assumed कुण counts as a pada-forming affix. If so, the stem is not treated as a bha-stem and the final आ is not deleted.

If कुण instead triggered deletion of the final आ, the result would be पीयूक्षिलकुण; I judged this less likely.

<answer>पीयूक्षिलाकुण</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses this affix, so this form comes from the usual rules of affixation alone.

The affix कुणप् has a final प्, which is only an marker and drops out. That leaves the suffix -कुण.

The stem कुञ्चित ends in -अ. Elision of a final अ (यस्येति च) happens only before a vowel-initial or ya-initial taddhita, and कुण begins with a consonant. So the stem's final -अ stays and the suffix is simply added.

<answer>कुञ्चितकुण</answer>

I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् after यक्ष्म, so the form below follows the general effect of the affix rather than a verified sūtra. The affix अञ् carries the marker ञ्, which triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem. यक्ष्म therefore becomes याक्ष्म, and the final अ of the stem drops before the affix's अ.

<answer>याक्ष्म</answer>

I could not tie this combination to a specific Pāṇinian rule for the affix यत्, so this is a mechanical derivation rather than a cited one. The stem शाल्मलिका ends in the feminine suffix ā (टाप्). Before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel or य्, the final अ/आ of the base is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148). That gives शाल्मलिक + य, which joins as शाल्मलिक्य.

<answer>शाल्मलिक्य</answer>

I applied the measure-sense rule for these affixes (Pāṇini 5.2.37, *pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātracaḥ*). The affix *dvayasac* is added to the stem to mean "of that measure". Its final *c* is only a marker and drops out, leaving *dvayasa*. The affix begins with a consonant (*dv*), so the stem's final *a* is not elided before it, as in the standard example ऊरुद्वयस. The derived stem is therefore दण्डकासन + द्वयस.

<answer>दण्डकासनद्वयस</answer>

This is formed by adding the affix थाल् to the stem उल्लापक. The final ल् of थाल् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the affix था. The stem ends in short अ, which is dropped before the affix beginning with a consonant-initial थ… actually it is retained, since थ is not a vowel-initial affix. So उल्लापक + था gives उल्लापकथा.

I am not certain this stem is a licensed input. In Pāṇini's rule 5.3.23, थाल् normally applies after pronouns, and उल्लापक is not one. I followed the table as given.

<answer>उल्लापकथा</answer>

This is formed with the taddhita affix दघ्नच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure), added directly to the stem वाराणसीश्वर. The affix begins with a consonant (द), so the final -अ of the stem is not dropped. The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter and disappears. The result is the stem वाराणसीश्वरदघ्न.

<answer>वाराणसीश्वरदघ्न</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces ञ्यट्, so this form is derived from the affix's markers alone and may not match an attested formation.

1. The stem तर्जिता ends in the feminine suffix -ā, and this -ā drops before the taddhita affix (यस्येति च), leaving तर्जित्.
2. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so त becomes ता (तर्जित् → तार्जित्).
3. Adding the affix -य gives तार्जित्य.
4. The ट् marker would make the feminine in ङीप्, but only the derived stem is asked for here, so I leave that out.

<answer>तार्जित्य</answer>

This is the taddhita affix *rūpya* (Pāṇini 4.3.81, हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यः). I am working from memory of the rule, and I did not check which meaning applies to this particular stem.

The affix begins with र, which is neither a vowel nor य. By 1.4.17 the base क्षमिन् therefore counts as a *pada* before it, not as a *bha* stem. The final न् of the stem is deleted by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), which gives क्षमि. Adding the affix gives क्षमिरूप्य.

I rejected the alternative क्षमरूप्य, which would follow if the stem were *bha* and 6.4.144 deleted its final टि.

<answer>क्षमिरूप्य</answer>

For this derivation I take ईयसुन् as the comparative suffix (the ईयसुन् of 5.3.57) and apply the rules below, without checking whether आडारक counts as a guṇavacana word.

1. The suffix ईयसुन् reduces to ईयस् after dropping its indicatory letters (उ and न्).
2. Under 6.4.154 (टेः), the ṭi of the stem is dropped before ईयसुन्. In आडारक the ṭi is the final अ, because the stem ends in a vowel. This leaves आडारक्.
3. Adding ईयस् gives आडारक् + ईयस् = आडारकीयस्.

<answer>आडारकीयस्</answer>

The stem रामायणीया ends in the feminine suffix टाप्, so the final आ is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) before the taddhita affix. Adding लच् to the remaining रामायणीय gives रामायणीयल. I have not tied this to a specific rule licensing लच् on this base; I took the problem's statement that any licensed meaning is acceptable as allowing the generic formation.

<answer>रामायणीयल</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses कुणप्, so this form rests on the affix's shape rather than a confirmed rule.

The affix is actually कुण. The final प् is only an indicatory marker (it affects accent), and the ण् is a real part of the affix, so there is no vṛddhi. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not elided by "yasyeti ca". The stem and affix therefore simply join.

<answer>शाबरायणकुण</answer>
<answer>वलयितृजातीय</answer>

The affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, प्रशंसायां रूपप्) is added to उभयानुमता in the sense of "praiseworthy". I am recalling the rules from memory and could not pin down the sūtra number for the shortening rule, so that step is less certain.

1. Before रूपप् (as before कल्पप्, चेलट् and similar affixes), a stem ending in a feminine ङीप्/ङीष्/आप् suffix is shortened. So उभयानुमता becomes उभयानुमत.

<answer>उभयानुमतरूप</answer>

Here the affix देशीयर् is added by P. 5.3.67, "ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः", and means "somewhat of a ...", i.e. slightly short of full. The final र् is only an indicatory letter, so it drops. <answer>वचस्त्व</answer>

This affix is caṇap, taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), "known by that". The standard examples are विद्याचणः and विद्याचुञ्चुः, formed from the instrumental sense "known by learning". Applying the same pattern to देविका, "known by Devikā", gives देविकाचणः.

The affix खञ् (KaY) is added to the masculine stem उत्पलाभ. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses this combination, so the form rests on the general mechanics of the affix.

<answer>ऐन्द्राग्नजातीय</answer>

<answer>शिलोरस्करूप्य</answer>

<answer>तैत्तिरीयतर</answer>

I formed this from the stem and affix by ordinary suffixation, without checking the governing rule closely. The affix त्रा is added to a nominal stem with a vowel-less initial consonant, so the stem is treated as a pada and its final -अ is unchanged. The neuter gender plays no further role here. Joining शुष्कक and त्रा gives शुष्ककत्रा.

<answer>शुष्ककत्रा</answer>

The stem शुश्रूषेण्य ends in -a, so the possessive affix इनि (by "ato 'ini-ṭhanau", A.5.2.115) can be added. The final -a of the stem drops before the affix, giving शुश्रूषेण्य + इन् → शुश्रूषेण्यिन्, meaning "one who has शुश्रूषेण्य".

<answer>शुश्रूषेण्यिन्</answer>

<answer>नेत्रोद्द्योती</answer>

This is the affix दघ्नच् of Pāṇini 5.2.37, which forms words of measure, as in ऊरुदघ्न. I did not check whether the rule applies to this particular stem, since any licensed meaning is accepted.

The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops. The affix itself begins with a consonant, so the stem before it counts as a pada. The final न् of मत्सरिन् is then deleted by 8.2.7, leaving मत्सरि + दघ्न. The result is मत्सरिदघ्न.

This is a derivation from memory, and I did not identify the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् here.

- The ञ् is an indicatory letter, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (Pāṇini 7.2.117, तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). Here the first vowel is the अ of श, which becomes शा.
- The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix.

So शम्बूकावर्त + ईन becomes शाम्बूकावर्तीन.

<answer>शाम्बूकावर्तीन</answer>

The stem is not an ordinary sarvanāma, so I simply attached the affix to it as given and did not check it against the rule that licenses थाल्.

1. The affix थाल् loses its indicatory ल्, leaving था.
2. थ begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped (यस्येति च does not apply).
3. The न of the stem does not become ण. The letter ष् is a trigger, but the intervening द् blocks the change.
4. The derived form is therefore षुदुवदीन + था. It is an indeclinable, so no case endings are added.

<answer>षुदुवदीनथा</answer>

Here जातीयर् is the affix taught in Pāṇini 5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्), which denotes "of that kind". The final र् is only an it-marker and drops out, leaving the affix जातीय. Adding it to मन्य involves no sandhi change, so the stem is मन्य + जातीय = मन्यजातीय, meaning "of the kind of मन्य".

<answer>मन्यजातीय</answer>

I could not recall the rule that introduces जाहच्, so this formation rests on the general mechanics of the affix rather than a cited sūtra.

In जाहच्, the final च् is only an indicatory marker (it-letter), so the affix that remains is जाह. It begins with a consonant and the affix has no marker that triggers deletion of the stem's final vowel, so the stem हसिर stays intact. The affix is simply added to it, giving हसिरजाह.

<answer>हसिरजाह</answer>

This form is derived from the rules as I recall them; I did not check it against a source.

The stem is गौपिक = ग् + औ + प् + इ + क् + अ. Before इष्ठन्, the stem takes the bha-designation, and the ṭi (the final vowel with any consonant after it) is dropped by P. 6.4.155 (टेः). Here the ṭi is the final अ. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) also removes a final अ before an affix beginning with इ.

So गौपिक् + इष्ठ gives गौपिकिष्ठ.

<answer>गौपिकिष्ठ</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) adds देशीयर् to a nominal stem to mean "slightly short of complete", that is, "almost X". The final र् is only a marker and drops. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not elided. This gives वेङ्कटेश्वर + देशीय.

<answer>वेङ्कटेश्वरदेशीय</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule for the affix जाहच् with certainty, so this form is derived by analogy with जातीयर्.

1. The final च् of जाहच् is an indicatory letter (it), which leaves the operative affix जाह. I assumed the initial ज् is retained, as in जातीयर्, and I did not verify this.
2. The affix has no ñ- or ṇ-marker, so there is no vṛddhi.
3. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem अन्तरेष keeps its final अ. The elision rule यस्येति च does not apply.
4. Joining the two gives अन्तरेष + जाह = अन्तरेषजाह.

<answer>अन्तरेषजाह</answer>

I applied Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*, which adds रूपप् to a word to express praise. The stem हस्तिन् counts as a pada before this taddhita suffix, so its final न् drops, leaving हस्ति. Adding -रूप gives हस्तिरूप, "an excellent elephant". I did not add any case ending.

<answer>हस्तिरूप</answer>

I took the stem वैयासव with मयट् in the sense of "made of / a modification of that". मयट् begins with म, not a vowel or य. So the stem does not count as भ and its final अ is not dropped. The stem simply takes मय, giving वैयासवमय. The ट् is only an indicatory letter and is dropped.

<answer>वैयासवमय</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so this form rests on the standard mechanics rather than a verified rule.

The affix देश्य is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It is added to a nominal base to mean "almost, nearly (but not quite) that". Adding it to बज gives बजदेश्य, "nearly a बज".

<answer>बजदेश्य</answer>

The affix मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to सौजामि. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -ि of the stem is not dropped. मात्रच् is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi, and the stem already has सौ-. The stem and affix simply join.

<answer>सौजामिमात्र</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that teaches ञ्यट्, so this form rests on the general rules for such an affix rather than a checked rule.

The affix is ञ्य with the markers ञ् and ट्. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so ह (with short अ) becomes हा. The final अ of हरिणेश is dropped before the affix by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). The result is हारिणेश्य.

<answer>हारिणेश्य</answer>

Applying the affix अण् (which is ṇit) to the stem प्राशितृ:

1. By तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (7.2.117), only the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. Here that vowel is already आ in प्रा, so nothing changes.
2. The final ऋ is not strengthened. Before the vowel अ, it becomes र् by the yaṇ substitution.
3. The result is प्राशित्र.

I derived this by applying the rules rather than from a stated sūtra for this exact word. The form also matches the known noun प्राशित्र.

Its initial च is a consonant and it has no ṇit/ñit marker, so there is no vṛddhi and no loss of the stem-final अ. This works the same way as आढ्य → आढ्यचर. I could not identify the specific Aṣṭādhyāyī rule that introduces ञ्यट्, so this derivation rests on the affix's markers alone.

2. Before a taddhita affix, the final टि of a stem in -न् is deleted (6.4.144 नस्तद्धिते). Here the टि is -इन्, so मलाकर्षिन् becomes मलाकर्ष्.
3. Adding -य gives मलाकर्ष्य.
4. Vṛddhi of the first vowel changes म (ma) to मा (mā). The ā in आकर्ष is not affected.

This gives मालाकर्ष्य.

<answer>मालाकर्ष्य</answer>

3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the suffix by यस्येति च, giving कार्ष्टोप्त्य.

The affix begins with a consonant and has no ञ or ण marker. So no vṛddhi or deletion of the stem-final आ is triggered, and the base सालेयिका keeps its final आ. I did not check whether any rule shortens that आ before a taddhita affix, and found none. The result is the stem सालेयिका + दघ्न.

Adding जातीय gives शिङ्घितजातीय, "of the शिङ्घित kind".

I could not tie this form to a specific Pāṇinian rule, so it is the most plausible formation rather than a certain one. The affix अस्ताति (the final ि is only a marker) leaves the ending -अस्तात्. This is the same ending seen in पुरस्तात्.

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् here, so this derivation is a best reconstruction rather than a confirmed rule-based result.

2. Before the ñit/ṇit taddhita अञ्, the final ā of the stem is dropped, leaving त्वेषित्.
3. The ñ marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so ए (in त्वे) becomes ऐ, giving त्वैषित्.

3. The feminine suffix टाप् is then added, giving हिक्कक + आ.
4. By 7.3.44, the अ before the क of a टाप् stem becomes इ, giving हिक्किका.
