I could not identify the exact sūtra that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this form is a best-judgement derivation rather than a confirmed one.

The affix खञ् has two markers. Its ख् is replaced by ईन (P.7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). Its ञ् is an indicatory letter that triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (P.7.2.117, तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). Applying both to कोमलाङ्ग:

- The first vowel ओ in को becomes औ, giving कौमलाङ्ग-.
- The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, and ईन is added.
- The result is कौमलाङ्गीन. The न् does not become ण् because no र, ष or ऋ precedes it.

<answer>कौमलाङ्गीन</answer>
<answer>हानीयमय</answer>
<answer>कृणुजाह</answer>

The affix तसि (तसिः) is added to the stem नर्क and gives an indeclinable ending in तस्, which becomes तः with a final visarga. This gives नर्क + तस् → नर्कतः.

<answer>नर्कतः</answer>

Adding मतुप् (the "possessing" affix) to पुष्पाञ्जलि gives पुष्पाञ्जलिमत्, meaning "having a handful of flowers".

The stem ends in इ, and the penultimate letter is ल्, not म or a vowel-ending म-type base. So the rule that changes म to व (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः) does not apply, and the affix stays as मत्.

<answer>पुष्पाञ्जलिमत्</answer>

I applied the affix अस्ताति (अस्तात्) to शोकाकुल from memory of the rule, not from a checked source. The affix is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.27 and is normally added to direction words, so this input is unusual, but the form follows mechanically. The stem's final अ drops before the vowel-initial affix, as in पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्. The final इ of the affix is a marker and does not appear in the output.

शोकाकुल + अस्तात् → शोकाकुलस्तात्

<answer>शोकाकुलस्तात्</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्) adds पाश after a nominal stem in the sense of something deficient or contemptible. Adding पाश to the stem ऐणिक gives the stem ऐणिकपाश.

<answer>ऐणिकपाश</answer>

The stem is formed by adding the comparative suffix ईयसुन् to रोरुक.

1. The final उन् of the suffix is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix ईयस्.
2. Before ईयसुन्, the stem loses its ṭi, the last vowel together with any consonants after it (P.6.4.155, ṭeḥ). In रोरुक that is the final अ, so the stem becomes रोरुक्.
3. Joining रोरुक् and ईयस् gives रोरुकीयस्.

<answer>रोरुकीयस्</answer>
<answer>पौल्कसता</answer>

The affix ka is probably the one Pāṇini teaches in 5.4.154 (śeṣād vibhāṣā), which optionally adds ka after a bahuvrīhi compound. I did not confirm that ऊनाक्षर is a bahuvrīhi, so this is an inference. Adding ka to the stem gives ऊनाक्षरक. If the final -a of the stem is dropped before the affix, the result is the same form.

<answer>ऊनाक्षरक</answer>
<answer>श्यामाङ्गिष्ठ</answer>

The affix जातीयर् is introduced by P.5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्), meaning "of that kind". Its final र् is only an indicatory marker and drops, so the suffix is जातीय.

Added to तृणोद्भव, the stem's final अ is elided before the affix beginning with a vowel-initial sequence under "यस्येति च". Because जातीय itself begins with ज, the written result is the stem followed directly by जातीय: तृणोद्भवजातीय, "of the kind that grows from grass".

<answer>तृणोद्भवजातीय</answer>

Applying the affix छ (Ca), whose substitute is ईय, to the stem विष्वद्रीचीना gives the form below. The final आ of the stem is dropped before the initial ई of ईय (by यस्येति च), so विष्वद्रीचीन् + ईय becomes विष्वद्रीचीनीय. I did not identify the specific sūtra licensing छ on this stem, so the derivation rests on the general substitution of ईय for छ.

<answer>विष्वद्रीचीनीय</answer>

Applying ṭhak to तबलाकृति gives ताबलाकृतिक, as follows:

- ṭhak becomes इक, since ṭh is replaced by ik.
- The first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (ādivṛddhi), so त becomes ता.
- The final -इ of the stem is dropped before the affix (yasyeti ca).

<answer>ताबलाकृतिक</answer>

The affix कुणप् is the one taught in 5.2.24, where the "p" is only an accent marker. It is added directly to the stem, as in पीलुकुणः, so I form it as stem + कुण.

The affix begins with a consonant. So the final अ of the stem is not dropped (6.4.148 applies only before vowel-initial affixes). Nothing else changes in the stem.

लोकानुकम्पक + कुण = लोकानुकम्पककुण

I did not check whether लोकानुकम्पक is on the word lists that rule is attached to. The task says any licensed meaning is acceptable, so I formed it directly.

<answer>लोकानुकम्पककुण</answer>

The derivative is formed by adding कन् to the stem and then dropping the इत् letter न्, leaving the suffix क. I derived this from the rules from memory rather than checking them against a source.

1. The stem अकुप्यक ends in अ, and the suffix क begins with a consonant. The elision rule यस्येति च does not apply here, because it needs a following affix that begins with a vowel or य.
2. The neuter gender adds no feminine आप्, so the इ-substitution of प्रत्ययस्थात्कात्पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः does not apply either.
3. The stem therefore stays whole and the suffix is appended directly: अकुप्यक + क = अकुप्यकक.

<answer>अकुप्यकक</answer>
<answer>पल्लवापीडितिष्ठ</answer>

The affix शस् (Sas) forms indeclinables such as एकशः, by Pāṇini 5.4.42–43. I did not check that होम्य fits any of the meanings listed there, so I attached the affix directly and applied no stem change. Adding शस् to होम्य gives होम्यशस्, whose final स् becomes visarga in the standard citation form.

<answer>होम्यशः</answer>

The affix चरट् is taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.53), meaning "formerly such". The stem तल्ली takes चरट्, whose final ट् is only a marker and drops out, leaving the stem तल्लीचर. I have kept the long ई of the base. I did not check whether any rule shortens it before चरट्, and I am not certain that none does.

This is the masculine/neuter stem. A feminine तल्लीचरी is also possible, and I chose the unmarked stem as the answer.

<answer>तल्लीचर</answer>
<answer>आवनतीयद्वयस</answer>

The affix चणप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, in the sense "known by that". It is added to the stem as चण; the final प् is only a marker. The initial च stays, as in the standard examples विद्याचणः and केशचणः. This is from memory, not checked against the text.

Adding it to सर्क gives सर्क + चण. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is unchanged.

<answer>सर्कचण</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses this affix, so this form is built mechanically rather than checked against a rule.

I treated कुणप् as the affix कुण, with the final प् as a marker that drops out. The initial ku of a taddhita affix is not elided under 1.3.8, and णू does not count as a marker here, so no vṛddhi applies. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -य of the stem is not elided under 6.4.148. The affix is simply added to the stem unchanged.

<answer>सवात्यकुण</answer>

This is a tentative answer. I could not identify which Pāṇinian rule licenses थमु after a stem like लोमाली; the only थमु rules I recall (इदमस्थमु, किमश्च) apply to इदम् and किम्, not this stem.

I formed the derivative by adding the affix directly to the stem. After the indicatory उ is dropped, the affix is थम्. It begins with a consonant, so the rule यस्येति च (which would delete a final ई before an affix beginning with a vowel) does not apply, and the stem-final ई stays.

<answer>लोमालीथम्</answer>

The affix देश्य (deSya) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः. It is added to a nominal stem in the sense of "slightly short of complete", that is, "almost a वेष्टक". The affix joins directly to the stem with no change, giving वेष्टकदेश्य.

<answer>वेष्टकदेश्य</answer>
<answer>चार्मिकपाश</answer>

This is a derivation by the patronymic rule अत इञ् (4.1.95), which applies to stems ending in short a, and धर्मोपध ends in -a. I derived it from memory of the rules rather than checking a source.

1. तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (7.2.117) gives vṛddhi to the first vowel of the stem, so धर्म becomes धार्म.
2. यस्येति च (6.4.148) drops the final -अ of the stem before the affix.
3. Adding इ gives धार्मोपधि.

<answer>धार्मोपधि</answer>

This is the affix दघ्नच् (daGnac) from Pāṇini 5.2.37, which is used for a measure. I did not check the exact meaning of this particular stem.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem is not dropped (यस्येति च does not apply). The affix simply attaches to the stem with its ending च् removed as an indicatory letter. This gives मौलभारिक + दघ्न.

<answer>मौलभारिकदघ्न</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that teaches the affix कुणप् from memory, so this derivation is a best guess rather than a confirmed result.

The final ā of तपस्या drops before the taddhita (6.4.148, यस्येति च). The affix is then added in the form कुण, since the final प् is only a marker. This gives तपस्+कुण = तपस्कुण.

<answer>तपस्कुण</answer>
<answer>लशुन्य</answer>

The stem भवीत्व ends in the vowel -अ, and इष्ठन् begins with इ. Since इष्ठन् is a taddhita affix beginning with इ, the stem takes bha status. Its final -अ is then dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), and the same result follows from टेः (6.4.155) before इष्ठन्. This gives भवीत्व् + इष्ठ, which joins as भवीत्विष्ठ. The affix's final न् is only a marker and does not appear in the form.

<answer>भवीत्विष्ठ</answer>

Adding the comparative affix तरप् (tarap) to the stem तूर्य: the final प् is only a marker and drops, leaving the suffix तर. This gives the stem तूर्यतर.

<answer>तूर्यतर</answer>
<answer>तवीषीतः</answer>

This is a derivation by rule application. The affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27 ff.) normally attaches to direction words, but I applied it to कक्षिन् as given.

1. The affix अस्ताति begins with a vowel, so the stem कक्षिन् takes the *bha* designation (1.4.18).
2. Under 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते), a *bha* stem ending in न् loses its final vowel-plus-consonant part (the *ṭi*) before a taddhita affix. Here that part is इन्, so कक्षिन् becomes कक्ष्.
3. Adding the affix gives कक्ष् + अस्ताति = कक्षस्ताति.

<answer>कक्षस्ताति</answer>
<answer>आढ्याडुसात्</answer>
<answer>टवत्</answer>

The affix चणप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, in the sense "known by that". The final प् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix is added to the stem as चण. I did not find a standard textbook example with मौञ्ज, so this form is built from the rule rather than recalled, and I assumed the stem takes no internal change.

<answer>मौञ्जचण</answer>
<answer>चतितत्व</answer>

Taking the affix क (ka) as the one that gives senses such as "unknown" or "small" (for example, Pāṇini 5.3.73–74), it is added directly to the stem. The stem ends in short अ and the form is masculine, so the इत्व change (7.3.44–45) that applies before feminine आ does not occur. The result is पृक्षक.

I chose the rule from memory and did not check it against a source.

<answer>पृक्षक</answer>
<answer>पुरञ्जरजातीय</answer>
<answer>गलोद्भवशः</answer>

Here ईयसुन् is the comparative affix (5.3.57). I first joined it to the stem: लवणाम्भस् + ईयस्. By the rule टेः (6.4.155), the ṭi (the last vowel with the consonant after it) of the stem is dropped before ईयस्. The ṭi of लवणाम्भस् is अस्, so the stem reduces to लवणाम्भ्. Adding ईयस् gives लवणाम्भ् + ईयस् = लवणाम्भीयस्.

<answer>लवणाम्भीयस्</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so this form rests on general rules and is not verified against that rule.

The final च् of जाहच् is an indicatory letter (it). The initial ज् stays, because the rule that drops an initial च-/ट-class consonant does not apply to taddhita affixes. The affix that is actually added is therefore जाह.

Since जाह begins with a consonant, the stem दीपिन् takes the pada form before it. The final न् is then deleted by the rule on the final न् of a nominal stem in a pada (8.2.7). This gives दीपि + जाह = दीपिजाह.

<answer>दीपिजाह</answer>

I could not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that introduces ठक् after this stem, so this form comes from the general ठक् derivation rules alone.

1. The affix ठक् becomes इक by ठस्येकः (7.3.50).
2. The first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (7.2.117), so भ becomes भा.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148).
4. This gives भान्ध्रुक् + इक = भान्ध्रुकिक.

<answer>भान्ध्रुकिक</answer>

The affix जातीयर् (P. 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added to रम्भिन्. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem takes the pada designation, and its final न् is dropped (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य). The result is रम्भिजातीय. The neuter gender of the source stem makes no further change.

<answer>रम्भिजातीय</answer>

नभ्या (स्त्रीलिङ्ग, नित्य-आबन्त) + तल् (भावे, "तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ") → नभ्याता। "तल्" में "ल्" इत् है और अंश "त" रहता है। यह प्रत्यय "त" से आरम्भ होता है, इसलिए "यस्येति च" से आ-लोप नहीं होता। नभ्या का आ ज्यों का त्यों रहता है, और स्त्रीलिङ्ग में टाप् जुड़कर "ता" बनता है। यहाँ मैंने पुंवद्भाव नहीं माना है, क्योंकि वह समानाधिकरण में लगता है, भाववाचक प्रत्यय में नहीं। यह निर्णय पक्का नहीं है; पुंवद्भाव मानने पर नभ्यता बनता।

<answer>नभ्याता</answer>

The stem is अध्वन्य and the affix is अण्, which is ñit/ṇit, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (7.2.117). The first अ becomes आ.

The final अ of अध्वन्य is dropped before the vowel-initial affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). Before a vowel-initial affix the stem is not a pada, so the य् is not pada-final and the special vṛddhi rule 7.3.3 does not apply.

अध्वन्य + अण् → आध्वन्य, meaning "relating to or belonging to अध्वन्य" (neuter singular आध्वन्यम्).

<answer>आध्वन्य</answer>
<answer>स्खदनता</answer>

The affix कल्पप् (kalpap) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः, and means "slightly short of complete". It is added directly to the stem कोटिका. I found no rule that shortens or otherwise changes the final आ here, since the ghādi shortening rule affects only ई-stems. The result is the taddhita stem कोटिकाकल्प, meaning "almost a कोटिका".

I did not add the feminine ṭāp, because the question asks for the derived stem. Adding it would give कोटिकाकल्पा, and I am not fully certain which of the two the question intends.

<answer>कोटिकाकल्प</answer>

I could not tie this to a specific sūtra with certainty. The answer comes from applying the usual rules for ईयसुन् after a stem ending in the feminine ई.

The stem वैमृधी ends in a feminine ई. Before the taddhita ईयसुन्, that final ई of the stem is deleted by the ṭi-deletion rule (6.4.155, with 6.4.148 as an alternative route). This leaves वैमृध् followed by ईयस्. Joining them gives वैमृधीयस्.

<answer>वैमृधीयस्</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् (comparative/superlative, "most …") is added to the stem यौतकी. Before इष्ठन्, the sūtra "ṭeḥ" (6.4.155) removes the ṭi-part of the stem, which is its last vowel and anything after it. Here that is the final ई. This leaves यौतक्, and adding इष्ठ gives यौतकिष्ठ.

This rests on my reading that ṭi-lopa removes the ई directly. If the ई were first replaced by the masculine form (यौतक) by puṃvad-bhāva, the ṭi-lopa would delete "अक" instead and give यौतिष्ठ. I did not find a rule that triggers puṃvad-bhāva before इष्ठन्, so I went with the first reading.

<answer>यौतकिष्ठ</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule for ञ्यट्, so this form is built from the affix's markers rather than from a cited sūtra.

1. The base is त्रैधातव्या. Its final आ drops before the affix beginning with य् (by "यस्येति च"), leaving त्रैधातव्.
2. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the part "य" after the markers ञ् and ट् are removed. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the first vowel is already ऐ, so nothing changes. This gives त्रैधातव्य.
3. The marker ट् makes the derivative feminine with ङीप् (the rule for taddhita affixes marked ṭ). The final अ of त्रैधातव्य drops before ई, giving त्रैधातव्यी.

<answer>त्रैधातव्यी</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् for this stem, so this form rests on the general operations for the affix.

1. The affix खञ् has its initial ख् replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, Pāṇini 7.1.2), and the ञ् is only an indicatory letter.
2. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (Pāṇini 7.2.117): पू → पौ.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial ईन.
4. The न of ईन stays dental. The intervening त् blocks the retroflex change that the preceding ष् and र् would otherwise cause.

I assumed vṛddhi of the first vowel only. If the stem belonged to a gaṇa that gives vṛddhi to both members, the form would differ, and I could not check that.

<answer>पौर्णाभिषिक्तीन</answer>

Applying ईयसुन् to लषित gives the comparative stem, with the final syllable of the base dropped before the affix.

1. The base is लषित and the affix is ईयसुन्. The ङ्-style markers उ and न् drop as it-letters, leaving ईयस्.
2. By Pāṇini 6.4.155 (टेः), the टि of the base is deleted before ईयसुन्. The टि is the last vowel together with any consonants after it, here इत.
3. This leaves लष् before ईयस्, and the two join as लषीयस्.

<answer>लषीयस्</answer>
<answer>मित्रेरविक</answer>

Taking चाञ्चल्य as the base, I add the comparative affix ईयसुन्, whose इत् letters उ and न् drop, leaving ईयस्. The final अ of the base is then deleted before the affix beginning with ई (यस्येति च), which gives चाञ्चल्य् + ईयस् = चाञ्चल्यीयस्.

<answer>चाञ्चल्यीयस्</answer>

Under the rule *abhūtatadbhāve kṛbhvastiyoge sampadyakartari cviḥ* (5.4.50), the affix cvi is added to the stem तुज्य. The affix is then dropped entirely, leaving only its effects. The final -a of the stem becomes -ī by *asya cvau* (7.4.32), so तुज्य becomes तुज्यी. This form is used with कृ, भू or अस् (for example तुज्यीकरोति).

<answer>तुज्यी</answer>
<answer>टिण्टिणिकल्प</answer>
<answer>सदृशकल्प</answer>
<answer>प्रथयितृकल्प</answer>

The affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (by आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्, 7.1.2). Before it, the stem क्लमिन् takes the भ-designation, since ईय begins with a vowel-initial affix (यचि भम्, 1.4.18). The final टि "इन्" is then dropped (नस्तद्धिते, 6.4.144), which gives क्लम् + ईय = क्लमीय.

I did not check which sūtra licenses छ after this particular stem, and I am not fully certain of how 6.4.144 applies to stems in -इन्. The form below follows that rule as I understand it.

<answer>क्लमीय</answer>

The affix कुणप् (kuṇap) is taken here as follows. Its final प् (p) is an anubandha (marker letter) and drops, leaving the affix कुण. The ण् sits inside the affix rather than at its end, so I treat it as part of the affix. It therefore does not trigger vṛddhi (strengthening of the first vowel).

The affix begins with a consonant (क्), so the rule that deletes the final अ of a stem before a vowel-initial taddhita does not apply, and the stem उप्य stays intact. Adding the affix gives उप्य + कुण = उप्यकुण.

I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses this affix, so this form rests on the general derivation above and is not checked against a source.

<answer>उप्यकुण</answer>

Applying the affix इञ् (P. 4.1.95 अत इञ्) to शिञ्जार gives:

1. The final अ of शिञ्जार is dropped before the vowel-initial affix इ.
2. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (P. 7.2.117). इ becomes ऐ.
3. The result is शैञ्जारि, meaning "descendant of शिञ्जार".

<answer>शैञ्जारि</answer>

This follows Pāṇini 5.2.26, "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ", where चणप् is added to a stem in the sense "known or found by that". The ending प् is only an indicatory marker and drops. The affix is then added as चण, with no further change to the stem. This is the same pattern as विद्याचणः, from which I took the form by analogy; I did not find a cited example for चन्द्राश्म.

<answer>चन्द्राश्मचण</answer>

This is a direct affixation. The affix मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, used for a measure) is added to the stem without altering it. The affix begins with म, so the final अ of the stem is not elided. The stem therefore stays whole, and the final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter and drops. The result is पूर्णाश्रमीय + मात्र.

<answer>पूर्णाश्रमीयमात्र</answer>
<answer>प्रौढिष्ठ</answer>

This is a derivation by rule, not a form I checked against a source.

The stem व्याध्य ends in -a, so इञ् (iY) can apply in the sense of "descendant" (अत इञ्, 4.1.95).

1. The affix इञ् leaves इ after dropping the markers ञ् (which makes the affix ñit, so vṛddhi applies) and its own final consonant.
2. The final -अ of the stem is dropped before the taddhita affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), leaving व्याध्य् + इ.
3. The first vowel of the stem is already आ, so vṛddhi (the ñit-triggered strengthening) changes nothing.

The result is व्याध्यि.

<answer>व्याध्यि</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), with the sense "known by that" (as in विद्याचुञ्चुः). The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped. The affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>भुवनाण्डकचुञ्चु</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.67, which means "slightly short of complete". It is added to the subanta stem, so the stem is simply extended without any internal change: उक्थायु + कल्पप् gives उक्थायुकल्प. The sense is "almost an उक्थायु". The masculine form is unchanged, so no feminine shortening or other adjustment applies.

<answer>उक्थायुकल्प</answer>

Here the affix छ (SLP1 `Ca`) is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). It is added to the stem श्रौताधान, and the stem's final अ drops before the initial ई of the affix. This gives श्रौताधान + ईय = श्रौताधानीय. I did not identify the specific rule licensing छ on this stem, so the derivation rests on the general replacement rule above.

<answer>श्रौताधानीय</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ठन् after this stem, so this form comes from applying the general taddhita rules mechanically, and I am not certain it matches an attested word.

1. The affix ठन् is replaced by इक, because ठ becomes इक (7.3.50).
2. The stem मूर्ध्वन् ends in -अन्, and before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel the final टि (अन्) is dropped (6.4.144). This leaves मूर्ध्व.
3. ठन् has no ञ् or ण् marker, so no vṛddhi applies to the first vowel.
4. Adding इक to मूर्ध्व gives मूर्ध्विक.

<answer>मूर्ध्विक</answer>

This is a derivation from the rule as I recall it, not a form I could check against a source. The affix वलच् is added after रजस्, कृषि, आसुति and परिषद् (Pāṇini 5.2.119), and also after दन्त and शिखा. Pāṇini's list does not include a stem आसना, so I derived the form as follows.

1. वलच् begins with a consonant. A stem before such an affix is a *pada* (1.4.17), not a *bha* stem.
2. The final आ of आसना is therefore not deleted by "यस्येति च", which applies only to *bha* stems.
3. The stem and affix simply join, and the final -अच् marker drops. This gives आसना + वल = आसनावल.

<answer>आसनावल</answer>

बिसिनी में ङीप् लगा है, इसलिए यह ङ्यन्त और अनेकाच् है। "ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः" (5.3.67) से इसके बाद कल्पप् लगता है। फिर "घरूपकल्पचेलड्ब्रुवगोत्रमतहतेषु ङ्योऽनेकाचो ह्रस्वः" (6.3.43) से पूर्व पद का अन्तिम ई ह्रस्व हो जाता है। (यह सूत्र-संख्या और पाठ मुझे स्मृति से याद हैं, पक्का नहीं।) इससे बिसिनि + कल्प बना, और स्त्रीलिंग में आप् जुड़ने पर रूप बिसिनिकल्पा होता है, जिसका अर्थ है "कुछ-कुछ बिसिनी जैसी, पूरी बिसिनी नहीं"। ह्रस्व न करने पर बिसिनीकल्पा भी बन सकता है, पर मैंने ह्रस्व वाला रूप चुना है।

<answer>बिसिनिकल्पा</answer>

The affix जातीयर् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्). Since जातीय is a taddhita suffix, the feminine stem takes masculine form before it (6.3.42, पुंवत् कर्मधारयजातीयदेशीयेषु). So प्रमाणिता becomes प्रमाणित- and then takes जातीय. This pumvadbhāva reading is my own choice and I did not confirm it against any other source. Without it the form would be प्रमाणिताजातीय.

<answer>प्रमाणितजातीय</answer>

Applying इनि to कण्वीय follows the possessive rule अत इनिठनौ (Pāṇini 5.2.115), which adds इनि or ठन् to a stem ending in short अ. I am recalling the rule from memory rather than checking it, and I chose the इनि option.

The final अ of कण्वीय is elided before the इनि suffix, giving कण्वीय + इन् → कण्वीयिन्, with the meaning "one who has the कण्वीय (text or school)".

<answer>कण्वीयिन्</answer>
<answer>क्रय्यीयस्</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses कुणप् with हन्मन्, so this form rests on general rules rather than a confirmed source.

The affix is कुण, with the final प् as a marker letter that drops out. It begins with a consonant, so the stem हन्मन् counts as a *pada* before it (1.4.17). That means the final न् is deleted (8.2.7), giving हन्म. Adding कुण gives हन्मकुण.

<answer>हन्मकुण</answer>

Under 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), the affix द्वयसच् loses its indicatory च्, leaving द्वयस. This begins with a consonant, so the stem हृतोत्तरा is not treated as a भ-stem (1.4.18 applies only before an affix beginning with य् or a vowel). The final आ of the टाप् suffix is therefore not deleted, and the stem simply takes the affix. I derived this from the rules as I recall them rather than from an attested example, so the retained आ is the part I am least sure of.

<answer>हृतोत्तराद्वयस</answer>

I formed this by attaching थाल् directly to the stem, without a verified Pāṇinian rule for this particular input. The stem सारण्यका is a feminine stem ending in the feminine suffix ā, which is not a sarvanāma. The usual sense of थाल् is "in that manner" (prakāra-vacana, 5.3.23).

Before थाल्, which is neither ṇit nor kit, I assumed the stem keeps its final ā unchanged. The final ल् of the affix is only a marker and drops, leaving -था. Taddhita affixes of this kind give indeclinables (1.1.38), so no case ending is added.

सारण्यका + थाल् → सारण्यकाथा

<answer>सारण्यकाथा</answer>
<answer>रूढदेशीय</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix रूप्य after this stem, so this form is a best guess. I simply added the affix to the stem. Because रूप्य begins with a consonant other than य, no vowel at the end of the stem is deleted.

<answer>शासनातिवृत्तिरूप्य</answer>
<answer>खशेटरूप</answer>

The affix कल्पप् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) is added after a nominal to express "slightly short of being, almost". The stem सहस्रार ends in short अ, and the affix is added directly with no change to the stem. The पित् marker (the final प्) only affects accent and leaves the form unchanged, so the derived stem is सहस्रार + कल्प.

<answer>सहस्रारकल्प</answer>

I formed this by applying the affix यत् directly to the stem, without tracing a specific rule that licenses it.

The stem is सेचित, which ends in अ. Before the affix य, the final अ of the stem is dropped (यस्येति च). That leaves सेचित् + य.

The affix यत् has only a non-triggering इत् letter (त्), not ण् or ञ्, so no vṛddhi applies. The result is सेचित्य.

<answer>सेचित्य</answer>

This is a formal derivation, since होतव्या is not listed in any of the गण lists that take लच्, so I did not check it against a specific Pāṇinian rule or meaning. The affix लच् leaves the suffix ल after the इत् letter च् is dropped. Because ल begins with a consonant, the final आ of the feminine stem होतव्या is not elided, so the result is होतव्या + ल = होतव्याल. I gave the masculine-looking stem here; a feminine would add the ā ending, giving होतव्याला.

<answer>होतव्याल</answer>

The affix देश्य is introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It is added to a subanta in the sense of "slightly short of complete", that is, "almost". Nothing in the stem or the affix triggers a sandhi change or a replacement. The stem कौबेरक therefore stays intact and the affix is simply attached: कौबेरक + देश्य = कौबेरकदेश्य.

<answer>कौबेरकदेश्य</answer>

I am not certain this combination is attested. The affix थमु (Tamu) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.24 (इदमस्थमुः) for the pronoun इदम्, as in इत्थम्. Since the task allows any licensed meaning, I applied it mechanically to the stem प्रोह.

The final उ of थमु is only a marker (it-letter), so the affix that attaches is थम्. The stem प्रोह ends in -a and the affix begins with a consonant, so nothing changes at the junction. The result is प्रोह + थम् = प्रोहथम्. As a taddhita formed with this affix, it is an indeclinable, so no case endings are added.

<answer>प्रोहथम्</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses कुणप् with मन्दाक्ष, so this form is built from the affix's shape alone and is a best guess.

In a taddhita affix the initial क् is not an indicatory letter (1.3.8 excludes taddhitas). The final प् is an indicatory letter, so the affix is simply कुण. Since कुण begins with a consonant, the final -अ of मन्दाक्ष is not elided. The affix has no initial ञ्, ण् or क् indicatory letter, so there is no vṛddhi. Joining मन्दाक्ष and कुण gives मन्दाक्षकुण.

<answer>मन्दाक्षकुण</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix कुणप् on this stem, so this form is a best guess. I attach कुण (the final प् is only a marker and drops) directly to कुम्ब्या and leave the final ā unchanged. Because the affix begins with a consonant, the vowel-deleting rule यस्येति च does not apply.

<answer>कुम्ब्याकुण</answer>
<answer>पिप्रीषुपाश</answer>

I took the derivation as क्षयथु + मतुप् (the affix reduces to -मत्, with the उप् letters as markers). The stem ends in -u and its penultimate letter is थ्, not म्, अ or आ. So the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9), which would change म to व, does not apply. The affix keeps its म.

<answer>क्षयथुमत्</answer>

This is a derivation by rule and a straightforward concatenation, not an attested word. The affix द्वयसच् is taught in Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), in the sense of "measure". The final च् is only an indicatory letter, so what is added is द्वयस.

The affix begins with a consonant (द्), so it does not trigger the bha-treatment of 1.4.18 (यचि भम्). The stem's final -अ therefore stays as it is, and the affix is added directly. This parallels ऊरु + द्वयसच् → ऊरुद्वयस.

मादद्य + द्वयस → मादद्यद्वयस

<answer>मादद्यद्वयस</answer>

<answer>नार्यङ्गवत्</answer>
<answer>वर्गीयात्व</answer>
<answer>लोलीय</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces ञ्यट्, so this derivation rests on the general rules for a ञित् taddhita affix.

1. After the markers ञ् and ट् are dropped, the affix is -य.
2. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117): चरु → चारु.
3. The final उ then takes guṇa before the taddhita affix (6.4.146): चारु → चारो.
4. Before the vowel-initial -य, ओ becomes अव् (6.1.78), giving चारव्य.

<answer>चारव्य</answer>

Taking this as the taddhita ka (diminutive/pity sense) added to a stem ending in ṭāp (-ā), the steps are:

1. रञ्जिका + क: the long ā before ka is shortened by 7.4.13 (केऽणः), giving रञ्जिकक.
2. The feminine ṭāp is added again, giving रञ्जिककआ.
3. By 7.3.44 (प्रत्ययस्थात्कात्पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः), the a before the pratyaya-ka that precedes ā becomes i, giving रञ्जिकिका.

I derived this from the rules as I recall them rather than from a cited attested form.

<answer>रञ्जिकिका</answer>

This is formed by 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), and the input stem and affix don't fit the sutra's own sense well, so the answer is a mechanical application of the affix.

1. The affix चुञ्चुप् leaves the form चुञ्चु, because ञ् and प् are only marker letters.
2. चुञ्चु begins with a consonant, so the stem before it takes pada status rather than bha status.
3. The final न् of मर्माविन् is therefore dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), and the इ stays. The टि-lopa rule नस्तद्धिते (6.4.144) applies only to bha stems, so it does not apply here.
4. This gives मर्माविचुञ्चु.

I did not check this against an attested form, so the pada-versus-bha step is the part to verify if this matters.

<answer>मर्माविचुञ्चु</answer>

This is a derivation I reasoned out from the rules rather than a form I could check against an attested example.

The affix अस्ताति (5.3.27) is added to the stem पूर्वोपपन्ना. The stem ends in the feminine -ā, and the affix begins with a vowel, so that final -ā is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). The result is पूर्वोपपन्न + अस्तात्, which gives पूर्वोपपन्नस्तात्.

The substitution पूर् → पुर् (5.3.39) applies only to the word पूर्व itself, so it does not apply here.

<answer>पूर्वोपपन्नस्तात्</answer>

I applied the usual comparative formation, assuming the stem श्रय is not replaced by श्र (that replacement, from "प्रशस्यस्य श्रः", applies only to the stem प्रशस्य). Adding ईयसुन् leaves the stem ending in अ. That final अ is dropped before the ई-initial taddhita (यस्येति च), giving श्रय् + ईयस्. The result is श्रयीयस्, the stem of the comparative.

<answer>श्रयीयस्</answer>
<answer>सामाजिकेय</answer>

This is the abhūtatadbhāve use of cvi (A. 5.4.50), which is normally followed by a form of कृ, भू or अस्. The affix च्वि leaves only व् after the markers are dropped, and that व् is then deleted entirely. The rule अस्य च्वौ (A. 7.4.32) then changes the final अ of the stem to ई. So पण्डित becomes पण्डिती, as in पण्डितीकरोति or पण्डितीभवति.

<answer>पण्डिती</answer>

This is a derivation by the affix चणप् (caṇap) under Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ. The affix is added after a stem in the instrumental sense "known by that." The final प् is only an indicatory marker, so what is attached is चण.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -य of उद्य is not dropped and no vṛddhi applies. Attaching चण directly to उद्य gives उद्यचण, meaning "known by उद्य."

<answer>उद्यचण</answer>

Adding the affix मयट् to the stem ऋत gives ऋतमय. The ट् is only a marker and drops, leaving the suffix मय. The suffix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of ऋत stays and no sandhi arises. This derivative would mean "made of or consisting of ऋत".

<answer>ऋतमय</answer>

The affix बहुच् is added before a subanta (P. 5.3.68, विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It conveys "somewhat, nearly" (ईषदसमाप्ति, P. 5.3.67). The feminine stem अश्वत्थिला stays unchanged, and बहु is placed in front of it. Internal sandhi then turns बहु + अश्वत्थिला into बह्वश्वत्थिला.

<answer>बह्वश्वत्थिला</answer>
<answer>तप्तव्यमय</answer>

I did not find "सरु" among the standard examples. The affix दघ्नच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसच्दघ्नच्मात्रचः), with the sense of "measure", as in ऊरुदघ्न, "thigh-deep". I applied it to सरु on that pattern. The affix is added directly to the stem, and the final च् is only a marker that drops out. This gives सरु + दघ्न = सरुदघ्न.

<answer>सरुदघ्न</answer>

This is Pāṇini 5.3.68, where बहुच् is added in the sense of "almost" or "somewhat" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is placed before the word, as in बहुपटु. I am recalling the rule from memory. Applied to कुसूल, it gives the stem below.

<answer>बहुकुसूल</answer>
<answer>जैर्य</answer>

The affix तसि begins with a consonant (त्), so it does not trigger लोप of the final ई of the feminine stem (यस्येति च applies only before vowel or य-initial affixes). The stem therefore keeps its ई. The affix leaves तस्, which becomes तः with a final visarga. This gives लिङ्गिनीतः, an indeclinable meaning something like "from the लिङ्गिनी" (ablative sense).

<answer>लिङ्गिनीतः</answer>
<answer>त्याज्यता</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule that licenses थाल् here. The usual थाल् rules are 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्, which applies to sarvanāmas) and 5.3.111 (the Vedic इव-sense words), and स्नेहका belongs to neither. I therefore applied the affix mechanically to the given stem.

The final ल् of थाल् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving थ. थ begins with a consonant and is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi and no change to the stem. The feminine आ of स्नेहका therefore stays, giving स्नेहका + था. A taddhita affix like this makes the word indeclinable, so no case ending is added.

<answer>स्नेहकाथा</answer>

I could not tie this combination to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The affix थमु is taught only after इदम् (5.3.24) and किम् (5.3.26), so ऐतिह्य is not a regular base for it. I formed the derivative by simply applying the affix to the stem.

The final उ of थमु is only a marker (it-letter) and drops, leaving the affix थम्. Because this affix begins with a consonant, the stem's final अ is not elided by यस्येति च, which applies only before affixes beginning with a vowel or य. The result is ऐतिह्य + थम् = ऐतिह्यथम्, an indeclinable.

<answer>ऐतिह्यथम्</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) expresses becoming what one was not before (अभूततद्भाव), and it is used with the verbs कृ, भू and अस्. The stem इभ्य ends in short अ. By "अस्य च्वौ" (7.4.32), that final अ becomes ई before च्वि. The च्वि affix itself is then wholly elided, so the derived stem is इभ्यी, as in इभ्यीभवति.

<answer>इभ्यी</answer>

The affix jAhac (जाहच्) is added to the stem रमलोत्कर्ष. I could not tie it to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra from memory, so I treated it like the other affixes that express "a kind of X" (such as जातीयर्).

The final च् only marks the accent, and the remaining affix is जाह. It begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not dropped, and no sandhi changes occur at the join. The result is therefore the stem followed directly by जाह.

<answer>रमलोत्कर्षजाह</answer>

The affix इञ् is added by the rule अत इञ् (4.1.95), which gives a patronymic-type derivative from a stem ending in -a. This is my reading of the table's input, and I could not tie the stem पुंसानुज to a more specific rule.

1. The final -अ of पुंसानुज is dropped before the affix, giving पुंसानुज्‌ + इ.
2. The first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (the तद्धितेष्वचामादेः rule, 7.2.117): उ becomes औ, so पुं becomes पौं.
3. The result is पौंसानुजि.

<answer>पौंसानुजि</answer>

The affix त्रा (trA) is attached directly to the stem with no change to the stem's final अ. I am working from my recollection of the rule that licenses त्रा, which I could not pin down exactly. The form below follows from simple concatenation.

<answer>द्वादशारत्रा</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् is one of the three affixes taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (पramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātrac). The final च् is only a marker, so the affix that is actually added is द्वयस.

The stem कसर्णील ends in अ. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem does not take the भ designation, and the rule that deletes a stem-final अ (यस्येति च, 6.4.148) does not apply. The stem therefore stays whole, and द्वयस is simply added after it. The result is a neuter stem in -a.

<answer>कसर्णीलद्वयस</answer>

I could not tie this affix to a specific Pāṇinian rule from memory, so this form is a best reconstruction rather than a verified derivation.

The affix साति begins with a consonant, so the final "a" of उदुम्बर is not dropped by the rule that elides a stem-final "a" before a vowel-initial taddhita (यस्येति च). The affix is simply added to the stem. The neuter gender of the source stem does not affect the result.

<answer>उदुम्बरसाति</answer>

I could not recall the Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप् with this stem, so the form below follows the general mechanics only.

In कुणप्, the final प् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the affix -कुण. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ of जपनीय is not deleted. Nothing else applies, so the affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>जपनीयकुण</answer>
<answer>हयोत्तमत्व</answer>

I recalled the affix rule from memory and could not confirm that दारकाचार्य is in the गणपाठ list (तिकादि) for this affix, so the form rests on that assumption.

I take the affix to be फिञ् from "तिकादिभ्यः फिञ्" (4.1.154), giving a descendant-sense derivative.

1. The initial फ् of the affix is replaced by आयन् (फ् → आयन्, by 7.1.2).
2. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem would take vṛddhi. Here the initial vowel is already दा, so nothing changes.
3. The final अ of the stem आचार्य drops before the affix (यस्येति च), leaving आचार्य् + आयन्.

Result: दारकाचार्य → दारकाचार्यायन.

<answer>दारकाचार्यायन</answer>

Following the standard rules for adding यत् (ya) to a feminine stem in -ā, the final आ of क्षुल्लका drops out before the affix, so क्षुल्लक् + य gives क्षुल्लक्य. I derived this from the rules and did not locate the specific sūtra licensing यत् here, so the result is not checked against a source.

<answer>क्षुल्लक्य</answer>

I derived this by applying ṭhak, which becomes इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50), to वधूटिका, but I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ṭhak here. Any meaning licensed for ṭhak is acceptable, so I left the meaning open.

1. The final आ of वधूटिका drops before the affix, because the affix begins with इ (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This leaves वधूटिक.
2. ṭhak has a क् as an indicatory letter, so it counts as kit. The first vowel of the stem therefore takes vṛddhi (किति च, 7.2.118), so व becomes वा. This gives वाधूटिक.
3. Adding इक gives वाधूटिक + इक = वाधूटिकिक.

<answer>वाधूटिकिक</answer>
<answer>तर्यवत्</answer>
<answer>कालञ्जराद्वयस</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् on this stem, so this derivation applies the general taddhita rules to it.

1. Start from the feminine stem अर्दिता, which ends in टाप्. Taddhita affixes can be added to such stems under the 4.1.1 adhikāra.
2. Before the taddhita affix, the final आ of the stem is deleted by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), leaving अर्दित्.
3. The affix अञ् carries ञ्, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (7.2.117). The initial अ becomes आ.
4. Adding the affix gives आर्दित.

<answer>आर्दित</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यङ् with this stem, so this form is derived from the affix markers alone and is not rule-confirmed.

The affix is ञ्यङ्, whose operative part is "य", and the markers ञ् and ङ् act as follows:
- The marker ञ् makes the affix ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: उदराग्नि becomes औदराग्नि.
- Before the affix "य", the final इ of अग्नि is dropped (यस्येति च), giving औदराग्न्य.

<answer>औदराग्न्य</answer>

This is a derivation by the possessive rule अत इनिठनौ (5.2.115), which adds ठन् to a stem ending in short अ. I did not check this against a source for this particular stem.

1. The stem शिखण्डिक ends in अ, so ठन् can be added.
2. The ठ of ठन् is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः, 7.3.50), giving the ending -इक.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the ending (यस्येति च, 6.4.148): शिखण्डिक् + इक.
4. ठन् is not marked ञ or ण, so there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel.

The result is शिखण्डिकिक.

<answer>शिखण्डिकिक</answer>

The affix बहुच् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु), used in the sense of "somewhat" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is placed before the subanta, so बहु is prefixed to सहम. The final च् of the affix is only a marker (इत्) and does not appear. The stem is already a neuter ending in short अ, so no further change applies.

<answer>बहुसहम</answer>
<answer>मानवीयिक</answer>

The affix caṇap (चणप्) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, with the sense "known or famed by that". The final प् is only an indicatory letter, so what is added is चण. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ of पृथुल is not dropped. This gives पृथुल + चण = पृथुलचण. I derived this from the rule and did not check it against an attested example.

<answer>पृथुलचण</answer>

Applying the taddhita affix क (ka) to the stem काथिक simply gives काथिकक. The rule that changes a stem-final अ to इ before क (7.3.44–45) applies only before a feminine आप् ending. Here the stem is neuter and has no such ending, so it does not apply. The stem's final क is also preceded by इ rather than अ, so there is nothing to change.

I did not identify a specific sūtra for this affix; the result rests on this reasoning alone.

<answer>काथिकक</answer>
<answer>पावमानतर</answer>

I could not fully confirm whether the affix is सात् or retains a final -इ; I took सात् (the तदधीनवचने / कार्त्स्न्य sense, as in अग्निसात्). This is from memory of the Aṣṭādhyāyī and Kāśikā, so the identification is not certain. On that reading, the affix is added directly to the stem पुलस्ति with no change to the stem, and the result is an indeclinable.

<answer>पुलस्तिसात्</answer>

Applying ञ्यङ् (YyaN) to the stem टाल gives the stem below. I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यङ् here, so this rests only on the general mechanics of the affix.

1. The ञ् in ञ्यङ् is an it-marker that calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The first vowel of टाल is already आ, so nothing changes.
2. The ङ् is also an it-marker, leaving the affix as -य.
3. The final अ of टाल drops before the affix by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148).

So टाल + य → टाल्य.

<answer>टाल्य</answer>
<answer>घातनजातीय</answer>

Without a specific governing rule I could pin down for this stem, I take the affix as the possessive (matvarthīya) इनि of अत इनिठनौ (5.2.115), which applies after stems ending in short अ. The stem सौयज्ञक ends in अ, so the final अ drops before इनि (the usual elision of the stem's final vowel before a vowel-initial affix). The result is सौयज्ञकिन्, "one who has a सौयज्ञक". इनि carries no ṇ marker, so the vowels of the stem do not change.

<answer>सौयज्ञकिन्</answer>

This follows the affix चणप् of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which is added to a stem to mean "known/famed by that", as in विद्याचण. I did not check whether असनिक is an attested base for this affix, so the form is derived by the rule alone.

The affix becomes चण after dropping the indicatory letters ञ् and प्. It is added directly to the stem असनिक. Since the stem ends in अ and the affix begins with a consonant, nothing is elided or altered, and the joined stem is असनिकचण.

<answer>असनिकचण</answer>

The affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, in the sense of praise) is added to a nominal stem. The final प् is only an indicatory letter and drops out, so the form is the stem followed by रूप.

Applied to प्राप्तापराध, this gives प्राप्तापराधरूप. I chose this meaning from the affix's usual sense and did not check whether the stem naturally carries a sense of praise.

<answer>प्राप्तापराधरूप</answer>

I applied rūpap (Pāṇini 5.3.66, in the sense of praise) to the neuter stem मज्मन्. I could not recall how Pāṇini's rules treat the stem before this affix, so the choice below is a judgement, not a confirmed derivation.

The affix attaches to a subanta, so the stem counts as a pada before it. That would trigger deletion of the final न् by 8.2.7. Adding the affix रूप to the resulting मज्म gives the stem below.

<answer>मज्मरूप</answer>

This is the affix द्वयसच् of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which is added to a nominal stem in the sense of measure. The ending च् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix that remains is द्वयस. Because द्वयस begins with a consonant, the final -अ of साभिमान is not elided (यस्येति च does not apply). The stem is simply joined to the affix, as in ऊरुद्वयस.

<answer>साभिमानद्वयस</answer>

The stem क्षैप्रा ends in the long vowel आ, so by 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः) the म् of मतुप् becomes व्. This gives क्षैप्रा + वत्. The nominal stem is therefore क्षैप्रावत्. I did not check this against a commentary. The feminine, if needed, would be क्षैप्रावती.

<answer>क्षैप्रावत्</answer>
<answer>औष्ट्रायणकीय</answer>

I did not derive this from a specific rule application beyond the general pattern. The affix अस्ताति (astāti) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.27, which gives forms like पुरस्तात् (purastāt) and is normally attached to direction words. I assumed the result ends in -astāt, as in पुरस्तात्, because the final i of the affix drops in actual forms. Applying that to the stem हरिद्रक, the final अ of the stem combines with the initial अ of -astāt, which gives हरिद्रकस्तात्. The stem itself is not a direction word, so I am relying on the instruction that any meaning licensed for the affix is acceptable.

<answer>हरिद्रकस्तात्</answer>

The input stem व्याम्य ends in a short a, and the affix कन् leaves the form क after its final न् is dropped as an indicatory marker. Because क begins with a consonant, the rule that elides a stem-final a before a vowel-initial taddhita (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148) does not apply. The stem therefore stays whole and the affix is simply added: व्याम्य + क = व्याम्यक. I did not trace this stem to a specific rule in the Aṣṭādhyāyī, so the formation follows the general pattern for कन्.

Applying ठन् to कुट्टिन्:

2. Before this तद्धित affix, the final टि (the last vowel with what follows it) of the stem is dropped (6.4.144, नस्तद्धिते). So कुट्टिन् becomes कुट्ट्.
3. कुट्ट् + इक gives कुट्टिक.

I derived this from the general rules and did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठन् after this stem.

<answer>कुट्टिक</answer>

I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule for this affix, so this form is derived by standard sandhi rather than checked against a source.

The affix जाहच् has an initial ज् and a final च्, which are both markers (it-letters) by the cuṭū rule, so the affix that is actually added is आह. The stem विश्वैकसार ends in a short अ, and that अ drops before a vowel-initial taddhita affix. This gives विश्वैकसार् + आह = विश्वैकसाराह.

<answer>विश्वैकसाराह</answer>

I could not place a specific Pāṇinian rule for this affix, so this form comes from the general derivation rules rather than a cited sūtra.

1. Start with हेला + ञ्य. The ञ् and ट् are marker letters (it-letters), so what remains of the affix is ञ्य.
2. The final आ of हेला drops before the taddhita affix by 6.4.148, giving हेल् + य.
3. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so हे becomes है, giving हैल्य.
4. The ट् marker makes the feminine take ङीप् by 4.1.15, giving हैल्य + ई.

This gives the feminine stem हैल्यी. I am least sure of step 4, since the question may expect the form without the feminine ending.

<answer>हैल्यी</answer>

The affix फिञ् is the one taught in "तिकादिभ्यः फिञ्" (4.1.154). I recalled this from memory rather than checking the गण, and I am assuming कौन्दी belongs to the तिकादि list.

1. फिञ् has फ् as its initial, which is replaced by आयन्. The ञ् marks the affix as ञित्, so the stem takes आदि-वृद्धि. The vowel in कौ is already vṛddhi, so it does not change.
2. The final ई of कौन्दी is dropped before the affix by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), leaving कौन्द्.

This gives आत्मोपम् + इष्ठ = आत्मोपमिष्ठ. I did not work out which rule governs a feminine stem before इष्ठन्. Either a puṃvat step or direct deletion of आ leads to the same result.

<answer>आत्मोपमिष्ठ</answer>

The affix फिञ् (PiY) is the one taught in 4.1.154, तिकादिभ्यः फिञ्. I did not confirm that सातु belongs to the तिकादि list, so I am applying the affix as the table directs.

1. The initial फ् of फिञ् is replaced by आयन् (फ → आयन्, 7.1.2), and the ञ् is only an indicatory marker.
2. Because of the ञित् marker, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. In सातु it is already आ, so nothing changes there.
3. The final उ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving सात् + आयनि.

The result is सातायनि.

<answer>सातायनि</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ", with the sense "known by that" (as in विद्याचुञ्चुः, "known by learning"). <answer>तमिचुञ्चु</answer>

<answer>प्रौढाकृष्टायनि</answer>

The affix is च्वि (cvi), which is used when something comes to be what it was not before, with a verb like कृ, भू or अस्. Before च्वि the final अ of the stem becomes ई (अस्य च्वौ, Pāṇini 7.4.32). So वाह्लीक becomes वाह्लीकी, as in वाह्लीकी भवति, "becomes a Vāhlīka". I did not need the neuter gender of the source stem to derive this form.

I formed this by adding the affix त्व (used for "the state of being X", per Pāṇini 5.1.119) to the feminine stem त्रैरात्रिका. This is my own derivation and I have not checked it against a source.

<answer>त्रैरात्रिकात्व</answer>

The affix खञ् (KaY) is substituted by ईन, because ख् becomes ईन (Pāṇini 7.1.2). The ञ् is only a marker. I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् for this stem, so the form rests on the general mechanics of the affix.

<answer>कालान्तकीन</answer>

I did not derive this from a sūtra with full confidence. I am assuming the usual rule for मात्रच्, Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), where it is added to a nominal stem to express measure.

The affix is मात्र after dropping the indicatory letters च्. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of मौदक is not elided by यस्येति च (6.4.148). The stem and affix simply join, giving मौदकमात्र.

<answer>मौदकमात्र</answer>

I could not identify the exact Pāṇinian rule that introduces ञ्यट्, so this derivation is based on how the affix's markers behave, not on a confirmed sūtra.

I did not check whether प्रतीक्षिन् fits a specific शस् rule such as the distributive sense of 5.4.43; I applied the affix as the table specifies.

<answer>प्रतीक्षिशः</answer>

The affix देश्य is introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which gives the sense "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is added after a subanta base.

The base चतुष्किन् is a pada before देश्य, because the affix is treated like a sup-initial suffix (1.4.17). The final न् is therefore dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), leaving चतुष्कि. Adding देश्य gives चतुष्किदेश्य. This follows the pattern of राजकल्प, where the final -n is likewise dropped.

<answer>चतुष्किदेश्य</answer>
<answer>वैणाल</answer>

This is a derivation from my recollection of the relevant rules, and I could not fully pin down the exact sūtra numbers, so I have not checked them. The affix वलच् (valac) loses its indicatory letters ल् and च् and becomes वल. The stem सौभासिनिक has the status of a pada before this affix, so its final अ is not elided by the rule that drops a stem-final अ before a taddhita. I also believe the lengthening rule for a stem-final vowel before वल (as in कृषीवल) applies only to stems ending in इ, उ, ऋ or ऌ, not to a final अ. So the stem stays as it is and takes वल directly.

<answer>सौभासिनिकवल</answer>

Here देशीयर् (the affix of P. 5.3.67, in the sense "somewhat, almost") is added to the stem समद्वन्.

1. देशीय begins with a consonant, so the base is a *pada* (P. 1.4.17).
2. The final न् of the base therefore drops (P. 8.2.7): समद्वन् → समद्व.
3. Adding the affix gives समद्व + देशीय = समद्वदेशीय.

I did not work out any further effect of the stem being neuter; the derived stem is the same as I would form for any gender.

<answer>समद्वदेशीय</answer>
<answer>शैलूषिकीयस्</answer>

This is the affix that Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः) prescribes after a word denoting measure. I am relying on that rule from memory and have not checked it against a source.

The final च् of द्वयसच् is only a marker (it), so the affix that is actually added is द्वयस. The affix carries no ñit or ṇit marker, so there is no vṛddhi. The final -अ of छादक is dropped before the affix by the rule यस्येति च. This gives छादक + द्वयस → छादकद्वयस.

<answer>छादकद्वयस</answer>
<answer>प्रौष्ठपदमात्र</answer>

Here प्राप्तव्या ends in the feminine suffix टाप् (the long आ), and the taddhita affix is मयट्. I derived it as follows:

1. Before the taddhita affix, the final आ of the stem is dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), giving प्राप्तव्य.
2. The affix मयट् is added; its ट् is only a marker and disappears, leaving मय.
3. प्राप्तव्य + मय gives प्राप्तव्यमय.

Because मयट् has the marker ट्, the feminine would take ङीप्, giving प्राप्तव्यमयी. I gave the base stem, since the task asks for the derived stem without a further feminine suffix.

<answer>प्राप्तव्यमय</answer>

Before the affix मतुप्, the stem तृप ends in अ, so the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9) applies. It changes the म of मत् to व, and तृप is not among the exceptions (यवादि). This is the same pattern as धनवत् and गुणवत्.

तृप + मतुप् → तृप + वत् → तृपवत्

<answer>तृपवत्</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that licenses this affix with certainty, so this form is built from the usual treatment of the affix and not checked against the rule itself. I took जाहच् as adding -जाह to the stem, with the final च् dropped as a marker (इत्). The supplied stem spelling भुतोपसृष्ट is kept unchanged.

<answer>भुतोपसृष्टजाह</answer>

This is the शस् of Pāṇini 5.4.43 (संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायाम्). It is added to an ekavacana subanta in the sense of distribution (vīpsā), so कामाशोक ("each kāmāśoka") gives कामाशोक + शस्. The result is an indeclinable, and its final स् becomes visarga. I chose this rule and meaning myself, since the table allows any meaning licensed for the affix.

<answer>कामाशोकशः</answer>

The stem सेधा ends in the feminine long ā. The affix इष्ठन् is added in the sense of excess (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ). Before it, the stem-final आ is dropped by "यस्येति च", leaving सेध्. Adding इष्ठ gives सेधिष्ठ, a stem ending in अ. I did not check whether a pumvadbhāva or other feminine-specific rule would change this.

<answer>सेधिष्ठ</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), the affix पाशप् is added to a nominal stem to mean "contemptible, only barely passable as such". Its final प् is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix पाश. Since पाश begins with a consonant, no vowel elision (such as ṭi-lopa) applies to the stem. मेण्ढक therefore takes पाश unchanged, giving मेण्ढकपाश.

<answer>मेण्ढकपाश</answer>

The stem वसिर takes the affix अण्, which gives the derivative in the sense of "descendant". The first vowel of the stem undergoes vṛddhi (व → वा) and the final अ is dropped before the affix. I have not confirmed which specific rule licenses अण् on this stem; the likely source is the शिवादि group (शिवादिभ्योऽण्, 4.1.112), but that is an assumption from memory.

<answer>वासिर</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, and I could not recall the specific sūtra that licenses वलच् after this stem, so I did not verify it against the rule.

The affix वलच् leaves the base वल after the markers (च्) drop. Because वल begins with a consonant, the stem-final अ is not elided by यस्येति च (6.4.148). The stem नैचाशाख therefore takes वल directly, giving नैचाशाखवल.

<answer>नैचाशाखवल</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that governs this affix, so this derivation is a best reconstruction rather than a verified rule.

I took the stem as अप्नवान, ending in -अ, with the affix कुणप्. The final प् is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix as कुण. This affix begins with क्, not a vowel or य्, so the stem-final -अ is not elided. I also assumed there is no वृद्धि, since the affix has no marker that would trigger it. Joining the stem and affix gives अप्नवानकुण.

<answer>अप्नवानकुण</answer>

Applying मतुप् (the ending becomes मत्) to the stem शाखीय gives a possessive meaning, "having शाखीय". Since the stem ends in अ, rule 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः) changes the म of मत् to व. The derived stem is therefore शाखीयवत्.

<answer>शाखीयवत्</answer>

I derived this from the feminine stem आश्मभारिका with the affix ठक् (Wak), working step by step and without checking it against a commentary.

1. A taddhita affix may be added to a stem ending in a feminine suffix such as टाप् (Pāṇini 4.1.1), so ठक् can attach to आश्मभारिका.
2. ठक् becomes इक: the initial ठ् is replaced by इक (7.3.50).
3. The final आ of the stem is dropped before the affix (6.4.148), leaving आश्मभारिक्.
4. The affix is कित्, so the initial vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.118). It is already आ, so nothing changes.
5. Adding इक gives आश्मभारिक् + इक = आश्मभारिकिक.

<answer>आश्मभारिकिक</answer>

The derived stem is आश्वाध्यक्ष. The affix अण् is a ṇit affix, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (अ → आ), and the stem-final अ is dropped before it. The stem अश्वाध्यक्ष does not appear to be in the अनुशतिकादि list, so I did not apply vṛddhi to both parts. I did not check this against a source.

<answer>आश्वाध्यक्ष</answer>

I did not locate a Pāṇinian rule that attaches वलच् to तुल्य, so this form comes from the general pattern rather than a specific sūtra. Rule 5.2.112 (रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच्) gives forms like कृषीवल, where the stem keeps its feminine ending before वल. By the same pattern, the feminine stem तुल्या keeps its final -ā before the affix, since वलच् begins with a consonant and the ā is not elided. Dropping the final ज्, च् and the इत् markers leaves वल, which gives तुल्या + वल.

<answer>तुल्यावल</answer>

Affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय by the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम् (7.1.2). The final अ of the stem व्यथान्वित is dropped before the affix, giving व्यथान्वित + ईय = व्यथान्वितीय. I did not check which specific rule licenses छ for this stem, since any meaning licensed for the affix is acceptable.

<answer>व्यथान्वितीय</answer>

Before the affix, जह्ल ends in the vowel अ, so the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9) applies. It changes the म् of मतुप् to व् after a stem ending in अ or म. जह्ल is not in the exception list (यवादि). The affix then becomes वत्, as in वृक्ष → वृक्षवत्, giving जह्लवत्.

<answer>जह्लवत्</answer>

Of the three affixes in P. 5.2.37 (*pramāṇe dvayasac-daghnac-mātrac*), the one that applies here is मात्रच्, which gives the sense "measure of ...". The final च् is only an indicatory marker and drops. Nothing shortens the long ई of the feminine base, because 1.2.47–48 apply only to a final or subordinate member. I am giving the neuter stem as the answer, taken from the pattern of the standard example ऊरुमात्रम्, without checking a specific commentary for this word.

<answer>दूषीमात्र</answer>
<answer>स्फूर्छिष्ठ</answer>

The affix कल्पप् is added by P. 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) with the sense "slightly short of complete". Here that is "almost a टट्टनी".

The stem टट्टनी ends in the feminine suffix ङी and has more than one syllable. By P. 6.3.43, a ङी-ending stem of more than one syllable takes a short final vowel before कल्पप्. So टट्टनी becomes टट्टनि, and adding कल्प gives टट्टनिकल्प. I am relying on memory for the rule number and its wording.

When the word is used as a feminine, it takes टाप् and becomes टट्टनिकल्पा. I have given the bare derived stem.

<answer>टट्टनिकल्प</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात् तु), the affix बहुच् is added before a subanta to mean "almost, somewhat". It therefore stands in front of the stem rather than after it, so I prefix बहु to तरणीया and leave the feminine ending unchanged. I did not check this against a worked example for a feminine stem, so the retention of the feminine ending is my reading of the rule.

<answer>बहुतरणीया</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that attaches वलच् to दाधिका, so this form is a best-effort derivation, not one checked against a rule.

The affix वलच् begins with a consonant (व्), so the stem before it is treated as a pada. In that case the final आ of दाधिका is not elided (the लोप rule यस्येति च does not apply). The final च् of वलच् is only a marker and drops. The result is दाधिका + वल.

<answer>दाधिकावल</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु), the affix बहुच् is placed before the subanta to give the sense "almost, not quite" (ईषदसमाप्ति), as in बहुपटुः. The final च् is only a marker and drops out. Applying this to कादम्बर gives बहुकादम्बर, with no sandhi change at the join.

<answer>बहुकादम्बर</answer>

The affix मतुप् is added to the stem अन्धीकृतात्मन्. Before this affix the stem counts as a pada (1.4.19), so the final न् is dropped (8.2.7), giving अन्धीकृतात्म. The stem now ends in अ and has म् as its penultimate sound, so the म् of मतुप् becomes व् (8.2.9). The resulting stem is अन्धीकृतात्मवत्.

<answer>अन्धीकृतात्मवत्</answer>

The stem अंहुर ends in the vowel अ, so the affix मतुप् is added to it. The rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9) then changes the म of मतुप् to व. This happens after a stem ending in अ, and अंहुर is not one of the exceptional यवादि stems. The result is अंहुर + वत्, giving अंहुरवत्. This is the same pattern as वृक्ष → वृक्षवत्.

<answer>अंहुरवत्</answer>
<answer>सहस्राप्सस्ता</answer>

Starting from the feminine stem कौलत्थीना (ending in the feminine suffix टाप्), I add अण् under the general rule 4.1.1 (ङ्याप्प्रातिपदिकात्).

1. The final आ of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial अण् (यस्येति च), leaving कौलत्थीन्.
2. अण् then adds अ, giving कौलत्थीन.
3. The initial vowel औ is already vṛddhi, so the usual first-vowel strengthening (आदिवृद्धि) changes nothing.

I did not trace the specific sense-rule (such as तस्येदम्) that licenses अण् here, so the meaning is assumed rather than derived.

<answer>कौलत्थीन</answer>

I formed this from the affix sāti (SLP1 sAti), which makes indeclinables in the "made dependent on" sense. For example, the usual illustration is अग्निसात्करोति. As I recall it, the final -i of the affix is dropped, so the derived form ends in -सात्. I did not check this against the source text. The stem ends in -i and takes the affix with no sandhi change, so the form is वामनाकृतिसात्.

<answer>वामनाकृतिसात्</answer>
<answer>वैच्युतीय</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses this affix, so this answer is a best guess rather than a verified derivation.

1. The final -ā of the feminine stem कुणपा is dropped before the taddhita affix, leaving कुणप.
2. In the affix कुणप्, the final प् is an indicatory letter (it-marker) and is removed, leaving कुण.
3. Adding कुण to कुणप gives कुणपकुण.

<answer>कुणपकुण</answer>

I could not tie this to a specific Pāṇinian rule, since धन is not among the stems on which थाल् is taught. The rules that give थाल् are 5.3.23 (after सर्वनाम forms, in the sense of manner) and 5.3.111 (after प्रत्न, पूर्व, विश्व, इम in Vedic). So I applied the affix mechanically to the stem as given.

The affix थाल् loses its indicatory ल्, leaving था. Adding it to धन gives the indeclinable धनथा.

<answer>धनथा</answer>

The stem द्विष ends in -a, and the affix च्वि (cvi) is added to it. Under the rule "asya cvau" (7.4.32), the final -a becomes -ī before cvi, and the affix itself is then deleted entirely. This gives द्विषी, an indeclinable form that is normally used with कृ, भू or अस् (for example द्विषीभवति).

<answer>द्विषी</answer>

Here the affix ka (क) is the one taught in Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.70 ff. (prāg-ivāt kaḥ). It is added in senses such as contempt, unknown, compassion or smallness. I am recalling these sūtra numbers from memory and have not checked them.

Adding ka to the stem रोध gives रोध + क = रोधक. The stem is masculine and ends in -a, so it takes the ordinary -a-stem form.

<answer>रोधक</answer>

Here the affix थाल् (SLP1 TAl) is the one taught for "manner" (प्रकारवचने थाल्, 5.3.23). I derived the form from the stem as given, without checking it against a specific attested example.

The final ल् of थाल् is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix as था. The affix begins with a consonant, so the rule that deletes a stem-final अ/आ before an ī- or y-initial affix (यस्येति च) does not apply. The stem's final आ therefore stays, and था is added directly.

सांनाय्योखा + था → सांनाय्योखाथा

<answer>सांनाय्योखाथा</answer>

I take the affix रूपप् to be the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशस्ते रूपप्), which is added to a nominal base in the sense "praiseworthy". The affix surfaces as the ending -रूप, and the base करित्व stays unchanged before it, with no sandhi. This gives करित्वरूप.

<answer>करित्वरूप</answer>

The affix रूपप् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), in the sense of praise. Since रूप begins with a consonant, the final अ of चक्रिय is not elided, so the stem is simply चक्रिय + रूप. The ṕ-marker only affects accent and does not change the form.

<answer>चक्रियरूप</answer>

This is from memory of the rule, not a checked derivation. The affix सातिः (Pāṇini 5.4.52–54) is added to the stem and the result is an indeclinable ending in सात्, as in अग्निसात् and राजसात्. Following that pattern, the final इ of the affix is dropped, which gives स्नेहनीयसात्.

<answer>स्नेहनीयसात्</answer>

The affix अञ् (aY) carries an ञ् marker, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (Pāṇini 7.2.117, तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). In सूप, the first vowel ऊ is replaced by औ, and the stem-final अ is dropped before the affix's अ. The result is सौप, meaning "relating to soup" (the तस्येदम् sense, 4.3.120).

<answer>सौप</answer>

I did not identify the specific rule that licenses लच् on this stem, so this is the general derivation.

The stem सालम्बना ends in the feminine suffix टाप् (आ). Before the taddhita affix लच्, the final आ is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), because अवर्ण includes आ. The affix itself is just ल, since the च only marks accent. This gives सालम्बन् + ल, which is सालम्बल.

<answer>सालम्बल</answer>

I could not confidently identify the exact rule for this input, so this is a best-effort derivation. The affix is tasi (Pāṇini's तसि, as in 5.4.44). The result is an indeclinable ending in -तस्, written with visarga. I assumed the form is built by adding the affix directly to the stem जैत्वा. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem takes the pada form and keeps its long आ unchanged. That gives जैत्वा + तस् → जैत्वातः.

<answer>जैत्वातः</answer>

This follows from the general rule for adding a taddhita affix to a stem ending in -a; I did not trace a specific Pāṇinian rule licensing वलच् for this stem.

The affix वलच् loses its marker letters (च्) and becomes -वल. The final -अ of घनारुद्ध is dropped before it by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). That gives घनारुद्ध + वल = घनारुद्धवल.

<answer>घनारुद्धवल</answer>
<answer>कादर</answer>

I take the affix to be रूप्य of Pāṇini 4.3.81, which is added optionally after words for human beings in the sense "come from that". This is from memory, and I did not check it against the text.

The stem हृदयेशा ends in the feminine आ, and the affix begins with र, not य or ई. The elision rule यस्येति च therefore does not apply, and the final आ stays. The affix is simply added to the whole stem.

<answer>हृदयेशारूप्य</answer>

Adding the abstract-noun affix तल् (meaning "the state of being X") to सूपतीर्थ्य gives सूपतीर्थ्य + ता. Since तल् begins with a consonant, the stem is not treated as a *bha* stem, and the final -य of the stem is not elided. The derivative takes the feminine ending -टाप्, which gives the stem सूपतीर्थ्यता.

<answer>सूपतीर्थ्यता</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् on this stem, so this derivation is my best reconstruction from the general rules for ञ्-marked taddhita affixes, not a confirmed form.

1. The stem is पटिमन्, and the affix is ञ्य (the ट् is only a marker, which would give the feminine in ङीप्).
2. Before the affix ञ्य, which begins with य, the stem takes the name भ. By नस्तद्धिते (6.4.144) its final टि, "अन्", drops, leaving पटिम्.
3. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel: प → पा.
4. Adding the affix gives पाटिम्य.

<answer>पाटिम्य</answer>

I did not find a specific rule that picks out केशवालय, so this follows the general rule for the affix, with the stem taken as given.

The affix दघ्नच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नमात्रचः) for the sense of measure. It is added to the nominal stem, and the anubandha च् drops. The remaining affix दघ्न begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ of केशवालय is not elided. The result is the stem plus दघ्न.

<answer>केशवालयदघ्न</answer>

I could not tie ईर्य to a specific Pāṇinian rule for थाल्. The affix is normally added to pronominal stems under 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्), as in तथा and यथा.
