The derivation uses affix जातीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्), which gives the sense "of that kind".

1. Add the affix: विद्मनापस् + जातीय. The final ् of जातीयर् is only a marker and drops out.
2. The affix begins with the consonant ज्, so the stem counts as a pada (1.4.17).
3. The final स् of the pada becomes रु (8.2.66), and रु becomes उ before the soft consonant ज् (6.1.113).
4. The preceding अ and this उ merge into ओ (6.1.87).

This gives विद्मनापोजातीय. I derived this by applying the rules rather than checking an attested form, so the sandhi outcome is the least certain step.

<answer>विद्मनापोजातीय</answer>

The affix देश्य is introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It is added to a subanta in the sense of "slightly short of complete", here "almost a काण्डाल". The base takes no internal change, so the affix is simply appended.

<answer>काण्डालदेश्य</answer>
<answer>सौवर्ण्यवल</answer>
<answer>पौर्वाशिन</answer>

Here सेद्धव्य takes the affix छ. By the rule छोऽ ईय (7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्), छ is replaced by ईय. The final अ of the stem is then dropped before ईय (6.4.148 यस्येति च). This gives सेद्धव्य् + ईय = सेद्धव्यीय.

I did not identify the specific rule that licenses छ on this stem. The stem's initial vowel ए is guṇa rather than vṛddhi, so it does not fit the common rule वृद्धाच्छः (4.2.114). I formed the word by the standard substitution only.

<answer>सेद्धव्यीय</answer>

The affix चणप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), meaning "known through that". The familiar example is विद्याचणः, "known through learning".

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as भ and its final long ā is not elided (compare विद्या + चणप् = विद्याचण). Adding it to त्रैपुरा therefore gives त्रैपुराचण.

I derived this by analogy with the standard examples rather than from a source that attests this exact form.

<answer>त्रैपुराचण</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that introduces this affix, so this answer is a best guess. I took कुणप् to be the affix कुण with a final marker प्, which drops out. Because the affix begins with a consonant, the stem अम stays intact before it.

<answer>अमकुण</answer>

The affix तसि is added after the stem, and the result is an indeclinable (a तद्धित that takes no case endings). The stem अटा keeps its long आ, because the rule shortening a feminine vowel before a taddhita (गोस्त्रियोरुपसर्जनस्य) applies only to subordinate members of a compound, and अटा is not one. So अटा + तसि gives अटातः. I have not checked this against a specific example in the grammatical tradition.

<answer>अटातः</answer>

The affix मयट् is added to the stem स्थायुक. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, giving स्थायुक् + मय. The ट् in the affix is only a marker and does not appear in the stem. The result is:

<answer>स्थायुकमय</answer>

The affix ठन् (SLP1 `Wan`) fits P. 5.2.115 अत इनिठनौ, which adds इनि or ठन् to a stem ending in अ in the sense of possession. I could not tie the stem मैत्रावरुणीय to a more specific ठन् rule, so this identification is my best fit rather than a certain one.

1. The affix ठन् has the final न् as an marker and the initial ठ् as the part that is replaced. By P. 7.3.50 ठस्येकः, ठ becomes इक. The affix is therefore -इक.
2. The stem मैत्रावरुणीय already has a vṛddhi vowel (ऐ) in its first syllable, so no further vowel change applies.
3. Before the affix, the final अ of the stem is dropped by यस्येति च (P. 6.4.148). This gives मैत्रावरुणीय् + इक, which joins as मैत्रावरुणीयिक.

<answer>मैत्रावरुणीयिक</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that attaches यत् to this stem, so this form rests on the general mechanics of the affix.

The stem सर्वादि ends in -i, and the affix यत् is not ञित् or णित्, so no vṛddhi applies. The final इ of the stem is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च), giving सर्वाद् + य, which is सर्वाद्य.

<answer>सर्वाद्य</answer>

Taddhita खञ् (KaY) is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन), and the ञ् is only an indicatory marker that calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The stem's initial vowel सा is already vṛddhi, so nothing changes there. Before the taddhita affix, the feminine आ of सांग्राहिका is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving सांग्राहिक. Adding ईन gives सांग्राहिकीन. I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् for this stem, so the derivation rests on the general rules above.

<answer>सांग्राहिकीन</answer>
<answer>बहुशेषाधिकारीय</answer>
<answer>यात्रिक</answer>
<answer>क्षेप्यमय</answer>

The affix तल् (SLP1 `tal`) is added in the sense of "state or quality" (भावे त्वतलौ, 5.1.119). The final ल् drops as an indicatory letter, leaving the affix त. Words ending in तल् are feminine (टाप्), so the stem becomes औष्ठ + ता. The stem औष्ठ takes no further change.

<answer>औष्ठता</answer>

Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*) gives the affix caṇap (चण) in the sense "known by that" (e.g. *vidyā-caṇaḥ*). Here the stem is प्राजापत्य, giving "one known by the Prājāpatya".

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not a "bha" stem. The final अ of -य therefore stays (no *yasyeti ca* elision). The first vowel of प्राजापत्य is already आ, so the vṛddhi triggered by the ṇ-marker changes nothing. The result is प्राजापत्य + चण.

<answer>प्राजापत्यचण</answer>
<answer>शल्लकमात्र</answer>

The affix त्रा is added to the stem as it stands. Because it begins with a consonant, the final -ā of the feminine stem is not elided (यस्येति च does not apply). The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>मदोर्जितात्रा</answer>

Following the rule for the affix cvi (अभूततद्भावे …), the final vowel of the stem lengthens before cvi (च्वौ च, 7.4.26). The affix itself then disappears, leaving only the lengthened vowel. So सुम्नयु becomes सुम्नयू.

<answer>सुम्नयू</answer>

नेत्रौषधी शब्द के अन्त में ङीप् है। थाल् का आरम्भ व्यञ्जन थ् से होता है, इसलिए शब्द के अन्तिम ई का लोप या परिवर्तन नहीं होता। थाल् में ल् इत्संज्ञक है, इसलिए प्रत्यय का शेष भाग "था" रहता है। इस प्रकार नेत्रौषधी + था से नेत्रौषधीथा बनता है। मैंने यह रूप नियम लगाकर निकाला है। पाणिनि के प्रकारवचने थाल् का सामान्य प्रयोग सर्वनाम शब्दों के बाद होता है, और यहाँ का प्रयोग उसी विधि का कृत्रिम विस्तार है।

<answer>नेत्रौषधीथा</answer>

This is a derivation by rule. The affix ञ्यट् is Pāṇini 5.3.114. The affix's initial ञ् and final ट् are indicatory letters, so only -य remains.

1. The stem ईप्सिता ends in the feminine -ā (ṭāp). Before the taddhita affix, the final आ is elided by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving ईप्सित् + य.
2. Because the affix has an indicatory ञ्, the first vowel takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (7.2.117). Vṛddhi of ई is ऐ, giving ऐप्सित्य.

<answer>ऐप्सित्य</answer>

Applying ईयसुन् (comparative) to the stem वस्त्रापहारिन् gives the form below.

1. The affix is ईयसुन्. Its उन् part is only a marker, so the affix that is actually added is ईयस्.
2. The stem ends in -इन्, from the kṛt suffix णिनि. Before ईयसुन्, rule 6.4.155 (टेः) drops the टि, which is the final vowel together with any consonant after it. Here that is इन्, so वस्त्रापहारिन् becomes वस्त्रापहार.
3. Adding ईयस् gives वस्त्रापहारीयस्.

<answer>वस्त्रापहारीयस्</answer>
<answer>यौजनशतिकचर</answer>

The affix साति (sāti) is the one taught for the sense of totality (कार्त्स्न्य) or of being made subject to something, as in अग्निसात् ("wholly to fire"). It is added to the stem जलेश, and its final इ is elided, as in अग्निसात्, so the result is an indeclinable ending in त्. I am recalling this from memory rather than checking the sūtra numbers.

जलेश + साति → जलेशसात्

<answer>जलेशसात्</answer>

Applying the affix ण्य (Rya) to नाधीत is a mechanical derivation. I did not identify a specific sūtra that licenses ण्य after this stem, so this rests on the general rules for a ṇit affix.

1. The ण् in ण्य is only a marker, so the stem's first vowel takes vṛddhi. Here the first vowel is already आ, so it stays as it is.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (टि-लोप), giving नाधीत् + य.
3. Joining the two gives नाधीत्य.

<answer>नाधीत्य</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), the affix रूपप् is added to a nominal stem to express praise. The final प् is only a marker and drops, leaving the ending -रूप. Attaching it to शर्वट gives शर्वटरूप, meaning "an excellent शर्वट".

<answer>शर्वटरूप</answer>
<answer>सादोत्सविक</answer>
<answer>नेत्रोपाध्यायजातीय</answer>

This is a judgement-based derivation, not a certain one.

The affix cvi (5.4.50) is added to a nominal stem when something becomes what it was not before. Its initial c comes before the vowel i, so the stem takes pada status under 1.4.17 (svādiṣu pade). Because of that, the final न् of उत्कर्षिन् is dropped by 8.2.7 (nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya). The affix itself is then deleted entirely (6.1.67), which leaves the stem ending in ई. I treated the nalopa as still applying after the affix is deleted. The alternative reading is that it does not apply, which would leave उत्कर्षिन् unchanged.

<answer>उत्कर्षी</answer>
<answer>साकल्यकामय</answer>

I derived this mechanically; I could not identify the specific rule that licenses यत् after this stem.

The stem मधूल ends in short अ. Before the taddhita affix य (from यत्), the final अ of the stem is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148). Joining the stem to the affix then gives मधूल्य.

I also considered ओर्गुणः (6.4.146), which would change a final उ or ऊ before the affix. It does not apply here, because the final sound of the stem is अ, not ऊ.

<answer>मधूल्य</answer>

This is the taddhita affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, प्रशस्ते रूपप्), which has the sense "praiseworthy X". It is added to the stem after the stem is treated as a pada, as in वैयाकरणरूप ("a praiseworthy grammarian"). The affix begins with a consonant other than य, so the stem मुथशिलिन् takes pada status. Its final न् is therefore dropped by नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (8.2.7), giving मुथशिलि + रूप. The result is the a-ending nominal stem मुथशिलिरूप.

<answer>मुथशिलिरूप</answer>

The affix क (ka) is added to the masculine stem रोलम्ब ("bee") in its general sense, with no change to the stem. This gives the stem रोलम्बक. I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that governs this stem, so this is the plain addition of the affix.

<answer>रोलम्बक</answer>
<answer>बहुवात्य</answer>

This is a derivation by rule application, and I did not identify which specific sūtra licenses the affix on this stem. It forms a secondary derivative from वैकृतिक with ठक्.

1. The affix ठक् is replaced by इक (ठ् → इक by "ठस्येकः").
2. The stem's final अ is dropped before the affix begins with a vowel.
3. The first vowel of the stem is already vṛddhi (ऐ), so it stays unchanged.
4. This gives वैकृतिक् + इक = वैकृतिकिक.

<answer>वैकृतिकिक</answer>

Before the affix च्वि (cvi), a final अ becomes ई (अस्य च्वौ, 7.4.32). So चारमिक becomes चारमिकी, as in चारमिकीकरोति or चारमिकीभवति.

<answer>चारमिकी</answer>
<answer>यौक्तिकतः</answer>
<answer>दुवस्युमत्</answer>

Here the affix छ (Ca) is substituted by ईय under the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्. Under the default छ of प्राक्क्रीताच्छः, the sense तस्मै हितम् ("beneficial to that") licenses it. The stem's final अ drops before the vowel-initial ईय, so खर्वक + ईय gives खर्वकीय. I did not check this derivation against a source.

<answer>खर्वकीय</answer>

Here चरट् is the affix of "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Pāṇini 5.3.53), which gives the sense "formerly was". It is added directly to the stem प्रथमार्ध, as in आढ्यचर "formerly rich". The ट् is only an marker letter and drops out, so the stem becomes प्रथमार्ध + चर = प्रथमार्धचर. I am working from memory of this rule, not from a source check.

<answer>प्रथमार्धचर</answer>

Under the rule that licenses this affix (Pāṇini 5.4.50, कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः), मायुराज takes च्वि when it is used with a form of कृ, भू or अस् to mean "becoming X". The whole affix is elided (वि-लोप), and the stem-final अ changes to ई by 7.4.32 (अस्य च्वौ). This gives मायुराजी, as in मायुराजीकरोति.

<answer>मायुराजी</answer>

The affix फिञ् becomes आयन् (फ् → आयन्), and the ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel. The final अ of व्याघ्राण is dropped before the affix. In a stem beginning with व्या-, rule 7.3.3 gives ऐ plus य्, as in व्याकरण → वैयाकरण and व्याघ्र → वैयाघ्र. The stem therefore becomes वैयाघ्राण + आयन्. The न of आयन् stays न, because the intervening ण blocks the retroflexion rule 8.4.2.

This relies on recalling that व्याघ्राण is covered by the affix (the तिकादि class, 4.1.154). I could not confirm that membership, so the form below rests on that assumption.

<answer>वैयाघ्राणायन</answer>
<answer>लहरिका</answer>

The affix कल्पप् (kalpap) is added by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) and means "almost, slightly deficient in the quality of". Since it begins with a consonant, the stem takes no internal change and the affix is simply appended to धार्म्यायण.

<answer>धार्म्यायणकल्प</answer>

Here रूपप् is the Pāṇinian affix for "praiseworthy" (प्रशंसा), which I am recalling from memory rather than checking against the sūtra text. It is added directly to the nominal stem, and the final प् only marks the accent. So सृत्वर + रूप gives सृत्वररूप, with no case ending added.

<answer>सृत्वररूप</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् here, so this derivation rests on the general rules for ñit and ṭit affixes.

1. Drop the final आ of the stem सूर्योढा, leaving सूर्योढ.
2. Add ञ्य. The marker ञ् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (7.2.117), so ऊ in सू becomes औ, giving सौर्योढ्य.
3. The marker ट् only licenses the feminine suffix ङीप् when the derived word is feminine in sense. I have left that out, since the table asks only for the taddhita derivative. With ङीप् the form would be सौर्योढ्यी.

<answer>सौर्योढ्य</answer>

This is the taddhita affix बहुच् of Pāṇini 5.3.68, "विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु". It is added before a subanta word and means "almost, not quite complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It therefore attaches in front of the stem, giving बहु + श्राद्धाभिमर्शन. No change to the stem is needed, so the derived stem is as below.

<answer>बहुश्राद्धाभिमर्शन</answer>

I read the affix as the बहुच् of Pāṇini 5.3.68–69, which means "slightly short of complete". It is placed before the base, so it gives बहु- as a prefix. The base गावामयनिक already ends in a short vowel, so the neuter shortening rule changes nothing. This is my own derivation, not checked against a source.

<answer>बहुगावामयनिक</answer>

The affix चरट् is added by P. 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), with the sense "formerly that". Applied to पृच्छा, it gives the stem पृच्छाचर, "formerly a question". The affix has a ṭ-marker, so a feminine form would take ṅīp and become पृच्छाचरी. I gave the stem before that feminine step, but the question is ambiguous on this point.

<answer>पृच्छाचर</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is optionally added after a subanta in the sense of "slightly less than complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it is placed before the stem. So बहु- is prefixed to करञ्जक, giving the stem बहुकरञ्जक.

<answer>बहुकरञ्जक</answer>

I could not match मदाढ्य to a rule that licenses थमु. Pāṇini's थमु (5.3.24–25) applies to इदम् and किम्, giving इत्थम् and कथम्. I therefore formed the derivative mechanically, treating the affix as a suffix meaning "in the manner of" (प्रकार).

The affix थमु has a final उ that is only a marker (इत्), so what is added is थम्. Because थम् begins with a consonant, the final अ of the stem is not deleted by यस्येति च (6.4.148). The result is an indeclinable (अव्यय) ending in म्.

मदाढ्य + थम् → मदाढ्यथम्

<answer>मदाढ्यथम्</answer>

I attached तरप् (the comparative affix, giving the stem ending -tara) directly to the neuter stem सुखेतर. The stem ends in -a, so no vowel change or other adjustment applies, and the result is सुखेतरतर.

<answer>सुखेतरतर</answer>

Forming the abstract noun (bhāva, "the state of being X") with the affix त्व under Pāṇini 5.1.119 *tasya bhāvas tvatalau*. The affix त्व carries no ṇit or ñit marker, so there is no vṛddhi or other change to the stem. The stem simply takes त्व.

धन्याष्टक + त्व → धन्याष्टकत्व

<answer>धन्याष्टकत्व</answer>
<answer>पथ्यतः</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces जाहच्, so this form is a best guess built from general rules rather than a confirmed derivation.

1. The affix जाहच् ends in च्, which is an indicatory marker (इत्), so what is added is जाह.
2. The stem दैवकी ends in the feminine ई. Before a taddhita affix this ई is dropped (यस्येति च), leaving दैवक.
3. Adding the affix gives दैवक + जाह = दैवकजाह.

I kept the initial ज् as part of the affix. If the initial ज् were also treated as an indicatory marker (चुटू), the result would instead be दैवकाह. I could not settle which reading is right.

<answer>दैवकजाह</answer>
<answer>कापिशायनतः</answer>

The stem लाघवान्विता ends in the feminine suffix ā (ṭāp). I assumed the अण् is the one taught in the sense "this belongs to it" (तस्येदम्, 4.3.120), though the table does not name a rule.

1. Before a taddhita affix the final ā of the stem is deleted (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), leaving लाघवान्वित्.
2. Adding अण् gives लाघवान्वित.
3. The affix is ṇit, so the first vowel would take vṛddhi. Here it is already ā (ला), so nothing changes.

<answer>लाघवान्वित</answer>

Derivation: मेषा + ठक्. The affix ठ् is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः), so the stem becomes मेषा + इक. The final आ of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च), giving मेष् + इक. The first vowel then takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि: ए → ऐ), giving मैषिक.

I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठक् here, so the form rests on the general taddhita rules above.

I applied this rule from memory and did not check it against the source text. The usual textbook uses of थमु are with इदम् and किम् (as in इत्थम्, कथम्), so applying it to this stem is an assumption.

3. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi: मे becomes मै.

2. तापिता + तल् becomes तापिता + ता, since the final ल् of the affix is only a marker (it).
3. Words in तल् are feminine, and the result takes the usual आ-stem form.

The stem ends in the vowel अ, but क begins with a consonant. So यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not delete that अ.

The ईकारान्त/feminine rule that changes अ to इ before क (7.3.44) does not apply here, because the source is neuter and the stem is not feminine.

The result is सौवर्णिक + क = सौवर्णिकक, which gives सौवर्णिककम् in the neuter nominative singular.

The affix साति (Pāṇini 5.4.52–54) gives an indeclinable ending in सात्. I could not recall for certain how the final ति is dropped, so I took the standard attested form (as in राजसात्, अग्निसात्) and followed it.

The affix begins with स, not a vowel or य, so the rule that elides a stem-final अ/आ (यस्येति च, 6.4.148) does not apply. The final आ of जुगुप्सनीया therefore stays, and the form is जुगुप्सनीया + सात्.

For a pada ending in स्, the final स् becomes रु (8.2.66), which then becomes a visarga before the following श (8.3.15). The affix's own final स् also becomes a visarga. This gives तरूषःशः. Rule 8.3.36 would also allow an optional variant तरूषश्शः, but I have given only the unmodified visarga form.

<answer>तरूषःशः</answer>

The stem is वाताप्य and the affix is यत्, which has no ित् or ण् marker, so there is no vṛddhi and no change to the initial vowel.

1. Before the affix यत्, the final अ of the stem's य is dropped by यस्येति च, giving वाताप्य् + य.

<answer>क्लमथुथम्</answer>

Under the rule टेः (6.4.155), the ṭi of the base (the last vowel with any consonant after it) is dropped before ईयसुन्. In गोधाशन the ṭi is अन्, so the base becomes गोधाश्. The affix, after its उ and न् markers are dropped (ईयसुन् → ईयस्), is then added: गोधाश् + ईयस् = गोधाशीयस्.

<answer>गोधाशीयस्</answer>

I could not recall which Pāṇinian rule introduces this affix, so this form rests on general reasoning rather than a located rule.

The affix जाहच् has a final च्, which is only an indicatory marker, so the affix that is actually added is जाह.

The affix begins with a consonant, so no vowel at the end of the stem is dropped. The affix is not marked as ञित् or णित्, so no vṛddhi applies to the first vowel of the stem. The stem therefore stays whole and the affix is added directly.

<answer>साम्प्रताधिपजाह</answer>
<answer>पृषातदेशीय</answer>
<answer>रथाङ्गशः</answer>

This is the possessive use of इनि, taught in "अत इनिठनौ" (A. 5.2.115), which attaches इनि to a-ending stems with the sense "having". I did not check this against a source, so it is my best derivation rather than a confirmed attested form.

The stem वेत्रासनासीन ends in अ. Before the affix इनि the final अ is dropped, and the result takes the stem form ending in -इन्.

इनि is not marked ṇit, so there is no vṛddhi. The न in the stem is not retroflexed (no ṇatva), because the स between the र and the न blocks it.

<answer>वेत्रासनासीनिन्</answer>
<answer>ध्रौवकिमात्र</answer>

I derived this from the stem पञ्चतय itself, without checking whether iṣṭhan can in fact apply to such a stem. The steps are:

1. The stem is पञ्चतय, so the affix attaches directly to पञ्चतय + इष्ठन्.
2. Before इष्ठन्, the final vowel of the stem (the ṭi) is dropped by the ṭi-lopa rule (6.4.155). This takes the final अ of पञ्चतय away and leaves पञ्चतय्.
3. Joining इष्ठ gives पञ्चतय् + इष्ठ = पञ्चतयिष्ठ.

<answer>पञ्चतयिष्ठ</answer>

This is formed by adding the affix मात्रच् to the stem अपम. I did not check whether the stem, or the measure sense of मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37), fits this particular word, so the form follows only from the combination rule.

- The final च् of मात्रच् is only an indicatory letter (it marks the accent), so the affix is simply -मात्र.
- Because the affix starts with a consonant, the stem's final अ is not dropped (6.4.148 applies only before affixes beginning with a vowel or ई).
- The affix is not marked ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi.

The result is the stem अपममात्र, which is neuter.

<answer>अपममात्र</answer>
<answer>शूकवल</answer>

Adding the superlative affix तमप् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ) to the stem कालागुरु needs no internal sandhi or other change. The final अ of the affix is the only residue of तमप् (the प् is a marker), so the result is कालागुरुतम.

<answer>कालागुरुतम</answer>

I formed this with the affix तल् (SLP1 `tal`), which gives the abstract sense "state of being X". Adding it to अनिमिषाक्ष gives अनिमिषाक्ष + ता. Words ending in तल् are feminine and take the feminine ending टाप्, so the stem ends in -ā. The result is अनिमिषाक्षता, "the state of having unblinking eyes".

<answer>अनिमिषाक्षता</answer>

Adding मतुप् to the stem फल्ग्व gives फल्ग्व + मत्. Because the stem ends in the vowel अ, the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9) changes the म of मत् to व, and फल्ग्व is not in the exceptional यवादि group. This gives the derived stem फल्ग्ववत्.

<answer>फल्ग्ववत्</answer>
<answer>सैद्धासनि</answer>

I could not recall the rule that introduces जाहच्, so this form is reasoned from general Pāṇinian principles rather than checked against a source.

1. In the affix जाहच्, the initial ज् is an it-letter by चुटू (1.3.7). The final च् is also an it-letter, so the operative affix is आह.
2. The stem केली ends in the feminine ई. Before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel, this ई is deleted by यस्येति च (6.4.148).
3. So केल् + आह gives केलाह.

<answer>केलाह</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule, so this form rests on an assumption about the affix.

थाल् is introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्), meaning "in the manner of". It is normally added to pronominal stems, as in तथा and यथा. शालोत्तरीय is not a pronoun, so I have assumed the affix is added regardless. The affix has no initial vowel, so the stem's final अ stays, and the form is शालोत्तरीय + था.

<answer>शालोत्तरीयथा</answer>

This is a derivation by rūpap, taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 for a word that is "praiseworthy of its kind".

1. The base is the feminine stem वैहंगा, so the sense is "a praiseworthy वैहंगा".
2. Before रूप, an āp-ending stem is shortened (6.3.43, from memory), so वैहंगा becomes वैहंग.
3. Adding रूपप् gives वैहंगरूप.
4. The word stays feminine, so ṭāp is added and the final stem is वैहंगरूपा.

I recalled the shortening rule from memory and did not check its exact number or whether it restricts the stem, so the shortening step is the least certain part.

<answer>वैहंगरूपा</answer>

This is a formation with the measure-sense affix दघ्नच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, as in ऊरुदघ्नम्). The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter, so the affix added is -दघ्न. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not elided. The result is श्राद्धाधिकार + दघ्न.

<answer>श्राद्धाधिकारदघ्न</answer>

This is a best guess, since I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप्. I took the affix to be कुण, with the final प् as a marker that drops out. Before a taddhita affix, the final -न् of भावितात्मन् is dropped (नस्तद्धिते, 6.4.144), which gives भावितात्म + कुण.

<answer>भावितात्मकुण</answer>

<answer>सीमिकत्रा</answer>
<answer>ग्लौचुकायनजातीय</answer>

I did not derive this from a fully verified rule. The affix सातिः (SLP1 sAti) is taught under the sūtras on "making something dependent on" the base's referent, as in अग्निसात् (from अग्नि). The result is an indeclinable that ends in सात्, and the base keeps its form, so the final ū of शुद्धायू stays unchanged.

<answer>शुद्धायूसात्</answer>

I did not match गताधि to a specific example in the grammatical tradition. I assumed the affix is the distributive (वीप्सा) शस्, which gives an indeclinable ending in -शः, and I formed the word on that basis.

<answer>गताधिशः</answer>
<answer>शृङ्गारिताता</answer>

The stem गम्यमाना ends in the feminine suffix टाप्. Before the taddhita affix ईयसुन् (which becomes ईयस्), the final आ is elided by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This gives गम्यमान् + ईयस् = गम्यमानीयस्. I derived this from my recollection of the rules rather than checking each sūtra, and I did not confirm whether ईयसुन् is formally licensed on a participial stem like this one. I took the question's "any meaning licensed" wording to cover that.

<answer>गम्यमानीयस्</answer>

Pāṇini 5.2.37 (*pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātracaḥ*) lets the affix *dvayasac* be added to a nominal stem to express measure. The affix is attached as द्वयस, because the final च् is only an indicatory marker.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of फलाराम is not dropped by *yasyeti ca* (6.4.148), which applies only before affixes beginning with a vowel or य. The stem and affix simply join, as in ऊरुद्वयस.

फलाराम + द्वयस = फलारामद्वयस

<answer>फलारामद्वयस</answer>

क्षोभ्य takes तमप् (rule अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, "most, in the highest degree") with no change to the stem. The अप् of the affix is only a marker and drops, leaving -तम.

<answer>क्षोभ्यतम</answer>

<answer>छन्दस्यात्रा</answer>

This is an application of Pāṇini 5.3.68 (vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu). The affix बहुच् is placed before a declined word to mean "somewhat" or "slightly". The stem परु therefore takes बहु- in front of it, which gives बहुपरु.

I worked from my recollection of the rule rather than a reference check.

<answer>बहुपरु</answer>

The derivative is formed by adding मयट् (mayaṭ) to the feminine stem उर्वरी, and I did not check this against a specific example from the grammar. Rule 4.3.143 allows मयट् for a modified product or a part, as in "made of" or "consisting of".

मयट् begins with a consonant, so the final ई of the feminine stem is not dropped. The rule 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), which deletes it, applies only before affixes that begin with a vowel. The final ट् of मयट् is only a marker and is dropped. The result is a stem in -a.

<answer>उर्वरीमय</answer>
<answer>शीतेतरकल्प</answer>

I formed this by applying the affix phiñ (फिञ्) in its usual way, without confirming which Pāṇinian rule licenses it for this stem.

1. The initial फ् of the affix is replaced by आयन्, and the ञ् marks vṛddhi (the strengthened vowel grade) of the stem's first vowel.
2. The first vowel of आत्मोपम is already आ, so vṛddhi changes nothing there.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving आत्मोपम + आयनि → आत्मोपमायनि.

<answer>आत्मोपमायनि</answer>

Here the affix चरट् is the one taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.53), meaning "formerly was so-and-so".

I formed the stem from memory of the rule rather than by checking a source. In a taddhita affix the initial च् is not an it-marker, so the affix reduces to चर, with ट् as the marker.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem पियारु does not take the bha status that would trigger guṇa. The stem ending is therefore unchanged, and the form is पियारुचर.

Here the affix is तसिल्, which follows the stem शापेयिन्. Because the affix begins with the consonant त्, the stem takes the pada designation before it, so the final न् drops by the rule on the final न् of a nominal stem. Adding तसि gives शापेयितः, and since the affix is a sārvavibhaktika taddhita, the result is an indeclinable.

<answer>शापेयितः</answer>
<answer>महोदारचर</answer>

I could not derive this with full certainty. I took the affix to be the distributive शस् (Sas). Its initial ष् is an it-marker (indicatory letter) and drops, leaving "अस्". Because this begins with a vowel, the stem is treated as "bha" (1.4.18). Rule 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) then deletes the stem-final अवर्ण, which includes the feminine आ, as in गङ्गा + ण → गाङ्ग. <answer>और्मिलेयमात्र</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that attaches खञ् to this feminine stem, so I formed the derivative by the general rules for the affix.

2. The affix is ञित्, so the stem takes vṛddhi on its first vowel (7.2.117). The first vowel of जात्या is already आ, so nothing changes.

<answer>जात्यीन</answer>

Applying the affix थाल् to the stem गोपन: the final ल् of थाल् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the actual suffix था. The stem ends in अ and the suffix begins with a consonant, so no vowel elision or other sandhi applies. The stem and suffix simply join as गोपन + था. I did not tie this to a specific Pāṇinian rule for थाल्, since the task accepts any licensed meaning.

<answer>गोपनथा</answer>

I applied the affix by Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ). It is added after a word in the instrumental sense and gives the meaning "known by it", as in विद्याचुञ्चुः "known for learning". The final प् is only a marker and is dropped, so the affix appears as चुञ्चु. It begins with a consonant, so शाब्दिक stays unchanged before it. The resulting stem ends in -u. <answer>योगार्णवमात्र</answer>

The feminine stem माल्लवी takes the affix यत्, which has the form -य. Before a taddhita affix, the stem-final ई is dropped by the rule "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). That leaves माल्लव. The final -अ is dropped by the same rule before -य, so the result is माल्लव् + य. Since यत् carries no ञ् marker, the stem's vowels are not strengthened further.

The affix अस्ताति (5.3.27, with 5.3.1 treating it as a vibhakti-type affix) leaves a form ending in -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात् and उत्तरस्तात्. I did not check that the affix's final इ drops this way. I took the pattern from those known forms.

Joining the stem and the affix: स्वाभीष्ट + अस्तात्. The stem's final अ is elided before the vowel-initial affix (6.4.148), giving स्वाभीष्ट् + अस्तात् = स्वाभीष्टस्तात्. The result is indeclinable.

<answer>स्वाभीष्टस्तात्</answer>

This is derived by reasoning from the rules, not checked against a derivation tool, and the choice between the two outcomes below is the uncertain step.

The affix अस्ताति (rule 5.3.27) surfaces as -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्. It is added to the stem ब्रह्मोज्झा.

The affix begins with a vowel and is a taddhita, so the stem counts as a *bha* stem. Rule 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) then deletes the stem-final आ, which gives ब्रह्मोज्झ + अस्तात् → ब्रह्मोज्झस्तात्.

The alternative outcome would keep the आ and give ब्रह्मोज्झास्तात्. I chose the form with the आ deleted because 6.4.148 applies to this stem.

<answer>ब्रह्मोज्झस्तात्</answer>
<answer>आनसशः</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् is added to the stem without any change to the stem. The final *c* of the affix is only a marker (anubandha) and drops, which leaves the suffix **-द्वयस**. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem is not elided. This is the same pattern as ऊरु + द्वयसच् → ऊरुद्वयस. The result is the stem प्राप्तापराध followed by द्वयस.

<answer>प्राप्तापराधद्वयस</answer>

ग्रन्थीक + शस् gives the indeclinable ग्रन्थीकशः. I could not identify a specific rule that licenses शस् after this particular stem, so this is the plain addition of the affix. The affix is the distributive one (as in बहुशः, एकशः), and the stem ending in ईक does not change anything.

<answer>ग्रन्थीकशः</answer>

The stem कणान्ना is a feminine stem ending in आ. When the taddhita affix कन् (which becomes क) is added to it, the final आ is shortened to अ by the rule केऽणः (7.4.13), which shortens an अण् vowel before a क suffix. This gives कणान्न + क = कणान्नक.

I stopped at this stem. A feminine form, if wanted, would add टाप् and change the vowel before it to इ (कणान्निका), but the task asks only for the derived stem, so I gave the unextended one. I derived this from memory of the rules, so the choice of stopping point is my judgment rather than something the table fixes.

<answer>कणान्नक</answer>
<answer>क्षुल्लता</answer>

This is my best reconstruction, not a derivation I could tie to a specific Pāṇinian rule, because I could not identify the sūtra that prescribes ञ्यङ् here.

The affix पाशप् is the one taught in "याप्ये पाशप्" (Pāṇini 5.3.47). It is added after a nominal stem in the sense of something deficient or contemptible (याप्य). The final प् only marks accent and drops out, so the affix is effectively -पाश.

It begins with a consonant other than य, so it does not trigger टि-लोप and the stem-final अ stays. Adding -पाश to सार्ध gives the stem सार्धपाश.

<answer>सार्धपाश</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that teaches ञ्यट्, so this form is derived from the general rules for a ञित् affix, not from a confirmed rule.

1. The ट् in the affix is only a marker and does not remain; the affix is read as -य.
2. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117). The ऊ of क्रू becomes औ, giving क्रौर-.
3. Before a taddhita affix, the final -अन् of आत्मन् loses its टि part (6.4.144), so आत्मन् becomes आत्म्.
4. Joining the pieces gives क्रौरात्म्य.

<answer>क्रौरात्म्य</answer>
<answer>हन्नचर</answer>

Applying ठक् to the stem परमाटिक, the steps are as follows.

1. The initial ठ् of ठक् is replaced by इक (7.3.50 ठस्येकः), so the affix becomes इक.
2. The final अ of the stem is elided before the affix, giving परमाटिक् + इक (6.4.148 यस्येति च).
3. The first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi because the affix is kit (7.2.117 together with 7.2.118 किति च). The अ of प becomes आ, giving पारमाटिकिक.

I did not identify which specific Pāṇinian rule licenses ठक् for this particular stem. The form above follows only the general ठक् derivation, which the prompt allows.

<answer>पारमाटिकिक</answer>

The affix is कुणप्, where the final प् is only an it-marker. What remains is the suffix कुण, which is added to ध्रुवा. I could not recall which Pāṇinian rule introduces this affix, so the form rests on the sandhi rule below and is my best reconstruction, not a verified result.

The stem ends in the feminine आ (आप्) and is followed by a suffix whose क is part of the suffix itself. By 7.3.44 (प्रत्ययस्थात्कात्पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः), the आ before that क becomes इ. This gives ध्रुवा → ध्रुवि + कुण.

The derived stem is ध्रुविकुण.

<answer>ध्रुविकुण</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.67, the affix कल्पप् is added to a subanta in the sense "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्तौ). The masculine stem जगुरि takes it without any internal change, since no sandhi or substitution rule applies here. The final प् of the affix is only an indicatory marker, so it leaves no trace in the form.

<answer>जगुरिकल्प</answer>

The affix लच् is applied to the stem योगा. The ending आ is not elided before the affix, because the elision rule (यस्येति च) covers only इ, ई and अ. This gives the stem योगाल. <answer>सावधानत्रा</answer>

This is a best-effort form rather than a fully checked derivation. I am relying on Pāṇini 5.2.37 (मात्रच् in the sense of "measure"), and I could not recall a rule that shortens the final ई or applies a masculine-form substitution (पुंवद्भाव) before this affix. So I add मात्र directly to the stem ज्येष्ठिनी and keep the ई unchanged.

<answer>ज्येष्ठिनीमात्र</answer>
<answer>त्राप्यचर</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), द्वयसच् is added to a nominal stem in the sense of measure. The final च् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix that is actually added is द्वयस.

The stem रिष्ट ends in अ, and द्वयस begins with a consonant. The rule that deletes a stem-final अ before a vowel-initial taddhita affix therefore does not apply, and the two parts simply join.

I am relying on this recalled rule rather than a checked source for this particular stem.

<answer>रिष्टद्वयस</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् (daghnac) is taught in the sense of "measure" (P. 5.2.37). Added to the stem कासा, it gives कासादघ्न. The final ā of the stem stays because दघ्न begins with a consonant, so the stem is not a bha-aṅga here and yasyeti ca (P. 6.4.148) does not delete it. The final च् is only an it-marker, so the stem is कासादघ्न, meaning "as much as a कासा in measure". I derived this from the rules as I recall them and did not check it against a source.

<answer>कासादघ्न</answer>

This derivation is reconstructed from memory, not checked against the grammar. The affix त्रा (trA) is added to a nominal stem and is indeclinable. It begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not dropped. This is the same pattern as देव + त्रा = देवत्रा. Applying it to स्फरित्र gives स्फरित्रत्रा.

<answer>स्फरित्रत्रा</answer>

The stem शचिष्ठा takes the affix इष्ठन्, whose final न् is only a marker, so the ending is -इष्ठ. Before it, the final आ of the stem is dropped (by यस्येति च, or equally by टेः, 6.4.155). This leaves शचिष्ठ्, and adding इष्ठ gives शचिष्ठिष्ठ. I reasoned this out from the rules rather than checking it against a source.

<answer>शचिष्ठिष्ठ</answer>

The stem महोन्माना (feminine, ending in ā) takes the affix तल्. The ल् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the suffix -ता. This is the तल् of "तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ", meaning "the state of being …". The result is a feminine stem ending in -ता.

The final आ of the stem would be dropped by "यस्येति च" only before a taddhita that begins with a vowel or य्. Since -ता begins with a consonant, the आ stays. I did not consider any पुंवद्भाव that might alter the base; this form follows only the reasoning above.

महोन्माना + ता = महोन्मानाता

<answer>महोन्मानाता</answer>

I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses वलच् after this stem, so this derivation rests on how the affix behaves elsewhere. I attached वलच् (stem-final -वल) to माकन्दिका and kept the final आ of the feminine ṭāp. I did this because the elision of final अ by यस्येति च does not apply to आ. The result is the masculine stem माकन्दिकावल.

<answer>माकन्दिकावल</answer>

Taking भट as an a-ending stem, the affix इनि applies in the possessive sense by Pāṇini 5.2.115 (अत इनिठनौ). The final अ of the stem drops before इनि, giving भट + इनि → भटिन्, "one who has soldiers". I did not check whether भट belongs to a specific गण; the derivation rests on the general a-stem rule.

<answer>भटिन्</answer>

I could not tie this stem to the rule that introduces अस्ताति, which normally applies to direction words (पुरस्तात्, अधस्तात्), so this is a mechanical formation. The affix is added to गर्भादि, and the final इ of the stem drops before the vowel-initial affix. That gives गर्भाद् + अस्तात् = गर्भादस्तात्.

<answer>गर्भादस्तात्</answer>

The affix is ञ्यङ् (SLP1 YyaN), with the stem तमि ending in इ. This is a reconstruction from the usual rules for ञित् and the deletion of a final इवर्ण or अवर्ण before a य-initial taddhita; I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses the affix on this stem.

1. The marker ञ् in ञ्यङ् makes it ञित्, which causes vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (तमि → तामि), and the affix is reduced to य.
2. Before this taddhita य, the final इ of the stem is deleted by यस्येति च (6.4.148), giving ताम् + य.
3. The result is the stem ताम्य.

I stopped at the taddhita stem. The feminine ending -ā (ताम्या) would be added only by the later rule यङश्चाप् (4.1.74).

<answer>ताम्य</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् is taught in the sense of measure (प्रमाणे), P. 5.2.37, and is added to the stem to give a form like ऊरुदघ्न. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as *bha* and its final ā is not dropped. The affix then reduces to दघ्न, which gives पनिष्ठा + दघ्न. I did not check this form against a source for this specific stem.

<answer>पनिष्ठादघ्न</answer>

I could not recall the exact sūtra that governs the affix सा‍ति, so this derivation is partly reasoned rather than checked against it.

The affix begins with स्, so it is a सित् affix. By सिति च (1.4.16) the stem before it takes the status of a pada. Since समद्वन् ends in न्, the final न् drops by नलोपः (8.2.7). This gives समद्व + साति.

<answer>समद्वसाति</answer>

Applying ṭhak (ठक्) to पञ्चकावली, the affix is replaced by इक by ठस्येकः (7.3.50). The final ई of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). ṭhak is neither ञित् nor णित्, so there is no ādi-vṛddhi (the first vowel stays short). This gives पञ्चकावल + इक = पञ्चकावलिक. I derived this from the rules rather than from an attested form.

<answer>पञ्चकावलिक</answer>
<answer>सहस्रांशुकल्प</answer>

This is the affix सातिँ, which Pāṇini teaches for something that is subject to the thing named by the stem (5.4.54, तदधीनवचने). The final इ is only a marker (इत्) and drops, leaving the ending सात्. Added to the stem काकाण्डक, it gives an indeclinable form that takes no case endings. I am relying on my memory of the rule here, so the sūtra number is not certain.

<answer>काकाण्डकसात्</answer>

This is the affix बहुच् taught in P. 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु), used in the sense of "slightly deficient" (ईषदसमाप्ति). I am recalling the rule from memory rather than checking it. It is added before the word, as in बहुपटु ("somewhat clever"). So it goes in front of the stem लोकाधिक, giving बहुलोकाधिक.

<answer>बहुलोकाधिक</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् for this stem, so this form follows the general operation of the affix rather than a confirmed sūtra.

The affix खञ् is replaced by ईन (kha → īna). Because it carries the marker ञ्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (प → पा). The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix. This gives पाञ्चाङ्गादिकीन.

<answer>पाञ्चाङ्गादिकीन</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्) and conveys "contemptible, bad", as in याज्ञिकपाशः "a bad sacrificer".

Since पाश begins with a consonant, the final -अ of the stem is not dropped. Adding पाश to धर्मायतनिक therefore gives धर्मायतनिकपाश, meaning roughly "a bad person of the धर्मायतनिक kind".

<answer>धर्मायतनिकपाश</answer>

This answer is a mechanical combination of the given stem and affix. I did not find a specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses थमु after a stem like उरस्य.

The affix थमु loses its marker उ and becomes थम्. It begins with a consonant, and the stem is not an ī/ya-initial case where the final अ would drop, so the stem उरस्य stays intact. Joining the two gives उरस्य + थम् = उरस्यथम्, which is indeclinable.

<answer>उरस्यथम्</answer>

The affix चणप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ). It attaches to a word in the instrumental sense and means "known by that", as in विद्याचण "known by learning". The final प् is only a marker, so the affix that remains is चण. It begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not dropped, and the derived stem is रम्भित + चण. This was formed from memory of the sūtra and its standard examples, not checked against a text.

<answer>रम्भितचण</answer>

The affix कुणप् ends in a marker प्, so it is the affix कुण. I could not recall the exact rule governing it, so this form is built from the general taddhita procedure and I am not certain of it.

1. The stem जाम्बुद्वीपका ends in the feminine suffix आ. Before a taddhita affix this आ is deleted (यस्येति च), leaving जाम्बुद्वीपक.
2. The first vowel of the stem is already जा, which is long, so no further vṛddhi changes it.
3. Adding कुण to जाम्बुद्वीपक gives जाम्बुद्वीपककुण, which ends in अ.

<answer>जाम्बुद्वीपककुण</answer>

The affix अञ् is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (ओ → औ in सो → सौ), and the final अ of सोमात्मक is dropped before the affix's अ. This gives सौमात्मक. I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् here, so this rests on the general ञित् rules.

<answer>सौमात्मक</answer>

The affix इञ् (iY) applies here in the patronymic sense, "descendant of Nāgādhipa", by अत इञ् (4.1.95), which adds it to stems ending in अ.

1. The final अ of नागाधिप is dropped before the affix, giving नागाधिप् + इ.
2. The first vowel takes vṛddhi, but the initial ना already has long ā, so it stays unchanged.
3. The result is the stem नागाधिपि.

<answer>नागाधिपि</answer>

Adding इष्ठन् to दाल follows the standard rule for the superlative: the final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), and the affix's final न् is only a marker and is dropped. This gives दाल्‌ + इष्ठ = दालिष्ठ. I assumed the stem takes the affix as given and did not check whether it qualifies as a guṇavacana (the class of quality words the affix normally attaches to).

<answer>दालिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>चारकावत्</answer>

This is my best reading rather than a fully verified derivation. I take the affix मात्रच् in the sense of measure (Pāṇini 5.2.37, प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः). The stem चतु is feminine but has no feminine suffix, so no gender change applies. The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory marker and drops, leaving मात्र, which is added directly to the stem. I did not apply any pada-related change to the stem before the affix. The result is चतुमात्र.

<answer>चतुमात्र</answer>

I could not identify the exact sūtra that licenses rūpya after वृश्चन, so this form rests on the general pattern rather than a confirmed rule. I assumed the affix attaches directly to the stem, with no vṛddhi, since the affix is marked only with p, and no elision of the final -a, since the affix begins with a consonant (र).

<answer>वृश्चनरूप्य</answer>

The affix ञ्यट् (Yyaw) has two markers that drop away: ञ् and ट्. What remains is the suffix -य. The ञ् marker causes vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so मु becomes मौ. The final -अ of मुस्तक drops before the suffix, which begins with य. This gives मौस्तक्य.

I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् for this stem, so the form is derived from the general rules for ञित् affixes and has not been checked against a source.

<answer>मौस्तक्य</answer>

Here फिञ् is the affix: फ् is replaced by आयन्, and ञ् only marks vṛddhi of the first vowel. The affix therefore becomes आयनि. The first vowel of सारघ is already long आ, so vṛddhi changes nothing. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, giving सारघ + आयनि → सारघायनि. I did not confirm which rule licenses फिञ् after this stem, so the derivation rests on the general affix mechanics.

<answer>सारघायनि</answer>

Here the affix is जाहच्, whose final च् is an indicatory letter (it-marker), so what is added is जाह. I could not recall the Pāṇinian rule that licenses this affix, so this derivation is a reconstruction. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem शक्तिन् keeps pada status. The final न् is therefore dropped (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), which gives शक्ति + जाह = शक्तिजाह.

<answer>शक्तिजाह</answer>
<answer>फुल्तिक</answer>

The affix देश्य (deśya) is added by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), in the sense of "slightly short of being complete". Added to स्नापक, it gives "something like a snāpaka, but not quite one". The affix begins with द, so it does not trigger any stem change, and the form is simply the concatenation.

<answer>स्नापकदेश्य</answer>
<answer>कूर्माङ्गत्व</answer>
<answer>आञ्जीकूलकात्रा</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this is derived from the general rules for the affix.

1. खञ् is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, by 7.1.2).
2. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel: पे → पै.
3. The final आ of the stem is dropped before the taddhita affix (6.4.148).
4. The न of ईन becomes ण after र, with only a vowel in between (8.4.2).

This gives पैर + ईन → पैरीण.

<answer>पैरीण</answer>
<answer>श्मशानिकतर</answer>
<answer>साहनमय</answer>

Here कल्पप् is the suffix taught in "ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः" (5.3.67). It means "almost, not quite complete", and it is added directly to the stem. The base ends in -i and is masculine, so no feminine shortening or other change applies. This gives त्रय्यारुणिकल्प, "almost a Trayyāruṇi".

<answer>त्रय्यारुणिकल्प</answer>

I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule that introduces this affix, so this derivation is partly inferred. Because the affix begins with a vowel and the stem ends in the feminine -ā, I assumed the final -ā of भ्रमरा is dropped (यस्येति च, or पुंवद्भाव before the affix). That gives भ्रमर + जाह, and the final form is भ्रमरजाह.

<answer>भ्रमरजाह</answer>

Applying मयट् to मङ्गलीय, the affix becomes मय (the ट् is only an indicatory letter). The final अ of the stem is dropped before it, and the result is the stem मङ्गलीयमय. I take the sense to be "abundant in that" (तत्प्रकृतवचने मयट्, 5.4.21), which is one of the meanings licensed for this affix.

<answer>मङ्गलीयमय</answer>

I could not place ञ्यट् in a specific Pāṇinian sūtra, so this form is built from the affix's markers alone and is not checked against a source.

1. The final आ of हिंस्रात्मता is dropped before the affix's initial य, by the rule यस्येति च, leaving हिंस्रात्मत्.
2. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so इ in हिंस्र- becomes ऐ, giving हैंस्रात्मत्.
3. Adding ञ्य (the अ of य is dropped again before the feminine ई in the next step) gives हैंस्रात्मत्य.
4. The ट् marker makes the derivative feminine with ङीप् (टिड्ढाणञ्… 4.1.15), so the final stem is हैंस्रात्मत्यी.

The ङीप् step is an assumption. If the affix does not take it, the form would be हैंस्रात्मत्य.

<answer>हैंस्रात्मत्यी</answer>

I could not pin down the governing Pāṇinian rules from memory, so this form is a best guess. I added the affix रूप्य to the feminine stem त्रैकककुभा without changing the stem. No rule I could recall shortens the final ā or drops it, because रूप्य begins with र and not with a vowel or य.

<answer>त्रैकककुभारूप्य</answer>

Following the standard derivation:

1. Before the taddhita affix अञ् (whose ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel), the stem वेगिन् is a bha-stem ending in न्.
2. By 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते), the ṭi part of the stem, इन्, is deleted. This gives वेग्.
3. The exception 6.4.164 (इनण्यनपत्ये) only covers the affix अण्, so it does not block the deletion here.
4. वेग् + अ becomes वेग, and the vṛddhi of ए to ऐ gives वैग.

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् after वेगिन्, so the form rests on the general rules above.

<answer>वैग</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific Aṣṭādhyāyī rule for थमु, since the rules I recall for it (इदमस्थमुः 5.3.24 and किमश्च 5.3.25) apply only to इदम् and किम्. So this answer rests on the general mechanics of the affix. The अनुबन्ध उ drops, leaving the affix as -थम्. Nothing in the stem changes before it, so the result is the stem followed by -थम्, which is an indeclinable.

<answer>सूक्ष्माक्षथम्</answer>

The result is सीमन्तिकातः. It is an indeclinable, formed by adding the affix तसि (5.4.44–45, a fifth-case-sense affix, not the तसिल् of 5.3.7) to the stem. I did not apply the पुंवद्भाव of 6.3.35, because that rule covers only the affixes from तसिल् up to कृत्वसुच्. This तसि falls after that range, so the stem keeps its long ā. I did not check this against a source.

<answer>सीमन्तिकातः</answer>

This is a best-effort answer. I could not recall the exact rule that licenses चरट् after वप्राभिघात, so I formed the derivative from the affix's standard mechanics.

The affix चरट् has a final ट् that is a marker (it), which leaves the operative affix as चर. Because चर begins with a consonant, the final -अ of the stem वप्राभिघात is not elided.

One uncertainty is whether the initial च् also counts as a marker. I kept it as part of the affix, which matches the identifier "caraw". The resulting stem is वप्राभिघातचर.

<answer>वप्राभिघातचर</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them, not a lookup. I could not confirm that आभूका is in the तिकादि list under 4.1.154 (तिकादिभ्यः फिञ्).

1. The affix फिञ् has initial फ्, which is replaced by आयन् (फ्→आयन्, 7.1.2), giving the ending -आयनि.
2. The final -आ of the stem आभूका is dropped before the affix, leaving आभूक्.
3. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel takes वृद्धि. The initial आ is already वृद्धि, so it does not change.
4. Joining the parts gives आभूक् + आयनि = आभूकायनि.

<answer>आभूकायनि</answer>

Adding the affix मयट् (मय, after dropping the indicatory ट्) to फुट gives फुटमय. The stem's final अ is dropped before the affix's initial vowel, and the two अ's merge into one, so the result is a regular a-stem meaning "made of or consisting of फुट".

<answer>फुटमय</answer>
<answer>वृक्षारोपणशः</answer>

The affix matup (मतुप्) is added to the stem मङ्गलावास. By Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः), the म of मतुप् becomes व when the stem ends in or has an upadhā containing अ/आ. मङ्गलावास ends in अ and has आ as its penultimate vowel, so the affix becomes वतुप्. The stem is therefore मङ्गलावासवत्, meaning "having an abode of auspiciousness".

<answer>मङ्गलावासवत्</answer>

I did not identify a specific sūtra for this stem, so this is the general derivation of सरणि with ठक्.

1. The affix ठक् has initial ठ्, which is replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50), and the final क् is an it-marker.
2. Because the affix carries ṭ, it is a ṇit/ṭit-type affix that triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (ādivṛddhi). So स → सा.
3. The stem-final इ is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148).
4. The result is सारण् + इक = सारणिक.

<answer>सारणिक</answer>

Any of the senses of the taddhita affix क (such as smallness or contempt) is acceptable, so I chose the diminutive sense. Adding क to the a-ending neuter stem वातायन gives वातायनक, meaning "a small window", and the stem needs no further change. Since the table asks for the stem without case endings, I give it as वातायनक rather than the neuter nominative वातायनकम्.

<answer>वातायनक</answer>
<answer>ईर्ष्यालुसात्</answer>
<answer>हरणाहरणवत्</answer>

The affix साति (sAti) is taught in Pāṇini 5.4.52 (विभाषा साति कार्त्स्न्ये). It is added to a nominal stem, with no change to the stem, in the sense of totality. Because यत् has a final इत् letter त् only, it does not trigger vṛddhi. The vowel of the base therefore stays as it is, and the resulting stem is च्यावित्य.

The affix is effectively चण, and the final प् is only a marker. It begins with a consonant and is not ṇit or ñit. So the final आ of कर्षणा stays unchanged and there is no vṛddhi. I formed this by analogy with विद्याचणः, so the result is कर्षणा + चण.

The affix त्व (by "bhāve tvatalau", 5.1.119) is added directly to the stem स्वाध्यायन, which ends in the vowel अ. No sandhi or other rule changes the stem. It contains no र, ष or ऋ, so the न does not turn into ण, and the "नस्तद्धिते" rule does not apply because the stem does not end in न्. The result is स्वाध्यायनत्व, meaning "the state of being स्वाध्यायन".

<answer>स्वाध्यायनत्व</answer>
<answer>बहुपट्टन</answer>

I formed this by adding इष्ठन् (the superlative affix, "most …") to लवणोदका. Before इष्ठन्, the final vowel and any consonants after it (the "ṭi" part) are dropped by the rule टेः (6.4.155). Here that final part is the feminine आ, so the stem becomes लवणोदक्. Adding इष्ठ gives लवणोदकिष्ठ. I did not check this against a reference; it follows from my reading of the rule.

<answer>लवणोदकिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>भोजनाच्छादनरूप</answer>
<answer>केवलशः</answer>

I formed this by appending the affix directly to the stem; I did not check that the stem actually fits the rule. The affix रूप्य is taught by Pāṇini 4.3.81 (हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यः), as I recall it, though ऐष्टिक is not obviously a hetu or manuṣya word. Because रूप्य begins with a consonant, the final -अ of the stem is not elided. The affix carries no ञित् or णित् marker, so there is no vṛddhi change either. The stem therefore stays intact and takes the affix.

<answer>ऐष्टिकरूप्य</answer>
<answer>तटाकदघ्न</answer>

Here मतुप् is added to the stem उपादिक, giving उपादिक + मत्.

The rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9) changes the म् of मतुप् to व् only when the stem ends in म, or when its penultimate sound is म, अ or आ. In उपादिक the sound before the final क् is इ, so the rule does not apply and the म stays.

The derived stem is therefore उपादिकमत्.

<answer>उपादिकमत्</answer>

The affix चरट् (5.3.53, "भूतपूर्वे चरट्") is added to the stem as it stands. I did not apply पुंवद्भाव (6.3.35), because आख्या has no masculine form in use and so does not qualify. The final आ therefore stays. I am not fully certain of this reading, since a derivation engine might apply पुंवद्भाव anyway and give पञ्चाब्दाख्यचर.

पञ्चाब्दाख्या + चरट् → पञ्चाब्दाख्याचर

<answer>पञ्चाब्दाख्याचर</answer>
<answer>रागोद्रेकमय</answer>

I did not derive this fully from the Pāṇinian rules. It rests on my recollection that the affix साति (Pāṇini 5.4.52–54) is added directly to a nominal stem and surfaces as सात् (as in अग्निसात्, राजसात्). On that basis, adding it to खादिता gives an indeclinable, and I assumed the stem's final ā stays unchanged.

<answer>खादितासात्</answer>
<answer>वेदाध्यायिरूप</answer>

I could not fully confirm the governing rule from memory, so this answer is a best reconstruction.

The affix देश्य is added under Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), with the sense "slightly short of complete". When the base is a feminine stem ending in a ṅyāp-type suffix, I believe the final long vowel shortens before this affix, so सालका gives सालक. The derivative is then सालक + देश्य = सालकदेश्य, and it takes the feminine ending ā again.

<answer>सालकदेश्या</answer>
<answer>मांसादिचर</answer>
<answer>औपनिषदतः</answer>
<answer>वर्धनीयतम</answer>
<answer>ध्वाङ्क्षस्तात्</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses this affix, so this form comes from the general rules for a खञ् derivation. I derived it as follows.

1. The affix खञ् becomes ईन, since ख is replaced by ईन (ख् → ईन, with ञ् as an it-marker).
2. The stem शालूकिनी is शालूकिन् plus the feminine ई. Before the ई-initial affix ईन, the final ई of the stem is dropped (यस्येति च), leaving शालूकिन्.
3. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. Here the first vowel is already long ā, so शा stays unchanged.
4. I did not apply नस्तद्धिते (dropping the टि of शालूकिन्). That rule precedes यस्येति च, and the later rule counts as not yet applied for it, so शालूकिन् is not treated as न्-final at that stage.
5. The result is शालूकिन + ईन = शालूकिनीन.

<answer>शालूकिनीन</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra for जाहच् with certainty, so this form rests on an assumption about how the affix's markers work.

I took the initial ज् and the final च् as markers (it) that drop away, leaving the operative affix आह. The stem-final अ of साम्प्रयोगिक is then deleted by यस्येति च, and आह is added. This gives साम्प्रयोगिक् + आह = साम्प्रयोगिकाह. If ज् is not a marker in this affix, the result would differ.

<answer>साम्प्रयोगिकाह</answer>
<answer>मेघोदकतर</answer>

Following the rule अत इनिठनौ (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.115), the affix इनि is added after a stem ending in short अ to express "possessing". The final अ of जीव drops before the affix, so जीव + इनि gives जीविन्, meaning "having life".

<answer>जीविन्</answer>

The stem किसलयिता is feminine and ends in the ṭāp suffix. Before the taddhita affix इष्ठन् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ), the final ā is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving किसलयित.

The टि-portion इत is then dropped by टेः (6.4.155), because the base is a भ-stem before इष्ठन्. This leaves किसलय.

Adding the affix gives किसलय + इष्ठ = किसलयिष्ठ.

<answer>किसलयिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>वीजितचण</answer>

Following P. 5.3.69 (prakāravacane jātīyar), jātīyar is added to the stem to express "of that kind." Before jātīyar, P. 6.3.42 (puṃvaj jātīyadeśīyeṣu) makes a feminine stem behave like its masculine counterpart (puṃvat). So the feminine ending -ā of मित्र्या is replaced by the masculine-type base मित्र्य, giving मित्र्य + जातीय. I read मित्र्या as the feminine of मित्र्य, which is my assumption since the table does not say how the stem was formed.

<answer>मित्र्यजातीय</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.4.50 (*kṛbhvastiyoge sampadyakartari ca cviḥ*), the affix cvi is added to कारुण्या when the sense is "becoming what it was not", used with *kṛ*, *bhū* or *as*. The affix cvi is wholly elided, but it still triggers the change of the stem-final vowel. By 7.4.32 (*asya cvau*), the final अ or आ of the stem is replaced by ई. So कारुण्या becomes कारुण्यी, as in कारुण्यीकरोति or कारुण्यी भवति.

<answer>कारुण्यी</answer>

I read ठन् here as the possessive affix taught in "अत इनिठनौ" (5.2.115), which applies after stems ending in short -a. श्रीयाक ends in -a, so the affix is available.

1. ठन् becomes -इक, since ठ् is replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50).
2. The final -अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving श्रीयाक् + इक.
3. The possessive sense carries no ञित् or णित् marker, so there is no vṛddhi.

The result is श्रीयाकिक, meaning "one who has श्रीयाक".

<answer>श्रीयाकिक</answer>

I could not match this stem to the usual context for थमु, which is इदम् → इत्थम् or किम् → कथम्. So I applied the affix directly to the stem कियाह.

The affix थमु drops its marker उ and leaves थम्. It begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not elided, and the two simply join. Since the result is an indeclinable, it takes no case endings.

<answer>कियाहथम्</answer>
<answer>सौमारौद्रेय</answer>

Adding the superlative affix तमप् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, 5.3.55) to the stem भौगक gives भौगकतम. The stem already ends in -a, so no further change applies.

<answer>भौगकतम</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्) adds the affix पाश (with the markers of पाशप्) to a nominal stem to denote something deficient or contemptible. Adding पाश to वोढव्य gives the stem वोढव्यपाश. I recalled the sūtra from memory and did not check it against a text.

<answer>वोढव्यपाश</answer>
<answer>जैनायनि</answer>

Because वैपुल्य ends in -a, I applied the rule "अत इञ्" (4.1.95), which gives an apatya (descendant) derivative. This is my own application of the rule; I did not check it against a source.

1. Add इञ् to वैपुल्य.
2. The final -अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). This gives वैपुल्य् + इ.
3. The affix is ñit, which would trigger vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the initial syllable already has ऐ, so nothing changes.
4. The result is वैपुल्यि.

<answer>वैपुल्यि</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) allows the affix देश्य after a nominal stem to mean "slightly short of complete". Adding it to सील gives the stem सीलदेश्य, "somewhat like सील". The neuter gender of the source stem causes no further change, and I give the stem without a case ending.

<answer>सीलदेश्य</answer>

The affix is *bahuc* (Pāṇini 5.3.68, विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु च). It is added after a subanta in the sense of "slightly less than complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it is placed before the stem as बहु. This is the same pattern as बहुपटुः from पटु. Applied to व्याजाभिप्राय, it gives बहुव्याजाभिप्राय. I formed this from the rule as I recall it, not from a checked source.

<answer>बहुव्याजाभिप्राय</answer>

The affix जातीयर् is added by P. 5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्), meaning "of that kind". I formed it as follows:

1. शर्धस् takes the affix जातीय (the final र् is only an indicatory letter and drops).
2. I treated the stem as a pada before the consonant-initial affix, which is what I recall from the standard handling of ghādi/jātīya forms, though I did not verify this. Its final स् then becomes रु (P. 8.2.66).
3. Before the voiced ज्, the अ + रु sequence gives ओ (P. 6.1.113).

I am not fully certain of step 2, so the alternative unsandhied spelling शर्धस्जातीय cannot be ruled out.

<answer>शर्धोजातीय</answer>

Before the consonant-initial taddhita affix तमप् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ), the stem स्तम्भिन् counts as a pada (स्वादिष्वसर्वनामस्थाने, 1.4.17). Its final न् is therefore dropped (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य, 8.2.7), giving स्तम्भि + तम. Gender does not affect this step.

<answer>स्तम्भितम</answer>
<answer>भुरुण्डकल्प</answer>

I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule behind this input, so this is a mechanical derivation of मूलिकार्थ + ठक्.

1. The affix ठक् is replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50).
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148), giving मूलिकार्थ् + इक.
3. Because ठक् carries the marker क्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (kiti ca, 7.2.118), so मू becomes मौ.

The result is मौलिकार्थिक.

<answer>मौलिकार्थिक</answer>

I recognise this as Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), where the affix चणप् is added in the sense "known by that". The final प् is only a marker and drops. The ण is part of the affix, so the affix is just चण. Since चण begins with a consonant, the final -इ of तरि stays unchanged, and no vṛddhi applies. The result is तरि + चण = तरिचण, meaning "known by the boat" (तरिचणः). I am reasoning from memory of this sūtra rather than checking it, and the feminine source gender doesn't change the stem.

<answer>तरिचण</answer>
<answer>मिच्चकजातीय</answer>

The stem युगला with the affix मयट् gives युगलामय. This is a form I derived by the rules rather than one I checked against a source.

The affix मयट् has an initial म, so it is not a ya-initial or vowel-initial affix. The stem before it is therefore a pada rather than a bha stem, and the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not delete the final ā of युगला. Compare शिलामय, formed from शिला in the same way.

<answer>युगलामय</answer>

I did not trace this to a specific rule for the stem नरिष्टा; I applied the general rule for मतुप् after a stem ending in आ.

1. The stem नरिष्टा ends in the feminine suffix टाप् (आ).
2. Under मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9), the म् of मतुप् becomes व् after a stem ending in आ, as in खट्वावत्.
3. So मत् becomes वत्, giving नरिष्टा + वत्.
4. The stem already ends in a long आ, so the lengthening rule for polysyllabic stems (6.3.119) changes nothing.

<answer>नरिष्टावत्</answer>

I formed this from the affix तसि (the affix usually called तसिल्), which is added after a feminine stem ending in आ. This is my own derivation from memory of the rules, not checked against the sutras, so the choice of rule is uncertain.

1. The stem द्वितीयिका ends in the feminine suffix आ.
2. The affix तसि begins with a consonant (त्), so the stem counts as a pada before it. The feminine आ is therefore kept and not replaced.
3. The affix becomes तस्, and a word ending in तस् is an indeclinable.
4. Final स् becomes a visarga, giving द्वितीयिकातः.

<answer>द्वितीयिकातः</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47, याप्ये पाशप्, and is added to a nominal stem in the sense of "contemptible" or "inferior". The final प् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix that is actually added is पाश. It begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ stays, and no vowel-deletion rule applies. The result is मकरन्दोद्यान + पाश = मकरन्दोद्यानपाश.

<answer>मकरन्दोद्यानपाश</answer>

I applied the affix थमु (Tamu) to the stem थौणेय and did not check this against a source.

In Pāṇini's grammar (5.3.24–25) this affix is taught after इदम् and किम्, giving इत्थम् and कथम्. The given stem is neither of those, so I formed the result by plain affixation, which may not be what the source intended.

The final उ of थमु is only a marker (anubandha) and drops, so the affix that is actually added is थम्. Nothing in थम् triggers vṛddhi or any other change in the stem. Adding थम् to थौणेय gives थौणेयथम्. As a taddhita formation ending in this affix, the result is indeclinable.

<answer>थौणेयथम्</answer>
<answer>ईहार्थिता</answer>

The affix ढक् is added to feminine stems under the rule स्त्रीभ्यो ढक् (4.1.120), which gives a derivative meaning "descendant of". I am not certain this is the exact rule for this stem, so the derivation is a best reading rather than a confirmed one.

1. The affix ढक् becomes एय (ढ् → एय by 7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).
2. The final आ of वार्ष्ट्या is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving वार्ष्ट्य्.
3. The first vowel is already आ, so the vṛddhi (strengthening) of the first syllable changes nothing.
4. Adding एय gives वार्ष्ट्य् + एय = वार्ष्ट्येय.

<answer>वार्ष्ट्येय</answer>
<answer>दृढानुतापदेशीय</answer>

चेटी में तरप् जोड़ने पर, घ-संज्ञक प्रत्यय (तरप्) परे रहने से ङी-अन्त अनेकाच् शब्द का ईकार ह्रस्व हो जाता है (६.३.४३, घरूपकल्पचेलड्ब्रुवगोत्रमतहतेषु ङ्यो ऽनेकाचो ह्रस्वः)। इससे चेटी का चेटि बनता है और चेटि + तर = चेटितर। टाप् जोड़कर स्त्रीलिंग रूप चेटितरा बनता, पर यहाँ प्रातिपदिक माँगा गया है, इसलिए तद्धित-अन्त रूप चेटितर दिया है।

<answer>चेटितर</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that introduces ञ्यट्, so this form comes from the affix's markers alone and is not checked against a rule.

In ञ्यट्, the initial ञ् and final ट् are indicatory letters, leaving the affix -य. The ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, and the stem already begins with long आ, so nothing changes there. The ट् only signals that the feminine takes ङीप्. The final अ of आर्धिक drops before the affix, giving आर्धिक्य.

<answer>आर्धिक्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses यत् after शालूक, so this form is derived from the general rules for adding यत्, not from a confirmed sūtra.

1. The base is शालूक and the affix is यत्, where the final त् is only a marker (it is dropped), leaving the affix as -य.
2. The base ends in short अ. By 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), this अ is dropped before the affix, giving शालूक् + य.
3. The affix यत् is not ñit or ṇit, so no vṛddhi applies to the first syllable.

The result is शालूक्य.

<answer>शालूक्य</answer>

Since the affix त्व begins with a consonant, the final आ of the feminine stem पुष्कला is not dropped (the rule यस्येति च applies only before a vowel-initial affix). The affix is simply added to the stem, as in खट्वात्वम्. I did not find a rule that forces पुंवद्भाव here, so I kept the आ, which gives पुष्कलात्व.

<answer>पुष्कलात्व</answer>

Assuming the affix attaches to this stem as the table states, the form follows from one sandhi step. The affix अस्ताति (astāti) begins with a vowel, and it is a taddhita affix. By Pāṇini 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), the final ई of the feminine stem अच्छूरी is therefore dropped, leaving अच्छूर्. Adding अस्ताति gives अच्छूरस्ताति, which is an indeclinable.

<answer>अच्छूरस्ताति</answer>

Adding the superlative affix तमप् (Pāṇini 5.3.55, अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ) to रोलम्ब leaves the stem unchanged before the suffix, giving रोलम्ब + तम.

<answer>रोलम्बतम</answer>

I could not pin down a specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses valac after वाहक, so this answer rests on the general pattern. Adding the affix वल (the च् is only a marker) to the a-ending stem वाहक gives an a-stem with no sandhi change. I did not apply any vowel lengthening before the affix.

<answer>वाहकवल</answer>

The derivative is formed by adding कन् to the stem अष्टिक. After the इत् letters are removed, कन् leaves the affix क. The stem ends in अ, and क is a consonant-initial affix. For this reason the vowel-initial elision rule (यस्येति च) does not apply, and the stem-final अ stays. The rule that turns -क into -इक before आप् applies only to feminines, so it does not apply here either.

This gives अष्टिक + क = अष्टिकक. I derived this from the general rules and did not identify the specific sūtra the table is based on.

<answer>अष्टिकक</answer>

I formed this by attaching मयट् to करा. The affix begins with a consonant (म्), so the stem's final आ is not dropped. The ट् is only a marker and falls away. I did not look up a specific sūtra for this stem, so the derivation rests on that general rule.

<answer>करामय</answer>

The stem तुम्बर ends in -a, so the affix इनि can apply in the sense of "possessing" (by the rule अत इनिठनौ, 5.2.115). The final -a of the stem drops before the affix, giving तुम्बर् + इन् = तुम्बरिन्, meaning "having tumbara." I applied this rule from memory and did not check any other sense of the stem.

<answer>तुम्बरिन्</answer>

Following P. 5.3.67–68, the affix बहुच् is placed before the subanta in the sense of "slightly, not quite complete." So बहु is prefixed to वातोपसृष्ट. The stem ends in -अ, so the neuter shortening rule changes nothing. No sandhi applies at the junction.

<answer>बहुवातोपसृष्ट</answer>

Taking the neuter stem आनुमाष्य with the affix ठक् (Wak), I derive the form as follows.

1. The initial letters of ठक् are replaced by इक् (Pāṇini 7.3.50, ठस्येकः), so the affix becomes इक.
2. Vṛddhi of the first vowel is required before this affix, but आ- is already vṛddhi, so nothing changes.
3. The final -य of the stem is not dropped. The deletion of taddhita -य after a consonant (6.4.150) applies only before the feminine ई, and no other rule removes it here.
4. Joining the stem and affix gives आनुमाष्य + इक = आनुमाष्यिक.

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठक् after this particular stem, so this derivation follows the general ठक् rules rather than a named rule for आनुमाष्य.

<answer>आनुमाष्यिक</answer>

This form is built on the affix चुञ्चुप्, which Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ) teaches after a word in the third case, meaning "known by that". For example, विद्याचुञ्चुः means "known by learning". The final प् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix that is actually added is चुञ्चु.

The stem मृगेन्द्रोत्तर ends in अ. That vowel drops before the taddhita affix (6.4.148, यस्येति च). Adding चुञ्चु to the remaining base gives the derived stem मृगेन्द्रोत्तरचुञ्चु.

<answer>मृगेन्द्रोत्तरचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>उपिलत्रा</answer>
<answer>दरणीयमय</answer>

Following the rule that matup's m becomes v only after a stem ending in or having penultimate m, a or ā (A.8.2.9), I checked वाणीची. It ends in ई, and its penultimate sound is च्, so the change does not apply. The affix stays मत्, and the derived stem is वाणीचीमत्. This stem is not attested, so I derived it from the rule alone.

<answer>वाणीचीमत्</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (deSIyar) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), with the sense "almost, not quite complete". The final र् is only a marker letter and drops out. The stem धुनान ends in -a, so no further change is needed: it takes -देशीय directly, giving the stem धुनानदेशीय.

<answer>धुनानदेशीय</answer>
<answer>कामठतर</answer>

The affix इञ् (iÑ) is added to a stem ending in अ by अत इञ् (4.1.95), which gives the patronymic sense "descendant of". Because the affix is ñit, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117), so अ becomes आ. The final अ of the stem drops before the इ of the affix.

अश्रूपहत + इ → आश्रूपहति

<answer>आश्रूपहति</answer>

The derivative is formed in three steps, using the rules as I recall them from Pāṇini:

1. The stem सिना takes the affix कन्, giving सिना + क.
2. Before क, the long ā of the stem is shortened by ke 'ṇaḥ (7.4.13), giving सिनक.
3. The feminine suffix टाप् is added, giving सिनका. Since the क is part of a pratyaya and is followed by आप्, the preceding अ becomes इ by pratyayasthāt kāt pūrvasyāta idāpy asupaḥ (7.3.44), giving सिनिका.

<answer>सिनिका</answer>
