<answer>यतितव्यकल्प</answer>

The affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (by आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The stem-final आ is then dropped before this vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च). So अष्टाङ्गा + ईय gives अष्टाङ्ग + ईय = अष्टाङ्गीय.

I derived this from the general rules and did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses छ after this stem.

<answer>अष्टाङ्गीय</answer>

The derived form is द्वैतीयकीतः. This is a derivation by rule from general principles, without checking a source for this exact word.

The affix तसि is added directly to the feminine stem द्वैतीयकी. I know of no rule that shortens or removes the final ई here (6.3.63 shortens it only in names and in Vedic usage), so the ई stays. The result is an indeclinable ending in -तस्, which is written with a final visarga.

<answer>द्वैतीयकीतः</answer>

I could not identify a specific sūtra that applies ञ्यङ् to साम्ब, so this form rests on the general rules for the affix. The only sūtra I could recall for ञ्यङ् is 4.1.171 (कोसलाजादाञ्ञ्यङ्), which covers Kosala and Ajāda, not साम्ब.

1. The affix is ञ्य, with ञ् and ङ् as markers.
2. Because of the marker ञ्, the first vowel of the stem takes ādi-vṛddhi. The initial सा already has long ā, so nothing changes.
3. The final अ of साम्ब is dropped before the affix's ya (6.4.148), giving साम्ब् + य.

<answer>साम्ब्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this form rests on the general rules for the affix rather than a confirmed source.

1. The affix खञ् (KaY) has the marker ञ्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. In श्रयितव्या the first syllable श्र (र् + अ) becomes श्रा.
2. The initial ख् of the affix is replaced by ईन.
3. The final आ of the feminine stem is dropped before the taddhita affix by यस्येति च. This leaves श्रायितव्य्, to which ईन is added.

The result is श्रायितव्य् + ईन = श्रायितव्यीन.

<answer>श्रायितव्यीन</answer>
<answer>सार्थकद्वयस</answer>
<answer>युद्धोपकरणमय</answer>

The affix is तसि(ल्), which has an ablative sense, "from धीराधीरा". The stem ends in the feminine -ā. Before तसिल् and similar affixes, a feminine stem takes the masculine form (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.35). So धीराधीरा becomes धीराधीर. Adding तस् gives धीराधीरतस्, an indeclinable, which is written with a final visarga. I am working from memory of the rule, not from a checked source.

<answer>धीराधीरतः</answer>

I applied the affix द्वयसच् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.37, "प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः", which gives forms like ऊरुद्वयसम्). The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops, leaving द्वयस. This affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of वलितक is not elided under यस्येति च (6.4.148). The stem is therefore वलितक + द्वयस.

<answer>वलितकद्वयस</answer>
<answer>लुप्तोपमानतर</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् is the superlative suffix added by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (5.3.55). Before इष्ठ, the rule टेः (6.4.155, under तुरिष्ठेमेयस्सु) deletes the ṭi of the stem. The ṭi is the last vowel together with any consonants after it. In वल्लरीक it is just the final अ of क. Deleting it leaves वल्लरीक्, and adding इष्ठ gives वल्लरीकिष्ठ.

<answer>वल्लरीकिष्ठ</answer>

Applying the rule अत इनिठनौ (Pāṇini 5.2.115), ṭhan can follow a stem ending in -a to mean "one who possesses…". Here बद्धानन्द ends in -a, and the derived stem means "one who has bound joy".

1. The affix ṭh- is replaced by -ik- (ठ् → इक), so the affix becomes -इक.
2. The final -a of the stem is dropped before the affix.
3. There is no vṛddhi, because ṭhan is not marked ñit or ṇit.

बद्धानन्द + इक → बद्धानन्दिक

<answer>बद्धानन्दिक</answer>

This is a derivation I worked out from the rules, not from a checked example, and the affix-licensing rule is from memory.

The taddhita affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (छ → ईय, by "आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्", Pāṇini 7.1.2). The stem सौपर्वा starts with a vṛddhi vowel (सौ), so छ is licensed by "वृद्धाच्छः" (4.2.114). I am unsure whether that rule applies to a feminine stem in -ā, but I took it as acceptable here.

Before the affix ईय, the final आ of the feminine stem is dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), as in खट्वा + ईय → खट्वीय. This gives सौपर्व + ईय = सौपर्वीय. The initial vowel is already vṛddhi, so it does not change.

<answer>सौपर्वीय</answer>
<answer>उत्तराशिका</answer>

Recalling the rule, I could not pin down the Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses चरट् after करम्भ, so this form is not checked against the sūtra. The formation: the affix चरट् is added to करम्भ, the final अ of the stem is dropped before it, and the ट् is only an indicatory letter. This gives करम्भचर.

<answer>करम्भचर</answer>

I could not tie the affix रूप्य to a specific Pāṇinian rule with certainty, so this form rests on treating रूप्य as a single affix unit added directly to the stem. Because the affix begins with र, it does not trigger loss of the stem's final अ, so the stem नर्तनागार stays intact and the affix is simply appended.

<answer>नर्तनागाररूप्य</answer>

This is a derivation I could not tie to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra, so I only worked out the form mechanically. The affix यत् has only a final इत् ् त्, with no ञ्, ण् or क्, so no vṛddhi or other internal change applies to the base. The final अ of स्थानेश्वर is dropped before the initial य of the affix (यस्येति च). That gives स्थानेश्वर् + य, which is स्थानेश्वर्य.

<answer>स्थानेश्वर्य</answer>

Taking the affix as ञ्यट् (`Yyaw`), the derivation runs as follows:

- The affix has ञ् as an indicatory letter, so the first vowel of the stem would take vṛddhi. Here it is already ऐ in स्फै, so nothing changes.
- The final इ of स्फैजायनि is elided before the affix (यस्येति च). This leaves स्फैजायन्.
- Adding the residual affix य gives स्फैजायन्य.

I did not confirm which sūtra licenses ञ्यट् on this particular stem, so the form rests on applying the affix mechanically.

<answer>स्फैजायन्य</answer>

I applied the affix अण् to मान्यव. The final अ of the stem drops by "yasyeti ca" (6.4.148), and the affix's अ is added. The affix is ञित्/णित्, so it calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. That vowel is already long (मा), so it stays unchanged. The result is spelled the same as the input stem. I did not verify this against a source for this specific stem.

<answer>मान्यव</answer>
<answer>प्रतीषितद्वयस</answer>

Rule 5.2.37 (pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātracaḥ) adds dvayasac to a word to give the sense "measure", as in ūrudvayasam. I did not verify that this rule covers वैतस्त्य itself. The final च् is only an accent marker and drops. The affix द्वयस begins with a consonant, so the elision rule 6.4.148 (yasyeti ca), which needs a following vowel or य, does not apply. The stem's final -य therefore stays, and the derived stem is वैतस्त्य + द्वयस.

<answer>वैतस्त्यद्वयस</answer>
<answer>कण्ठागतवत्</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule for थाल्. Rule 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्) gives the meaning "in the manner of", but it is normally taken after sarvanāmas such as किम्, सर्व and तद्. I therefore simply attached the affix to the stem. The final ल् of थाल् is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving था. The resulting stem रन्ध्र + था gives an indeclinable.

<answer>रन्ध्रथा</answer>

I could not place this stem in the sources I recall for the affix valac. The closest rule I know, Pāṇini 5.2.112 (रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच्), lists other stems, such as रजस् and कृषि. So this form rests on applying the affix mechanically.

The stem कठल्य ends in a short -a. The affix वलच् loses its indicatory ch (and the a stays as the affix's own vowel), leaving -वल. The stem's final -a is dropped before the vowel-initial... in fact the affix begins with a consonant (व), so the stem is simply joined to it, giving कठल्य + वल. The result is कठल्यवल, with no vowel lengthening, since that happens only with stems like कृषि.

<answer>कठल्यवल</answer>

Here the affix तल् is the abstract-noun suffix (Pāṇini 5.1.119, "tasya bhāvastvatalau", meaning "the state of being X"). Adding it to मथ leaves त, since the ल् is only a marker. Words formed with तल् are feminine and take the feminine ending टाप् (आ). This gives मथ + त + आ = मथता.

<answer>मथता</answer>

Here the affix छ (SLP1 Ca) is added to दाक्षिणेय. I did not identify a specific sūtra for this, so the derivation rests on my recollection of the rule वृद्धाच्छः (4.2.114).

1. The stem दाक्षिणेय begins with long आ in its first syllable, so it counts as a vṛddha stem, which is the condition for छ.
2. The affix छ is replaced by ईय (आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्, 7.1.2).
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before ईय (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This gives दाक्षिणेय् + ईय.
4. Joining the two gives दाक्षिणेयीय.

<answer>दाक्षिणेयीय</answer>

I could not fully verify this derivation. The result follows the pattern of पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्, which come from the same affix.

The affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27) is a taddhita that yields an indeclinable, and its output ends in -स्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्. Attached to a stem ending in -इन्, it works as follows:

1. The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem takes the भ-designation (1.4.18).
2. Before a taddhita, the टि (final vowel plus any following consonant) of a stem ending in न् is dropped (6.4.144). So विषयैषिन् loses इन्, leaving विषयैष्.
3. Adding अस्तात् gives विषयैषस्तात्.

I could not identify which specific rule licenses अञ् on this stem. The form follows from the sandhi alone.

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses रूप्य after टङ्गण, so this form is my best construction rather than a verified derivation. The affix begins with a consonant (र्), so the final अ of टङ्गण is not elided, and the affix is simply added to the stem.

The affix मयट् begins with म, not a vowel, so the final अ of पृच्छक is not elided. The affix has a ट् marker but no ञ् or ण् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. Following the standard rule, the affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (छोऽनीयादेशः, via ईय substitution for छ). This is a derivation from Pāṇinian rules recalled from memory, not checked against a source. I take the affix इष्ठन् to be the superlative suffix of "atiśayane tamabiṣṭhanau" (5.3.55).

3. Adding इष्ठ gives सोपचार् + इष्ठ = सोपचारिष्ठ.

The stem आनुनाश्य is neuter and ends in -य. I could not identify the specific rule that licenses ठक् on this stem, so I derived the form from the general mechanics of the affix.

2. The stem already begins with आ, so vowel strengthening (आदिवृद्धि) changes nothing.
3. Before the vowel-initial affix इक, the stem's final अ is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). This gives आनुनाश्य् + इक.
4. Joining the parts gives आनुनाश्यिक.

I did not apply the rule that deletes a final -य of an apatya suffix after a consonant (6.4.151). I treated आनुनाश्य as a basic stem rather than a derived one, so that deletion is not triggered.

Following the table's own premise that थाल् applies to this stem, I attach it directly. I could not match सौमेचक to a specific Pāṇinian rule for थाल्. The usual rule for it, 5.3.23 प्रकारवचने थाल्, applies to pronoun-type stems, which सौमेचक is not.

The final ल् of थाल् is only a marker and drops, leaving the ending -था. Added to the stem सौमेचक (ending in -a), it gives सौमेचक + था = सौमेचकथा, an indeclinable.

<answer>सौमेचकथा</answer>

I formed the derivative by adding the affix कन् directly to the stem बुद्धानुस्मृति. The affix drops its markers (the final न् and the कित् marking) and leaves the suffix -क. The short -ि of the stem is unchanged, so the derived stem is बुद्धानुस्मृतिक. This is my own derivation and I did not check it against the Aṣṭādhyāyī.

<answer>बुद्धानुस्मृतिक</answer>
<answer>तरन्ततम</answer>

The affix तसि (SLP1 `tasi`) is added to the stem लज्जापयितृ. Before this affix the stem has pada status (1.4.17), so the final ऋ takes no guṇa or other change. The result ends in तस्, which as an indeclinable is written with visarga: तः.

<answer>लज्जापयितृतः</answer>

This is a derivation from memory of P. 5.3.68 (*vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*), which I have not checked against the text. The affix बहुच् is added to a subanta in the sense of "slightly, not quite complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is placed before the word, so it appears as the prefix बहु-. Here that gives बहु + कलाम्बिका. I am not certain whether any feminine shortening applies before a bahuc prefix; I assume none does, so the stem stays unchanged.

<answer>बहुकलाम्बिका</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that prescribes ठक् after अहीन्द्र, so this form rests on the general rules for ठक् alone.

1. The affix ठक् has an initial ठ, which is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः, 7.3.50).
2. The ठ marks ṭ-it, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: अ becomes आ (आदिवृद्धि, 7.2.117).
3. The final अ of अहीन्द्र is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148).
4. Combining these gives आहीन्द्र + इक = आहीन्द्रिक.

<answer>आहीन्द्रिक</answer>

Taking कीर्णा as ending in the feminine suffix टाप्, I derived the form by the usual rules for kan after such a stem. I worked this from memory of the Aṣṭādhyāyī rather than checking it against a source.

1. Adding कन् gives कीर्णा + क. By "ke aṇaḥ" (7.4.13), the final long आ before क becomes short, giving कीर्णक.
2. The feminine suffix टाप् is then added, giving कीर्णका.
3. By "pratyayasthāt kāt pūrvasyāta idāpy asupaḥ" (7.3.44), the अ just before the क of the affix becomes इ when आप् follows. So कीर्णका becomes कीर्णिका.

<answer>कीर्णिका</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् is the superlative suffix (atiśayane tamabiṣṭhanau, 5.3.55). Before इष्ठन्, the "ṭi" part of the stem is dropped by ṭeḥ (6.4.155). The "ṭi" is the last vowel together with any consonants after it, which here is the final अ of शैक्ष. Dropping it leaves शैक्ष्, and adding इष्ठ gives शैक्षिष्ठ.

<answer>शैक्षिष्ठ</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् (iṣṭhan) is the superlative suffix of "अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ" (A. 5.3.55). The stem चित्तापहारिन् ends in -इन्. Before a taddhita beginning with a vowel the stem counts as भ (bha), so टि-लोप (A. 6.4.155) and "नस्तद्धिते" (A. 6.4.144) remove the final -इन्.

This leaves चित्तापहार्, and adding इष्ठ gives चित्तापहारिष्ठ.

<answer>चित्तापहारिष्ठ</answer>

Taking "nyap" to mean the feminine suffix ṭāp, the stem उद्ग्रहणिका ends in आ. I added मतुप् (the possessive "having …") to it.

Since the stem ends in आ, the म of मतुप् changes to व by 8.2.9, as in खट्वावत्. The result is उद्ग्रहणिकावत्. I recalled the wording of 8.2.9 from memory and was not fully certain of it, but the pattern खट्वावान् / मालावान् for stems in आ is standard.

<answer>उद्ग्रहणिकावत्</answer>

The affix तरप् (तर) is added to the stem तरिन्. The affix begins with a consonant other than य्, so the stem counts as a pada before it (1.4.17). That makes the final न् drop by 8.2.7, giving तरि + तर. The neuter gender changes nothing here, because the stem's vowel is already short.

<answer>तरितर</answer>
<answer>उद्वत्सरीयचर</answer>
<answer>क्षेत्रियरूप</answer>

बोध्य + ईयसुन् से तरप्-अर्थ वाला रूप बनता है। सुन् का उ और न् इत्संज्ञक होकर हटते हैं, इसलिए प्रत्यय ईयस् बचता है। "टेः" (6.4.155) से अङ्ग के टि-भाग का लोप होता है, और यहाँ टि केवल अन्तिम अ है। इस तरह बोध्य् + ईयस् मिलकर बोध्यीयस् बनता है।

<answer>बोध्यीयस्</answer>

I could not pin this to a specific rule, so the answer rests on the general pattern. The stem is फलिक, and the affix क (ka) is added to it. The stem's final -अ drops before the affix, giving फलिक् + क = फलिकक. The ā→i substitution (7.3.44) applies only to feminine stems in -ā, so it does not apply to this masculine stem.

<answer>फलिकक</answer>
<answer>संकेतितथम्</answer>

Reasoning from the Aṣṭādhyāyī rules as I recall them (not checked against the text):

1. The comparative affix ईयसुन् falls within the range of affixes from तसिल् to कृत्वसुच्. Before these, a feminine stem is treated as masculine (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.35). So नैवारा reverts to नैवार.
2. Before ईयसुन्, the final टि (the last vowel) of the stem is dropped (6.4.155). The final अ of नैवार goes, leaving नैवार्.
3. Adding ईयस् gives नैवारीयस्.

<answer>नैवारीयस्</answer>

I could not identify the exact rule that licenses an affix "rUpya", so this form is a best attempt rather than a confirmed derivation.

I took the affix to be added directly to the stem काण्डीरा. A taddhita beginning with र् does not give the stem the technical status (भ-संज्ञा) that would trigger यस्येति च (6.4.148), the rule that deletes a final आ/अ/ई before such affixes. The final आ of the stem is therefore not deleted, and no shortening rule I know of applies to an आप्-final stem here. The result is the stem followed directly by the affix.

<answer>काण्डीरारूप्य</answer>
<answer>सर्पावासी</answer>

Applying ठक् to लिष्ट, with the usual ठक् operations:

1. The initial ठ् of ठक् is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः), and the final क् is a mere marker, so the affix becomes -इक.
2. The ठक् affix is कित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: इ becomes ऐ, giving लैष्ट-.
3. Adding -इक gives लैष्टिक.

I did not identify a specific sūtra or meaning for this stem, so the choice of ठक् here rests on the task's statement that any licensed meaning is acceptable.

<answer>लैष्टिक</answer>

I took this to be the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26, "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ", which gives forms like विद्याचणः ("known by learning") and केशचणः. I did not verify the rule against a source.

Its marker प् drops, leaving the affix चण. Its initial च stays, as in the traditional examples. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not deleted. The stem पूर्णोत्कट therefore simply takes चण.

<answer>पूर्णोत्कटचण</answer>
<answer>क्रौञ्चार्णदेश्य</answer>

Adding अण् to श्रद्धालु involves two changes:

1. Before a taddhita affix with a ञित्/णित् marker, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (आदेः अचः). The अ in श्र becomes आ, giving श्रा-.
2. A stem-final उ takes guṇa before a taddhita affix (ओर्गुणः), so उ becomes ओ. Before the अ of अण्, ओ becomes अव्.

So श्रद्धालु + अण् gives श्राद्धालव.

<answer>श्राद्धालव</answer>
<answer>माकरन्ददेशीय</answer>

I could not match "rūpya" to a Pāṇinian taddhita rule with this base. The nearest rule, 5.2.120, attaches *yap* to *rūpa*, not "rūpya" to a stem like अल्पेच्छु. So this answer rests on simply adding the affix to the stem, not on a confirmed rule.

The affix begins with the consonant र, so the stem is not treated as a *bha* stem and its final उ does not take guṇa. The stem stays अल्पेच्छु, and the affix is added to it unchanged. Since the feminine form of this adjective is the same as the masculine, the gender input does not alter the stem.

<answer>अल्पेच्छुरूप्य</answer>
<answer>कृतीयस्</answer>

I applied the superlative affix इष्ठन् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, 5.3.55) to the stem कर्मोद्युक्त. Before इष्ठन्, the final टि of the stem is dropped (टेः, 6.4.155). The final अ of -युक्त is the टि, so the stem becomes कर्मोद्युक्त्, which takes इष्ठ and gives कर्मोद्युक्तिष्ठ ("most intent on work"). This follows the standard rules, but I did not check whether 5.3.55 applies to a past-participle stem like this one.

<answer>कर्मोद्युक्तिष्ठ</answer>

I could not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that attaches this affix to दर्शन. I took रूप्य as an affix that is simply appended to the stem. Since it begins with a consonant, nothing is deleted or changed at the junction, so दर्शन + रूप्य gives दर्शनरूप्य.

<answer>दर्शनरूप्य</answer>

The stem is taken as given, श्रवणस्. This is a sketch, not a verified derivation, and I did not check it against a rule or a source.

कन् loses its indicatory न्, leaving the affix क. The stem-final स् stays as स् before क, as in forms like यशस्क and पयस्क. The result is the stem श्रवणस्क.

<answer>श्रवणस्क</answer>
<answer>दक्षिणान्तिकास्तात्</answer>

This is an application of Pāṇini 5.3.27, which adds the affix अस्ताति to a direction-word stem. I did not check whether the stem भूतानद्यतन counts as such a word, so I took the affix as given. The affix surfaces as -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्, because the final -इ is dropped. I assumed this from the familiar form rather than confirming it against a source.

The stem ends in -अ, which is deleted before the vowel-initial affix (6.4.148). So भूतानद्यतन् + अस्तात् gives भूतानद्यतनस्तात्. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>भूतानद्यतनस्तात्</answer>
<answer>रेवतोत्तरतम</answer>

Affix जातीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added to the stem महाह्न. The final ् of the affix is only an indicatory marker (इत्) and drops, leaving जातीय.

Because जातीय begins with a consonant (ज्), the stem keeps its form as a pada. The final अ of महाह्न is therefore not elided, and the two parts simply join.

<answer>महाह्नजातीय</answer>

I treated ठक् as ठ् + अ + क्, so the steps are:

1. ठ् is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः).
2. Because the affix has a कित् marker, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (किति च), so न becomes ना.
3. Before a taddhita affix, the final टि "अन्" of the stem ending in न् is deleted (नस्तद्धिते), leaving नदनिम्.

Combining these gives नादनिमिक.

<answer>नादनिमिक</answer>

The affix चरट् (5.3.53, भूतपूर्वे चरट्) attaches to a complete subanta stem to mean "formerly was such". It is added directly to रौद्राक्षी, giving रौद्राक्षी + चर. I did not apply any shortening of the final ई, since I recall no rule that shortens it before चरट्. This is from memory of the rules, not checked against a source.

<answer>रौद्राक्षीचर</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in A. 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), in the sense "known or famous for that". I am recalling this sūtra from memory rather than checking it.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -ि of the stem is not elided. The marker प् leaves the stem form unchanged, so लवि + चुञ्चु gives लविचुञ्चु.

<answer>लविचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), and it is added to a nominal stem to express something deficient or contemptible. The final प् is only a marker, and no sandhi or other change applies to the stem वासव. Joining वासव with पाश gives the derived stem वासवपाश.

<answer>वासवपाश</answer>

This is the measure suffix दघ्नच् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.37), as in ऊरुदघ्न. I did not check which specific meaning of वाप्य it fits, since any licensed meaning is accepted.

The affix has the indicatory च्, which drops, leaving the added element दघ्न. It begins with a consonant, so the stem is a pada before it and its final अ is not dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). Adding दघ्न to वाप्य gives वाप्यदघ्न.

<answer>वाप्यदघ्न</answer>
<answer>यादवकत्व</answer>

This form comes from memory of the rules, and I could not pin down the exact sūtra number for the shortening step.

The affix देश्य is added to a subanta in the sense "almost, somewhat" (Pāṇini 5.3.67, with कल्पप् and देशीयर्). Before such an affix, a stem ending in the feminine āp-suffix is shortened, so the final -ā of प्रलीनेन्द्रिया becomes -a. This gives प्रलीनेन्द्रिय + देश्य, "somewhat like one whose senses are withdrawn."

If the feminine is wanted, ṭāp could be added afterwards to give प्रलीनेन्द्रियदेश्या. I give the taddhita stem itself.

<answer>प्रलीनेन्द्रियदेश्य</answer>

Following the default rule that ठक् applies in the 4.4 senses (e.g. "he plays with a board"), the derivation runs as follows:

1. The affix ठक् becomes इक by "ṭhasyekaḥ" (7.3.50).
2. The initial vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi because of the ञित्/णित्/कित् effect of the affix: फ → फा.
3. The final अ of फलक is dropped before the affix by "yasyeti ca" (6.4.148).
4. The stem does not end in इक्, इस्, उक् or त्, so the extra क of 7.3.51 does not apply.

फलक + इक → फालकिक

<answer>फालकिक</answer>

The affix is कन् added to the feminine stem सोभया. I derived this from my recollection of the relevant Pāṇinian rules and did not check them against the text.

1. Before the affix क, the stem-final long आ shortens by 7.4.13 (केऽणः), giving सोभय + क = सोभयक.
2. The feminine आप् (टाप्) is then added, giving सोभयका.
3. By 7.3.44 (प्रत्ययस्थात् कात् पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः), the अ before a क that belongs to a suffix becomes इ before आप्, giving सोभयिका.

<answer>सोभयिका</answer>
<answer>वृक्षावासक</answer>

Here the stem शाकिना ends in आ, and the affix मतुप् is added in the sense "having this" (तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्, 5.2.94). By the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9), the म् of मतुप् becomes व् after a stem ending in आ, and शाकिना is not in the यवादि group. This gives शाकिनावत्. I did not weigh the vārttika on शाकी, which shortens the vowel before मतुप्, because it concerns the stem शाकी rather than शाकिना.

<answer>शाकिनावत्</answer>

The affix थाल् has an indicatory ल्, which drops, so what is added is just "था".

The stem भेण्डी ends in a feminine ī. The affix begins with a consonant, so it does not get the bha designation (यचि भम्, 1.4.18). That means यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not delete the ī, and the stem stays unchanged before the affix. The result is भेण्डी + था = भेण्डीथा, an indeclinable, since the affix is a taddhita that takes no case endings.

This follows the general rules for the affix. I did not identify a specific sūtra that licenses थाल् after this particular stem.

<answer>भेण्डीथा</answer>

Taking आरुणी as a stem ending in the feminine suffix ङीप् (आरुण + ङीप्), I attach the affix मयट् to it. The ट् of मयट् is only an indicatory marker and drops, leaving the ending मय.

The affix begins with a consonant (म्), so the stem is not treated as a "bha" stem before it. The final ई of आरुणी is therefore not elided and stays in place. This gives आरुणी + मय = आरुणीमय. I derived this from the general rules rather than from a cited example, so it is the most likely form rather than a confirmed one.

<answer>आरुणीमय</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule that licenses वलच्, so I formed the derivative by the general method for adding the affix.

The affix वलच् leaves the base वल after the markers च् and अ are dropped. The final अ of मुषितक is elided before it (यस्येति च), giving मुषितक् + वल.

The lengthening rule for a final इक् before वल (as in कृषीवल) does not apply, because the stem does not end in an इक् vowel.

<answer>मुषितकवल</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule licensing ṭhak on this stem, so this derivation applies only the general rules for the affix.

1. The affix ठक् (ṭhak) takes the substitute ika (ṭh → ika, 7.3.50). The ṭ and k are indicatory letters and drop out.
2. The final a of the stem वलम्भ is elided before the affix, giving वलम्भ् + इक.
3. Because the affix has an indicatory k, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.118 किति च, with 7.2.117 तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). So व becomes वा.

The result is वालम्भिक.

<answer>वालम्भिक</answer>

The affix मात्रच् is added after the feminine stem भर्त्सना. Because मात्रच् begins with a consonant (म्), the stem-final आ is not elided by the rule that drops stem-final अ/आ before affixes beginning with ई or य. The stem therefore stays intact and takes the affix: भर्त्सना + मात्र = भर्त्सनामात्र. I am giving the bare stem, which would decline as a neuter noun (e.g. भर्त्सनामात्रम्).

<answer>भर्त्सनामात्र</answer>
<answer>वक्रदेशीय</answer>

Here the affix तल् (the "-ness" suffix, in the sense of bhāva) is added to the stem मेधस. तल् leaves the ending -ता, and the derived stem takes the feminine ending -टाप्, giving the stem मेधसता.

<answer>मेधसता</answer>
<answer>महाभिमानक</answer>
<answer>स्नेहकल्प</answer>
<answer>महोदरतः</answer>
<answer>सेचनतर</answer>

The stem गङ्गेश ends in अ. Before the taddhita affix कन्, the कित् marker and the final न् drop as markers, leaving the suffix क. The stem's final अ is elided before it, which gives गङ्गेश् + क = गङ्गेशक. I formed the word by these steps and did not check a specific sūtra, and I did not choose among the meanings (such as the diminutive or the pejorative) that the affix can express.

<answer>गङ्गेशक</answer>

I derived this by applying the rules from memory, and some steps are uncertain, so it is a best-fit answer.

The affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27) is attached to the stem क्षिप्रेषु. I assumed the affix begins with a vowel, so the stem takes the bha designation (1.4.18). The final उ then undergoes guṇa before a taddhita affix (6.4.146 ओर्गुणः), giving क्षिप्रेषो. Then ओ + अ becomes अव्, giving क्षिप्रेषव.

Adding the affix gives क्षिप्रेषवस्ताति. I dropped the final इ so the form ends in त्, as in पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्. I was not certain of the rule that removes that इ, so the ending is the least secure part of this answer.

<answer>क्षिप्रेषवस्तात्</answer>
<answer>ससमय</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule behind this pairing, so this is a plain application of the general taddhita mechanics rather than a verified rule citation.

1. The affix खञ् is ख + ञ्. The ख becomes ईन (by 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The ञ् is only a marker that triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel.
2. The stem's final अ drops before the affix.
3. Vṛddhi of the first vowel turns the क in कल्याण… into का.
4. The न of ईन is not retroflexed, because no ऋ, र or ष precedes it.

This gives काल्याणाभिजनीन.

<answer>काल्याणाभिजनीन</answer>

I did not verify this against Pāṇini's text. The affix मात्रच् (mātrac) is taught for "measure" (प्रमाणे, 5.2.37), as in ऊरुमात्रम्. It begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as *bha* before it. The final ā of ललाटिका therefore stays, and the affix is simply added, with the final च् being only an indicatory letter. This gives ललाटिकामात्र.

<answer>ललाटिकामात्र</answer>

Applying the affix च्वि (cvi) to the stem जङ्गमेतर changes its final अ to ई by the rule अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32). The affix itself disappears, leaving जङ्गमेतरी. The derivative is used with verbs like कृ, भू and अस्, as in जङ्गमेतरीकरोति, "makes something that is not जङ्गमेतर into it".

<answer>जङ्गमेतरी</answer>

The affix चणप् is added by Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), in the sense "known by or famous for that". The final प् is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix चण.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of ताम्राक्ष is not elided by 6.4.148. The stem and affix simply join as ताम्राक्ष + चण = ताम्राक्षचण.

I derived this from the rule and did not check it against an attested example.

<answer>ताम्राक्षचण</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra or the meaning that licenses this affix, so this form is reconstructed from the affix's shape rather than checked against a source.

In कुणप्, the final प् is only an it-marker (for accent), so the affix that is actually added is कुण. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of लान्द्रक is not dropped. The affix carries no marker that would trigger vṛddhi. The result is लान्द्रक + कुण.

<answer>लान्द्रककुण</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), in the sense "known by that". I recalled this from memory and did not check it against a source. Before the taddhita affix, the final आ of the feminine stem इतराङ्गा is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). This leaves इतराङ्ग, and adding चुञ्चु (the प् is only an indicatory letter) gives the stem below.

<answer>इतराङ्गचुञ्चु</answer>

Here is the derivation as I worked it out. The result rests on my own reading of the rules, not on a rule I could pin to this exact input.

1. The affix थाल् is added to the stem लोहिताजा, which already ends in the feminine suffix आ (टाप्).
2. थाल् begins with the consonant थ, so the stem does not take the भ-designation (it counts as a pada). Its final आ therefore stays unchanged.
3. I found no rule that shortens the आ or substitutes the masculine form (पुंवद्भाव) here.
4. A taddhita ending in थाल् gives an indeclinable (अव्यय) word, so no case endings are added.

This gives लोहिताजा + था.

<answer>लोहिताजाथा</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this derivation applies the general mechanics of the affix rather than a particular sūtra.

1. The affix खञ् (KaY) becomes ईन (the initial ख् is replaced by ईन, and ञ् is only a marker).
2. The final आ of the stem नृपेच्छा is dropped before the affix.
3. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, so the ऋ in नृ- becomes आर्.

This gives नार्पेच्छीन.

<answer>नार्पेच्छीन</answer>

This form follows the general pattern for a consonant-initial taddhita added to a feminine stem; I did not locate a specific rule that licenses वलच् after स्वेद्या. The affix वलच् loses its च् and becomes -वल. The stem स्वेद्या ends in the feminine -ā, and this is not dropped before a consonant-initial taddhita, so it is kept. That gives स्वेद्या + वल = स्वेद्यावल.

<answer>स्वेद्यावल</answer>
<answer>हसितदेश्य</answer>

The stem श्रद्धान्विता ends in the feminine suffix -ā. Before the taddhita अण्, this final आ is dropped (यस्येति च). The initial vowel of the stem then takes vṛddhi (तद्धितेष्वचामादेः), so the first अ in श्र becomes आ and gives श्रा-. This yields श्राद्धान्वित, with no change from ṇatva because the intervening letters block it.

<answer>श्राद्धान्वित</answer>
<answer>भूष्णुशः</answer>

The affix मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) takes the final च् as an indicatory marker, so what is added is मात्र. It begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ is not elided by यस्येति च (6.4.148). The stem is simply followed by मात्र, giving मन्त्रणार्हीय + मात्र = मन्त्रणार्हीयमात्र.

<answer>मन्त्रणार्हीयमात्र</answer>

The affix कल्पप् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ, "almost, not quite complete") is added to the stem मरणात्मिका. A stem ending in ā takes no shortening here, so it stays unchanged before the affix. The result is मरणात्मिकाकल्प, with the feminine ending ā added afterwards when the word is used in the feminine. This is my best reconstruction, and I did not confirm every sūtra reference.

<answer>मरणात्मिकाकल्प</answer>

<answer>गृभिका</answer>

The stem रङ्गाङ्गन is a neuter nominal stem. The affix शस् (Sas) is added by P. 5.4.43 (संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायाम्), which gives a distributive sense ("one by one", "each"), as in माषशः "by the māṣa each". So रङ्गाङ्गन plus शस् gives रङ्गाङ्गनशस्, a distributive indeclinable. Its final स् becomes visarga.

I left the न unchanged. The stem is a compound, and the retroflexion rule (8.4.1–2) does not apply across the members of a compound, so the र in the first member does not turn the न in the second member into ण.

<answer>रङ्गाङ्गनशः</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that licenses this affix, so this form rests on the standard operations rather than a confirmed rule.

In जाहच्, the initial ज् and final च् are इत् markers, so the affix that remains is आह. Before this vowel-initial taddhita affix, the final ई of उरी is dropped (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). That gives उर् + आह = उराह.

<answer>उराह</answer>

I could not recall the exact rule that licenses जाहच्, so this form is based on how the affix attaches rather than on a confirmed citation. The affix is added as जाह (the final च् is only a marker). It begins with ज्, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped.

<answer>अङ्गारकितजाह</answer>

I applied the taddhita affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27). I am relying on my recollection that its surface shape is -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्. I was not able to confirm this against the sūtra text.

<answer>दुःखालीढस्तात्</answer>
<answer>जलौकश्चर</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses ञ्यट् on this stem, so this form comes from applying the affix's markers by general Pāṇinian rules. The affix reduces to -य. Its ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, and its ट् marker only matters for feminine formation.

1. Start with the stem हयास्यक.
2. Add -य. The final अ of the stem drops (यस्येति च), giving हयास्यक्् + य.
3. Because of the ञ् marker, the first vowel undergoes vṛddhi: ह → हा.

<answer>हायास्यक्य</answer>

The stem त्रैपुरुषा ends in the feminine -ā. Before a taddhita affix this -ā is deleted by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), which removes a final a, ā, i or ī. That leaves त्रैपुरुष + दघ्न, which joins as त्रैपुरुषदघ्न.

<answer>त्रैपुरुषदघ्न</answer>

थमु loses its final उ (the marker उ is dropped), leaving थम्. Since थम् begins with a consonant, the final अ of कुड्मल stays unchanged. The result is कुड्मल + थम् = कुड्मलथम्. As a taddhita ending that takes no case endings, it is an indeclinable (अव्यय).

<answer>कुड्मलथम्</answer>

The affix ढक् (P. 4.1.119, स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्) is added to a feminine stem to express offspring.

1. ढक् becomes एय by P. 7.1.2 (आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).
2. The final आ of तुलसिका is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (P. 6.4.148), giving तुलसिक् + एय.
3. Because ढक् is a kit affix, the first vowel takes vṛddhi (P. 7.2.118, किति च), so तु becomes तौ.

This gives तौलसिकेय.

<answer>तौलसिकेय</answer>

<answer>कङ्कतदेशीय</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that attaches ठन् to गूर्त, so this answer rests on the general mechanics of the affix rather than a confirmed rule.

The affix ठन् becomes ठ after the final न् is dropped as an indicatory letter. The initial ठ् is replaced by इक (ṭh → ika), giving गूर्त + इक.

Unlike ठञ्, the affix ठन् is not marked ञित् or णित्, so it does not trigger vṛddhi of the first vowel. The long ū in गूर्त therefore stays as it is.

<answer>गूर्तिक</answer>

The affix रूप्य is taught in Pāṇini 4.3.81 (हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यः), where it gives the sense "come from". I could not confirm the rule number and sense from a text, only recall them.

The stem श्रावयितव्या ends in the feminine ā. The affix रूप्य begins with र, which is neither a vowel nor य. The stem is therefore not in the *bha* state, so 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) does not delete its final आ. रूप्य carries no ञित् or णित् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. The stem and affix simply join: श्रावयितव्या + रूप्य → श्रावयितव्यारूप्य.

I assumed the final ā stays on this reasoning and did not check it against a worked example.

<answer>श्रावयितव्यारूप्य</answer>
<answer>अत्यन्तीनता</answer>

<answer>शङ्कितव्यचर</answer>

The affix ईयसुन् (the comparative affix) is added to the stem वैवस्वतीय. Before इष्ठन्, इमनिच् and ईयसुन्, the टि (the last vowel and any consonants after it) of the stem is dropped (Pāṇini 6.4.155). <answer>देवेन्द्राश्रमी</answer>

Under 6.3.36 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः), a feminine stem ending in टाप् takes the masculine form before affixes from तसिल् up to कृत्वसुच्. थमु (5.3.24) falls in that range, so पौतृका reverts to पौतृक. I treated सुरेन्द्रा as an ordinary stem ending in आ and added मतुप्, which reduces to मत् as the nominal stem. Under the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9), as I recall it, the म of मत् becomes व after a stem ending in आ, as in खट्वा → खट्वावत्. This gives सुरेन्द्रा + वत् = सुरेन्द्रावत्, meaning "possessing Surendrā". I did not check the sandhi rule in detail.

<answer>सुरेन्द्रावत्</answer>

I applied the affix अस्ताति (astāti), which yields indeclinables ending in -astāt (as in पुरस्तात्). This is a derivation by the usual rules, not a form I could check against a source. The stem कपि is not a direction word, so the affix's normal condition is not met here, and I formed the word anyway as the task asks.

1. The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem कपि takes the technical name *bha* under the rule यचि भम् (1.4.18).
2. Because it is a *bha* stem, the final इ of कपि is dropped before the affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This leaves कप्.
3. Adding the affix, which surfaces as -अस्तात्, gives कपस्तात्.

<answer>कपस्तात्</answer>

The affix खञ् (KaY) is replaced by its substitute ईन by the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम् (7.1.2), since ख् at the start of a affix becomes ईन. I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् after शार्मण, so the choice of affix rests on the table and the form is not checked against a rule.

1. The stem is शार्मण, which ends in अ and already has आ as its first vowel.
2. The final अ of the stem drops before the vowel-initial affix, giving शार्मण् + ईन.
3. The ञित् marker would cause vṛddhi of the first vowel, but it is already आ, so nothing changes.
4. Joining the two gives शार्मणीन, and the ण already present needs no change.

<answer>शार्मणीन</answer>

Applying यत् (प्रत्यय `य`) to the stem gives the form below. This is a reasoned derivation; I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses यत् for this particular stem.

1. The stem अच्छिद्रोति ends in इ, and the affix `य` begins with a य्, so the stem is treated as a भ-stem before it.
2. By यस्येति च (6.4.148), the final इ of the stem is deleted, leaving अच्छिद्रोत्.
3. Adding `य` gives अच्छिद्रोत्य.

<answer>अच्छिद्रोत्य</answer>

The affix अस्ताति (astAti) is added by Pāṇini 5.3.27. It is normally taken after direction words, as in पुरस्तात्, so जातायन is not its usual base. I formed the derivative anyway because the task accepts any licensed use. The final ति of the affix drops, leaving the ending -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्. The final अ of जातायन is also dropped before the vowel-initial affix, by 6.4.148. This gives जातायन् + अस्तात् = जातायनस्तात्. I reasoned the dropping of ति from the known form पुरस्तात् rather than from a rule I could confirm.

<answer>जातायनस्तात्</answer>

I formed this by attaching मयट् (the ṭit marks the feminine ending ई) to the stem as it stands. I did not check this against the Aṣṭādhyāyī rules and am working from memory of how मयट् behaves. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final ā is not dropped before it. That gives the masculine/neuter stem गलनामय, with feminine गलनामयी.

<answer>गलनामय</answer>

Adding the taddhita affix कन् (kan) to मित्रयु gives मित्रयु + क. The final उ is not an इवर्ण or अवर्ण, so it is not deleted by "यस्येति च". The affix's न् is only an indicatory letter and drops out. The result is the masculine stem मित्रयुक. This is the standard derivation, which I did not check against any specific sūtra.

<answer>मित्रयुक</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses ञ्यट् on this stem, so this form is derived from the affix's markers and not checked against a source.

1. The final ई of चपेटी is dropped before the affix, by "यस्येति च".
2. The ञ् in ञ्यट् is a marker that calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, so च becomes चा.
3. The ट् is also only a marker. It would add a feminine ङीप् if a feminine were formed, but I give the base derivative.
4. The remaining affix is -य, which gives चापेट्य.

<answer>चापेट्य</answer>
<answer>वापुष्यि</answer>
<answer>यन्त्रारूढिक</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), the affix कल्पप् is added to a nominal stem to mean "slightly short of complete", that is, "almost". Adding कल्प to चित्तापहारक gives चित्तापहारककल्प, "almost a heart-stealer". The affix is marked with प्, so the word takes no accent change that affects the written form, and it stays masculine.

<answer>चित्तापहारककल्प</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप् after विमुद, so this derivation is a best reconstruction rather than a confirmed one. The stem विमुद ends in -अ, and कुण begins with a consonant, so the elision of final अ (यस्येति च, 6.4.148) does not apply. The पित् marker (the प् in कुणप्) causes no vṛddhi. The stem and the affix therefore simply join.

<answer>विमुदकुण</answer>

This is a construction from the affix rules, not an attested word. Tamu (थमु) is the affix of इत्थम् and कथम्, normally added to इदम् and किम्. After dropping the marker उ, the affix is थम्.

The stem श्रविष्ठीय ends in -अ, and थम् begins with a consonant. No vowel or stem-final change applies, so the affix is simply added. The result is an indeclinable, so no case ending follows.

<answer>श्रविष्ठीयथम्</answer>
<answer>सुखार्ततर</answer>
<answer>रूढस्तात्</answer>

Starting from the feminine stem नारसिंही, the affix मयट् is added without changing the stem, because the affix begins with म. The ई is therefore not dropped, since the "yaci bham" condition (affix beginning with य or a vowel) does not apply. This gives the stem नारसिंहीमय, for example in the sense "abundant in Nārasiṃhī" (तत्प्रकृतवचने मयट्).

<answer>नारसिंहीमय</answer>

I derived this by applying the rules from memory, so the result is not checked against a source.

The affix वलच् is added to the stem कर्पासकी. The final ī of the stem is kept: the elision rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) applies only before affixes that begin with a vowel, and वलच् begins with the consonant व. After the indicatory letters च् and the initial ल्-sound marker are dropped, the affix is वल. Adding it gives कर्पासकी + वल.

<answer>कर्पासकीवल</answer>

The affix बहुच् (अष्टाध्यायी 5.3.68, in the sense of "somewhat, almost") is placed before the word. It therefore gives बहु + कङ्कणी, meaning "somewhat a कङ्कणी". The rule that shortens a stem-final ई (6.3.43) lists घ, रूपप्, कल्पप् and similar affixes, but not बहुच्. Because बहुच् stands before the stem, the stem is also not modified. कङ्कणी keeps its long ई.

I worked this out from memory of the rules rather than from a source, so the treatment of the final ई is the part I am least sure of.

<answer>बहुकङ्कणी</answer>

I did not match this stem to a specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यङ् here. So I formed the word from the general rules for the affix.

1. The affix ञ्यङ् reduces to the suffix -य. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, and the ङ् marker makes the stem take bha-status.
2. The first vowel of मानीन्ध is already आ, so vṛddhi changes nothing.
3. The final -अ of the stem is deleted by यस्येति च, giving मानीन्ध् + य.
4. Joining the two gives मानीन्ध्य.

<answer>मानीन्ध्य</answer>
<answer>और्मिलेयतर</answer>

I could not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses त्रा after क्रीड, so this is a plain concatenation of the stem and the affix. I did not verify the form against a rule or a source.

<answer>क्रीडत्रा</answer>

This is the affix मात्रच् of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which denotes extent or measure. The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops, leaving the ending -मात्र. It begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of रमल is not elided (6.4.148 does not apply). The derived stem is therefore रमल + मात्र.

<answer>रमलमात्र</answer>

The affix बहुच् (Pāṇini 5.3.69, *vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāttu*) is placed before a subanta word to express "slightly deficient" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It therefore works as a prefix, so बहु- is put before करालम्ब, giving बहुकरालम्ब. This relies on my recollection of the rule; I have not checked it against a text.

<answer>बहुकरालम्ब</answer>
<answer>कौप्येय</answer>

Here बहुच् (Pāṇini 5.3.68, "विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु") is placed before the base and conveys "slightly short of complete". Prefixing बहु to the stem पराञ्चिन् gives बहुपराञ्चिन्. I did not check this against a source, and I assumed the neuter shortening rule (1.2.47) has no visible effect because the stem ends in a consonant.

<answer>बहुपराञ्चिन्</answer>
<answer>राव्य</answer>

I treated भल्लात as an ordinary neuter nominal stem (the marking-nut) and added इष्ठन् in its comparative-superlative sense (अतिशायने). The affix is इष्ठ, since the final न् is only a marker.

Before इष्ठ the stem is a भ-संज्ञा stem, so its final अ drops by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). That gives भल्लात् + इष्ठ = भल्लातिष्ठ.

I did not check whether this word is actually attested; the form follows from applying the rules to the stem as given.

<answer>भल्लातिष्ठ</answer>

The stem बन्धुकिन् takes the affix जातीयर् (P.5.3.69, in the sense of "a kind of"). Because जातीय begins with a consonant, the stem counts as a pada before it. Its final न् is therefore dropped by P.8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य). The final र् of the affix is only a marker and does not remain. The neuter gender of the source does not change the result.

This gives बन्धुकि + जातीय = बन्धुकिजातीय.

<answer>बन्धुकिजातीय</answer>

This is a derivation by rule, not a recalled attested form. I could not identify the specific sūtra that gives KaY after भारय, so I derived the result from the general affix rules.

1. The affix खञ् has ख as its first sound. By 7.1.2 (आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्), ख is replaced by ईन्. The ञ् is only a marker, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel.
2. The first vowel of भारय is already long ā, so vṛddhi changes nothing.
3. The final अ of भारय is dropped before the affix by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), which gives भारय् + ईन.

Joining the two parts gives भारयीन.

<answer>भारयीन</answer>

I could not fully confirm whether the final -इ of अस्ताति survives in the output, so this form is partly from memory. In attested words built with this affix, such as पुरस्तात्, अधस्तात् and अवस्तात्, the result ends in -स्तात्. I followed that pattern.

The affix अस्ताति (5.3.27) is normally added to direction words, so attaching it to खेदयितव्य is only a mechanical application.

Because the affix begins with a vowel, the stem-final अ of खेदयितव्य is dropped before it. This gives खेदयितव्य्+अस्तात्, and the combined indeclinable is खेदयितव्यस्तात्.

<answer>खेदयितव्यस्तात्</answer>

Because the affix थाल् takes the indicatory ल्, only "था" is added to the stem. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of रोहितेय is not dropped. The affix is also not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi. The result is an indeclinable (taddhita-ending avyaya), so no case endings are added.

<answer>रोहितेयथा</answer>

I derived this by applying the affix to the stem as it stands, without checking it against a source. The affix दघ्नच् is taught in the sense of "measure" (प्रमाणे, Pāṇini 5.2.37), as in ऊरुदघ्नम्, "reaching up to the thigh". I know of no rule that shortens the final आ of कञ्चिका before this affix, so the stem is kept whole. The final अ of the affix is added after the stem, and the result takes neuter endings.

<answer>कञ्चिकादघ्नम्</answer>

Applying the affix त्रा (taken here as the one given by the rule for देव-, मनुष्य-, पुरुष-type stems) to मुकुलित needs no change to the stem. The result is simply the stem followed by the affix, and it is an indeclinable. I did not check that this rule actually covers मुकुलित, so the form rests on that assumption.

<answer>मुकुलितत्रा</answer>

I could not identify the base stem चविका with certainty, so I formed the derivative by the general rule for this affix.

The affix चणप् (caṇap) is the one taught in the rule "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ" (Pāṇini 5.2.26, "known by that"). Its final प् is only a marker and drops, leaving the actual affix चण (caṇa).

The affix begins with a consonant other than य, so the stem keeps its pada status before it. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148), which would delete a final vowel of the stem, applies only before an affix beginning with a vowel or य. So the final आ of चविका stays and चण is added directly.

चविका + चण → चविकाचण

<answer>चविकाचण</answer>

This is a mechanical derivation. The input मनुष्येषु looks like a locative plural, but the table says to treat it as a basic stem ending in short उ.

The affix मतुप् becomes -मत्, since उ and प् are markers. The change of म to व under 8.2.9–10 does not apply here. That rule needs a stem ending in म, अ or आ, or with one of those as the penultimate vowel, or a stem ending in a झय् consonant. This stem ends in उ and its penultimate sound is ष्, so -मत् stays as it is.

The derived stem is मनुष्येषु + मत् = मनुष्येषुमत्.

<answer>मनुष्येषुमत्</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप्, so this form is derived from the affix's markers alone and is not confirmed against a source.

- In कुणप्, the final प् is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, as does the ण् that marks vṛddhi (ṇit). That leaves the operative affix कुण.
- The ṇit marker calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. In नादेय the first vowel is already long (ना), so nothing changes.
- The affix कुण begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not deleted by the rule on stem-final अ before a vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च).

Joining the stem and the affix gives नादेयकुण.

<answer>नादेयकुण</answer>

This follows Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ). The affix चुञ्चुप् is added to a nominal stem in the sense "known by that". The final प् is only a marker (it governs accent) and does not appear in the form, so the affix that is added is चुञ्चु. Nothing in the stem ओजायित changes before it, because the affix begins with a consonant. The result is ओजायितचुञ्चु. I did not check this against a worked example for this particular stem; the formation follows the general rule.

<answer>ओजायितचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्) and is added to a nominal stem to express something despicable or barely tolerable. Here it attaches to वरी, giving वरीपाश.

I believe the long ई stays. The shortening rule for stems ending in a feminine suffix before certain taddhita affixes (6.3.42) lists घ, रूपप्, कल्पप्, चेलट्, ब्रुव, गोत्र, मत and हत, and पाशप् is not among them. I am working from memory here, so this is not fully verified.

<answer>वरीपाश</answer>

Applying the affix थमु (Tamu) to the stem युध्यामधि is a mechanical formation. The उ in थमु is only a marker and drops, so the affix is added as थम्. Nothing in the stem changes before the consonant-initial थ, which gives an indeclinable form. I did not trace a sūtra that licenses the affix on this particular stem, so the form follows from the generic rule of affixation.

<answer>युध्यामधिथम्</answer>

The affix मात्रच् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.37, in the sense of "measure") leaves the stem मात्र after the इत् letter च् drops. I assumed no rule removes or shortens the feminine ending आ before this affix, so the base माध्या stays whole and the two parts simply join. This is a reasoned choice rather than something I checked against a source. The derivative means "as much as माध्या" and is a neuter stem.

<answer>माध्यामात्र</answer>

The affix मात्रच् (P. 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to मकरन्द without changing the stem. The result is मकरन्दमात्र, meaning "as much as the nectar" or "of the extent of nectar".

<answer>मकरन्दमात्र</answer>

Without the full derivation, I am not certain of this form, because I could not pin down which rule produces the affix रूप्य. I took रूप्य as an affix added to the stem विलिस्तेङ्गा. The affix begins with a consonant (र), so no vowel sandhi occurs with the stem's final आ. I also judged that the rule shortening a feminine final vowel before certain affixes (6.3.43) does not apply, since it names रूप, not रूप्य. The stem therefore keeps its आ.

<answer>विलिस्तेङ्गारूप्य</answer>

I did not trace the affix to a specific rule with certainty. I took it to be the taddhita *rūpya* (probably Pāṇini 4.3.81, "from that, come from"), and I assumed that a feminine stem in -ā may take it.

*rūpya* begins with a consonant, so the stem does not take the "bha" status that would trigger puṃvadbhāva or elision of its final -ā. The -ā of समानोदर्का therefore stays, and the affix is simply joined to it.

समानोदर्का + रूप्य → समानोदर्कारूप्य

<answer>समानोदर्कारूप्य</answer>

Taking this as the possessive sense ("having साक्तुसैन्धव"), the affix is added by Pāṇini 5.2.115, *ata iniṭhanau*. This rule adds इनि (or ठन्) to stems ending in short अ. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, which gives साक्तुसैन्धविन्. I chose this rule from memory of the grammar rather than from anything in the table, so the meaning assumed is my own pick among those licensed.

<answer>साक्तुसैन्धविन्</answer>

I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule that introduces जाहच्, so this form is a best reconstruction.

The affix जाहच् is added to the stem वृन्दारा, which ends in the feminine suffix -ā. I assumed the final -ā is replaced by the masculine-type base (puṃvad treatment) or shortened, as happens before similar affixes such as जातीयर्. That gives the base वृन्दार. Adding the affix जाह (the चित्-marker is dropped) gives वृन्दारजाह.

<answer>वृन्दारजाह</answer>

This derivation is reconstructed rather than tied to a specific rule, since I could not identify which sūtra licenses यत् on प्राजापत. Adding the affix gives प्राजापत + य. Before the affix, the final अ of the stem is dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), leaving प्राजापत् + य. The affix यत् carries no ṇit or ñit marker, so no further vṛddhi applies, and the stem's initial आ is already long. The result is प्राजापत्य.

<answer>प्राजापत्य</answer>

I applied the affix शस् (5.4.42–43, in the sense of "many" or "each") directly to the stem. This is a quick derivation and I did not check the stem's fit against the rules in detail.

1. The affix keeps its initial श्, because the rule that makes an initial श् an indicatory letter (it-marker) does not apply to taddhita affixes. The stem and affix combine as प्राहुणी + शस्.
2. शस् does not begin with a vowel or य, so the preceding stem is not treated as a *bha* stem. The stem's final ई is therefore kept (no *yasyeti ca* deletion).
3. The result is an indeclinable (avyaya), so no case ending is added, and the final स् becomes visarga.

<answer>प्राहुणीशः</answer>

I could not recall with certainty how rules on shortening a feminine stem apply here, so this form is reasoned rather than fully checked. The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It means "somewhat" or "nearly" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it is placed before the inflected word, not after it. So the stem मनिता stays unchanged and बहु- is added in front.

<answer>बहुमनिता</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), where याप्य means "contemptible" or "barely tolerable". It is added directly to the stem युगलाक्ष. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem is not elided. The result is the masculine stem युगलाक्षपाश, "a contemptible युगलाक्ष".

<answer>युगलाक्षपाश</answer>

Applying the affix क (ka) to the feminine stem आटा, the steps are:

1. Before क, the long आ of the stem is shortened by 7.4.13 (केऽणः), giving आटक.
2. The feminine suffix टाप् is added again, giving आटका.
3. Under 7.3.44 (प्रत्ययस्थात्कात्पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः), the अ before this pratyaya-क becomes इ when आप् follows, giving आटिका.

<answer>आटिका</answer>

I could not identify with certainty which Pāṇinian rule the affix रूप्य comes from. I assumed it works like the praise suffix रूपप् (5.3.66, as in विद्वद्रूपः), which is added to the whole word and means "a praiseworthy such-and-such".

On that assumption, रूप्य is attached directly to ब्राह्मणिक. The affix begins with र, so it does not trigger the usual deletion of the stem's final अ. The stem therefore stays whole and the result is ब्राह्मणिकरूप्य.

The form below follows the standard derivation, but I did not locate a specific rule or attested example for this exact combination.

The affix शस् (Sas) is a taddhita that makes indeclinables, as in बहुशः. Its initial श is not an it-marker, because 1.3.8 (लशक्वतद्धिते) exempts taddhita affixes. The affix therefore stays whole as -शस्.

The stem दैहिकी does not lose its final ई. The deletion of a final vowel before a taddhita (यस्येति च) applies only to a stem that counts as bha-aṅga, and this stem does not qualify. शस् does not begin with a vowel or with य, which are the conditions for bha status. So दैहिकी + शस् gives दैहिकीशस्.

The resulting word is an indeclinable, so any case ending is dropped. The final स् becomes visarga at the end of the word, giving दैहिकीशः.

<answer>दैहिकीशः</answer>

The affix begins with a consonant, so it does not trigger the elision of the stem's final -अ (यस्येति च needs a vowel or य beginning). It is also not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi. The stem वैष्वक्सेन्य therefore stays unchanged and takes -दघ्न directly. I derived this from the rules rather than from an attested example.

The affix begins with a consonant and carries no ṇit or ṅit marker. The stem therefore keeps its final अ and takes no vṛddhi, and nothing is elided at the joining point. This gives आनुशातिक + द्वयस = आनुशातिकद्वयस.

I could not recall the sūtra that licenses कुणप् here, so this form comes from applying the general taddhita rules to the stem, not from the sūtra itself.

1. The affix ईयसुन् leaves the base ending in ईयस्, since the markers उ and न् drop.
2. Before ईयसुन्, the final vowel with any following consonant of the base is dropped by the rule टेः (6.4.155). Here the final vowel इ of विनोक्ति is lost, giving विनोक्त्.
3. Joining विनोक्त् with ईयस् gives विनोक्तीयस्.
4. The stem ends in a basic feminine -i, not in a feminine suffix such as ङीप्. So पुंवद्भाव does not apply, and the base keeps its form.

<answer>विनोक्तीयस्</answer>

The affix is *rūpap* (Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṁsāyāṃ rūpap*), which is added to a nominal stem to express praise. It gives *yojayitṛrūpa*, meaning "an excellent yojayitṛ". This is the same pattern as *vaiyākaraṇarūpa*, "an excellent grammarian".

The stem keeps its final ṛ because the affix's *p* is only a marker and causes no vṛddhi or other change. The affix begins with *r*, so the base does not take the *bha* treatment and nothing else changes. The result is a masculine stem ending in -a.

<answer>योजयितृरूप</answer>

Applying the aṇ affix to सोपन्यास involves two steps:

1. Aṇ triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (ādyaci vṛddhi). The vowel ओ in सो becomes औ, giving सौपन्यास.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix's अ, so the stem ends in a single अ.

I did not pin down which sūtra and meaning apply here, for instance "this belongs to it" (तस्येदम्). Any meaning licensed for aṇ gives the same form.

<answer>सौपन्यास</answer>

I did not trace a rule specifically for प्रतीताश्व with this affix, so this form is built from the affix's general behaviour. I take चणप् to be the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), meaning "known by that". Its final प् is only an indicatory marker and drops. The ण is part of the affix, so it does not trigger vṛddhi. The affix therefore appears as चण and is added directly to the stem, as in विद्याचण.

प्रतीताश्व + चण → प्रतीताश्वचण

<answer>प्रतीताश्वचण</answer>

I derived this by applying Pāṇini's rules from memory, without checking them against a source, so the choice between the two candidate forms is not certain.

The affix क is a taddhita whose initial क् is an indicatory letter, so what attaches is effectively just अ. Because it begins with a vowel, the stem नागिन् counts as a "bha" stem (P. 1.4.18). Rule 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते) then deletes the final इन् ("ṭi") of the stem, leaving नाग्. Adding क gives नागक. The competing form नागिनक would keep the final -in.

<answer>नागक</answer>

This is a mechanical derivation, since I did not identify the specific rule licensing यत् after this stem. The stem काश्मीरिक ends in short अ. The affix यत् leaves य after the indicatory letters drop. Before य, the final अ of the stem is dropped (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), giving काश्मीरिक् + य. The vowel of the first syllable is already long, so no further vṛddhi applies.

<answer>काश्मीरिक्य</answer>

This is a derivation from the rule at Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.24, which lists कुणप् among the affixes. I could not confirm that this affix is licensed after ध्वजोत्थापन, so I assumed it. The task says any licensed meaning is acceptable.

1. The final अ of ध्वजोत्थापन is dropped before the taddhita affix (6.4.148), giving ध्वजोत्थापन् + कुण.
2. The p of कुणप् is only an indicatory letter. It causes no vṛddhi and no other change to the stem.
3. The stem has no ऋ, र् or ष् before the न, so it does not become ण.
4. Joining the two parts gives ध्वजोत्थापनकुण.

<answer>ध्वजोत्थापनकुण</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् (cuYcup) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, *तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ*, with the sense "known by that" (e.g. विद्याचुञ्चुः). I did not derive the form rule by rule. I am assuming the affix attaches directly after the ङीप्-ending stem जैवी, with no change to the stem. The final प् of the affix is only an accent marker and drops out, leaving the stem जैवी + चुञ्चु.

<answer>जैवीचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix मयट् is added to the stem कौसुमायुध. The final अ of the stem stays, because मय begins with a consonant and so does not trigger the elision of a stem-final अ (यस्येति च). The ट् is only an indicatory letter (it gives the feminine in ङीप्) and does not appear in the masculine stem.

<answer>कौसुमायुधमय</answer>

I applied the affix mechanically to the given stem. The stem कङ्कणा is not a direction word, so this goes beyond the usual scope of the affix, but the prompt allows any licensed meaning.

1. The affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27) yields indeclinables such as पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्, so its final इ is not retained. The affix therefore behaves as -अस्तात्.
2. The final आ of the stem कङ्कणा is elided before a vowel-initial taddhita affix (6.4.148, यस्येति च). This leaves कङ्कण्.
3. Joining कङ्कण् with अस्तात् gives कङ्कणस्तात्, an indeclinable.

<answer>कङ्कणस्तात्</answer>

This is a formation with देशीयर् (P. 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which means "almost, not quite" the thing named. The affix attaches directly to the stem मल्लिका, and the final र् is only an indicatory letter, so it drops. This gives मल्लिका + देशीय = मल्लिकादेशीय.

I did not shorten the final ā. The shortening rule P. 6.3.43 applies only to stems ending in the ṅī suffix, and देशीयर् is not among the items it lists. I also did not apply masculine-form substitution (puṃvadbhāva). I am not confident that मल्लिका counts as a word that is also used in the masculine for the same meaning, which that rule requires.

<answer>मल्लिकादेशीय</answer>

Here बहुच् is the prefixed affix of P. 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is used in the sense of "nearly, not quite" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it is placed before the base. The stem डाहलाधीश therefore becomes बहुडाहलाधीश, "almost a lord of Dāhala".

<answer>बहुडाहलाधीश</answer>
<answer>वारीयसेय</answer>

I could not match थमु (Tamu) to a rule that applies to ग्रहण, so this form is a mechanical application of the affix. The affix is taught only after इदम् and किम् (as in इत्थम्, कथम्). Here it is simply attached to the stem as given.

The final उ of थमु is an anubandha (indicatory letter) and drops, leaving थम्. Nothing in the affix triggers vṛddhi or any other change in the stem. Adding थम् to ग्रहण gives ग्रहणथम्, which counts as an indeclinable (avyaya) because it is a taddhita form that takes no case endings.

<answer>ग्रहणथम्</answer>

I did not find any special rule that alters this combination. Adding तरप् (the comparative suffix) to the masculine stem धियायु gives धियायुतर. The stem ends in उ, and उ followed by त involves no sandhi change.

<answer>धियायुतर</answer>

The stem शाक्वर ends in अ, so मतुप् takes the form वत् by मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9), as in वृक्षवान्. The stem is not in the यवादि exception list. I applied the rule from memory, and my recollection of its exact wording is slightly uncertain, but the outcome for an अ-ending stem matches the standard examples.

Adding the affix gives the stem शाक्वरवत्.

<answer>शाक्वरवत्</answer>

I could not match the affix रूप्य to a specific Pāṇinian rule. Pāṇini's nearby affixes are रूपप् (5.3.66) and यप् after रूप (5.2.120). I therefore simply attached the affix to the stem, with no sandhi change and no vṛddhi, and I did not verify this against a rule.

<answer>ज्ञप्तरूप्य</answer>
<answer>समानोदर्यक</answer>

Applying khañ (KaY) to the stem महास्पदा gives माहास्पदीन. I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses khañ after this stem. I took the affix as given and derived the form mechanically.

1. The affix खञ् has ख् as its operative part and ञ् as an indicatory letter.
2. Because ञ् marks the affix as ñit, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. The अ of म becomes आ, giving माहास्पदा.
3. The initial ख् of the affix is replaced by ईन (7.1.2), so the affix is added as -ईन.
4. The final आ of the stem is dropped before the affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148).

This gives माहास्पदीन.

<answer>माहास्पदीन</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces जाहच् with certainty, so this form rests on reasoning rather than a confirmed rule.

The final च् of the affix is an indicatory letter (it), so the affix that actually attaches is जाह. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem शास्त्राध्यापक is not elided. The stem and the affix simply join.

<answer>शास्त्राध्यापकजाह</answer>

I did not find a specific rule that attaches ईयसुन् to this stem. I assumed the ordinary comparative use of the affix (P. 5.3.57), although P. 5.3.58 would normally restrict it to quality words, which this stem is not.

The affix ईयसुन् loses its marker letters उ and न्, leaving ईयस्. Before it, the final अ of पूर्वोपसृत is elided by P. 6.4.155 (टेः). So पूर्वोपसृत् + ईयस् gives पूर्वोपसृतीयस्.

<answer>पूर्वोपसृतीयस्</answer>

The affix रूपप् is added in the sense of praise (प्रशंसायां रूपप्, Pāṇini 5.3.66), as in वैयाकरणरूपः. Adding it to the stem अस्पन्दासु gives a stem ending in -a. I did not work through any further sandhi or accent considerations beyond this simple concatenation.

<answer>अस्पन्दासुरूप</answer>

This is a derivation I reasoned out rather than looked up, and I did not pin down the exact governing rule. The affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय by the rule "आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्". The final अ of कृतालय drops before the vowel-initial affix, so कृतालय + ईय gives कृतालयीय. A meaning such as "beneficial to that" (तस्मै हितम्) would license छ here, but I have not confirmed the sūtra.

<answer>कृतालयीय</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses अञ् on this stem, so this form rests on the general mechanics of the affix.

1. The stem पारमार्थिक ends in a short अ, which is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This leaves पारमार्थिक्.
2. The affix अञ् is added. Its ञ् is only a marker and triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the first vowel in पा is already long आ, so nothing changes.
3. The result is पारमार्थिक्+अ = पारमार्थिक.

<answer>पारमार्थिक</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् after पण्ड्र, so this is the standard derivation for an अञ् taddhita, not a rule-checked one.

1. The ञ् in अञ् is only an indicatory marker, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: पण्ड्र → पाण्ड्र.
2. The final अ of the stem is elided before the affix अ, so पाण्ड्र + अ gives पाण्ड्र.

<answer>पाण्ड्र</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), the affix दघ्नच् is added to the stem in the sense of measure. The final च् is only a marker and drops out, leaving the affix -दघ्न. Adding it to पाराशर gives पाराशरदघ्न. I did not check this against a source for this particular stem, and the question allows any licensed meaning, so I went with the direct combination.

<answer>पाराशरदघ्न</answer>

Taking यतितव्या as a feminine stem in -ā, the steps are:

1. Before the taddhita अण्, the final -ā of the stem is dropped (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This leaves यतितव्य्.
2. Adding अण् gives यतितव्य्+अ, which is यतितव्य.
3. The first vowel takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि, 7.2.117), so य becomes या. The result is यातितव्य.

<answer>यातितव्य</answer>

<answer>पुरुषावत्</answer>

This is a straightforward application of the affix. The affix वलच् loses its final च्, which only marks accent, leaving -वल. It attaches directly to the stem यन्त्रापीड with no change to either part, giving "possessing a यन्त्रापीड". I could not match this stem to a rule that licenses वलच् for it (Pāṇini 5.2.96 lists only रजस्, कृषि, आसुति and परिषद्), so the form rests on this direct combination.

<answer>यन्त्रापीडवल</answer>

The stem वैष्णव्य ends in short -a, so the affix तसि (taddhita *tas*) is added directly to it. The result is an indeclinable that takes no further case endings. I am relying on my recollection of Pāṇini's rules for this affix (for example 5.4.44, "pratiyoge pañcamyās tasiḥ", on a word in the fifth case) and have not checked the exact sūtra.

वैष्णव्य + तस् gives वैष्णव्यतः.

<answer>वैष्णव्यतः</answer>

I could not identify a rule specific to ध्मान with this affix, so I took the general sense of the affix. Affixed to ध्मान, the affix क (ka) can express the senses "unknown", "contemptible" or "endearment" (Pāṇini 5.3.73–76). The derived stem is ध्मान + क = ध्मानक. The final अ of ध्मान is dropped before the affix's initial अ (by यस्येति च), and the two then combine into ध्मानक.

<answer>ध्मानक</answer>

The affix देश्य is added by P. 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It attaches to a subanta in the sense "slightly deficient" (ईषदसमाप्ति). The stem लोलुप ends in short अ, so nothing in it changes. The affix is simply added after it, giving "somewhat of a lolupa".

<answer>लोलुपदेश्य</answer>

The stem द्वरि takes the superlative affix इष्ठन् (दरिष्ठ-type formation, "most …") by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (5.3.55). Before इष्ठन्, the final vowel with what follows it (the टि part) is dropped by टेः (6.4.155), so द्वरि becomes द्वर्. Adding इष्ठ gives द्वरिष्ठ. The feminine gender of the source stem does not change the result, because it has no ङीप्/टाप् suffix that could trigger पुंवद्भाव.

<answer>द्वरिष्ठ</answer>

I formed this by simple concatenation, without confirming the specific Pāṇinian rule for trā. I only partly recall it, probably the Pāṇini 5.4.55–56 rule that gives forms like देवत्रा. The affix त्रा begins with a consonant, so the stem should stay unchanged before it. The final -ā of the feminine stem अपोहिता is therefore retained, and the result is अपोहिता + त्रा = अपोहितात्रा.

<answer>अपोहितात्रा</answer>

I could not fully confirm this derivation; the form follows from my recollection of the rules, so treat it with some caution.

<answer>बहुकण्डु</answer>

I could not find a specific Pāṇinian rule for this stem, so this is the general ṭhak derivation.

The affix ठक् (Wak) has the initial ठ् replaced by इक (7.3.50). The stem's first vowel takes vṛddhi (7.2.117), so अ becomes आ. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix's vowel इ, which gives आर्तुक् + इक = आर्तुकिक.

I did not apply 7.3.51 (ṭha becoming ka after stems ending in इस्, उस्, उक् or त्). The stem ends in a vowel अ, so it does not meet that condition.

<answer>आर्तुकिक</answer>
<answer>लिखिखिल्लथा</answer>

Taking the stem तृम्पणीय as an ordinary nominal stem ending in short अ, the affix इञ् is added by the rule अत इञ् (4.1.95) in the sense of "descendant" (apatya). I did not check whether the neuter gender of the source stem changes anything.

1. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च), giving तृम्पणीय् + इ.
2. The ञ् marker of इञ् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (ञ्णित्यादिर्नित्यम्, 7.2.117). The first vowel ऋ becomes आर्, so तृ becomes तार्.
3. The result is तार्म्पणीयि. The ण is already retroflex and stays so.

<answer>तार्म्पणीयि</answer>

I applied Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), by which रूपप् is added to a word to express praise. The affix has a ‑प् marker, which is dropped, leaving रूप. Added to शौण्डि, it needs no sandhi or other change, so the stem is शौण्डिरूप ("a praiseworthy शौण्डि").

<answer>वेदान्ताभिहिततम</answer>

The affix तल् (SLP1 `tal`) is the one taught in "तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ" (5.1.119) to express the abstract sense "state of being X". It is added to the stem पूर्वापर्य, which is already complete as a stem. The final ल् of तल् is only an indicatory letter (it), so what remains is ता, and taddhita तल् forms feminine nouns (टाप्). The initial त of तल् is a consonant, so "यस्येति च" (6.4.148) does not delete the final अ of the stem, and the stem stays intact.

<answer>पूर्वापर्यता</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that introduces कुणप्, so this form is derived by general principles and may not match the intended rule.

The affix is कुण, with प् as a marker that only affects accent. Before a consonant-initial affix, रण्वन् has pada status (1.4.17). Its final न् is therefore dropped (8.2.7), giving रण्व + कुण.

<answer>रण्वकुण</answer>

This is derived from the affix rules alone. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that applies to this stem.

1. The affix खञ् (KaY) has ख् replaced by ईन (Pāṇini 7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).

The result is शैलाटीन.

The affix रूपप् (P. 5.3.66, प्रशस्तवचनात् रूपप्) is added to a word meaning "praiseworthy", giving a sense like "an excellent X". Adding it to खात्र gives the stem खात्ररूप, ending in अ. <answer>खात्ररूप</answer>

I could not match this stem to the specific rule that licenses वलच्. The affix is taught for रजस्, कृषि, आसुति, परिषद् (रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच्, 5.2.112) and for दन्त and शिखा (5.2.113), none of which is this stem. I formed the derivative mechanically.

<answer>युञ्जन्दक</answer>

The affix चरट् (caraw) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, भूतपूर्वे चरट्, and it means "formerly was so-and-so". Adding चर to शोध gives शोधचर, "formerly a शोध". The final ट् is only an indicatory letter, so it drops out and no sandhi changes occur.

<answer>मद्रकाधमात्व</answer>

Applying the affix द्वयसच् (P. 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) to हिंसीर gives हिंसीर + द्वयस. The final च् of the affix is only a marker, and the affix causes no vṛddhi or other change to the stem.
