I derived this by applying the ठक् → इक substitution and dropping the stem-final अ. I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ठक् after this stem, so the meaning is unspecified.

1. The affix ठक् (Wak) has the initial ठ् replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50), so the affix becomes -इक.
2. The stem लौहायन already begins with a vṛddhi vowel (औ), so no further vowel strengthening is needed.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148), giving लौहायन् + इक.

Applying इष्ठन् (the superlative affix) to सौप्तिका gives the stem below. I worked this out from memory of the rules without checking a source.

1. The stem सौप्तिका is सौप्तिक plus the feminine ending आ (टाप्).
2. Before इष्ठन्, the final part of the stem (टि) is dropped by टेः (6.4.155).
3. Whether the feminine ending is dropped on its own or the stem is first treated as masculine, the base reduces to सौप्तिक्.
4. Adding इष्ठ gives सौप्तिक् + इष्ठ = सौप्तिकिष्ठ.

<answer>सौप्तिकिष्ठ</answer>

The affix कल्पप् (rule 5.3.67, "slightly incomplete") is added after the whole word पूत्रिमा. Before कल्पप्, a polysyllabic stem ending in ṅī or āp takes a short final vowel (rule 6.3.43), so पूत्रिमा becomes पूत्रिम. This gives पूत्रिमकल्प. I am recalling rule 6.3.43 from memory, and I chose the bare taddhita stem over the feminine पूत्रिमकल्पा, which a separate ṭāp would produce.

<answer>पूत्रिमकल्प</answer>
<answer>तीक्ष्णाग्रसात्</answer>

The stem कतिपयथा ends in the feminine suffix ā. Before the taddhita कन् (क), that final ā drops, giving कतिपयथ + क = कतिपयथक. The feminine suffix टाप् is then added, giving कतिपयथका. Under 7.3.44, the a before the pratyaya-क becomes i when a feminine ā-suffix follows, so कतिपयथका becomes कतिपयथिका.

I did not settle whether 7.3.46 (अभाषितपुंस्क) restricts this i-substitution for a base like this. I chose the form with i, which 7.3.44 directly licenses.

<answer>कतिपयथिका</answer>

<answer>कार्णिकचर</answer>

The affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27) is added to the stem योजनिक. Its form is -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्. The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem-final अ of योजनिक drops by यस्येति च (6.4.148). Joining योजनिक् with अस्तात् gives योजनिकस्तात्, an indeclinable.

Taking the affix as सात् (the stem is treated as a pada before it), the final न् of कलत्रिन् is dropped by "नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य". Adding सात् gives an indeclinable. I derived this from memory of the rules, without checking a source.

The stem सांधिवेली already ends in the long ई. The affix च्वि (cvi) requires the stem's final vowel to become ई, and a stem already ending in ई stays unchanged. The stem वागुस ends in a short अ and is masculine, so तरप् (SLP1 tarap) attaches directly to the stem. No sandhi or other change applies here, and the result is a stem ending in -अ, which gives the comparative-type stem वागुसतर.

The affix बहुच् (Pāṇini 5.3.68–69, *vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*) is added before a subanta, in the sense "somewhat, not quite". It does not change the base. The feminine stem श्रौता therefore keeps its ending, and बहुच् is prefixed to give बहुश्रौता. I am not certain whether the pumvat rule (6.3.35) or a shortening rule would alter the base here. Following Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), the affix देश्य is added to a nominal in the sense of "slightly deficient, almost". The sup ending is dropped, and the stem ends in short अ, so no further change is needed. This gives सूपस्थानदेश्य, "a somewhat deficient सूपस्थान".

<answer>सूपस्थानदेश्य</answer>

I could not check this derivation against the rule text, so it rests on my recollection of the rules.

The affix द्वयसच् is taught in "प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः" (5.2.37). It denotes measure, as in ऊरुद्वयस "thigh-deep".

The final च् is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix द्वयस. Since द्वयस begins with a consonant, the stem is not treated as भ and the ending ई is not elided by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). I also assumed no shortening of the final ई applies, since the stem is not a गोस्त्रियोरुपसर्जनस्य case. Whether another shortening rule such as "एकतद्धिते च" would give the short-ि variant गुहागरिद्वयस is the point I am least sure of.

The result is गुहागरी + द्वयस = गुहागरीद्वयस.

<answer>गुहागरीद्वयस</answer>

Applying Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, the affix चणप् means "known by that." The final प् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix चण. It attaches to the stem without changing it. For example, केशैः वित्तः gives केशचणः. So भसित + चण gives भसितचण, "known by भसित."

<answer>भसितचण</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that introduces this affix, so this form is a best guess. I read कुणप् as the affix कुण, with the final प् being an indicatory letter (it) that marks accent only. In a taddhita affix the initial क् is not dropped, and the ण् in the middle is not an it-letter. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final उ of मादयित्नु undergoes no guṇa or elision. The affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>मादयित्नुकुण</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), the affix पाशप् is added to the stem to express something contemptible or nearly beyond remedy. The stem तटाकिनी ends in the feminine suffix ङीप्. The shortening rule for such stems (6.3.43) lists only घ, रूपप्, कल्पप्, चेलट्, ब्रुव, गोत्र, मत and हत, and पाश is not among them. The long ई therefore stays, and the pāśa element is simply appended. This is reasoned from memory of the rules rather than checked against a source.

<answer>तटाकिनीपाश</answer>

This is a best-fit derivation, since I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् after this stem. Adding a taddhita affix marked ञ् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so व (with अ) becomes वा. The final अ of the stem is elided before the affix's अ. That gives वारासन from वरासन.

<answer>वारासन</answer>

I formed this by adding मतुप् (the "possessing" suffix) directly to the stem सौरभी, so it means "that in which there is सौरभी". I did not check this against Pāṇini's rules or a reference. The stem ends in ई, not in म् or a short vowel before the final consonant, so the मतुप् → वतुप् change (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः) does not apply. The suffix therefore stays as मत्, giving the stem सौरभीमत्, whose feminine would be सौरभीमती.

<answer>सौरभीमत्</answer>
<answer>आध्वरिकतर</answer>

Taking the affix as Pāṇini's *śas* (5.4.43, used in the distributive sense, e.g. "tallīṃ tallīṃ dadāti"), I formed it as follows.

- In a taddhita affix the initial *ś* is not an it-marker, because 1.3.8 *laśakvataddhite* excludes taddhitas. The affix is therefore the full *śas*.
- It begins with a consonant, so the stem-final ई of तल्ली is not dropped (6.4.148 only applies before vowel-initial affixes).
- The result तल्लीशस् is an indeclinable, so final *s* becomes visarga.

<answer>तल्लीशः</answer>

I applied iṣṭhan to छगलिका without checking that it is licensed on a feminine stem. The stem takes the bha designation before the taddhita affix. The ṭi, here the final ā, is then deleted by ṭeḥ (6.4.155) or yasyeti ca (6.4.148), leaving छगलिक् + इष्ठ. Joining these gives छगलिकिष्ठ.

<answer>छगलिकिष्ठ</answer>

Adding the comparative affix तरप् (tarap) to the a-stem अर्ण gives अर्णतर. The final प् of the affix drops as an indicatory letter, leaving तर. The stem's final अ is also dropped before the affix's initial vowel-less consonant is attached, so no sandhi or vowel change applies. The neuter gender does not alter the stem here. The ण is already present, so no ṇatva change is needed.

<answer>अर्णतर</answer>

I could not match this affix to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The nearest rules are 5.2.120 (यप् after रूप) and 5.3.66 (रूपप्). I therefore treated रूप्य as a whole affix added to the stem दिशान.

The affix begins with र, not with य or ई. The elision of a final अ before such affixes (यस्येति च, 6.4.148) therefore does not apply. The stem stays intact and the affix is simply added after it.

<answer>दिशानरूप्य</answer>
<answer>गण्डीरजातीय</answer>

<answer>गौलक्षणिकरूप</answer>

I could not confirm that स्तायु is listed in the gavādi gaṇa, so this derivation is my best reading rather than a checked one.

- The affix यत् after a stem ending in उ fits the rule उगवादिभ्यो यत् (Pāṇini 5.1.2).
- Before यत्, the final उ takes guṇa by ओर्गुणः (6.4.146), giving स्तायो + य.
- Then ओ becomes अव् before य by वान्तो यि प्रत्यये (6.1.79).

This gives स्तायव्य.

<answer>स्तायव्य</answer>

असन के साथ च्वि जोड़ने पर, पाणिनि 5.4.50 के अनुसार अभूततद्भाव (जो पहले नहीं था वह बनना) के अर्थ में रूप बनता है। च्वि प्रत्यय का सम्पूर्ण लोप हो जाता है (वह केवल निमित्त रहता है)। फिर 7.4.32 (अस्य च्वौ) से अंतिम अ के स्थान पर ई हो जाता है। इस प्रकार असन + च्वि → असनी, जैसे "असनी भवति / करोति"।

<answer>असनी</answer>

I could not match this stem to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The one rule I know for थमु is इदमस्थमुः (5.3.24), which applies only to इदम्, as in इत्थम्. I therefore applied the affix mechanically.

The final उ of थमु is an indicatory letter (it-marker) and drops, leaving the suffix थम्. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of भवाग्र is not elided. Joining the two gives भवाग्र + थम् = भवाग्रथम्. A word ending in a taddhita affix of this kind is an indeclinable (1.1.38), so no case ending is added.

<answer>भवाग्रथम्</answer>

This is a best guess: I could not identify the rule that licenses the affix साति (sAti) with certainty, and the stem रोशंसा looks unusual.

Since साति begins with a consonant, I assumed the stem keeps its final आ unchanged. The affix is simply added after it.

<answer>रोशंसासाति</answer>

Starting from the feminine stem तपन्ती (ending in ङीप्), the affix तमप् (अतिशायने, P. 5.3.55) is added. Under P. 6.3.43, a stem with more than one syllable that ends in a feminine suffix (ङी/ आप्) shortens its final vowel before तमप् (a "घ" affix). So तपन्ती becomes तपन्ति, and adding तम gives तपन्तितम.

<answer>तपन्तितम</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that attaches खञ् to this stem, so this form comes from applying the general mechanics of the affix to कृतान्तर.

1. The affix खञ् has initial ख, which is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन), and ञ् is a marker that triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel. So कृ becomes कार्, giving कार्तान्तर + ईन.
2. The न of ईन follows the final र of अन्तर with only the vowel ई between them. By the rule on retroflexion of न (8.4.2), it becomes ण. The earlier र in कार्त does not affect it because the dental त intervenes.

The result is कार्तान्तरीण.

<answer>कार्तान्तरीण</answer>

I could not match अवम with थमु to a specific rule. The nearest rules are 5.3.24 इदमस्थमुः and 5.3.25 किमश्च, which apply to other stems. So this is a mechanical formation, not a verified one.

The affix थमु loses its marker उ, leaving थम्. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of अवम stays. The stem plus the affix gives अवमथम्, which is an indeclinable.

<answer>अवमथम्</answer>

<answer>वन्दारुतः</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses this affix, so this form is a best-guess derivation rather than a confirmed one.

I read the affix कुणप् as कुण, with the final प् as an indicatory letter and the ण् treated as part of the affix, not an indicatory letter. Because कुण begins with a vowel, the final आ of धरा is elided by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). No vṛddhi applies, since the ण् is not an indicatory letter.

धरा + कुण → धर + कुण → धरकुण

This is a best-effort derivation. I could not pin down which sūtra introduces जाहच्, so the form rests on the general rules for adding a taddhita suffix.

In जाहच्, the final च् is only an indicatory letter (it), so the operative affix is जाह. It begins with a consonant, so it does not give the base the "bha" status needed for यस्येति च (6.4.148). The final -a of भूतेज्य therefore stays, and the affix is simply added.

भूतेज्य + जाह = भूतेज्यजाह

<answer>भूतेज्यजाह</answer>

I could not tie this to a specific rule. थाल् (5.3.23, प्रकारवचने थाल्) is normally taught after सर्वनाम words such as तथा and यथा, and मैथिल is not one. I formed the derivative mechanically instead.

The ल् in थाल् is only a marker, so the affix that is actually added is था. It begins with a consonant and is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi. The final अ of मैथिल is not dropped either, because the rule यस्येति च applies only before affixes that begin with a vowel or य. Adding the affix gives मैथिल + था = मैथिलथा, an indeclinable meaning "in the manner of a Maithila".

<answer>मैथिलथा</answer>

This derivation rests on Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.115, *ata ini-ṭhanau*. That rule lets the affixes ini and ṭhan express possession after a stem ending in short a. I chose it because मिष ends in a, and I did not find a more specific rule for ṭhan with this stem.

1. The affix ठन् (ṭhan) has its initial ठ replaced by इक (ik) under 7.3.50 (*ṭhasyeka*).
2. The final अ of मिष is dropped before the affix, giving मिष् + इक.
3. There is no vṛddhi, because ṭhan is not marked with ṇ.
4. The result is मिषिक, with the meaning "one who has miṣa", on the pattern of दण्डिक beside दण्डी.

<answer>मिषिक</answer>

This is a direct application of the affix. I did not check the grammatical conditions under which थाल् is licensed for this stem. I formed the word on the assumption that the affix attaches to the stem as given.

The affix थाल् loses its marker ल्, leaving था. It begins with a consonant, so the stem is not modified. Adding it to शयण्डक gives शयण्डकथा, an indeclinable.

<answer>शयण्डकथा</answer>

Using ञ्यट्, the ञित् marker would normally call for vṛddhi of the first vowel. In दानु the first vowel दा is already long, so nothing changes there. The final उ takes guṇa before the taddhita (ओर्गुणः), giving दानो + य, and ओ then becomes अव् by एचोऽयवायावः, giving दानव्य. The ट् marker only matters for forming the feminine.

<answer>दानव्य</answer>

Under 7.3.50 (ṭhasyekaḥ) the affix ṭhak becomes -ika. The final ī of the stem भीती is dropped before it by 6.4.148 (yasyeti ca). I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ṭhak on this stem, so the derivation rests on these general rules.

<answer>भैतिक</answer>
<answer>सात्वतवत्</answer>

I did not derive this from a specific rule application. The affix रूप्य is the one taught in the sūtra for "coming from" (पञ्चम्यर्थ), as in समरूप्य. It begins with a consonant (र), so the stem counts as a pada before it. Because of that, the final आ of चर्मा is not dropped by यस्येति च, and the affix is simply added to the stem. The stem चर्मा is not a typical input for this affix, but the formation still goes through.

The affix तल् is added in the sense of "state or quality of that" (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ, 5.1.119). The final ल् of तल् is a marker and drops, leaving the suffix -ता. The result is a feminine stem in -ā, formed by adding टाप्. No sound change applies to बाल्हायन here.

<answer>बाल्हायनता</answer>

This is a rule-based derivation, and I did not tie it to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for this affix.

The affix वलच् has च् as an indicatory letter, so only वल is added. It begins with the consonant व, not with य or a vowel, so the stem बन्धुकिन् counts as a pada before it. The final न् is therefore dropped (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य, 8.2.7), which gives बन्धुकि + वल = बन्धुकिवल.

<answer>बन्धुकिवल</answer>
<answer>भीरुद्वयस</answer>

This is an application of P. 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcupcaṇapau*), where caṇap is added to a stem in the sense "known by that". I did not look up the rule text, so I am relying on memory for the rule and for the model forms *vidyā-caṇa* and *keśa-caṇa*.

The affix is attached directly to the stem, and its final form is -caṇa. The indicatory p does not change the stem, so the final ā of नागरोत्था is not shortened or altered, as in *vidyā-caṇa*. The meaning is "known by Nāgarotthā".

<answer>औपशमिकदेश्य</answer>

The affix पाशप् (pāśap) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47, "याप्ये पाशप्" (it applies in the sense of something defective or contemptible). It attaches directly to the nominal stem. The affix begins with a consonant, and the stem ends in a short अ that stays unchanged. No vowel is elided, so the result is simply the stem followed by -पाश.

श्वितान + पाश = श्वितानपाश

I applied the affix मयट् (mayaṭ) to the stem as given and did not check the rule or the meaning against a specific sūtra.

मयट् begins with म्, which is neither a vowel nor य्. So the stem is not given the भ-संज्ञा (bha designation) that 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) needs in order to drop a final अ. The stem therefore keeps its final अ, and the ट् is only an indicatory letter that drops out. The result is अयासोमीय + मय = अयासोमीयमय, with no vṛddhi.

<answer>अयासोमीयमय</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra for रूप्य with certainty, so this form rests on my best reading rather than a confirmed rule.

I took रूप्य as the affix to be added directly to the stem जोहूत्रा.

<answer>जोहूत्रारूप्य</answer>
<answer>घूर्णद्वयस</answer>

<answer>टेकवत्</answer>

The derivative follows the usual pattern of adding वलच् to the stem. I did not find a specific sūtra that licenses वलच् after शिखण्ड itself. Applying इष्ठन् to the stem gives the superlative. Before इष्ठन्, the stem is a भ-stem, so its final टि (the last vowel with anything following it) is dropped by the rule टेः (6.4.155). The stem साह्नोक ends in क, so its टि is the final अ, and removing it leaves साह्नोक्. Adding इष्ठ then gives साह्नोकिष्ठ. I applied this rule directly and did not check the stem against any dictionary or against other rules.

<answer>साह्नोकिष्ठ</answer>

Applying शस् to the feminine stem भयावदीर्णा follows the usual taddhita pattern. The शस् affix is added to the base (as in बहुशः), and after the affix's initial श् drops as an indicatory letter, what remains is the ending -अस्. Since this ending begins with a vowel, the stem takes the भ designation. The final -आ of the feminine stem is then deleted by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This gives भयावदीर्ण + शस्, which is the indeclinable भयावदीर्णशः. I derived this from the rules rather than from an attested example, so it rests on that reasoning.

<answer>भयावदीर्णशः</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), where it is added to a third-case word in the sense "known by". The final प् is only a marker and drops. The ञ् inside the affix is not final, so it stays in the form, as in विद्याचुञ्चुः. I recalled the sūtra and its examples from memory rather than checking a source. Adding the affix to वृष्टि gives the stem वृष्टिचुञ्चु.

<answer>वृष्टिचुञ्चु</answer>

This derivation is reconstructed from memory of the rules, not checked against the Aṣṭādhyāyī. I am not certain of the key step.

The affix चरट् is taught by "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (5.3.53), meaning "formerly such". Because चरट् falls within the तसिल्-class affixes, the feminine base takes masculine-like form before it (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.35), as in आढ्या → आढ्यचर. By that logic, the final -ā of महानना is replaced by -a, giving महानन, and चरट् then adds the suffix चर. The result is महाननचर, with the feminine counterpart being महाननचरी.

The weak point is whether महानना qualifies as a "भाषितपुंस्क" word, which पुंवद्भाव requires. If it does not, the form would be महाननाचर instead. I chose the पुंवद्भाव form.

<answer>महाननचर</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.67 allows देशीयर् after a subanta in the sense of "slightly incomplete". The ā-ending stem प्राणादा is a nyap-final feminine, so I checked whether it would be shortened. The rule that shortens a feminine ā or ī before certain affixes (घ, रूपप्, कल्पप्, चेलट्, ब्रुव, गोत्र, मत, हत) does not list देशीयर्. The stem therefore stays unshortened, and the final अ of देशीय is what remains after the इत् र् is dropped. I worked this out from memory of the rules rather than checking a source.

प्राणादा + देशीय = प्राणादादेशीय

<answer>प्राणादादेशीय</answer>
<answer>क्ष्विण्णदेशीय</answer>

The affix त्रा is added to the stem अन्योन्याश्रिता.

I did not apply the feminine-to-masculine replacement (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.35). That rule covers affixes from तसिल् up to कृत्वसुच्, and I believe त्रा falls outside that range. I am not fully certain of this.

The final आ also stays. The elision rule यस्येति च needs a following vowel or ya-initial affix, and त्रा begins with a consonant.

So the stem and affix simply join as अन्योन्याश्रिता + त्रा = अन्योन्याश्रितात्रा.

<answer>अन्योन्याश्रितात्रा</answer>
<answer>बभ्रुकदेश्य</answer>

Applying अण् to वार्द्धुष्य gives, by my derivation, the same surface form वार्द्धुष्य. I derived it from the general rules rather than from a specific sūtra I could confirm.

1. The stem वार्द्धुष्य ends in य् + अ. Its initial vowel is already आ, so no further vṛddhi can apply.
2. Before the taddhita अण्, the final अ of the stem is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). That leaves वार्द्धुष्य् + अण्.
3. The ण् is only an indicatory letter, so what remains is वार्द्धुष्य् + अ. The य् joins the अ, and the result is again वार्द्धुष्य.

<answer>वार्द्धुष्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses वलच् after एकादशम, so this form comes from the general mechanics of the affix, not from a located sūtra.

The affix वलच् loses its indicatory letters च् and अ (the अ of ल् in the form वलच् being part of the affix itself), leaving the operative suffix वल. The stem ends in अ, and the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) would delete that अ only before an affix beginning with a vowel or ई. Since वल begins with the consonant व्, the stem's final अ stays.

एकादशम + वल → एकादशमवल

<answer>एकादशमवल</answer>

Since पार्जन्य ends in short अ, the patronymic rule अत इञ् (4.1.95) allows the affix इञ्. The initial vowel is already आ, so vṛddhi changes nothing. The final अ of the stem drops before इ by यस्येति च (6.4.148), giving पार्जन्य् + इ = पार्जन्यि. I derived this from the rules rather than checking it against an attested form.

<answer>पार्जन्यि</answer>
<answer>न्यायागतत्व</answer>

Since the stem स्तौपिक ends in short अ, the possessive affix इनि (Pāṇini 5.2.115, अत इनिठनौ) can be added to it. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, which gives स्तौपिक + इन् → स्तौपिकिन्, "having a स्तौपिक". I have not checked this against a specific attested form.

<answer>स्तौपिकिन्</answer>

The affix चरट् is the one taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Pāṇini 5.3.53), which means "formerly such". Added to लघु ("light"), it gives लघुचर ("formerly light"). The feminine ending is not part of the taddhita stem, so I give the stem without it.

<answer>लघुचर</answer>
<answer>राढीयीन</answer>
<answer>वाधौलवत्</answer>

The affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*) is added to a nominal word to express praise, so a "praiseworthy व्रणिल" is व्रणिलरूप. The final a of व्रणिल and the initial र of रूप do not trigger any sandhi change, so the two simply join. The result is a masculine a-stem.

<answer>व्रणिलरूप</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.53, *bhūtapūrve caraṭ* ("formerly was"). It is added directly to a nominal stem, and the indicatory ṭ is dropped, leaving the affix *cara*.

Since *cara* begins with a consonant, the final -a of the stem is not deleted (6.4.148 applies only before vowel-initial taddhitas). The stem is also already in its full form, so *cātur-māsaka* + *cara* simply joins as *cāturmāsakacara*, meaning "formerly a cāturmāsaka".

I reconstructed the rule from memory rather than checking it against a text, so the sūtra reference is the least certain part.

<answer>चातुर्मासकचर</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses कुणप्, so this form rests on the general rules for adding a taddhita affix.

The affix is कुण, with प् as a non-surviving marker. It begins with a consonant, so the rule that drops a stem-final अ (यस्येति च) does not apply. The stem अविकृताङ्ग therefore stays whole and the affix is attached directly.

<answer>अविकृताङ्गकुण</answer>

I took this to be the affix *deśya* of Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which means "slightly incomplete", "almost". It is added to a subanta, and the case ending is then dropped, as in पटु → पटुदेश्य. Here the stem परमेक्षु ends in -u, so adding देश्य causes no sandhi change.

<answer>परमेक्षुदेश्य</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces this affix, so this form rests on the usual it-letter rules rather than a verified rule.

The affix जाहच् loses its initial ज् and its final च् as indicators (इत्), leaving the operative affix आह. The stem दृभीक ends in short अ, which is elided before an affix beginning with a vowel. Adding आह then gives दृभीकाह. The result is the same if the अ is instead joined with आ by simple vowel coalescence.

<answer>दृभीकाह</answer>

The affix बहुच् is added before a subanta (Pāṇini 5.3.68, विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु), with the sense of "somewhat" or "almost" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is placed in front of the stem, as in बहुपटु ("somewhat clever"). Applied to हास्त, it gives बहुहास्त ("somewhat हास्त").

<answer>बहुहास्त</answer>

The stem वैतनिक already begins with a vṛddhi vowel (ऐ), so it counts as vṛddha. The affix छ can therefore be added to it, for example by Pāṇini 4.2.114 (वृद्धाच्छः).

The affix छ is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The final अ of वैतनिक is dropped before the vowel-initial affix, which gives वैतनिक् + ईय = वैतनिकीय.

<answer>वैतनिकीय</answer>

Taking the stem as a basic masculine nominal stem, I added इष्ठन् (the "most" affix, तमप् and इष्ठन् being the pair used for the superlative). Before the affix, the final टि of the stem is dropped (ṭi-lopa, 6.4.155). The final अ of उपोपयात goes, leaving उपोपयात्. Adding इष्ठ gives उपोपयातिष्ठ. I derived this from the rules as I remember them, not from a source for this specific word.

<answer>उपोपयातिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>गुदाङ्कुरदेश्य</answer>

The stem अमुका (feminine, ending in टाप्) takes कन्. Before a affix with क, the final long vowel is shortened by 7.4.13 (केऽणः), so अमुका becomes अमुक. Adding कन् with its ण/न् marker dropped gives the stem अमुकक.

I stop at the taddhita stem. If the feminine were added afterwards, 7.3.44 would give अमुकिका.

<answer>अमुकक</answer>
<answer>अन्वष्टक्यता</answer>

The affix kalpap is added by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (īṣad-asamāptau kalpab-deśya-deśīyaraḥ) to express "slightly incomplete", so the sense is "almost yellow". Because it is a taddhita, the case ending is dropped and the affix attaches directly to the stem. The final stem is पीतक + कल्प = पीतककल्प. Its gender is not given, and the neuter stem needs no vowel change.

<answer>पीतककल्प</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses वलच् on this stem, so this answer rests only on the general mechanics of the affix. The affix वलच् has a final च् that is only a marker (it drops out), leaving the suffix as वल. The stem पञ्चार्थ ends in अ, and this अ is elided before the affix. That gives पञ्चार्थ + वल → पञ्चार्थवल.

<answer>पञ्चार्थवल</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47, याप्ये पाशप्, and I applied it to the stem without checking any attested usage. The stem साद्यस्क्र ends in -a, but पाश begins with a consonant, so nothing is elided or altered and the affix is simply attached.

<answer>साद्यस्क्रपाश</answer>

Here थाल् is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्), which denotes "manner". Its final ल् is only an it-marker, so the affix that is actually added is था. The stem अवोक्षणीय ends in अ, but the affix begins with the consonant थ, so the final अ is not dropped under 6.4.148. Adding था gives अवोक्षणीयथा, an indeclinable.

Pāṇini's rule is stated for sarvanāma-type stems, and अवोक्षणीय is not one. I applied the affix mechanically, as the task asks.

<answer>अवोक्षणीयथा</answer>
<answer>सास्थितर</answer>

The affix जातीयर् is added under the rule "प्रकारवचने जातीयर्" (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.69), meaning "of that kind". The marker र् drops out, leaving the affix as जातीय.

The stem पारीण ends in अ, and the affix begins with a consonant (ज्), so no vowel elision or other sandhi applies. The affix is simply attached to the stem.

पारीण + जातीय = पारीणजातीय, meaning "of the पारीण kind".

<answer>पारीणजातीय</answer>

I treated रद्द as an ordinary masculine a-stem and added अञ् (SLP1 aY). The ञ् marker is only an it-letter; it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so the initial अ becomes आ (र → रा). The stem's final अ is dropped before the affix's अ, giving राद्द. I did not match the stem to a specific sūtra, since it is not a standard Sanskrit stem.

<answer>राद्द</answer>
<answer>व्यावहारांशीन</answer>

I could not trace the exact sūtra that introduces ञ्यट्, so this derivation rests on the general rules for the affix's markers, not on a located rule.

1. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the suffix **-य** after the markers are dropped. The marker ञ् makes the affix ञित्, and the marker ट् only conditions the feminine in -ई.
2. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि): सेना → सैना, since ए becomes ऐ.
3. The final अ of अधिप is dropped before य (यस्येति च). This gives सैनाधिप् + य = सैनाधिप्य.

<answer>सैनाधिप्य</answer>

The affix चरट् is taught in Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.53, "भूतपूर्वे चरट्", and means "formerly that". The final ट् is only a marker and drops, leaving the ending -चर. Added to चाष, it gives चाषचर, "formerly a chāṣa (blue jay)". I am giving this from memory of the sūtra and the standard example आढ्यचर, not from a checked source.

<answer>चाषचर</answer>
<answer>आनृतकरूप</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*. It is added to a word in the instrumental sense and means "known by" that word, as in विद्याचुञ्चुः ("known for learning").

Here the base फणिकेश्वर takes चुञ्चु, and the final प् is only an indicatory letter that drops. Since चुञ्चु begins with a consonant, the final -अ of the base is not elided. No vṛddhi applies either, because the affix is not ञित् or णित्.

The result is फणिकेश्वरचुञ्चु, a masculine stem.

<answer>फणिकेश्वरचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>तनिष्ठीय</answer>
<answer>जरितारिदेशीय</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् (superlative) is added to the stem वाताली. Before इष्ठन्, the final ई of the stem is dropped by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). This gives वाताल् + इष्ठ = वातालिष्ठ.

<answer>वातालिष्ठ</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् on this stem, so this form rests on general Pāṇinian rules and is a best guess.

3. Before a taddhita affix, the final आ of the base is dropped by यस्येति च, giving सामर् + य.
4. This yields the stem सामर्य.

Because the affix carries ट्, a feminine form with ङीप् (सामर्यी) would also be possible. I am giving the base derived stem, सामर्य, since the question asks for the stem without further endings.

Taking इनि in the sense of possession (matvartha), I used the rule अत इनिठनौ (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.115), which adds इनि to stems ending in short अ. The stem हिंसनीय ends in अ, so it qualifies.

The final अ of the stem is dropped by यस्येति च, which gives हिंसनीय् + इन् = हिंसनीयिन्. The result is a stem ending in न्.

<answer>हिंसनीयिन्</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् (rule 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) has the indicatory letter च्, which drops. What remains is दघ्न, which begins with a consonant. <answer>वैप्रश्निकदघ्न</answer>

The stem मकक ends in short अ, and the affix इनि is the possessive (matvarthīya) suffix added to such stems by Pāṇini 5.2.115, "अत इनिठनौ". Before the affix, the final अ of the stem drops, so मकक + इन् gives मककिन्. This is the stem form, meaning "one who has a मकक". I could not identify the word मकक itself, so I treated it as an ordinary a-stem.

The affix cuñcup is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*), meaning "known by that". The stem takes the affix after the third-case relation, as in *vidyā-cuñcu* "known for learning". <answer>प्रौढाङ्गनाचुञ्चु</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them; I did not check it against a source.

1. The affix ठक् (ṭhak) has its ठ replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50), so the affix becomes इक.

<answer>आजमीढकिक</answer>

I could not fully confirm the exact form of the affix from memory. It is Pāṇini's affix *sāti* (A. 5.4.52), which gives indeclinables such as *agnisāt*, and I took the final *i* to drop in the resulting form. Adding it to the stem नानुरक्त gives the indeclinable below.

<answer>नानुरक्तसात्</answer>

I formed this by attaching the affix सात् (सातिः, SLP1 sAti) directly to the stem ह्रादका. I am relying on memory of Pāṇini 5.4.52–54 for the affix's meanings (totality, or dependence on the stem's referent). No sandhi change applies, and the result is indeclinable.

<answer>ह्रादकासात्</answer>
<answer>लोकानुवृत्तक</answer>

I applied the affix इष्ठन् (the superlative sense, अतिशायने) to the stem. Before इष्ठन्, the rule टेः (6.4.155) drops the stem's final vowel together with whatever follows it. In माषीण that final part is ईण, so माष् remains. Adding इष्ठ gives माषिष्ठ. I could not identify a rule that applies थमु specifically to रङ्क. The only Pāṇinian source I recall for it is 5.3.24 (इदमस्थमुः), which covers इदम्, so I applied the affix to रङ्क by analogy rather than from a licensing rule.

The final उ of थमु is an *it* marker and drops, leaving थम्. This is added to the stem रङ्क, which ends in अ and is unchanged. The result is रङ्क + थम् = रङ्कथम्. As a taddhita ending in this affix, it is an indeclinable.

<answer>रङ्कथम्</answer>

Applying `yat` to the stem यन्त्रावली gives यन्त्रावल्य. The taddhita `yat` here has the sense "good in/at that" (तत्र साधुः, 4.4.98). This is one of the senses licensed for the affix, and I chose it from recall rather than checking each candidate rule.

The final ई of the stem is dropped before a taddhita beginning with `y`, by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). That leaves यन्त्रावल् + य. The affix `yat` carries no ṇit marker, so there is no vṛddhi.

I could not tie this stem to a rule that licenses थाल् directly. Pāṇini 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्) is normally taught for सर्वनाम words such as तथा and यथा, and मृगाधिराज is not one. I formed the derivative on the assumption that the affix is added in the sense of "manner" (prakāra).

The final ल् of थाल् is only a marker (it) and drops, leaving the affix था. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of मृगाधिराज is not deleted. The result is मृगाधिराज + था, an indeclinable form.

<answer>मृगाधिराजथा</answer>
<answer>पाल्लक्य</answer>
<answer>परमार्तरूप</answer>

This is a derivation from the general taddhita rules rather than from a specific sūtra I could identify.

1. The affix खञ् has ख replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, 7.1.2), and the ञ् is only a marker.
2. The final ई of दान्तिकी is dropped before a taddhita affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), leaving दान्तिक्.
3. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, but दान्तिक् already begins with आ, so nothing changes.
4. Adding ईन gives दान्तिक् + ईन = दान्तिकीन.

<answer>दान्तिकीन</answer>

The stem प्रैयक ends in short अ, so the affix इञ् (iY) applies by the rule "अत इञ्" (the patronymic affix after a-ending stems). Before the ñit affix the final अ of the stem drops. The first vowel ऐ is already vṛddhi, so it needs no change. This gives प्रैयक् + इ = प्रैयकि.

<answer>प्रैयकि</answer>

I derived the stem by applying the elision rule for the agent suffix before the comparative affix. This is from memory of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, and I did not check the rule against a text.

1. भणितृ is formed from the root भण् with the augment इट् and the agent suffix तृ.
2. Before the affix ईयसुन्, rule 6.4.154 (तुरिष्ठेमेयस्सु) elides the suffix तृ, leaving the base भण्.
3. Adding ईयस् to the base gives भण् + ईयस् = भणीयस्.
4. The letters उ and न् of ईयसुन् are markers only. They matter when case endings are added, for example nominative भणीयान्, but not for the stem.

<answer>भणीयस्</answer>

I could not identify the rule that introduces ञ्यट्, so this form rests on the standard effects of its markers rather than on a rule I could cite.

- The ञ् in ञ्यट् is an indicatory letter (ञित्). It triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (अचामादेः): स → सा.
- The ट् is also indicatory (it supplies the feminine in ङीप्) and is dropped, leaving the suffix -य.
- The stem's final अ is elided before the vowel-initial suffix (यस्येति च).

So समुद्रोन्मादन + य gives सामुद्रोन्मादन्य.

<answer>सामुद्रोन्मादन्य</answer>

This is a derivation from the rule that shortens a stem-final long vowel of a feminine stem before the affixes tarap and tamap (Pāṇini 6.3.43, ṅyāpoḥ… hrasvaḥ). It is cited from memory rather than checked.

1. The stem साम्यावस्था ends in the feminine long आ.
2. Before तरप्, that आ shortens to अ, giving साम्यावस्थ.
3. Adding तरप् (whose final प् drops) gives साम्यावस्थतर.

I have given the stem as formed by the taddhita affix itself. If the feminine ending were added afterwards, it would be साम्यावस्थतरा.

<answer>साम्यावस्थतर</answer>

I applied चरट् by Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), which means "formerly such". I recalled this from memory and did not check it against a source.

The affix attaches to the whole subanta, so the stem क्षुरी is kept as it is. I did not find that the stem's final ई is shortened or replaced by a masculine form before चरट्. The rule for masculine-form substitution (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.39) covers only affixes from तसिल् to कृत्वसुच्, and चरट् is not among them. The final ट् of the affix is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the ending -चर.

So क्षुरी + चरट् gives क्षुरी + चर, i.e. क्षुरीचर, meaning "formerly a razor".

<answer>क्षुरीचर</answer>

I derived this as the indeclinable formed by adding the affix अस्ताति (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.27 ff.) to the stem. Two points are uncertain. The stem is not a direction word, so the affix does not normally apply to it, and I treated the table as a purely formal exercise. I also recalled from memory that the final ति of the affix drops, as in पुरस्तात्, and did not verify the rule.

1. The stem ends in -य (य् + अ). Before the vowel-initial affix, its final अ drops (6.4.148), leaving वानप्रस्थ्य्.
2. Adding the affix, with its final इ dropped as in पुरस्तात्, gives वानप्रस्थ्यस्तात्.
3. Taddhita-derived forms are indeclinable (1.1.38), so no case or number ending follows.

<answer>वानप्रस्थ्यस्तात्</answer>

I could not match this stem and affix to a specific Pāṇinian rule. As far as I recall, थमु is licensed only after इदम् (5.3.24, as in इत्थम्) and किम् (as in कथम्), so पौत्रिक is not a stem it normally attaches to. I therefore applied the affix mechanically.

The final उ of थमु is an it-marker and drops, leaving थम्. The affix has no ञित् or णित् marker, so there is no vṛddhi, and the stem is unchanged. The result is an indeclinable, पौत्रिक + थम् = पौत्रिकथम्.

<answer>पौत्रिकथम्</answer>

This is a guess based on my recollection of the shortening rule, which I did not check against the Aṣṭādhyāyī.

तरप् is a ghá-type affix. Before such an affix, a stem ending in the feminine suffix ā (or ī) takes a short final vowel (Pāṇini 6.3.43, as I recall it). So the final आ of वेतालाख्यायिका shortens to अ before तरप्. This gives वेतालाख्यायिक + तर = वेतालाख्यायिकतर.

<answer>वेतालाख्यायिकतर</answer>
<answer>तासूनीसात्</answer>
<answer>ग्रैष्मिकतम</answer>

Since the stem व्यवहारालोक ends in अ, the affix इञ् is added by the rule *अत इञ्* (A. 4.1.95), which gives the meaning "descendant". The steps are:

1. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (A. 7.2.117). The first vowel is the अ after व्य, which becomes आ, giving व्यावहारालोक.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (A. 6.4.148).
3. Adding इ gives व्यावहारालोकि.

<answer>व्यावहारालोकि</answer>
<answer>वीटकतर</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु) and means "somewhat X", that is, X incompletely realised. It is placed before the word, so the affix बहु comes first and the stem आनुदृष्टेय follows.

बहु + आनुदृष्टेय: the final उ of बहु meets the initial आ, and उ becomes व् before a dissimilar vowel (यण् sandhi). This gives बह्वानुदृष्टेय.

<answer>बह्वानुदृष्टेय</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this is a mechanical derivation of the affix, not a confirmed attested form.

1. खञ् is replaced by its substitute ईन (7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).
2. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (7.2.117, तद्धितेष्वचामादेः), so स becomes सा, giving सारस्य.
3. The final अ of the stem is deleted before ईन (6.4.148, यस्येति च), which leaves सारस्य् + ईन.

Joining these gives सारस्यीन.

<answer>सारस्यीन</answer>
<answer>विञ्जोलीत्व</answer>

Deriving the stem व्रातीनादेशीय with देशीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, in the sense "almost, not quite") takes the feminine stem व्रातीना, which ends in the ṭāp suffix. By the shortening rule for feminine stems ending in ṅī or āp before देशीयर्, the final आ becomes short अ, giving व्रातीन. Adding देशीय then gives व्रातीनदेशीय. I am recalling the sūtra from memory and did not check its number.

<answer>व्रातीनदेशीय</answer>

I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses वलच् after दिलीर. I simply added the affix in the ordinary way: the final च् is only a marker and drops, leaving the suffix -वल. Attached to the stem दिलीर, this gives the stem दिलीरवल.

<answer>दिलीरवल</answer>
<answer>धौतात्मनीन</answer>

This follows Pāṇini 5.3.67, where देश्य is added to a subanta word to mean "slightly incomplete". I did not check any rule that would alter a short-इ stem before देश्य. The stem अजाजि is already a basic feminine stem ending in short इ, so I assumed no vowel shortening or masculine-form substitution applies. The affix is then simply appended.

<answer>अजाजिदेश्य</answer>

I applied भूतपूर्वे चरट् (5.3.53), which means "formerly was". The base आगस् is treated as a pada before the consonant-initial affix चर (1.4.17). Its final स् becomes रु and then visarga, which turns into स् before the following खर् sound (8.3.34). Before च, the स् then becomes श् by ścutva (8.4.40). This gives आगश्चर. I reasoned this through from memory of the rules and did not check it against a reference.

<answer>आगश्चर</answer>
<answer>कुहरितर</answer>

The stem and affix match the vīpsā rule (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.43), which allows शस् after a word in the singular to express distribution, so रक्ताक्ष + शस् gives रक्ताक्षशस्. The indeclinable ends in visarga: रक्ताक्षशः. I recalled this rule from memory and did not confirm it against the text. A stem meaning "many" or "few" would also fit 5.4.42, but रक्ताक्ष does not, so I took the vīpsā reading.

<answer>रक्ताक्षशः</answer>
<answer>एनस्यत्रा</answer>

The most likely derivation uses अत इञ् (4.1.95), which adds इञ् to a stem ending in short अ to give a derivative such as a patronymic. I am assuming that is the licensed use here, since the table does not name the sense.

1. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: द → दा, giving दाक्षाध्वर.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before इ, giving दाक्षाध्वरि.

If the second member अध्वर also took vṛddhi, its initial vowel would merge with the preceding अ into the same long आ, so the result would not change.

<answer>दाक्षाध्वरि</answer>

This is a derivation under Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*), which adds चणप् to a word in the instrumental sense "known by". Here that word is वार्केणी.

The affix चणप् has only its final प् as an indicatory letter. What remains is the affix चण, with its initial च retained.

Since चण begins with a consonant, the final ई of the base is not dropped. I also did not apply any shortening of ई, which I believe applies only in compounds, so it does not arise here. This gives the stem वार्केणीचण.

<answer>वार्केणीचण</answer>

I could not pin down which Pāṇinian rule licenses त्रा here, so I did not apply any special rule. I simply appended the affix to the stem as given, which already ends in the feminine -ā, and left that vowel unchanged. This is a best-effort derivation, not one checked against a specific sūtra.

<answer>आक्तात्रा</answer>

The affix तमप् (SLP1 `tamap`) is the superlative suffix of "अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ" (Pāṇini 5.3.55). The final प् is only a marker and drops. Adding तम to the stem द्रव्यादर्श gives the stem द्रव्यादर्शतम.

<answer>द्रव्यादर्शतम</answer>
<answer>चाण्डाल्य</answer>

I could not match this input to a rule that licenses थमु (Pāṇini teaches it only after इदम् and किम्, as in इत्थम् and कथम्). So I applied the affix mechanically to the given stem.

थमु begins with a consonant, so the stem does not count as *bha* (भ) before it. That means the feminine stem is not replaced by its masculine form (no puṃvadbhāva). The ending -ā stays, and the affix is added directly, giving ज्यायमानाथम्.

<answer>ज्यायमानाथम्</answer>

I did not trace a specific Pāṇinian rule for adding वलच् to this stem, so this rests on the general mechanics of the affix. The affix वलच् leaves the base वल after its indicatory letters ल् and च् drop. Because वल begins with a consonant, the final ा of नावनीया is not elided. Attaching it directly gives the stem नावनीयावल.

<answer>नावनीयावल</answer>

The affix देश्य (deśya) is one of the affixes taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, which are added to a nominal in the sense of "slightly short of complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). Adding it to शिङ्गय needs no sandhi or other change, so the derived stem is शिङ्गयदेश्य, meaning roughly "almost a Śiṅgaya".

<answer>शिङ्गयदेश्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses यत् after इलावृत, so this form is derived mechanically rather than from a confirmed sūtra.

The affix यत् is not ñit or ṇit, so it triggers no vṛddhi (strengthening) of the stem's initial vowel. Before the affix's initial य, the stem-final अ of इलावृत is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148). That gives इलावृत् + य, which joins as इलावृत्य.

<answer>इलावृत्य</answer>

I did not trace the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् after तुत्थ, so this form rests on the general mechanism and my recollection. अञ् (aY) is a ञित् affix, so it causes vṛddhi of the first vowel (उ → औ). The final अ of तुत्थ drops before the affix.

तुत्थ + अञ् → तौत्थ

<answer>तौत्थ</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation; I did not check it against a source.

1. The affix च्वि is added to हुताशिन्. Its initial च् and its final इ drop as markers, which leaves only व्.
2. The remaining व् is deleted by 6.1.67 (वेरपृक्तस्य).
3. The affix falls in the range of affixes that make the stem a pada (1.4.17 and following). The final न् of the stem therefore drops by 8.2.7, giving हुताशि.
4. Before च्वि, the final vowel of an अच्-ending stem is lengthened by 7.4.26 (च्वौ च). So इ becomes ई, giving हुताशी.

The result is an indeclinable, as in "हुताशी भवति".

<answer>हुताशी</answer>

I applied दघ्नच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) to the stem, but I did not check that this affix is licensed for सदृक् specifically.

The affix is added directly, and the final च् is only a marker, so it leaves दघ्न. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem सदृक् counts as a pada (1.4.17). Its final क् therefore becomes ग् by 8.2.39. This gives सदृग् + दघ्न.

<answer>सदृग्दघ्न</answer>

I applied द्वयसच् (dvayasac, taught in 5.2.37) to विद्या. I did not check that the affix's meaning condition is actually met for विद्या; the task allows any licensed meaning, so I took it as satisfied.

The affix begins with द्, which is neither a vowel nor य्. So the stem does not count as a "bha" stem before it (यचि भम्, 1.4.18). The elision of the final आ by यस्येति च (6.4.148) therefore does not apply, and the stem keeps its आ. The result is विद्या + द्वयस. The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter and drops out.

<answer>विद्याद्वयस</answer>

The derivative is formed by adding the taddhita affix कन् to the stem रिप्र. The affix loses its marker letters (the final न्, and the क् is the affix itself, which remains) and surfaces as the suffix -क. This gives the stem रिप्रक. I did not trace a specific Pāṇinian rule for this stem and gender, so this is the regular -क formation. The meaning could be any licensed for कन्, such as contempt or diminutive.

<answer>रिप्रक</answer>
<answer>सूत्रयितव्यदेश्य</answer>

Here मात्रच् is added to the stem भौरिकिक under the rule that gives measure (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नमात्रचः, 5.2.37). The affix मात्र begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped. The affix is not ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi. The derived stem is therefore भौरिकिक + मात्र.

<answer>भौरिकिकमात्र</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses the affix कुणप् (kuṇap), so this form is a derivation from general taddhita principles, not a confirmed one.

The affix is कुण with a final-p marker that only affects accent. Its ण् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem: असनिका becomes आसनिका.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final -ā is not dropped. I assumed no shortening of the ā applies, though I could not confirm this. Adding कुण gives the form below.

<answer>आसनिकाकुण</answer>
<answer>रोध्यदेश्य</answer>

I added मतुप् to the stem पौष्पिण्ड्य and applied the usual substitution of व for the म of मत् (8.2.9). The stem ends in अ, which triggers that substitution, so मत् becomes वत्. The stem is a pada before मतुप्, so the final अ of -ड्य is not dropped by यस्येति च. The resulting stem is पौष्पिण्ड्यवत् (nominative singular पौष्पिण्ड्यवान्).

<answer>पौष्पिण्ड्यवत्</answer>

Here the affix चुञ्चुप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), used in the sense "known by that". I recalled this sūtra from memory rather than checking it.

The final प् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix as चुञ्चु. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of ओदनिक is not elided (the elision rule यस्येति च needs a vowel-initial or ई/य-type affix). The stem therefore simply takes the affix.

<answer>ओदनिकचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>ईश्वराधीनजातीय</answer>

Applying मयट् (P.4.3.82, in the sense of "made of" or "a modification of") to क्षिप्रेषु gives the derivative below. The final ट् of the affix is only an indicatory marker, so the affix is effectively मय.

Because मय begins with a consonant other than य, the stem is not treated as *bha*, so the guṇa rule ओर्गुणः (P.6.4.146) does not apply. The final उ of the stem therefore stays unchanged, as in अश्ममय.

<answer>क्षिप्रेषुमय</answer>
<answer>फालिक</answer>

The affix ञ्यट् contributes -य. Its ञ् marks vṛddhi of the first vowel, so अ becomes आ. Its ट् only licenses the feminine in -ई. I could not identify the specific sūtra for this affix, so the form rests on the standard rules for ञित् taddhita affixes.

1. अर्घीश + य, with vṛddhi of the first syllable, gives आर्घीश + य.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the taddhita य by यस्येति च, which gives आर्घीश्य.

The ई inside the stem is not word-final, so it stays.

<answer>आर्घीश्य</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, not checked against a source. I take the affix चणप् to be the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), used in the sense "known by that". The final प् is only an indicatory marker and drops out.

The affix is चण. It is added to याष्टीक, and the stem's final अ is deleted before it by "यस्येति च". The result is याष्टीकचण. I did not work out the meaning or the gender in any further detail.

<answer>याष्टीकचण</answer>
<answer>आहेयतम</answer>

This derivation is applied mechanically: द्यूत is not a direction word (दिक्शब्द), which is what Pāṇini's rule for this affix (5.3.27) normally requires. I formed it as follows.

1. The affix अस्ताति is added to the stem द्यूत, giving द्यूत + अस्ताति.
2. The stem's final अ is dropped before the affix, by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च).
3. The final इ of the affix is dropped, as in पुरस्तात्, leaving the ending अस्तात्.
4. The result is the indeclinable द्यूतस्तात्.

<answer>द्यूतस्तात्</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) is added to the stem to mean "somewhat, not quite". The neuter stem शात्रवेङ्गित already ends in a short -a, so it takes the affix directly and no vowel shortening (1.2.47) is needed. The affix gives a stem ending in -a, meaning roughly "somewhat like शात्रवेङ्गित".

<answer>शात्रवेङ्गितदेशीय</answer>

Applying ढक् (Qak) to the stem पुस्ता follows these steps:

1. The initial ढ् of the affix is replaced by एय (ḍh → eya).
2. The final आ of the stem पुस्ता is dropped before the affix.
3. The first vowel takes vṛddhi, so पु becomes पौ.

This gives पौस्तेय. I did not recall the exact sūtra or example list that includes पुस्ता, so the choice of ढक् with the apatya ("descendant") sense rests on the general rule for feminine stems (स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्, 4.1.120).

<answer>पौस्तेय</answer>

This is an application of the affix *dvayasac* (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure). The final *c* of the affix is only an indicatory letter, and *dvayasac* is not marked as ḍit. So the final *a* of the base वैभोज is not deleted, because the affix begins with a consonant. The affix *-dvayasa* is simply added to the base. I did not check whether this particular base is attested with the affix.

<answer>वैभोजद्वयस</answer>

The affix रूपप् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्) to a word that expresses praise, so खण्डक with रूपप् means "an excellent खण्डक". The final प् is only a marker, so what remains is रूप, which attaches directly to the stem without any change. This gives the stem खण्डकरूप.

<answer>खण्डकरूप</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule, so the form below is a best-effort derivation rather than a confirmed one. Pāṇini 5.3.27 normally attaches the affix अस्ताति to direction words, as in पुरस्तात्, and कूड्य is not one. I formed it mechanically: the stem कूड्य plus the vowel-initial affix, whose final इ drops out as in पुरस्तात्, leaves अस्तात्. The stem-final अ is deleted before that vowel-initial affix (6.4.148), giving कूड्य् + अस्तात्.

<answer>कूड्यस्तात्</answer>
<answer>औदन्वतस्तात्</answer>
<answer>पाशुपतिक</answer>

Derivation (the puṃvadbhāva step is my reading of the rule, not something I confirmed):

1. The stem श्वेतौही is the feminine of श्वेतवाह. It is built with ङीप्, and ऊठ् replaces वाह् (वाह ऊठ्), giving श्वेतौही.
2. The affix तसिल् (written तसि here) is added to a stem in the fifth-case (ablative) sense.
3. Before तसिल् and similar affixes, rule 6.3.35 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः) gives a feminine stem the masculine form (पुंवद्भाव). I take this to apply here, so श्वेतौही reverts to श्वेतवाह.
4. श्वेतवाह + तसि gives श्वेतवाहतः.

<answer>श्वेतवाहतः</answer>

The affix तल् (SLP1 `tal`) is added in the sense of "state or quality" (भावे, "the state of being …"). The final ल् and the initial त् of तल् are markers (इत्) that drop out, leaving only त. A stem formed with तल् is always feminine, so the feminine ending ā (टाप्) is added, giving ता.

वलितापाङ्ग + तल् → वलितापाङ्ग + ता → वलितापाङ्गता

<answer>वलितापाङ्गता</answer>

The affix चरट् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, "भूतपूर्वे चरट्", meaning "formerly so-and-so". It is added to the nominal stem बलाबल. The ट् is only a marker letter and drops, leaving the suffix -चर. The final अ of the stem is not affected here, so the form is simply बलाबल + चर.

<answer>बलाबलचर</answer>
<answer>कलाशुरिमत्</answer>

I am forming this from my memory of the rule rather than checking a source. The affix साति is added to a stem to mean "made dependent on" or "wholly" (as in राजसात् करोति, "makes it dependent on the king"). The final इ is only a marker, so the affix appears as सात्, and the stem तैकायन is unchanged. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>तैकायनसात्</answer>

Applying अण् to कौमोदी, the stem-final ई is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), leaving कौमोद + अ. The first vowel औ is already vṛddhi, so अण् (which has the ṇ marker) causes no further change. The result is कौमोद.

<answer>कौमोद</answer>
<answer>कौस्तुभ</answer>

I could not match the stem to a specific rule that licenses लच् (the affix surfaces as -ल), so this derivation is a best-effort application of the general mechanism rather than a confirmed one.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem does not take the "bha" designation (1.4.18) and the vowel-deletion rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not apply. The final -ā of the feminine stem therefore stays, and -ल is simply added to it.

<answer>रतारम्भावसानिकाल</answer>
<answer>उभयीयास्तात्</answer>
<answer>वासनीयता</answer>

Applying the affix अण् to नीव:

1. The affix अण् carries a ण् marker, which triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem. So नी becomes नै.
2. The final अ of नीव is dropped before the affix's initial vowel, leaving नैव्.
3. Adding अ gives नैव.

This is an application of the general rules, not a specific sūtra that names नीव. The meaning, such as "related to नीव", is left open.

<answer>नैव</answer>

The affix कन् (kan) is added to the stem कहय. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, and the affix's own marker letters (क् and न्) are removed, which leaves just क. This gives कहय् + क = कहयक. I did not check this against a specific sūtra, and the stem कहय is unusual, so this is the regular formation rather than a confirmed attested word.

<answer>कहयक</answer>

I could not match this exact stem to a documented example, so this form comes from applying the general rule rather than a known attested word.

The affix द्वयसच् is taught in the measure sense by प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः (5.2.37). The final च् is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix द्वयस. Because द्वयस begins with a consonant, the rule यस्य च (6.4.148), which deletes a stem-final अ before a vowel-initial affix, does not apply. The stem's final अ therefore stays, and the form is लोहितक + द्वयस.

<answer>लोहितकद्वयस</answer>

The stem ध्वस्ति (feminine, ending in -i) takes the affix कन्. The final न् is an it-marker and drops, leaving the affix -क. Adding it gives ध्वस्ति + क = ध्वस्तिक. I did not add the feminine suffix टाप् (which would give ध्वस्तिका), since the task asks only for the taddhita derivative itself. I also did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule for this stem, so the derivation is the general one.

<answer>ध्वस्तिक</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule example, so this is a straightforward formation. The affix दघ्नच् (daghnac) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), in the sense of measure. The final -च् is only a marker and drops. The affix is appended directly to the stem भार्गवोपाख्यान, giving the stem form below.

<answer>भार्गवोपाख्यानदघ्न</answer>
<answer>खाण्डविका</answer>

I formed this by adding the superlative suffix तमप् (the final प् is only a marker) directly to the nominal stem आभयजात. This follows the rule अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, under which तमप् is added to a nominal stem to mean "most". No sandhi or other change applies here, so the result is आभयजात + तम.

<answer>आभयजाततम</answer>
<answer>आप्यदेशीय</answer>

Applying the affix khañ to आरट gives आरटीन. I could not trace which sūtra licenses khañ for this stem, so this derivation rests only on the general rules for the affix.

1. The initial kh of खञ् is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, Pāṇini 7.1.2).
2. The ञ् is only an indicatory letter. It triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the initial आ of आरट is already a vṛddhi vowel, so nothing changes.
3. The final अ of आरट is dropped before the affix, giving आरट् + ईन = आरटीन.

<answer>आरटीन</answer>

Because शैर्ष्य begins with a vṛddhi vowel (ऐ), it is a vṛddha stem. Pāṇini 4.2.114, *vṛddhāc chaḥ*, then lets the affix छ apply in the sense "belonging to that" (śaiṣika). I am taking this rule as the licence for the affix here.

1. छ is replaced by ईय (7.1.2, *āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām*), giving शैर्ष्य + ईय.
2. The final अ of शैर्ष्य is dropped before ईय (6.4.148, *yasyeti ca*), which leaves शैर्ष्य् + ईय.
3. Joining these gives शैर्ष्यीय.

<answer>शैर्ष्यीय</answer>
<answer>ऐतरतः</answer>

Per Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), the affix देशीयर् is added to a subanta in the sense "almost, but not completely." The final र् is only an indicatory letter and drops out, leaving the affix देशीय.

The affix begins with a consonant (द), so स्यूमन् still counts as a pada before it. The final न् of the stem is therefore deleted (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य). This gives स्यूम + देशीय = स्यूमदेशीय.

<answer>स्यूमदेशीय</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), the affix चुञ्चुप् leaves the form चुञ्चु after the final indicatory letter drops. It is added to a stem meaning "known by it", as in विद्याचुञ्चु. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem धृतक keeps its final -अ and the two simply join.

<answer>धृतकचुञ्चु</answer>

<answer>लाट</answer>

This is a derivation from the stem लाट with अण्. The first vowel is already ā, so the vṛddhi substitution leaves the stem unchanged, and the final अ of the stem drops before the affix अ. The result is लाट, meaning "belonging to Lāṭa" (the tasyedam sense). I did not check this against a source.
<answer>मौल्यजातीय</answer>

The affix ईयसुन् forms a comparative from the stem. Before ईयसुन्, rule 6.4.154 (तुरिष्ठेमेयःसु) deletes the टि of the base. For ग्रहाह्वय, the टि is the final अ. This leaves ग्रहाह्वय्, which joins with ईयस् to give ग्रहाह्वयीयस्. I derived this from the grammar rules and did not check it against a reference form.

<answer>ग्रहाह्वयीयस्</answer>

Rule 5.4.45 (apādāne ca) allows तसि (tasiL) after a nominal stem in the sense of separation (ablative), as in ग्रामतः and मथुरातः. This is from memory, not checked against a text. I could not identify a rule that changes a stem in -ā before this affix, so the stem शीपल्या stays unchanged. Adding तस् gives शीपल्यातस्, and the final स् becomes visarga because the form is an indeclinable.

<answer>शीपल्यातः</answer>

I could not find a rule that licenses थमु after the stem दारि. In Pāṇini's grammar this affix is taught only after इदम् (इत्थम्) and किम् (कथम्). I therefore simply attached the affix to the stem as given. The final उ of थमु is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the ending थम्. The stem's final इ undergoes no change before a consonant-initial affix, so the form is दारिथम्. This is an unverified, mechanical formation.

<answer>दारिथम्</answer>

The stem फाली ends in the feminine suffix ई. Before a taddhita affix, this ई is dropped by the rule यस्येति च, leaving फाल्. The affix ठन् has initial ठ, which is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः). Since ठन् is not marked ञित् or णित्, there is no vṛddhi. This gives फाल् + इक = फालिक. I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठन् after फाली, so the derivation rests on the general affix rules above.

<answer>फालिक</answer>

The affix चणप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), meaning "known or famed by that". It is added to a word in the instrumental sense. I am recalling this rule from memory rather than checking it.

The final प् is only a marker and drops out, so the affix is effectively -चण. The stem ends in -अ and the affix begins with a consonant, so no vowel change applies. The result is the stem plus the affix.

<answer>अभ्रायितचण</answer>
<answer>द्वारकमात्र</answer>

I did not derive this step by step. I reasoned from the rule I recall for this affix, Pāṇini 5.2.37, where दघ्नच् is added in the sense of a measure (as in जानुदघ्न, "knee-deep"). I am not certain the affix is licensed for this particular stem, but it is the reading I used.

The affix begins with a consonant (द्), so the stem's final ई is not dropped by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148), which only applies before affixes starting with a vowel or य्. The stem therefore stays सागरापाङ्गी. The final च् of दघ्नच् is only a marker (it) and drops, leaving दघ्न.

<answer>सागरापाङ्गीदघ्न</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् (P. 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to the stem. The final च् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix is द्वयस. It begins with a consonant, so the stem दर्शनावरणीय is left unchanged and the affix is simply attached. This gives the derived stem ending in -अ.

<answer>दर्शनावरणीयद्वयस</answer>

I could not identify a specific rule that licenses अञ् on this stem, so this is a mechanical derivation rather than a rule-backed one.

The stem पापानुबन्ध ends in अ, and that final अ is dropped before the affix. The affix अञ् has ञ् as an indicatory letter, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. That vowel is already पा (long आ), so nothing changes. Adding the affix's अ gives पापानुबन्ध, identical in spelling to the stem.

<answer>पापानुबन्ध</answer>

I could not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that attaches वलच् to कौशी, so this is a best-effort derivation rather than a rule-backed one. I simply added वलच् (with the final च् as a marker that drops) to the stem as it stands. I kept the long ई, as in the licensed forms like कृषीवल. I did not apply any shortening of the feminine ई.

<answer>कौशीवल</answer>
<answer>अरण्यकमय</answer>

The derivative is formed by adding तमप् (tamap) to the feminine stem द्वैतवना.

Before the ghа affixes तरप् and तमप्, a stem ending in a feminine suffix (ङ्यāप्) takes a short final vowel (P. 6.3.43). I am recalling that rule from memory rather than checking it, so the shortening is the part I am least sure of. On that basis, द्वैतवना becomes द्वैतवन, and adding तमप् gives द्वैतवनतम. The feminine form would be द्वैतवनतमा.

<answer>द्वैतवनतम</answer>

The affix बहुच् (Pāṇini 5.3.68, *vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt*) is added before the word, in the sense of "somewhat, almost" (*īṣadasamāpti*). It therefore gives बहु + भ्राजिन्. The base keeps its final न्, since the stem is treated as a basic nominal stem, and the result is बहुभ्राजिन्.

<answer>बहुभ्राजिन्</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), where it marks something defective or deserving of censure. It is added to the stem जोटिङ्ग with no change to the stem's final vowel. The result is the stem जोटिङ्गपाश, as in the pattern याज्ञिकपाश.

<answer>जोटिङ्गपाश</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation. I could not tie the affix "rūpya" cleanly to a single Pāṇinian rule for this input, so I treated it as an affix of the rūpa type.

The input stem पाचनीया is feminine and already ends in a feminine suffix. It has more than one syllable, so the shortening rule 6.3.43 applies before rūpa-type affixes. Final ā becomes a, giving पाचनीय. Adding the affix gives पाचनीय + रूप्य = पाचनीयरूप्य.

<answer>पाचनीयरूप्य</answer>
<answer>नूततम</answer>

I treated भस्मका as the feminine of भस्मक and applied the standard steps for adding अण् to a stem ending in ā:

1. Before the taddhita affix अण्, the final feminine ā of भस्मका is dropped (6.4.148), leaving भस्मक.
2. Since अण् is a ṇit affix, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (भ → भा, 7.2.117).
3. Adding अण् gives भास्मक.

I derived this from the rules as I recall them and did not check it against a dictionary or commentary.

<answer>भास्मक</answer>

I could not match रजत to a licensed use of this affix. Pāṇini's rule for थमु (5.3.24, 5.3.25) applies only to इदम् and किम्, so this answer is a mechanical formation, not an attested word.

The final उ of थमु is an indicatory letter (it) and drops, leaving the affix as थम्. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of रजत is not elided. The result is रजत + थम् = रजतथम्. As a taddhita ending in a non-case-varying affix, it is indeclinable.

The stem तीव्रान्ता ends in ā, so I applied the rule प्राणिस्थादातो लजन्यतरस्याम् (5.2.96). That rule adds लच् to an ā-ending stem, in the sense "having that", as in चूडा → चूडालः.

I assumed तीव्रान्ता qualifies as a word for something located in a living being, because the table does not confirm this.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as a *bha* stem and the final ā is not elided. Adding the masculine ending of the derivative's stem gives:

तीव्रान्ता + ल → तीव्रान्तालः, with stem तीव्रान्तालः.

<answer>तीव्रान्तालः</answer>

Adding the affix यत् (initial य) to the stem उदवसानीय gives the result below. The stem ends in the vowel अ, which is dropped before a taddhita beginning with य (rule 6.4.148, यस्येति च). This leaves उदवसानीय् followed by य, which joins as उदवसानीय्य. I did not identify the specific sūtra licensing यत् here, so this rests only on the sandhi rule.

<answer>उदवसानीय्य</answer>

In Pāṇini 5.4.52 (*vibhāṣā sāti kārtsnye*) the affix is the one that yields forms like *agnisāt*. I am relying on memory for the final shape: the surface suffix is सात्, with the final -इ of the technical name साति not appearing in the output. The result is an indeclinable.

The stem सातय ends in -a, and सात् begins with a consonant, so nothing is elided or changed at the junction. The form is therefore सातय + सात् = सातयसात्.

<answer>सातयसात्</answer>

This is a standard application of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), where द्वयसच् is added to a noun to denote measure. I did not check whether भ्रमि is a usual base for this affix. The final च् of द्वयसच् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the suffix द्वयस.

The suffix begins with a consonant, so the base does not take the "bha" status under 1.4.18 (यचि भम्). Because of that, the final इ of भ्रमि is not elided under 6.4.148, and the stem stays intact: भ्रमि + द्वयस = भ्रमिद्वयस.

<answer>भ्रमिद्वयस</answer>
<answer>समन्तालोकीय</answer>

I could not identify which Pāṇinian rule introduces रूप्य after पुष. Pāṇini 5.2.120 gives यप् after रूप, not after पुष. I therefore simply joined the stem and the affix, assuming no sandhi or other change applies. This is a best guess.

<answer>पुषरूप्य</answer>

I could not match the affix थमु (Tamu) to शाली by any specific Pāṇinian rule. Pāṇini's थमु (5.3.24–25) is taught only after इदम् and किम्. So I applied it to शाली directly, and the result is a best guess rather than a derivation I could confirm.

थमु has a final उ as an indicator letter, which drops, leaving the affix -थम्. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem does not take the भ designation (1.4.18 requires an affix beginning with य् or a vowel). That means the final ई of शाली is neither deleted nor shortened. Adding -थम् gives an indeclinable form.

<answer>शालीथम्</answer>

I could not identify the rule that introduces जाहच्, so this form rests on an assumed analysis of the affix rather than a confirmed source.

I took the initial ज् and final च् as indicatory letters, which leaves the actual affix as आह. Because the affix is जित्, the first vowel of the stem would take vṛddhi. The stem's first vowel is already ऐ, so nothing changes there. The final अ of वैद्यावतंस is dropped before the vowel-initial affix, giving वैद्यावतंस + आह = वैद्यावतंसाह.

<answer>वैद्यावतंसाह</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them, not checked against the Aṣṭādhyāyī text. I also could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ṭhak on this stem, so the meaning is unspecified.

1. The affix ṭhak becomes ika by "ṭhasyekaḥ".
2. The affix is kit, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi by "kiti ca": pa → pā, giving पावीतृ + इक.
3. The final ṛ meets the initial vowel i of the suffix. I assumed yaṇ-sandhi applies here, as in pitṛ + ya → pitrya and bhrātṛ + īya → bhrātrīya. That turns ṛ into र् and gives the stem पावीत्रिक.

<answer>पावीत्रिक</answer>

The taddhita affix रूपप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*, and is added after a subanta word in the sense of praise. The sup ending is dropped, so the stem स्थौलाष्टीवि simply takes रूप after it, as in पटुरूप or विद्वद्रूप. This gives the derived stem स्थौलाष्टीविरूप, meaning "an excellent Sthaulāṣṭīvi".

<answer>स्थौलाष्टीविरूप</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् on this stem, so this derivation applies the general taddhita rules and is not checked against a source.

1. The affix is ञ्यट्, which leaves the suffix -य after dropping the markers ञ् and ट्.
2. Because the suffix is ञित् (carries the marker ञ्), the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: सृ becomes सार्.
3. The stem ends in -इन्. Before a taddhita suffix, the final syllable (ṭi) of a stem ending in न् is dropped (नस्तद्धिते, 6.4.144). So सृगायिन् becomes सृगाय्.
4. Adding य gives सृगाय् + य, and with the vṛddhi from step 2 this is सार्गाय्य.

<answer>सार्गाय्य</answer>
<answer>कृतानुसारशः</answer>

I did not trace the exact Pāṇinian rule number for this affix, so this derivation is partly from memory. The affix त्रा replaces a second-case or seventh-case ending, as in देवत्रा. I take 6.3.35 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः), which gives the masculine-like (pumvat) stem before affixes from तसिल् up to कृत्वसुच्, not to cover त्रा. So the feminine stem keeps its long आ and the affix is added directly: अमृताभिषिक्ता + त्रा.
