3. ढक् carries the marker क्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117–118): म → मा.
4. Combining gives मात्त + एय = मात्तेय.

<answer>मात्तेय</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् here, so this form comes from applying the affix's markers to the stem, not from a confirmed rule.

The affix is ञ्यट्, whose actual ending is ‑य. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, so ओ becomes औ. The final अ of ओजायित is dropped before the ending (6.4.148). Adding ‑य gives औजायित्य. The marker ट् only shapes the feminine, so it does not change this stem form.

<answer>औजायित्य</answer>

This is a direct affixation. The affix दघ्नच् (daghnac) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37, where it denotes measure. Its final च् is only an indicatory marker (it), so the affix effectively adds दघ्न to the stem. Because the affix begins with a consonant, the final अ of शोणाक is not elided (the elision rule 6.4.148 applies only before vowel-initial affixes). The stem and affix therefore simply join, giving शोणाकदघ्न. I have not checked whether this particular stem is attested with the affix.

<answer>शोणाकदघ्न</answer>

I formed this by hand from the grammar rules, without checking it against a source. The affix ठन् (ṭhan) has its ठ replaced by इक by the rule ठस्येकः (7.3.50). The stem's final -अ is dropped before the affix. ठन् carries no ञ or ण marker, so there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel. The special substitution of क for ठ (7.3.51) does not apply, because the stem ends in neither इस्, उस्, उक् nor त. The result is महानुशंसक + इक.

<answer>महानुशंसकिक</answer>

I have not matched this to a specific rule, since the stem भार्याट is unusual. This form follows the general pattern for the affix थाल्.

The affix is थाल्, and its final ल् is only a marker (it-letter) that drops. What remains is the ending था, which is added directly to the stem. The affix begins with a consonant, so nothing is deleted from the stem's final अ, and no sandhi change applies. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>भार्याटथा</answer>
<answer>वैयापदेय</answer>
<answer>आनकतर</answer>

Rule 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*, adds the affix रूपप् to a nominal stem when the sense is "praiseworthy". The final प् is only a marker and drops out. Adding रूप to the stem ऋच requires no sandhi change, so the result is ऋचरूप, "a praiseworthy ṛc".

<answer>ऋचरूप</answer>

I did not fully settle whether पुंवद्भाव (the masculine-form substitution before a taddhita) applies here. I assumed it does not, because तल् (5.1.119) falls outside the range of 6.3.38. On that basis the stem's final ा is kept, and तल् becomes ता, which takes the feminine ā-ending (टाप्). This gives निहाका + ता = निहाकाता.

<answer>निहाकाता</answer>

The affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय by the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम् (7.1.2). This gives रश्मन् + ईय. The stem ends in न्, so before this taddhita affix its final अन् (the टि) is dropped by नस्तद्धिते (6.4.144). The result is रश्म् + ईय = रश्मीय.

I did not identify which specific rule licenses छ after रश्मन्. The form follows only from the standard छ → ईय substitution and the टि-deletion.

<answer>रश्मीय</answer>
<answer>वैरण</answer>

The affix कल्पप् is taught in P. 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), where it means "slightly less than complete". It is added directly to the nominal stem. The stem वातोन ends in -a, so nothing changes at the junction, and the final प् is only an indicator letter (it affects accent) and does not appear in the form.

वातोन + कल्प = वातोनकल्प

<answer>वातोनकल्प</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.2.37, the affix मात्रच् is added in the sense of measure (pramāṇa). The final च् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix is effectively मात्र. It is not marked ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi and the stem आर stays unchanged. Adding मात्र to आर gives आरमात्र.

<answer>आरमात्र</answer>
<answer>समानोदर्कथा</answer>

I take the affix to be the one in Pāṇini 5.2.26, "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ", which gives forms like केशचण, "known by (his) hair". This is a recalled sūtra, and I did not find a source that attests a form built on मलीमस.

The affix चण begins with a consonant. Pāṇini 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), which drops a final अ before a vowel-initial affix, therefore does not apply. The final अ of मलीमस stays, and no vṛddhi applies, so the form is simply मलीमस + चण.

<answer>मलीमसचण</answer>

The affix मयट् is added to वृक्ष to give the derived stem वृक्षमय, "made of wood" or "consisting of a tree". I am recalling the relevant rules (such as 4.3.150) from memory rather than checking them. The final ट् drops as an indicatory letter (it-marker), leaving the ending -मय, which joins the a-ending stem: वृक्ष + मय → वृक्षमय. The ट् marker would give the feminine वृक्षमयी, but the question asks for the base stem.

<answer>वृक्षमय</answer>

I took the affix ठक् (Wak) as the usual taddhita ending with इक substituted for ठ. I did not identify a special rule for this particular stem, so the derivation follows the general rules.

1. In ठक्, the initial ठ् is replaced by इक (7.3.50), and the final क् is a marker that drops. The affix therefore acts as इक.
2. Because the affix has a marker क्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.118 *किति च*). So क becomes का.
3. The final इ of कच्छपारि is dropped before the affix (6.4.148 *यस्येति च*).
4. This gives काच्छपार् + इक = काच्छपारिक.

<answer>काच्छपारिक</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which means "almost, not quite complete". It is added to the subanta (stem with its case ending). Since कल्पप् begins with a consonant, वपुस् counts as a pada before it, so its final स् becomes a visarga. A visarga after उ and before क is replaced by ष् (8.3.41). This gives वपुष्कल्प, "almost a body" (not quite a body).

<answer>वपुष्कल्प</answer>

The stem लौमायना is feminine and ends in -ā. Before the affix जातीयर् (P. 5.3.69, in the प्रकार "kind of" sense), a feminine stem takes masculine treatment (पुंवद्भाव, P. 6.3.35). The feminine -ā is therefore dropped, giving लौमायन + जातीय. This is my reading of the rule, not a check against a source.

<answer>लौमायनजातीय</answer>

This is a derivation from memory of the relevant Pāṇinian rules, not one I checked against a source.

तरप् is added to the whole word त्रैनिष्किका, which is already feminine, so the result is त्रैनिष्किका + तर. The rule that shortens a final vowel before तरप् (6.3.43, ङ्योऽनेकाचो ह्रस्वः) covers stems ending in ङी-type suffixes, as in ब्राह्मणितरा. It does not cover a stem ending in the टाप् feminine ā, so the ā stays long. Since the source is feminine, the derivative takes the feminine ending again, giving त्रैनिष्किकातरा. I am not fully certain the question wants the feminine form rather than the bare stem त्रैनिष्किकातर.

<answer>त्रैनिष्किकातरा</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), the affix कल्पप् is added after a nominal stem to mean "almost, nearly" (ईषदसमाप्ति). The final प् is only a marker and drops out, leaving the ending -कल्प. Adding it to वोर gives the stem वोरकल्प ("almost a वोर").

<answer>वोरकल्प</answer>

The stem लावण्यार्जिता ends in the feminine suffix टाप् (long ā), and the affix मतुप् is added to it with its ā retained. Because the stem ends in the vowel आ, मतुप् takes the form वत् (by 8.2.9, मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः). This gives लावण्यार्जितावत्, "possessed of charm-won qualities" (a possessive derivative).

<answer>लावण्यार्जितावत्</answer>

I could not identify the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix साति, so this form rests on an assumption. Because साति begins with the consonant स्, the stem should keep its final -ā rather than lose it as it would before a vowel-initial taddhita. I therefore simply joined the stem and the affix.

<answer>इन्धासाति</answer>

The affix लच् is added to the feminine stem उत्कण्ठिता, which ends in आ. Before the taddhita affix, the final आ of the stem drops (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), leaving उत्कण्ठित. Adding ल (the च् is only an it-marker) gives उत्कण्ठित + ल = उत्कण्ठितल.

I did not trace this to a specific example in the grammar. The rule I relied on is 5.2.96, which allows ल after a stem ending in आ, but it is stated for stems denoting something in a living being, and उत्कण्ठिता does not obviously fit that. The result is therefore my best derivation rather than a confirmed attested form.

<answer>उत्कण्ठितल</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces ञ्यट्, so this derivation rests on the markers in the affix, not on a rule I could cite.

The affix itself is just "य". The initial ञ् is an it-letter that makes the initial vowel take vṛddhi. The final ट् is also an it-letter, which only conditions the feminine ending ङीप्.

The first vowel of आनन्दाश्रम is already आ, a vṛddhi vowel, so vṛddhi changes nothing. The final अ of the stem drops before the vowel-initial affix. This gives आनन्दाश्रम् + य = आनन्दाश्रम्य.

<answer>आनन्दाश्रम्य</answer>

Adding तल् (bhāva sense, "the state of being X") to कौरुकुल्लक gives कौरुकुल्लक + तल्. The final ल् is a marker (it) and drops, leaving the suffix त. A stem formed with तल् is feminine (by P. 4.1.3, टाप् is added), so it ends in ता. No other change applies to the stem. The result is कौरुकुल्लकता.

<answer>कौरुकुल्लकता</answer>

The affix कल्पप् (kalpap, Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.67, "somewhat like") is added to the stem शालभा. Since the stem ends in a feminine ā-suffix, its final vowel is shortened before the affix (I recall this as 6.3.43 but did not check the sūtra number), giving शालभ + कल्प. The derivative keeps the feminine gender of the source, so the stem takes the feminine -ā: शालभकल्पा.

I reconstructed the shortening rule and the feminine ending from memory, so the form rests on that recollection.

<answer>शालभकल्पा</answer>

I could not tie this affix to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The nearest rule, 5.2.120, adds *yap* to the base *rūpa*, which does not fit this stem. So I treated रूप्य as an ordinary suffix added directly to the stem पेष्ट्र (peṣṭra), a stem ending in -a.

The suffix begins with the consonant र, not a vowel or *y*. The rule that drops a stem-final -a (6.4.148) therefore does not apply, and the stem stays unchanged. The result is plain concatenation.

<answer>पेष्ट्ररूप्य</answer>

The taddhita affix तल् (tal) is added to the stem मेत्थित to express the sense of "state or quality" (bhāva). The affix leaves only ता, and the derivative takes the feminine ending -ā. It joins the stem without any sandhi change, giving मेत्थितता.

<answer>मेत्थितता</answer>

This is my own derivation from the general rules, since I did not identify a specific sūtra for ठक् on a feminine stem ending in आ.

1. ठक् becomes इक by ṭhasyekaḥ (7.3.50), after the initial ठ is replaced.
2. The final आ of प्रेमा drops before the taddhita ending by yasyeti ca (6.4.148), leaving प्रेम् + इक.
3. ठक् carries the marker क्, so it is kit. The first vowel therefore takes vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (7.2.117) and kiti ca (7.2.118). The ए of प्रे is replaced by ऐ, giving प्रैम् + इक = प्रैमिक.

<answer>प्रैमिक</answer>
<answer>कौलीनक</answer>
<answer>क्षौद्रकता</answer>

The affix cvi is added to a nominal stem with the sense "becoming what it was not before". The rule *asya cvau* (7.4.32) replaces the final -a of the stem with ī before cvi, and cvi itself is then wholly elided. The stem वादान्य ends in -a, so it becomes वादान्यी (for example, in वादान्यीभवति).

<answer>वादान्यी</answer>

The affix is कल्पप् (ईषदसमाप्तौ, "almost, not quite complete"), so भेला + कल्पप् gives "one who is nearly a भेला". I did not confirm whether the rule that shortens a stem-final long vowel before कल्पप् (6.3.43) applies to a stem ending in आ. I assumed it covers only stems ending in ई, so the आ stays long.

<answer>भेलाकल्पा</answer>

I derived this from the general rules, not from a specific sūtra that I could pin down.

The stem is कॢप्ता, a feminine ṭāp-stem in -ā, and the affix is यत्, which leaves the suffix -य after the markers are dropped. A stem-final -ā is elided before an affix beginning with य, by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), as I understand that rule. So कॢप्त् + य gives कॢप्त्य.

<answer>कॢप्त्य</answer>

This is the affix चरट् of Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), added to a nominal stem to mean "formerly that". I could not confirm whether a puṃvadbhāva (masculine-form substitution) rule applies to a feminine stem here, so I added the affix to निमित्तका without changing its final ā. This is my best judgment, not a verified derivation.

<answer>निमित्तकाचर</answer>

The stem मारिषा loses its final -ā before the vowel-initial affix, by the rule "yasyeti ca" (6.4.148). In ठक्, the initial ठ् is replaced by इक (7.3.50), so the affix becomes -इक. Joining them gives मारिष + इक = मारिषिक. The stem already begins with a long vowel, and ठक् does not cause vṛddhi, so the first syllable stays unchanged.

I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठक् after this stem. The form rests on the standard replacement and elision rules above.

<answer>मारिषिक</answer>

The affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*) is added to a word to express praise. Here it gives "praiseworthy Śaṅkarānanda". The affix is attached directly to the stem शंकरानन्द, and the result is the stem शंकरानन्दरूप.

<answer>शंकरानन्दरूप</answer>

Applying अण् to दस्म्य gives दास्म्य. I did not check this against a known attested form, so it rests on the two standard rules below.

1. Before a ञित्/णित् taddhita such as अण्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi, so दस्म्य becomes दास्म्य.
2. The stem-final अ is then dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving दास्म्य् plus the affix's अ, which is दास्म्य.

<answer>दास्म्य</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) is added after a stem when something becomes what it was not before, in construction with कृ, भू or अस्. Before च्वि, the final vowel of the stem is lengthened (च्वौ च, 7.4.26), so दिधिषु becomes दिधिषू. The affix itself is then completely elided (सर्वापहारी लोप), leaving the lengthened stem. This is my own derivation from the rules, not checked against a source.

<answer>दिधिषू</answer>

The affix तल् is added in the sense of "state or quality of that" (भाव) by the rule तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ (Pāṇini 5.1.119). The final ल् is an indicatory letter that drops, leaving the affix त. Words ending in तल् take the feminine ending टाप्. So करम्बित + तल् gives करम्बित + ता, which is करम्बितता.

<answer>करम्बितता</answer>
<answer>चिह्नित्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् after शन्ति, so I derived the form from the general behaviour of the affix.

1. The affix खञ् takes the substitute ईन, because ख is replaced by ईन (ख् → ईन).
2. The ञ् is an indicatory letter, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: श → शा, giving शान्ति.
3. The final इ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving शान्त् + ईन.

<answer>शान्तीन</answer>
<answer>क्षूणजातीय</answer>

Applying the affix खञ् to इरा gives the stem ऐरीण. I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् for इरा, so this form comes from applying the general rules for the affix rather than from a confirmed source.

1. The affix खञ् has initial ख, which is replaced by ईन् (Pāṇini 7.1.2).
2. The marker ञ् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so इ becomes ऐ.
3. The final -ā of इरा drops before the vowel-initial affix.

इरा + ईन → ऐर् + ईन → ऐरीण

<answer>ऐरीण</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप् here, so this form comes from applying the affix's markers directly rather than from a confirmed rule.

In कुणप्, the final प् is a marker (it) that drops out, and the ण् is a marker that calls for vṛddhi (lengthening) of the first vowel. The stem वैषुवतीय already begins with the vṛddhi vowel वै, so nothing changes there.

The affix begins with a consonant, so it does not trigger deletion of the stem's final अ. I take the stem's final अ to stay, which gives वैषुवतीय + कुण = वैषुवतीयकुण.

<answer>वैषुवतीयकुण</answer>
<answer>सुवर्णसदेश्य</answer>

The sūtra 6.3.39 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः) makes a feminine stem behave like its masculine form before the affixes from तसिल् up to कृत्वसुच्, and थाल् falls in that range. So the feminine stem वधना (ending in the feminine suffix ā) is treated as masculine वध before the affix.

The affix थाल् begins with a consonant, so the stem is not a भ-stem and the final अ is not elided by 6.4.148. Dropping the marker ल्, the result is वध + था = वधथा, an indeclinable.

<answer>वधथा</answer>

Applying अण् to आनुबन्धिक, the stem's final अ is dropped by "यस्येति च" and अण् is added. The initial आ is already vṛddhi, so no further vowel change occurs, and the form is unchanged. I did not identify the specific sūtra licensing अण् here, so this rests on the sandhi reasoning alone.

<answer>आनुबन्धिक</answer>
<answer>भवनोदरता</answer>
<answer>मार्जालीयावत्</answer>

The affix cvi is used with the sense "becoming what one was not" (abhūtatadbhāva), typically with kṛ, bhū or as. Under Pāṇini 7.4.32 (*asya cvau ca*), a final -a of the stem becomes ī before cvi, and the affix itself is then entirely deleted. So कवर becomes कवरी, as in कवरीभवति.

<answer>कवरी</answer>

This is an application of the affix सात् (identified here as `sAti`) to the feminine stem खेटा. The ending -ā is retained before the affix, and the result is an indeclinable. I derived this from memory of the rule rather than checking a source, so the retention of -ā is my best reading.

<answer>खेटासात्</answer>

I applied the standard अण् rule: the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi, and the final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix.

1. In धूपाङ्गद, the first vowel ऊ becomes औ, giving धौपाङ्गद.
2. The final अ is elided before the affix अ, so the stem ends in the affix's अ.

I did not check this against a specific sūtra or a Kāśikā example.

<answer>धौपाङ्गद</answer>

I attached तमप् (the superlative affix) directly to the stem. The final प् is only a marker and drops, leaving -तम. The stem ends in short अ, which is not altered before तम, so no sandhi or other change applies.

<answer>वर्मिताङ्गतम</answer>
<answer>वचनीयसात्</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्) gives the affix चरट् in the sense "formerly was". Because चरट् falls in the तसिलादि group (5.3.7 to 5.4.17), 6.3.35 requires पुंवद्भाव before it. So the feminine stem रसाढ्या reverts to the masculine-form base रसाढ्य before the affix. Adding चरट् (with the final ट् dropped) gives रसाढ्यचर, meaning "one who was formerly rich in juice/essence". I am reasoning from memory of these rules, and the choice of the bare stem (not the feminine रसाढ्यचरी) is my own.

<answer>रसाढ्यचर</answer>

This is my own derivation from the rule as I remember it (Pāṇini 5.2.37), not checked against a source. That rule gives the affixes द्वयसच्, दघ्नच् and मात्रच् in the sense of measure. The affix is added directly to the stem दंसु. The final -c is only an indicatory letter and drops out, so the affix is -द्वयस. No sandhi or stem change applies, because the final उ is followed by the consonant द. This gives दंसुद्वयस, parallel to the textbook example ऊरुद्वयसम्, as a neuter stem.

<answer>दंसुद्वयस</answer>

The affix देश्य is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), used in the sense of "almost, not quite complete". It is added directly to the stem without changing it, so the derivative is त्रिंशांशकदेश्य, "almost a त्रिंशांशक". I worked this out from memory of the rule rather than checking a source.

<answer>त्रिंशांशकदेश्य</answer>

This is the affix पाशप् of Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), which is added to a subanta in the sense of "despicable". I am recalling the rule and its sense from memory rather than from a checked source.

The affix comes in the range of affixes from sup to kap, so 1.4.17 gives the stem the status of pada before a consonant-initial affix. The final न् of चुलुम्पिन् is then dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य).

I take 8.2.7 rather than the ṭi-lopa of 6.4.144 (which would give चुलुम्पपाश), because 6.4.144 applies only to a bha stem, and here the stem is pada. This is the step I am least sure of.

चुलुम्पिन् + पाश → चुलुम्पि + पाश → चुलुम्पिपाश

<answer>चुलुम्पिपाश</answer>

Following A.5.2.115 (अत इनिठनौ), the affix इनि is added to a stem ending in short अ to express possession. The final अ of मदन drops before the affix, giving मदन् + इन् = मदनिन्, "possessing madana" (love or intoxication).

<answer>मदनिन्</answer>

I derived this from Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*), which adds चणप् in the sense "known by that". The marker प् drops out as an it-letter, leaving the suffix चण.

The suffix begins with च, a consonant other than य, so the stem does not take the bha designation (1.4.18). The rule *yasyeti ca* (6.4.148) therefore does not delete the final आ of the feminine stem. This matches the traditional examples such as विद्याचणः, where the आ stays.

स्वादुष्किलीया + चण gives स्वादुष्किलीयाचण. I have not checked this particular stem against a Kāśikā example, so the result rests on the rule reasoning above.

<answer>स्वादुष्किलीयाचण</answer>
<answer>कृतार्थक</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् (5.2.37, "प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः") is added to a word for a measure. The final च् is only an indicatory marker, so the operative affix is दघ्न.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -ā of the feminine stem प्रोद्गता is not dropped by यस्येति च, which applies only before vowel-initial affixes. I did not find a rule that shortens the -ā here, so I am reasoning from the general pattern rather than from a confirmed example. The stem therefore stays whole and takes the affix: प्रोद्गता + दघ्न = प्रोद्गतादघ्न.

<answer>प्रोद्गतादघ्न</answer>
<answer>मेथनमात्र</answer>
<answer>उदन्युतम</answer>

पुष्पाशिन् + अञ् → पौष्पाश

मैंने इस विशेष अञ्-सूत्र को पहचाना नहीं है। इसलिए यह रूप केवल सामान्य तद्धित-संधिनियमों से बना है।

1. अञ् में ञ् इत् है, इसलिए आदि अच् की वृद्धि होती है: पु → पौ।
2. "नस्तद्धिते" (६.४.१४४) से नकारान्त भ-अङ्ग के टि का लोप होता है, इसलिए इन् हट जाता है: पुष्पाशिन् → पुष्पाश्।
3. "इनण्यनपत्ये" (६.४.१६४) का प्रकृतिभाव केवल अण् पर लगता है, अञ् पर नहीं, इसलिए यहाँ यह रोक नहीं लगती।
4. अकारान्त अङ्ग में अञ् का अ जुड़ने पर पौष्पाश बनता है।

<answer>पौष्पाश</answer>

This is the affix from Pāṇini 5.3.53, *bhūtapūrve caraṭ*, which means "formerly that". The final ṭ is only an indicatory letter (it-marker) and drops, leaving the suffix -cara. Adding it to the stem शाकुन gives शाकुन + चर = शाकुनचर. No vṛddhi or other change applies, because the initial c of the suffix is not marked ñit or ṇit.

<answer>शाकुनचर</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses छ after अधि here, so this is a plain derivation rather than a rule-by-rule one.

The affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (by आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). Adding ईय to अधि gives अधि + ईय. The final इ of the stem is dropped before the affix (by यस्येति च), which yields अध् + ईय = अधीय.

<answer>अधीय</answer>

The form below is derived by the usual ढक् rules, but I did not check it against a source for this particular stem.

ढक् is added to the feminine stem सात्रासाहका (P. 4.1.120, स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्).

1. The initial ḍh of ढक् is replaced by एय (P. 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्), and the final k is a marker that drops out.
2. The stem-final आ of सात्रासाहका is deleted before the taddhita affix (P. 6.4.148, यस्येति च), leaving सात्रासाहक.
3. Adding एय gives सात्रासाहकेय. The first vowel of the stem is already ā, so the initial vowel strengthening (ādi-vṛddhi) changes nothing.

<answer>सात्रासाहकेय</answer>

I did not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses छ after लोहाभिसार, so the form rests only on the general rule for the affix.

The affix छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (the rule "आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्"). It carries no ञ or ण marker, so the first vowel is not strengthened (no vṛddhi), and the stem लोहाभिसार stays unchanged before it. The final अ of the stem drops before ईय.

लोहाभिसार + ईय → लोहाभिसारीय

<answer>लोहाभिसारीय</answer>

I treated the stem as a basic nominal stem ending in -an and applied अञ् to it. I could not identify a specific rule that licenses this affix on this stem, so this is a mechanical derivation.

1. The stem होत्वन् ends in न्, so before a taddhita affix it takes the प्रत्यय-style elision of its last vowel and what follows (टि-लोप, Pāṇini 6.4.144 नस्तद्धिते). The final अन् is removed, leaving होत्व्.
2. Adding अ from the अञ् affix (the ञ् is only a marker) gives होत्व.
3. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (आदिवृद्धि, 7.2.117). The first vowel ओ becomes औ, giving हौत्व.

<answer>हौत्व</answer>

Here the affix तल् (SLP1 `tal`) is the one that forms abstract nouns meaning "state of being X" (भावे त्वतलौ). The final ल् is only a marker and drops out, and the त् is also an indicatory letter (तित्). What remains is the abstract suffix ता, so the derived word is a feminine stem taking टाप्. Adding it to स्परण gives स्परण + ता = स्परणता.

<answer>स्परणता</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which means "almost, nearly". Adding कल्प to the masculine stem नालिकेल gives नालिकेलकल्प, "almost a coconut". Because the stem is a basic masculine stem and not one ending in a feminine suffix, there is no change to the stem before the affix.

<answer>नालिकेलकल्प</answer>

This is the affix रूपप् (P. 5.3.66, प्रशस्ते रूपप्), which is added to a nominal word to express "praiseworthy". I am working from memory of the rule and its standard examples, such as वैयाकरणरूपः, and have not checked them against a source. Adding it to चन्द्रांशु gives चन्द्रांशुरूप, meaning "an excellent moon-ray".

<answer>चन्द्रांशुरूप</answer>

The derivative is the stem unchanged, शार्ङ्गरवी. The suffix च्वि (cvi) is added under the rule अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः. A final अ would become ई by अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32), and a final इ or उ would be lengthened by च्वौ च (7.4.26). The stem already ends in long ई, so it is unchanged, and च्वि itself is wholly elided. I reasoned this from the rules as I recall them and did not check it against a commentary.

<answer>शार्ङ्गरवी</answer>

Here तल् is the affix that denotes the state or quality (bhāva). It is added to the stem शीतलक, and the final ल् drops out as an indicatory letter, leaving त. Because तल् forms feminine words, टाप् is then added, giving the ending -ता. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of शीतलक is not dropped. This gives शीतलक + ता = शीतलकता.

<answer>शीतलकता</answer>
<answer>वेषजाह</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) is added to a stem to express "becoming what it was not before" (अभूततद्भावे, P. 5.4.50), and is used with कृ, भू or अस् forms. The affix itself is wholly elided (सर्वापहारी लोप), leaving only its effect on the stem.

Before च्वि, the final vowel of the stem is lengthened by च्वौ च (P. 7.4.26). The final उ of अणु therefore becomes ऊ, giving अणू. This is the form seen in अणूभवति, "becomes minute".

<answer>अणू</answer>

Adding the taddhita affix त्व (in the sense of "state or quality of") to the stem आल gives आलत्व. The affix त्व does not cause vṛddhi or any other change to the stem, so the two simply join.

<answer>आलत्व</answer>

This follows the usual Pāṇinian procedure, but I did not find a specific sūtra licensing वलच् after आधारिन्, so the form rests on the general rules.

वलच् begins with व, which is neither य nor a vowel, so the rule यचि भम् does not apply. आधारिन् therefore keeps pada status before the affix. The final न् is then dropped by नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (8.2.7), giving आधारि + वल = आधारिवल.

I also considered whether the final इ would be lengthened, as in कृषीवल. I could not confirm that any rule applies here, so I left it short.

<answer>आधारिवल</answer>
<answer>भेदिकातः</answer>

I formed this with the affix त्व in the sense "state or quality of" (bhāve tva, Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.1.119). The stem वृश्चीव ends in अ. The rule that drops a final अ (यस्येति च, 6.4.148) applies only before affixes that begin with a vowel or य. त्व begins with a consonant, so nothing is dropped and no other change applies. The affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>वृश्चीवत्व</answer>

Following Pāṇini 5.3.53 (*bhūtapūrve caraṭ*), the affix चरट् is added to a nominal base in the sense "formerly was". The final ट् only marks the affix and drops out, leaving the ending -चर. Adding it to कपीन्द्र gives कपीन्द्रचर, "formerly a monkey-king".

<answer>कपीन्द्रचर</answer>

Here the affix दघ्नच् (daGnac) is added in the sense of measure (प्रमाणे, Pāṇini 5.2.37). Its final च् is only an indicatory marker, so the affix is effectively दघ्न.

The affix begins with a consonant. The stem is therefore not a "bha" stem, and यस्येति च does not delete the final आ of लाटीया. The stem is simply joined with दघ्न, giving the neuter stem लाटीयादघ्न. I derived this from the rules as I recall them rather than from an attested form.

<answer>लाटीयादघ्न</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् for this stem, so this derivation rests on the general taddhita procedure rather than on a confirmed rule. The affix अञ् is a ñit affix, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi and the final -इ is dropped before the suffix:

बन्धाकि → ब becomes बा (vṛddhi of the first vowel), final इ is dropped, then add अ → बान्धाक.

<answer>वैखानसिष्ठ</answer>

I could not match the affix रूप्य (rUpya) to a specific Pāṇinian rule, so this form rests on simple concatenation and not on a rule derivation. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not elided. Nothing indicates a vṛddhi or other marker, so the stem is left unchanged.

<answer>रम्भाभिसाररूप्य</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses the affix रूप्य, so this form rests on an assumption. I treated रूप्य as a single affix added directly to the stem इत्वरी. The affix रूपप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशस्ते रूपप्), where it is added to a subanta to express praise. The final प् is only a marker and drops out, so the stem हेमालंकार takes the ending -रूप. The result is हेमालंकाररूप, meaning "an excellent golden ornament".

The affix देशीयर् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ) attaches to the whole subanta, so it is added to वैष्टपा as it stands. The final र् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving -देशीय. The affix ईयसुन् (the comparative suffix) is added to the stem आनुरोहिणी. I formed this from memory of the rules and did not check it against a source.

2. Before this taddhita affix, the stem is a "bha" stem, so its final ṭi-part (here the final ई) is dropped by the ṭi-lopa rule (ṭeḥ, 6.4.143). That gives आनुरोहिण्.
3. Adding ईयस् gives आनुरोहिण् + ईयस् = आनुरोहिणीयस्. The ण् was already correct because of the preceding र्.

I applied the affix इष्ठन् (the superlative suffix, "most …") to the stem धेय.

1. Before इष्ठन्, the stem takes the bha designation, because the affix begins with a vowel.

Adding ईयस् (the न् of ईयसुन् is only a marker) gives कुम्भीकीयस्. I did not treat कुम्भीकिन् as a विन्-stem, so the elision rule for विन् (5.3.65) does not apply.

<answer>कुम्भीकीयस्</answer>

The affix शस् (Sas) is added under P. 5.4.43, which gives शस् in the sense of distribution (vīpsā), as in कार्षापणशः. I am assuming that rule applies here; the stem कारतन्तविकी is unusual and I could not tie it to a specific attested example.

Here is the derivation I followed:

- The affix देशीयर् is added by P. 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It means "somewhat" or "almost", i.e. incompletely the thing named by the stem.
- The stem वेषणा is a feminine ending in the ā-suffix. Before देशीयर्, P. 6.3.42 (पुंवत्कर्मधारयजातीयदेशीयेषु) makes it behave like its masculine form. The final ā is dropped, giving वेषण.
- Adding देशीय gives वेषणदेशीय.

I am not certain the pumvat rule is meant to apply here. It requires a masculine counterpart of वेषणा, which I did not verify. If it did not apply, the form would be वेषणादेशीय.

<answer>वेषणदेशीय</answer>

The affix देश्य (SLP1 `deSya`) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः. It is added to a subanta to express "slightly incomplete", so it means "almost a पौणिकेर". The stem ends in अ and the affix begins with a consonant, so there is no sandhi or other internal change, and the two simply join.

<answer>पौणिकेरदेश्य</answer>

The affix ञ्यट् is ञित्, so it calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. That vowel in हैरण्यिक is already ऐ, so nothing changes there. The final अ of the stem is then dropped before the taddhita affix beginning with य (यस्येति च). This gives हैरण्यिक् + य = हैरण्यिक्य.

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that introduces ञ्यट् here, so the derivation rests on the standard ञित् and यस्येति च rules.

<answer>हैरण्यिक्य</answer>

The affix चरट् (caraṭ) is added in the sense "formerly was" by भूतपूर्वे चरट् (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.53). Adding it to कठिका gives कठिका + चर, so the derived stem is कठिकाचर, meaning "formerly a कठिका". The feminine of this would be कठिकाचरी. I did not check whether a rule substitutes masculine-like (पुंवत्) behaviour before चरट्, so I formed the stem by simple addition.

<answer>कठिकाचर</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation. I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that teaches ञ्यङ् after ग्राभ, so I did not verify it.

The affix ञ्यङ् leaves the suffix -य after the markers ञ् and ङ् drop. Because of the ञ् marker, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. In ग्राभ it is already long आ, so nothing changes. The final अ of the stem is then elided before the suffix (यस्येति च). This gives ग्राभ्य.

<answer>ग्राभ्य</answer>
<answer>दैवादिकमात्र</answer>

This is an application of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which gives दघ्नच् in the sense of measure. I did not check whether this affix is normally added to a stem like पाङ्क्तेय, but the table asks for the formation, so I derived it directly.

The final च् of दघ्नच् is only an it-marker, so the affix is effectively दघ्न. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) deletes a stem-final अ only before an affix beginning with a vowel or ई. दघ्न begins with the consonant द, so the final अ of पाङ्क्तेय stays. The derived stem is therefore पाङ्क्तेय + दघ्न.

<answer>पाङ्क्तेयदघ्न</answer>

The affix चणप् (SLP1 caRap) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, with the sense "known by that". The final प् is only an marker letter, so what is added is चण. Since चण begins with a consonant, the base undergoes no vṛddhi and no loss of its final sound, and the stem is simply joined to the affix.

खार्जूरकर्ण + चण = खार्जूरकर्णचण

<answer>खार्जूरकर्णचण</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation, not a confirmed one: I could not recall the Pāṇinian rule that introduces जाहच्. I took the affix to be जाह, since the final च् and the initial ज् are markers (it्-letters) that drop out.

The stem महय्या ends in the feminine suffix आ. Before a vowel-initial taddhita affix, the stem counts as a भ-aṅga, and "यस्येति च" (6.4.148) deletes its final आ. This leaves महय्य, and adding जाह gives महय्यजाह.

<answer>महय्यजाह</answer>

The affix बहुच् (P. 5.3.68, in the sense of "nearly, not quite") is placed before the base, not after it. Adding it to the feminine stem भण्डिका gives बहुभण्डिका.

I am not certain whether the pumvadbhāva rule (P. 6.3.35) would change the final form. I could not confirm that भण्डिका has a masculine counterpart. Even if the rule applied, re-adding the feminine suffix would restore the same final form.

<answer>बहुभण्डिका</answer>

The affix बहुच् (A. 5.3.68–69) is placed before a subanta word, with the sense "almost, nearly". Before it, the base takes puṃvadbhāva (A. 6.3.35), so ऐकाग्निका becomes ऐकाग्निक. Prefixing बहु gives बहु + ऐकाग्निक, and internal sandhi (u + ai → vai) gives बह्वैकाग्निक. I have left off the feminine ā that would be added afterwards as a separate step. I derived this from memory of the rules, and the choice not to add the feminine ending is a judgment call, so I am not fully certain of it.

<answer>बह्वैकाग्निक</answer>
<answer>मात्रिकायनि</answer>

The affix तल् (SLP1 `tal`) is added in the sense of "state or quality" (भावे त्वतलौ, 5.1.119). The final ल् is an indicatory letter and drops out, leaving the suffix ता. Words ending in तल् are feminine, so the stem takes the feminine ending -ā.

I applied the taddhita affix *astāti* (Pāṇini 5.3.27) to the stem कार्पास, without checking the form against a grammar text or a source that attests it. The stem is not a typical direction word, so this is a mechanical application of the affix.

1. The affix surfaces as *-astāt*. I took the final *i* of *astāti* to be a marker that drops, as in *purastāt*.
2. The final *a* of कार्पास is elided before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148).
3. This gives कार्पास् + अस्तात् = कार्पासस्तात्.

<answer>कार्पासस्तात्</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix रूप्य, so this answer rests on a simple derivation rather than a confirmed source.

The affix रूप्य begins with the consonant र, so the stem निष्ट्य keeps its final अ. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148), which deletes a stem-final अ, applies only before affixes beginning with a vowel or य. Nothing else changes, so the affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>निष्ट्यरूप्य</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), with the sense "despicable" or "barely passable". It is added to आर्ची, giving आर्ची + पाश.

The feminine ending ई is dropped before a taddhita affix by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). The stem आर्च already has a long आ, so nothing else changes. Pāśap carries no ṇit marker, so there is no vṛddhi. Rule 6.3.35, which gives masculine-like (puṃvat) treatment, applies only before jātīya and deśīya, so it does not apply here either.

The result is आर्चपाश.

<answer>आर्चपाश</answer>

1. The final अ of कुणप् is only an accent marker (पित्), so the affix is effectively कुण. The ण् in it is also an indicatory letter, which triggers vṛddhi.
2. Before this taddhita affix, the final ई of तपन्ती is dropped by यस्येति च, leaving तपन्त.
3. Because the affix has ण्, the first vowel of the base takes vṛddhi, so त becomes ता, giving तापन्त.
4. Adding कुण gives तापन्तकुण.

Before इष्ठन्, the stem takes the "bha" status. Rule 6.4.155 (टेः) then drops the "ṭi" part of the stem, which is the final vowel with anything after it. For घृतान्वक्त that is the final अ.

<answer>सानुरागीय</answer>

Using Pāṇini 5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्), the affix जातीयर् is added to शाङ्खायनिन्. Because the affix begins with a consonant, the stem counts as a pada (1.4.17). Here I take अष्टक्या as a feminine stem in -ā and join it directly to वलच्. This is a best guess, since I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses वलच् after this stem. 2. The stem वर्तका ends in the feminine suffix आ. That आ drops before the affix by "यस्येति च", leaving वर्तक्.
3. Vṛddhi of the first vowel changes व to वा, giving वार्तक्.

I applied इष्ठन् to the stem शिवाकु, but I am relying on memory of the rules and have not checked them against the text.

2. The stem takes the bha-designation before इष्ठन्, so the टि (its last vowel with any consonant after it) is dropped, per टेः (6.4.155). Here the टि is just the final उ, which leaves शिवाक्.
3. Adding इष्ठ gives शिवाक् + इष्ठ = शिवाकिष्ठ.

I found no special rule that changes this result for this stem.

The affix is तरप् (the comparative suffix), added to the feminine stem जालकिनी, which ends in ई.

Before तरप् (and तमप्), a polysyllabic feminine stem ending in ई or ऊ shortens its final vowel (Pāṇini 6.3.43). So जालकिनी becomes जालकिनि, and adding तर gives जालकिनितर. I am recalling that rule from memory rather than checking it against the text. I have given the bare derived stem, without the feminine टाप् ending that would turn it into जालकिनितरा.

<answer>जालकिनितर</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, and I could not confirm the shortening rule it relies on.

The stem कौलेया ends in the feminine suffix आ. When तरप् (-तर) is added after such a feminine stem, the final आ is shortened before the affix. I believe this is Pāṇini 6.3.43, which applies to stems ending in ṅī or āp when they have more than one syllable. That gives कौलेय + तर = कौलेयतर. Any further feminine ending (-आ) would be added afterwards, so I give the stem without it.

This is a best-effort derivation. I could not recall the specific rule that licenses कुणप्, so I am not certain of the form.

The stem वैंशतिकी is feminine and ends in the feminine ई. थाल् belongs to the तसिल्-group of affixes (तसिलादि), and before these a feminine stem takes the masculine form (पुंवद्भाव, Pāṇini 6.3.35–36). So वैंशतिकी reverts to वैंशतिक, and adding थाल् (with the final ल् dropped as an indicatory letter) gives वैंशतिक + था.

This rests on my recollection of those sūtras. The affix is normally taught after सर्व, एक, अन्य, किम्, यद् and तद्, but the task allows any licensed meaning, so I formed it on the stem given.

This follows Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), where देश्य is added to a nominal stem to mean "slightly short of being that". <answer>चाणाररूप्यातः</answer>

I took the affix as कुण, with the final प् as an it-marker that drops. It begins with a consonant, so the stem पाठ्या is not treated as a bha-aṅga, and no vowel deletion or vṛddhi applies. I assumed the stem-final ā of the feminine suffix shortens before the affix, giving पाठ्य + कुण. I did not verify that shortening against a specific rule, so the choice between पाठ्यकुण and पाठ्याकुण is uncertain.

<answer>पाठ्यकुण</answer>
<answer>चौतपल्लवि</answer>
<answer>वैलात्यमय</answer>
<answer>वर्षिकी</answer>

Taking यती as a feminine stem in ई, the affix अण् is added to it. The final ई is dropped before the taddhita affix by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). The first vowel then takes vṛddhi, so य becomes या. This gives यात्‌ + अ, which is यात. I did not pin down which specific meaning rule licenses this, so the choice of meaning is open.

<answer>यात</answer>

शासन + त्व gives शासनत्व, with the affix added by the rule "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (5.1.119), which forms abstract nouns meaning "the state of being X". The affix त्व is not marked with ñ or ṇ, so there is no vṛddhi. Its initial consonant त also leaves the final अ of the stem intact.

<answer>शासनत्व</answer>
<answer>पुण्डसात्</answer>

This is the superlative suffix *tamap* (Pāṇini 5.3.55, *atiśayane tamabiṣṭhanau*). It attaches directly to the stem जि, which is masculine and not feminine, so there is no shortening or other change. The derived stem is जि + तम = जितम.

<answer>जितम</answer>

The stem कुलाङ्कुर ends in short अ. Under 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः), the म of मतुप् becomes व after a stem ending in अ. The stem is not one of the exceptions (यव etc.), so मतुप् becomes वतुप्. With the इत् letters dropped, the affix is वत्. The result is the stem कुलाङ्कुरवत्, with no case ending added.

<answer>कुलाङ्कुरवत्</answer>
<answer>वदनोदरतम</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप्, so this form comes from the general taddhita mechanics rather than from a rule I could cite.

The final प् is an *it* marker and drops, so the affix is कुण. Its initial क् is not dropped, because the rule that makes an initial ku-varga letter an *it* does not apply to taddhitas. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of सायतन is not elided. There is no vowel-initial affix to trigger that elision, and no other change applies. The stem and affix simply join.

<answer>सायतनकुण</answer>

The affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, प्रशंसायां रूपप्) is added to a word to express "praiseworthy, excellent". I applied it to the neuter stem स्वेदोद, which gives स्वेदोदरूप, meaning "excellent sweat-water".

<answer>स्वेदोदरूप</answer>

I took the affix to be चणप् from Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, which gives "known by that". The standard examples are विद्याचणः and अक्षरचणः, so by analogy चर्चया वित्तः gives चर्चाचण. I did not check this against a source that attests the चर्चा form.

The final ā of चर्चा is not deleted. The affix चण begins with च, so the stem does not take the भ-designation under यचि भम्, and the ā is not removed by यस्येति च. The stem therefore keeps its ā and the affix is simply added: चर्चा + चण = चर्चाचण. The p of चणप् is only a marker and does not appear in the result.

<answer>चर्चाचण</answer>
<answer>जानुकि</answer>

The form is वैजवतः. The affix तसि (तसिल्) gives the sense "from Vaijava". It is added to वैजव with no change to the stem, and the final स् becomes visarga as the form ends. This is a standard formation and I did not check it against a specific sūtra.

<answer>वैजवतः</answer>

Rūpap (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*) is added to a subanta to express praise. Here मोक्षेच्छा ("desire for liberation") takes rūpap with the sense "praiseworthy desire for liberation". The ā of the stem stays unchanged, because the shortening before rūpap (6.3.42) applies only to stems ending in the ṅī feminine suffix. The result is a masculine/neuter-type stem, मोक्षेच्छारूप. I have given the bare stem, not the feminine form मोक्षेच्छारूपा, since the task asks for the stem.

<answer>मोक्षेच्छारूप</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses ञ्यट् for this stem, so this derivation is a best guess based on the general behaviour of the affix's markers.

1. The ञ् in ञ्यट् is an indicatory letter, so the affix triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem: उ becomes औ.
2. The final आ of उपत्यका is deleted before a तद्धित affix marked with an indicatory letter (यस्येति च), leaving उपत्यक्.
3. Adding the affix ्य gives औपत्यक्य.

The ट् is also an indicatory letter and would normally yield a feminine in ङीप् (औपत्यक्यी). I have given the base stem without that feminine suffix.

<answer>औपत्यक्य</answer>

Applying the affix कन् to the masculine stem खटक gives खटक + कन्. The final न् of कन् is only a marker (it drops), leaving the affix as क with the added अ. The rule that turns the stem's अ into इ before क (7.3.44–45) applies only when the feminine suffix आप् follows. That is not the case here, since the source is masculine. The stem is therefore unchanged, and the result is खटककः in the nominative, which gives the stem खटकक.

<answer>खटकक</answer>

The stem पीतावशेषा ends in the feminine suffix ā (ṭāp), and the taddhita affix क is added after it. Before क, the ā of the stem is replaced by इ (my recollection of the rule is P. 7.3.44, which I did not check). That gives पीतावशेष + इ + क, and the feminine ā is then added again to form पीतावशेषिका.

<answer>पीतावशेषिका</answer>
<answer>पूर्वाह्णकवल</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses छ on this stem, so I used the general rule for the affix. The affix छ is replaced by ईय (Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The final अ of क्षूण is dropped before the vowel-initial ईय. छ-affixes do not trigger vṛddhi, so the stem vowels stay as they are. This gives क्षूण + ईय = क्षूणीय.

<answer>क्षूणीय</answer>

Here the affix is चुञ्चुप् (cuñcup), taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*. The ञ् is part of the affix's own consonant cluster, so it is not an *it* marker, and only the प् is dropped. The affix is therefore added as चुञ्चु.

It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not deleted under *yasyeti ca* (6.4.148). The stem तिकीय simply takes the affix.

<answer>तिकीयचुञ्चु</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The affix थाल् is normally taught for the pronominal words सर्व, एक, अन्य, किम्, यद् and तद् (5.3.23), so this is a mechanical formation.

The ल् of थाल् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix reduces to था. Because था begins with a consonant, the final अ of the stem is not dropped. Adding the affix gives धनार्घ + था = धनार्घथा, which is an indeclinable.

<answer>धनार्घथा</answer>

The affix जातीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added after a word to mean "a kind of" that thing. Because the base मार्मिका is a feminine stem ending in ṭāp, 6.3.39 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः) applies. It gives masculine-like treatment (pumvadbhāva) before affixes from tasil through kṛtvasuc, and जातीयर् falls in that range. So the feminine ending is dropped: मार्मिका becomes मार्मिक. Adding जातीय gives the stem मार्मिकजातीय. The feminine of the derivative, मार्मिकजातीया, would then be formed from this stem.

<answer>मार्मिकजातीय</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rule for द्वयसच् (P. 5.2.37, प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), worked out from memory rather than checked against a source.

The affix द्वयसच् leaves the stem द्वयस after the इत् letters drop. It begins with द, a consonant, so the stem वैरोट्या is not treated as a "भ" stem under 1.4.18 (यचि भम्). Its final आ therefore stays unchanged. The rule for the masculine-like replacement of a feminine stem (पुंवद्भाव) does not apply either: 6.3.35 covers compounds, and 6.3.39 covers only the affixes तसिल् etc. The result is वैरोट्या + द्वयस.

<answer>वैरोट्याद्वयस</answer>
<answer>पिचिलचर</answer>
<answer>धियायिष्ठ</answer>

I took the affix as बहुच् (P. 5.3.68, "विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु"). It is added to a subanta in the sense of "somewhat, nearly" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it appears before the base as the element बहु. This is the same pattern as बहुपटु, "somewhat skilled". Applying it to मरणीय gives the stem below.

<answer>बहुमरणीय</answer>

The affix रूपप् (P. 5.3.66, in the sense of praise) is added to the stem शिष्टाशिन्. Before this consonant-initial taddhita affix, the stem counts as a pada, so the final न् is dropped by 8.2.7. This gives शिष्टाशि + रूप, and the derived stem ends in -a.

<answer>शिष्टाशिरूप</answer>

I applied the affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27) to the stem, using the usual outcome of this affix, which surfaces as ‑स्तात् (as in पुरस्तात्). The final अ of उपवसथीय drops before the vowel-initial affix (6.4.148), giving उपवसथीय् + अस्तात्. I did not check the ending of the affix against a source; I assumed the final इ is only a marker that does not appear in the surface form.

<answer>उपवसथीयस्तात्</answer>

The affix चरट् is the one taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Pāṇini 5.3.53), used for "formerly was so-and-so". The final ट् is only a marker and drops. What is left is the element -चर, which is added directly to the stem चेतसक. This gives चेतसकचर, meaning "one who formerly was a चेतसक".

<answer>चेतसकचर</answer>

I could not confirm the affix's rule with certainty. I took रूप्य to be the affix of Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.3.81 (हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यः), used in the sense "come from that". This is from memory, and the input stem is not clearly a "hetu" or "human" word.

The stem रत्नाकरायिता ends in the feminine -ā. रूप्य begins with र, not with a vowel or य. The stem therefore counts as a pada before it and not as a bha stem, so 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) does not delete the final -ā. The result is the stem with रूप्य added directly.

<answer>रत्नाकरायितारूप्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses अञ् on this stem, so this form rests on the general rules for ञित् affixes. A ञित् taddhita affix triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (अचामादेः, 7.2.117). The stem's first vowel is the अ of स, which becomes आ, giving सार्वाश्य. The final अ of the stem is elided before the affix's अ (यस्येति च), and the same अ is restored by the affix, so the form is unchanged.

<answer>सार्वाश्य</answer>

I applied ईयसुन् to the stem द्रावयाण by the usual comparative rules, assuming a stem of this shape is permissible.

1. Before ईयसुन्, the "ṭi" part of the stem is deleted (ṭeḥ, 6.4.155). The ṭi is the last vowel together with the consonant after it, here "आण". That leaves द्रावय.
2. The final अ of द्रावय is then dropped before the initial ई of the affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148). Joining the remainder with ईयस् gives द्रावयीयस्.

<answer>द्रावयीयस्</answer>

I could not identify a specific sūtra that applies यत् to this stem, so this is a derivation from the general rules rather than a confirmed sourced form.

The stem is कुपया, ending in the feminine ā. The affix यत् leaves the taddhita suffix -य, since the final त् is only an indicatory letter (it). Under यस्येति च (6.4.148), the final आ of the stem is deleted before a taddhita beginning with य. This gives कुपय् + य, which is कुपय्य. Because यत् is not ṇit, there is no vṛddhi.

<answer>कुपय्य</answer>

The stem is लोलन्ती, a feminine ṅīp stem derived from the present participle लोलत्. The affix देशीयर् (P. 5.3.67) gives the sense "almost, not quite".

Before जातीयर् and देशीयर्, a feminine word whose masculine form is in use takes the masculine base (पुंवद्भाव, P. 6.3.42). So लोलन्ती reverts to लोलत्.

Because देशीय begins with द, which is neither य nor a vowel, the stem counts as a पद. Its final त् therefore becomes द् (jaśtva), giving लोलद्देशीय.

I reconstructed the sūtra numbering from memory, so I'm not fully certain of it, and I did not settle the पुंवद्भाव step beyond this reading.

<answer>लोलद्देशीय</answer>
<answer>मन्दोदकिक</answer>
<answer>सांव्यवहारिकत्रा</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्) gives the affix थाल्. Its final ल् is only an indicatory letter (it), so what is added is "था". The stem ends in अ, but the affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not dropped. This gives सुन्दरानन्द + था = सुन्दरानन्दथा, which is indeclinable.

I did not apply णत्व (retroflexion of न), because the र् and the न fall in different members of the compound. I am unsure of this point. I also know of no attested use of थाल् after this stem, so the form is a mechanical derivation.

<answer>सुन्दरानन्दथा</answer>

Taking तनिष्ठ as the base, the affix ईयसुन् gives तनिष्ठीयस्. Under 6.4.154 (टेः), the ṭi (the final अ) of the base is dropped before ईयसुन्, so तनिष्ठ् + ईयस् gives तनिष्ठीयस्. This is a formal derivation of the stem, since तनिष्ठ already carries the superlative sense.

<answer>तनिष्ठीयस्</answer>

This is my best derivation. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् on छिक्का, so the form follows from the general rules for adding a taddhita affix.

1. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the pratyaya **-य**. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, and the ट् marker does not affect the stem itself.
2. The final आ of छिक्का is dropped before the affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148), giving छिक्क् + य.
3. Vṛddhi of the first vowel changes इ to ऐ, giving छैक्क्य.

I give the base stem छैक्क्य. A feminine form would add -ई, because the ट् marker makes ङीप् available.

<answer>छैक्क्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses थाल् on this stem, so this is a best-judgement formation. The affix थाल् (5.3.23, in the sense of "manner") gives forms like तथा and यथा, but रुचिष्या is not one of the usual stems for it.

थाल् begins with a consonant, so the stem stays a pada before it. This means the final आ of रुचिष्या is not dropped. The ल् is an indicatory letter and is removed. Joining रुचिष्या with -था gives the indeclinable form below.

<answer>रुचिष्याथा</answer>

I could not tie this to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The affix तसि gives the ending तस्, and I did not apply pumvadbhāva (6.3.35) to the stem चर्चरिका, because 6.3.35 covers only the affixes from तसिल् to कृत्वसुच्. Attaching the ending gives the indeclinable चर्चरिकातस्, and the final स् becomes visarga. The visarga form is my assumption about which output is expected.

<answer>चर्चरिकातः</answer>
<answer>साखिदत्तेयतर</answer>
<answer>प्रतीतदघ्न</answer>

The affix मात्रच् is added directly to the stem, with no vowel strengthening (vṛddhi) or other change, since it carries no marker that triggers one. This gives योगोपदेश + मात्र = योगोपदेशमात्र. I formed this from the affix's general rule for measure (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नमात्रचः, 5.2.37) and did not check a specific attested example.

<answer>योगोपदेशमात्र</answer>
<answer>शोभनीयदघ्न</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् is added after a nominal stem in the sense of measure (Pāṇini 5.2.37, प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः). The final च् is only a marker (it), so what is added is द्वयस.

The stem सोमार्य ends in अ, but the affix begins with the consonant द. The elision of the stem-final अ (यस्येति च) applies only before a vowel or य, so it does not apply here. The stem is therefore left intact and the affix is simply added.

सोमार्य + द्वयस → सोमार्यद्वयस

<answer>सोमार्यद्वयस</answer>

I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses चरट् after कीलाल, so this form is my best reconstruction rather than a verified derivation.

The affix चरट् leaves "चर" once the इत् marker ट् is dropped. Since "चर" begins with a consonant, the final अ of कीलाल is not elided, and the stem is simply joined to the affix.

<answer>कीलालचर</answer>
<answer>मारिचिकदेशीय</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) is used in the sense of becoming what one was not before (abhūtatadbhāva), usually with कृ, भू or अस्. Following अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32), the final -अ of the stem becomes -ई before च्वि. The affix itself is then removed completely, which leaves बल्यी (as in बल्यी भवति).

<answer>बल्यी</answer>

I could not pin down the exact rule behind this affix. The likely source is the "कन्" affix of the aṣṭādhyāyī, but I did not verify the rule number or its meaning. On that basis, कन् leaves the stem पयस् unchanged and adds क. The स् stays as it is, so the stem is पयस्क.

<answer>पयस्क</answer>

The affix कल्पप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) in the sense of "slightly short of complete". It is added directly to the stem आञ्छित without any change to it, giving आञ्छितकल्प.

<answer>आञ्छितकल्प</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् is added to शंस्तृ in the sense of "most …", and the final तृ is dropped before it. This follows 6.4.154 (तुरिष्ठेमेयस्सु), which elides the तृ of a tṛ-ending stem before इष्ठन्, इमन् and ईयसुन्. शंस्तृ gives शंस् + इष्ठ, which is शंसिष्ठ. I am applying 6.4.154 from memory and did not check how the Kāśikā treats this particular stem.

<answer>शंसिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>शङ्किलवल</answer>

The affix मयट् (4.3.82 / 5.4.21 सामान्य sense "consisting of, abundant in") is added to शुद्धात्मन्. मयट् begins with a consonant other than य, so the stem counts as a pada before it (1.4.17). The final न् is then deleted (8.2.7). The ट् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the suffix as मय. This gives शुद्धात्ममय, "consisting of the pure self".

<answer>शुद्धात्ममय</answer>
<answer>रत्नोद्भवशः</answer>

The affix is *tasil* (तसिल्, SLP1 `tasi`), which is added to a nominal stem, here लूम, and gives an indeclinable ending in -तस्. The stem ends in short अ, so the ending joins directly: लूम + तस् gives लूमतस्. Final -स् becomes visarga, so the finished indeclinable is लूमतः. I assumed the "from ..." (ablative) sense licensed by the sūtra पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (5.3.7).

<answer>लूमतः</answer>

Affixing छ (Ca) to the stem क्रुशिक replaces छ with its substitute ईय. The final अ of the stem drops before ईय, so क्रुशिक + ईय gives क्रुशिकीय. I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses छ after this stem, so this rests on the general छ → ईय substitution.

<answer>क्रुशिकीय</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is added optionally to a subanta in the sense "slightly short of complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). Unlike most taddhita affixes, it is placed before the base, as in बहुपटु. The base शाष्पेयिन् therefore stays unchanged, with बहु prefixed.

<answer>बहुशाष्पेयिन्</answer>
<answer>सिंहेन्द्रथम्</answer>

Applying the affix बन् is not needed here. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses खञ् after this stem, so this derivation rests on the general rules for the affix.

1. The affix खञ् becomes ईन, since the initial ख् is replaced by ईन् (the rule `ख → ईन्`).
2. The feminine ending -ā of आमोहनिका drops before the taddhita affix, leaving आमोहनिक.
3. Because the affix has the marker ञ्, the first vowel takes vṛddhi. The initial आ is already vṛddhi, so it does not change.
4. Adding ईन to आमोहनिक gives आमोहनिकीन.

<answer>आमोहनिकीन</answer>

This is a mechanical derivation, since I could not identify a specific rule that adds यत् to this stem.

The stem औजस्य ends in अ, and the affix यत् loses its final त् as an indicatory letter, leaving य. A taddhita affix that begins with य triggers the deletion of the stem's final अ by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). The stem therefore becomes औजस्य्, and adding य gives औजस्य्य. The initial vowel औ is already vṛddhi, so there is no further change.

<answer>औजस्य्य</answer>
<answer>स्थौणावशेषिक</answer>

The affix इनि is the possessive taddhita of the rule "अत इनिठनौ", added to a stem ending in short अ. I did not look up a specific attested use of सौचिक्य, so this derivation rests on that rule alone.

सौचिक्य ends in अ. Before इनि, that final अ is dropped by "यस्येति च". This gives सौचिक्य् + इन्, which joins as सौचिक्यिन्, meaning "one who possesses सौचिक्य".

<answer>सौचिक्यिन्</answer>
<answer>पौरण्टकतर</answer>

This is a reconstruction, not a recalled citation. I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses this affix with this stem. I took the affix शस् (Sas) to be the distributive/adverbial one, as in बहुशः and एकशः. Adding it to करोटि gives करोटिशस्, an indeclinable whose final स् becomes visarga.

<answer>करोटिशः</answer>
<answer>धुतथा</answer>

I derived this from memory of the relevant rules, and did not check them against a text. शतिन् means "one who has a hundred". The affix कन् is the one Pāṇini teaches for contempt, unknown reference, and similar senses. Its final न् is only a marker, so what is added is क.

Before क, the stem is treated as a pada, so the final न् of शतिन् drops by "नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य" (8.2.7). This gives शति + क, i.e. शतिक. I have not checked this step against the commentaries. Another reading of the stem's status would delete only its final vowel and consonant (ṭi) and give a different result.

<answer>शतिक</answer>
<answer>पनयाय्यचर</answer>

Following the rules for the Tamu affix mechanically, I get this form. The affix is थमु, whose final उ is an it-marker, so only थम् is added. It begins with a consonant, so the stem is not a bha stem and the final आ is not dropped. This gives द्योतिता + थम् = द्योतिताथम्.

This is a mechanical result. In Pāṇini the affix is taught only after इदम् and किम् (5.3.24–25), so the given stem is not a standard base for it.

<answer>द्योतिताथम्</answer>
<answer>चक्राकृतिदेशीय</answer>

The affix बहुच् is introduced by P. 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is optional after a subanta word in the sense of "slightly less than complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति), and it is placed before the word. So बहुच् gives बहु + गवाकृति. No sandhi applies, so the result is बहुगवाकृति. I recalled this rule from memory rather than checking a source.

<answer>बहुगवाकृति</answer>

This is a derivation from the stem and affix alone; I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses ञ्यङ् after दास, so the form rests on the general rules below.

The affix ञ्यङ् reduces to य after the markers ञ् and ङ् drop. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The first vowel of दास is already long आ, so the stem is unchanged. The final अ of दास is dropped before the affix, giving दास्‌ + य.

The masculine stem is therefore दास्य.

<answer>दास्य</answer>
<answer>गर्वथा</answer>

This is an application of the affix दघ्नच् taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which gives a word meaning "as much as X in measure". The pattern is the same as in ऊरुदघ्न.

1. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final आ of the feminine stem वरेणा is not elided. Rule 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) deletes a stem-final आ only before a vowel-initial affix.
2. The final च् of दघ्नच् is an इत् marker and drops, leaving दघ्न.
3. Joining the stem and the affix gives वरेणा + दघ्न = वरेणादघ्न.

I derived this by analogy with ऊरुदघ्न, so the retained आ is an inference from rule 6.4.148 rather than a form I checked in a source.

<answer>वरेणादघ्न</answer>

This is a derivation by rule rather than an attested word, and I am least sure of the first step.

The affix थाल् loses its marker ल्, leaving था. The final आ of ककाटिका drops before the taddhita affix (यस्येति च), giving ककाटिक + था.

<answer>ककाटिकथा</answer>
<answer>कार्शनीयीन</answer>

The affix देश्य (SLP1 `deSya`) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः. It is added to a subanta in the sense of "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). No stem change applies here, so ध्रौव + देश्य gives ध्रौवदेश्य, meaning "somewhat of a ध्रौव".

<answer>ध्रौवदेश्य</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific rule for ञ्यङ्. The form below comes from the general mechanics of the affix, not from a sūtra I could cite.

1. The affix ञ्यङ् leaves the ending -य after the markers ञ् and ङ् drop.
2. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel is strengthened (vṛddhi). In धान्व the first vowel धा is already long, so nothing changes.
3. The final -अ of the stem is elided before the affix (यस्येति च). This gives धान्व् + य.
4. The result is धान्व्य.

<answer>धान्व्य</answer>

This is the taddhita affix पाशप्, taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्). It is added to a nominal stem to express something deficient or blameworthy (याप्य).

Adding पाश to चातुर्वैद्य gives चातुर्वैद्यपाश. The final अ of the stem is not dropped, because पाश begins with a consonant. The प् of पाशप् is only an indicatory marker (it affects accent) and leaves no trace in the form.

<answer>चातुर्वैद्यपाश</answer>

Here iṣṭhan (the superlative affix, तमबिष्ठनौ 5.3.55) is added to the stem आजपथिक, and the result is formed as follows.

1. Before iṣṭhan the final ṭi of the stem is dropped by टेः (6.4.155). The ṭi of आजपथिक is its final अ, so the stem becomes आजपथिक्.
2. Adding इष्ठ gives आजपथिक् + इष्ठ = आजपथिकिष्ठ.

I did not check whether other rules might apply to a stem of this kind, so this is the result from the standard ṭi-lopa derivation.

<answer>आजपथिकिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>जिज्ञासकस्तात्</answer>

The affix देश्य is introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), in the sense of "almost, nearly (but not quite) X". It is added directly to the base without any change. The base परीष्ट therefore gives परीष्टदेश्य, "almost परीष्ट".

<answer>परीष्टदेश्य</answer>
<answer>भ्रुतः</answer>

Following the standard formation rules, the affix थमु drops its marker उ, leaving थम्. Because थम् begins with a consonant, the final अ of वैदग्धक is not elided, so the affix is simply added to the stem. The result is an indeclinable (अव्यय).

The affix थमु is normally taught only for इदम् and किम् (इदमस्थमुः, किमश्च), so this derivation with वैदग्धक is not attested.

<answer>वैदग्धकथम्</answer>
<answer>लोचनानन्दकल्प</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) lets the affix देशीयर् attach to a nominal stem to express "slightly short of complete", that is, "almost X". The final र् is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix देशीय. Since देशीय begins with a consonant, the final -a of डवित्थ is not elided. So डवित्थ + देशीय gives डवित्थदेशीय, meaning "somewhat like Ḍavittha".

<answer>डवित्थदेशीय</answer>

The given stem is पूर्णापूर्णा, so I took it as written. I did not decide whether the doubled form is a deliberate stem or an error.

The affix ईयसुन् is the comparative suffix. Its उ and न् are indicatory, so it contributes ईयस्.

The stem's final feminine आ (the टाप् suffix) is dropped before the affix, which begins with ई. This is the lopa under यस्येति च (6.4.148). Whether the same result comes through पुंवद्भाव or through this lopa, the base is पूर्णापूर्ण.

Adding ईयस् gives पूर्णापूर्ण + ईयस् = पूर्णापूर्णीयस्.

<answer>पूर्णापूर्णीयस्</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that introduces this affix, so this derivation is my best reconstruction rather than a confirmed rule.

Reading जाहच् by the standard it-marker rules, the initial ज् and final च् are markers. The actual suffix is therefore आह. Because the affix carries ज्, it triggers vṛddhi of the stem's first vowel, and the stem-final अ drops before the vowel-initial suffix.

1. Start with मृषार्थ + आह.
2. Vṛddhi of the first vowel ऋ gives आर्, so मृ becomes मार्.
3. The final अ of मृषार्थ is deleted before आह (यस्येति च), leaving मार्षार्थ् + आह.
4. Joining these gives मार्षार्थाह.

<answer>मार्षार्थाह</answer>

The affix पाशप् is the one taught in "याप्ये पाशप्" (Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.47), used for something defective or contemptible. It is added directly to the stem व्यष्टक.

The affix begins with प, so the rule "यस्येति च" does not delete the stem-final अ. The stem and affix simply join.

<answer>व्यष्टकपाश</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix रूप्य after पिशङ्ग, so this form rests on my best reading of the table rather than a confirmed rule.

I assumed रूप्य carries no marker letters that would trigger vṛddhi. Because रूप्य begins with a consonant (र), the final अ of the stem is not elided, so the affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>पिशङ्गरूप्य</answer>
<answer>कलतर</answer>

The affix छ (SLP1 Ca) is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघाम्). It is added after a "vṛddha" stem (4.2.114, वृद्धाच्छः). The stem औशिज has औ, a vṛddha vowel, in its first syllable, so it qualifies.

Before ईय, the final अ of the stem is dropped (6.4.148), so औशिज + ईय gives औशिजीय.

<answer>औशिजीय</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), with the sense of something contemptible or barely tolerable. I recalled this from memory rather than checking the sūtra. It attaches to the nominal stem यविष्ठ, and the final प् is only a marker, so the added element is पाश. Joining them gives यविष्ठपाश, which ends in -a.

<answer>यविष्ठपाश</answer>

I could not match this affix to a specific Pāṇinian rule with confidence, so this form is a direct combination of the stem and affix.

The affix रूप्य begins with a consonant, so the final -a of the stem उषिज is not elided. The stem and affix are simply joined.

<answer>उषिजरूप्य</answer>
<answer>गायत्रितः</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses this affix on द्रमिट, so this is a general derivation rather than a cited one. The affix छ (SLP1 Ca) is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The final अ of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial affix, which gives द्रमिट + ईय = द्रमिटीय.

<answer>द्रमिटीय</answer>

I could not derive this form with certainty. I assumed that the affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27) simply attaches to the stem and that its final -इ drops away, as in पुरस्तात् and अधरस्तात्. On that basis स्रौवा + अस्तात् gives स्रौवास्तात्. The final आ of the stem and the initial अ of the affix merge into a single long आ by सवर्णदीर्घ.

<answer>स्रौवास्तात्</answer>

Here the affix च्वि (cvi) is added to शर्करक in the sense of coming to be what it was not before (अभूततद्भाव), with the verbs कृ, भू or अस् (as in 5.4.50). The affix itself disappears completely, leaving only its effect, and the final अ of the stem becomes ई by "अस्य च्वौ" (7.4.32). So शर्करक becomes शर्करकी, as in शर्करकी स्यात् or शर्करकी करोति.

<answer>शर्करकी</answer>

जातीयर् (सूत्र 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने) को योध्य के बाद जोड़ने पर अन्तिम र् इत्संज्ञक होकर हट जाता है और प्रत्यय जातीय रह जाता है। जातीय का आदि वर्ण ज् व्यंजन है, इसलिए यस्येति च (6.4.148) से योध्य के अन्तिम अ का लोप नहीं होता। इस प्रकार योध्य + जातीय = योध्यजातीय बनता है, जिसका अर्थ "योध्य प्रकार का" है।

<answer>योध्यजातीय</answer>

This is an application of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), where दघ्नच् is added in the sense of "measure". The final च् is only an indicatory marker (it), so the affix is effectively -दघ्न. Because दघ्न begins with a consonant, the stem-final अ of रुचिट is not dropped by "यस्येति च". The stem and affix therefore simply join as रुचिट + दघ्न, giving the stem रुचिटदघ्न.

<answer>रुचिटदघ्न</answer>

Treating मङ्कि as a plain masculine stem, I take the affix अञ् to be the one taught for the बिदादि group (4.1.104), used for descendants. I did not confirm that मङ्कि is actually listed in that group, so this is an assumption.

1. The affix अञ् carries the marker ञ्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: म → मा, giving माङ्कि + अ.
2. The final इ of the stem is dropped before the affix by यस्येति च, giving माङ्क + अ.
3. The conjunct ङ्क stays as it is, so the stem is माङ्क.

<answer>माङ्क</answer>

I formed this by pāṇinian affixation as a straightforward derivation, without checking whether the affix is strictly licensed for this stem. The affix थाल् (TAl) leaves the form था after dropping the marker ल्. Added to the stem कामोद, it gives कामोद + था = कामोदथा. The result is an indeclinable, so no case or number endings are added. The meaning would be "in the manner of कामोद" (प्रकारवचने थाल्, 5.3.23).

<answer>कामोदथा</answer>

The stem भालुक already has a long ā in its first syllable, so the vṛddhi that अण् normally triggers changes nothing. The final अ of the stem drops before the vowel-initial affix, giving भालुक्, and adding अ restores the same spelling. The derivative therefore looks identical to the base stem. I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule licensing अण् after this stem, so this rests on the general rules of अण् formation.

<answer>भालुक</answer>

This is a form built from the stem सेलग with the affix शस् (Sas), which is added under P.5.4.43 (संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायाम्). That rule applies to a word in the singular with distributive (vīpsā) meaning, so सेलगं सेलगं "each सेलग" becomes सेलग + शस्. The result is an indeclinable, and the final स् of शस् appears as visarga.

<answer>सेलगशः</answer>

This is the affix साति (sāti) of Pāṇini 5.4.52 (विभाषा साति कार्त्स्न्ये), which is added optionally to a nominal stem when totality is meant. It is used with कृ, भू or अस् and gives an indeclinable. The stem पानस takes the affix with no change to its final अ, which I am assuming because I could not recall a rule that would alter it here, giving पानस + साति = पानससाति.

<answer>पानससाति</answer>
<answer>सारितम</answer>

This is a rule-based derivation; the stem तव्य does not match any specific aञ् rule I could identify, so I applied the general taddhita steps.

1. The affix अञ् has a ञ् marker, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem: त → ता, giving ताव्य-.
2. The final अ of the stem तव्य is dropped before the vowel-initial affix, by यस्येति च (6.4.148), giving तव्य्-.
3. Adding the affix अ (with its ञ् marker removed) gives ताव्य्+अ = ताव्य.

<answer>ताव्य</answer>
<answer>साधकक</answer>

I did not trace a specific sūtra for this form, so the result rests on a rule-based reasoning that I am not fully certain of.

The affix ka (as in "प्रागिवात् कः", used for contempt or ignorance) attaches to the stem श्वित्रिन्.

The stem ends in -न्. The ka affix is not a sit affix and does not begin with a vowel or y, so the stem is neither a pada nor a bha stem before it. Rules that would drop the final -न् (8.2.7 and 6.4.144) therefore do not apply, and the -न् stays.

Joining the stem and affix gives श्वित्रिन् + क = श्वित्रिनक.

<answer>श्वित्रिनक</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*), the affix चुञ्चुप् is added to a stem in the sense "known by that" (as in विद्याचुञ्चुः). In चुञ्चुप्, the final प् is only an indicatory marker and drops. The ञ् is part of the affix's actual form चुञ्चु.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of स्थगित is not elided. Joining the two gives स्थगितचुञ्चु.

<answer>स्थगितचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>रामाधिपतिक</answer>

This is a straightforward application of the affix, assuming the stem takes द्वयसच् in the sense of measure (प्रमाणे, Pāṇini 5.2.37).

The final च् of द्वयसच् is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix द्वयस. It begins with a consonant other than य्, so the stem's final अ is not elided (the rule यस्येति च does not apply). The affix also has no ञ् or ण् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. The stem therefore stays whole and the affix is added directly, as in ऊरुद्वयस.

सौमाग्न + द्वयस gives सौमाग्नद्वयस.

<answer>सौमाग्नद्वयस</answer>
<answer>कटुरक</answer>
<answer>पीताम्बरथा</answer>
<answer>फल्कीय</answer>
<answer>भोज्यान्नजातीय</answer>
<answer>दमिसात्</answer>

Adding the superlative affix तमप् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, 5.3.55) to the stem मशाक gives मशाकतम. The final प् is only an indicatory marker and drops, and no further sandhi or substitution applies here.

<answer>मशाकतम</answer>

Taking the affix as चणप् from Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), the form follows the pattern of विद्याचण (like विद्याचुञ्चु). I reasoned this from memory of the sūtra and its examples, not from a checked source.

The affix is added after the instrumental-sense base, with its initial च retained and the प् dropped as an indicatory letter. This gives चण.

Before the consonant-initial affix चण, the stem गरीयसा counts as a pada (1.4.17), not a bha stem. The final आ is therefore not dropped by 6.4.148, as in विद्या + चण. The result is गरीयसा + चण = गरीयसाचण.

<answer>गरीयसाचण</answer>
<answer>ध्यानदेश्य</answer>

I read the affix as क (ka) from the rule प्रागिवात् कः (5.3.70), which adds it to a nominal stem for meanings such as "unknown" or "contemptible." No sandhi change applies when क is added to the final अ of भूतार्त, and since the stem is masculine there is no feminine-suffix adjustment. The result is भूतार्तक.

<answer>भूतार्तक</answer>

The stem पारषद ends in अ, and the affix पाश begins with a consonant, so nothing is elided, and the neuter gender requires no shortening. The two parts simply join: पारषद + पाश.

<answer>पारषदपाश</answer>

The stem नुदिता ends in the feminine ā (ṭāp), so I work through the derivation step by step.

1. Before the taddhita affix इष्ठन् (the final न् is only a marker), the final ā of नुदिता is dropped (P. 6.4.148, यस्येति च). This gives नुदित् + इष्ठ.
2. Before इष्ठन् the ṭi-portion of the stem is also dropped (P. 6.4.155, टेः). The ṭi here is the final vowel together with the consonant after it, so the "इत्" of नुदित् goes. This leaves नुद् + इष्ठ.
3. Joining these gives नुदिष्ठ. Treating the feminine as masculine first (puṃvat) would give नुदित + इष्ठ and reach the same result.

<answer>नुदिष्ठ</answer>

The result is कारंधम + क = कारंधमक, which follows the same pattern as अश्व → अश्वक.

Only the affix's technical identifier is supplied, so I could not locate a specific rule for कुणप् and cannot confirm which meaning licenses it. The form below follows from the mechanics of the affix's markers, and I did not verify it against a source.

1. In कुणप्, the final ण् and प् are indicatory (it) letters, so the affix that remains is कु. The initial क् is not an it letter, by 1.3.8 (लशक्वतद्धिते).

3. The stem-final अ is deleted before a taddhita only when the affix begins with a vowel or य् (6.4.148). Since कु begins with a consonant, the अ stays, and कु is added directly.

This gives धार्मायतन + कु = धार्मायतनकु.

<answer>धार्मायतनकु</answer>
