The affix देशीयर् is taught in P. 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It is added to a subanta stem and means "slightly short of complete".

1. The affix begins with द, a consonant, so the stem वामार्चिस् takes the status of a pada (1.4.17).
2. The final स् of a pada becomes रु (8.2.66).
3. Before the voiced consonant द, this रु is realised as र्.
4. The stem has no ṅī or ṅyāp ending, so the feminine gender triggers no further change such as shortening.

Result: वामार्चिस् + देशीय → वामार्चिर्देशीय

<answer>वामार्चिर्देशीय</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in the sense of "याप्य", something barely sustained or despicable (Pāṇini 5.3.47). I am recalling the shortening rule from memory and could not pin down its exact sūtra number. As I remember it, a stem ending in the feminine suffix ङी or आप् takes a short final vowel before affixes such as तरप्, तमप्, रूपप्, कल्पप् and पाशप्. So दारणी becomes दारणि before पाश.

<answer>दारणिपाश</answer>
<answer>शोद्धव्यावत्</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), with the sense "known by that". It is added to the stem पनितृ.

The प् in चुञ्चुप् is only a marker (for accent), and the affix has no ञ् or ण् marker that would trigger vṛddhi. The affix also begins with a consonant, so the stem is not altered before it and the final ऋ stays. This gives पनितृ + चुञ्चु.

<answer>पनितृचुञ्चु</answer>

This is my best derivation; I could not tie it to a specific Pāṇinian rule.

1. The affix खञ् (KaY) is replaced by ईन, because the initial ख् of an affix becomes ईन. The ञ् is only a marker, and it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem.
2. Vṛddhi turns the first vowel of सर्व into आ, giving सार्व-.
3. The final ई of सर्वानुक्रमणी is dropped before the vowel-initial ईन, by यस्येति च.
4. The न of ईन should stay न, since the intervening ण should block ṇatva.

This gives सार्वानुक्रमण् + ईन = सार्वानुक्रमणीन.

<answer>सार्वानुक्रमणीन</answer>
<answer>नभस्यतर</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra for the affix साति with confidence. This answer assumes it attaches like the related affix सात् (as in अग्निसात्), with no change to the stem. So I simply added साति to the stem पत्त्रित.

<answer>पत्त्रितसाति</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses खञ् after तैतिलि, so this form rests on the general mechanics of the affix, not on a cited rule.

The affix खञ् leaves the substitute ईन, because initial ख becomes ईन (ख् → ईन्, by 7.1.2). The ञ् is only an indicatory letter and calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The first vowel of तैतिलि is already ऐ, which is vṛddhi, so nothing changes there.

The final इ of the stem drops before the ई-initial taddhita (6.4.148). This gives तैतिल् + ईन = तैतिलीन.

<answer>तैतिलीन</answer>

The affix साति (sAti) is added to the nominal stem to form an indeclinable, as in अग्निसात् from अग्नि. I am relying on memory of that pattern rather than a checked source, and in particular on the final -ि of the affix dropping, so the result is कंसिक + साति → कंसिकसात्. The stem कंसिक needs no change before the affix.

<answer>कंसिकसात्</answer>

The stem कूष्माण्ड takes यत्, and the final अ of the stem drops before the य of the affix by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). Since यत् is not a ṇit or ñit affix, there is no vṛddhi. This gives कूष्माण्ड् + य = कूष्माण्ड्य. I formed this from the general rules and did not locate the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses यत् after कूष्माण्ड.

<answer>कूष्माण्ड्य</answer>

The affix जातीयर् (rule 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added to the stem to express "of that kind". The final र् is only a marker and drops out. No other change applies to the stem, so जातीय is attached directly to औपस्थान.

<answer>औपस्थानजातीय</answer>

कोष्ठिका के बाद तमप् लगता है, तो प्रत्यय का तम जुड़ता है। मेरी स्मृति के अनुसार ह्रस्व करने वाला विधान (6.3.42-43) ṅī-अन्त शब्दों पर लगता है, ṭāp-अन्त पर नहीं। इसलिए कोष्ठिका का ā ज्यों का त्यों रहता है। मैंने सूत्र-संख्याएँ स्मृति से ली हैं और जाँची नहीं हैं।

तमप् का अनुबन्ध हटने पर तम बचता है, इसलिए तद्धित प्रातिपदिक कोष्ठिकातम बनता है। इसका स्त्रीलिंग रूप कोष्ठिकातमा होगा, पर प्रश्न तद्धित-प्रातिपदिक माँगता है, इसलिए मैंने स्त्री-प्रत्यय नहीं जोड़ा।

<answer>कोष्ठिकातम</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् (daGnac) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 with the sense of "measure". The final च् is only a marker (it drops out), so the affix added is दघ्न. Since दघ्न begins with a consonant, the final अ of अक्ष is not elided, and the result is simply अक्ष + दघ्न. I derived this from the affix's rule and did not check an attested form such as अक्षदघ्न in a text.

<answer>अक्षदघ्न</answer>
<answer>आतिजगत</answer>

Following the usual Pāṇinian steps for the affix खञ् (KaY), the derivation runs as follows:

1. The affix खञ् is replaced by ईन (by "आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्"), leaving the marker ञ् as an indicatory letter.
2. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (by "तद्धितेषु अचामादेः"). The stem त्वेष्य begins with ए, which becomes ऐ, giving त्वैष्य.
3. The final अ of the stem is deleted before ईन (by "यस्येति च"), leaving त्वैष्य् + ईन.
4. Joining the two parts gives त्वैष्यीन.

<answer>त्वैष्यीन</answer>
<answer>प्रान्तायन</answer>

I treated the input as the feminine stem वैनाशिका with its ā kept, and added मयट् to it. The affix is replaced by its operative form मय, and the final ā of the stem stays. The rule that drops a final a or ā (यस्येति च) only applies before affixes beginning with ī or y, and मय begins with m, so nothing is elided. I derived this by reasoning from the rules rather than checking an attested form.

वैनाशिका + मय → वैनाशिकामय

<answer>वैनाशिकामय</answer>
<answer>साप्तलेयदेश्य</answer>

The affix तल् is the abstract-noun suffix introduced by Pāṇini 5.1.119, "तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ" (the state or quality of that). Adding it to नड gives नड + ता. The result is a feminine stem formed with टाप्, so the derived stem is नडता, meaning "the state of being a reed".

<answer>नडता</answer>
<answer>बहुमुग्धानन</answer>

Under the supplied analysis, the form is built as follows:

1. The affix ठन् (Wan) takes ठ्, which is replaced by इक by ṭhasyekaḥ (7.3.50), so the affix becomes इक.
2. The stem सौपन्थ्य already has its initial vṛddhi (सौ), so adding the affix causes no further vowel change.
3. Before the affix, the final अ of सौपन्थ्य is dropped by yasyeti ca (6.4.148), leaving सौपन्थ्य्.
4. Adding इक gives सौपन्थ्यिक.

I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ठन् after this particular stem, so the derivation rests on the standard treatment of the affix.

<answer>सौपन्थ्यिक</answer>

This is a derivation by rule from the table's inputs; I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठक् after क्वथन.

The affix ठक् has its ठ् replaced by इक (ठस्येकः), and the final क् is an indicatory letter, so the affix acts as a कित् taddhita. Before a कित् taddhita the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (तद्धितेष्वचामादेः and किति च). So the अ in क्व becomes आ, giving क्वाथन. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix's initial vowel, so क्वाथन् + इक becomes क्वाथनिक.

<answer>क्वाथनिक</answer>
<answer>वल्लरीकमात्र</answer>

I formed this by adding the affix दघ्नच् (one of द्वयसच्, दघ्नच्, मात्रच् under Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) directly to the stem अयान्वित. The affix is not ṇit or ñit, so there is no vṛddhi and no deletion of the stem's final vowel. The affix's च् is only an accent marker and drops, leaving the stem अयान्वित + दघ्न.

<answer>अयान्वितदघ्न</answer>
<answer>यथोत्तरमात्र</answer>

The affix पाशप् (pASap) is the one taught in "याप्ये पाशप्" (Pāṇini 5.3.47). It denotes something defective, or kept going only by palliatives, and it is added to the stem after the word कौशाम्भस्.

Because पाशप् begins with a consonant, the stem counts as a pada before it, so its final स् would normally become a visarga before प्. I recall a rule for पाश, कल्प, क and काम्य (8.3.38 as I remember it, number not checked) that keeps the स् in this position. I cite it from memory, as in पयस्पाश, and I have not checked the rule number or wording. So the स् stays, and the form is कौशाम्भस्पाश.

<answer>कौशाम्भस्पाश</answer>
<answer>जरिष्णुकल्प</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them, not from a checked source.

The affix ईयसुन् leaves the operative ending ईयस्, because उ and न् are indicatory letters. Before it, the final vowel of the stem is dropped by the rule that deletes the ṭi-portion of a stem before iṣṭha, imān and īyas (भस्य टेर्लोपः, 6.4.155). So तित्तिरि loses its final इ, leaving तित्तिर्. Adding ईयस् gives तित्तिरीयस्.

<answer>तित्तिरीयस्</answer>

The stem चैकितानेय ends in अ, so the affix इनि is added by the rule "अत इनिठनौ" (Pāṇini 5.2.115), which gives the sense "having that". The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix by "यस्येति च", so चैकितानेय् + इन् gives चैकितानेयिन्, meaning "one who has or possesses (a Chaikitaneya)". I identified the rule from memory and did not check it against a source.

<answer>चैकितानेयिन्</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses रूप्य after क्षुल्ल. The closest candidates are 5.2.120 (यप् after रूप) and 5.3.66 (रूपप्), and neither applies to this stem. I therefore simply joined the affix to the stem. Since क्षुल्ल is a basic a-ending stem, no sandhi or other change arises at the junction.

<answer>क्षुल्लरूप्य</answer>

Pāṇini 4.1.120 (स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्) adds ढक् to a stem ending in a feminine suffix to give a descendant sense. Here the stem is पलिता, ending in टाप्.

1. ढक् becomes एय, since ढ् is replaced by एय (7.1.2).
2. The final आ of पलिता drops before the taddhita ending.
3. The first vowel takes vṛddhi (7.2.117): प → पा.

The result is पालितेय, meaning a descendant of Palitā.

<answer>पालितेय</answer>

The affix जातीयर् (P. 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added to the stem. By 6.3.35 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः), the feminine stem सत्याषाढी takes masculine form (पुंवद्भाव) before an affix in this range. Treating सत्याषाढी as a feminine with a masculine counterpart (सत्याषाढ) is my own judgement, not something I verified. The stem therefore reverts to सत्याषाढ, and जातीयर् is added to give सत्याषाढजातीय. The alternative without पुंवद्भाव, सत्याषाढीजातीय, is the one I rejected.

<answer>सत्याषाढजातीय</answer>

श्रेयस् में वलच् जोड़ने पर, `तसौ मत्वर्थे` (1.4.19) से स्-अन्त शब्द मत्वर्थीय प्रत्यय के पहले भ-संज्ञक होता है, इसलिए अन्तिम स् में रुत्व या लोप नहीं होता। वलच् का च् इत्संज्ञक है और अकार शेष रहता है। इसलिए श्रेयस् + वल = श्रेयस्वल। यह रूप मैंने इसी नियम के आधार पर बनाया है। यह सूत्र-क्रम से सत्यापित नहीं है कि श्रेयस् के साथ वलच् किस विशेष सूत्र से आता है।

<answer>श्रेयस्वल</answer>

The stem is शद्वला, to which the affix खञ् is added. I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule licensing this pairing, so I derived the form from the general rules for the affix's markers.

1. In खञ्, the initial ख् is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन, 7.1.2).
2. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (7.2.117), so श becomes शा.
3. The final -ा of the stem is deleted before the affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148).

This gives शाद्वल + ईन = शाद्वलीन.

<answer>शाद्वलीन</answer>

I applied the affix ईयसुन् (the comparative affix) to पूरण by hand-derivation from the standard rules; I did not check this against a reference.

1. The affix begins with a vowel, so पूरण takes the *bha* designation (यचि भम्, 1.4.18).
2. Under टेर्लोपः (6.4.155), the *ṭi* of a *bha* stem is dropped. The *ṭi* is the last vowel together with what follows it, here "अण्", so पूरण becomes पूर्.
3. Adding the affix's remaining part ईयस् gives पूर् + ईयस्, which is पूरीयस्.

<answer>पूरीयस्</answer>
<answer>जापकासात्</answer>

Following the affix rule 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), the affix दघ्नच् is added directly to the nominal stem, and its final च् is only a marker that drops. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -य of the stem is not elided. The stem therefore stays whole and takes the affix as it is: चौक्र्य + दघ्न.

<answer>चौक्र्यदघ्न</answer>
<answer>सतितर</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation, not a confirmed one. I could not recall the rule that teaches जाहच्, so I did not verify its meaning or conditions.

The affix जाहच् loses its final च् as an indicatory letter and leaves जाह. I assumed, by analogy with जातीयर् (as in पटुजातीय), that the initial ज् is retained. The stem रेचकित ends in short अ, and the affix begins with a consonant, so no vowel elision applies. The stem and affix simply join.

रेचकित + जाह = रेचकितजाह

<answer>रेचकितजाह</answer>

This is a derivation I could not fully verify. I did not identify the exact sūtra that licenses the affix *tasi* after a feminine stem in *-ī*, so I assumed the stem is unchanged before *tasi*. The result is *bharujī* + *tas* = *bharujītas*, an indeclinable. I wrote it with a final visarga, *bharujītaḥ*, as is usual for the complete form. The visarga is my assumption about the expected output format.

<answer>भरुजीतः</answer>

The affix रूपप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), where it conveys praise and is added to a subanta. It is added to हिङ्गुलि, and the ending is the stem-final form रूप, giving हिङ्गुलिरूप. The meaning is "an excellent हिङ्गुलि". I recalled the sūtra from memory and did not check it against the text.

<answer>हिङ्गुलिरूप</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.68–69 (`विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु`), the affix `बहुच्` is added to a subanta in the sense of "slightly short of complete". It is placed before the word, as in `बहुपटुः`. So `बहुच्` is prefixed to `महीलुका`. I did not find a rule that shortens the final vowel or turns the feminine into a masculine-type form here, so the stem is kept as it is. This is my reading from memory of the rules, not something I checked against a text.

<answer>बहुमहीलुका</answer>

I could not identify which Pāṇinian rule licenses अञ् after बाध्या, so this derivation rests on the general rules for adding a ñit taddhita affix to a feminine stem.

1. The stem बाध्या is the base बाध्य plus the feminine suffix टाप् (ā).
2. Before the taddhita affix, the feminine ā is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving बाध्य. Applying यस्येति च again to the final a of बाध्य would reduce it to बाध्य्, with a bare य्.
3. अञ् is a ñit affix, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi. Here it is already ā (बा), so nothing changes.
4. Adding अ to बाध्य् gives बाध्य.

<answer>बाध्य</answer>

Before the affix च्वि (cvi), the final अ/आ of the stem is replaced by ई (7.4.32 अस्य च्वौ). I am relying on a recalled reading that this rule covers a stem-final आ as well as अ, which I have not checked. On that reading, जृम्भिका becomes जृम्भिकी. The affix itself then drops, leaving the stem that combines with कृ, भू or अस् in the sense "becoming what it was not before".

<answer>जृम्भिकी</answer>

The affix इञ् is added by the rule अत इञ् (4.1.95), which applies to stems ending in short अ and gives the sense "descendant of". The stem आनुवासनिक ends in अ, so the final अ drops before इ. The affix is ञित्, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi, but it is already आ, so it stays unchanged. This gives आनुवासनिक् + इ = आनुवासनिकि, meaning "descendant of Ānuvāsanika".

<answer>आनुवासनिकि</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68, with the sense of "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति) from 5.3.67. It is placed before the base (पुरस्तात्), so it appears as the prefix बहु-.

The base रान्द्र्य already ends in short -a. The neuter shortening rule (1.2.47) therefore changes nothing, and the base stays as it is.

Prefixing gives बहु + रान्द्र्य = बहुरान्द्र्य. I have not checked what रान्द्र्य itself means, as the formation does not depend on it.

<answer>बहुरान्द्र्य</answer>

Taddhita छ (SLP1 `Ca`) is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The stem लाव्य has the vṛddhi vowel ā in its first syllable, so it counts as vṛddha and takes छ by 4.2.114 (वृद्धाच्छः).

Adding ईय gives लाव्य + ईय. Before the ई-initial affix, the final अ of the stem is deleted by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), leaving लाव्य् + ईय. The य् stays, so the form is लाव्यीय.

<answer>लाव्यीय</answer>
<answer>भार्यतम</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific example in the grammar, so this derivation is partly inferred. The affix द्वयसच् (dvayasac) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः) for words denoting measure.

The affix is द्वयस, and the final च् is only an indicatory letter. It begins with a consonant and carries no ñit/ṇit marker, so the stem takes no vṛddhi and no ending of the stem is dropped. The stem सहस्रोति simply takes the affix.

सहस्रोति + द्वयस = सहस्रोतिद्वयस

<answer>सहस्रोतिद्वयस</answer>
<answer>अम्बरान्तक</answer>
<answer>सामासिकिन्</answer>

This is a derivation from memory of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which I did not check against the text. The affix चणप् is added in the sense "known by that". Its final प् is only an indicatory letter and drops, so the affix is चण.

The model examples, as I recall them, are विद्याचणः and केशचणः. In विद्याचणः the long ā of the feminine base is kept, so I keep it here too. I am following that pattern rather than a rule I could confirm.

सौभद्रा + चण gives सौभद्राचण, with no case ending added.

<answer>सौभद्राचण</answer>

I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses त्रा after सनिष्यद. The most familiar rule for this affix is 5.4.56, which gives forms like देवत्रा after nouns such as देव. I applied the affix by analogy with that pattern.

The affix त्रा begins with a consonant, so the stem is unchanged and the affix is simply attached. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>सनिष्यदत्रा</answer>
<answer>चमूथा</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), the affix देशीयर् is added to a nominal stem to mean "somewhat, almost, not quite complete". The final र् is only a marker and drops out, leaving the affix देशीय. Since देशीय begins with a consonant, the final -अ of the stem is not elided, and the stem takes the affix unchanged.

पूपालिक + देशीय gives पूपालिकदेशीय, meaning "somewhat like a pūpālika".

<answer>पूपालिकदेशीय</answer>
<answer>सुतासुतिशस्</answer>
<answer>जयोद्धुरीय</answer>

Applying the taddhita affix त्रा (trA) to the stem वृद्धक gives the indeclinable वृद्धकत्रा. I did not trace a specific Pāṇinian rule for this stem, so the formation is the simple one of adding the affix directly to the stem.

<answer>वृद्धकत्रा</answer>

The affix चरट् (caraṭ) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, *bhūtapūrve caraṭ*, "formerly was so-and-so". It lies within the तसिल्-आदि group of affixes (5.3.7 to 5.4.17). Before affixes in that group, a feminine stem takes the masculine form (*pumvat*, 6.3.35). So the feminine-marking आ of ज्ञानोल्का is replaced and the stem becomes ज्ञानोल्क. Adding चर gives the taddhita stem ज्ञानोल्कचर, meaning roughly "one who was formerly a ज्ञानोल्का". I derived this from memory of the rules rather than from a source text.

<answer>ज्ञानोल्कचर</answer>

Since the affix अण् is ṇit, the first vowel of the base takes vṛddhi, and the final अ of the base drops by "yasyeti ca" (6.4.148).

1. The base is त्यजनीय (tyajanīya). Its first vowel is the अ of त्य, which becomes आ by vṛddhi, giving त्याजनीय.
2. The final अ of the base drops before the affix's अ, so the result is त्याजनीय (tyājanīya). One licensed meaning is the descendant sense, "his offspring" (tasyāpatyam, 4.1.92).

<answer>त्याजनीय</answer>

The affix caraṭ is added by the rule "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (A. 5.3.53), meaning "formerly was". I am recalling the rule number and the steps below from memory rather than checking them against the text.

1. The stem दुन्दुभ्या is feminine and ends in the ā of ṭāp. Caraṭ falls in the range of affixes (tasil through kṛtvasuc) before which a feminine stem takes masculine form (6.3.35). So the final -ā is replaced and the stem becomes दुन्दुभ्य.
2. Adding चर to दुन्दुभ्य gives दुन्दुभ्यचर. This is the taddhita stem. If a feminine form were wanted, the ṭit marker of caraṭ would add ṅīp, giving दुन्दुभ्यचरी, but I have taken the answer to be the stem without that step.

I am not certain whether the intended answer includes the feminine ṅīp.

<answer>दुन्दुभ्यचर</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rules for adding तरप् (comparative), as I recall them, and I did not check it against the text of the sūtras.

तरप् is added directly to the stem कर्बूरिता. The shortening rule 6.3.43 (ङ्यः … ह्रस्वः) applies to stems ending in ङी, not to stems ending in आ (आप्). So the final आ of कर्बूरिता stays long, and no other rule shortens it. This gives कर्बूरिता + तर = कर्बूरितातर.

<answer>कर्बूरितातर</answer>
<answer>खण्डिकोपाध्यायता</answer>

Adding अण् to भाल gives भाल्+अ. The stem-final अ is dropped before the taddhita affix (यस्येति च), and the first vowel is already long, so vṛddhi changes nothing. The result is भाल, for example in the sense "belonging to the forehead" (तस्येदम्).

<answer>भाल</answer>
<answer>भूतारब्धदेश्य</answer>
<answer>क्षुभितदेशीय</answer>
<answer>बादरमय</answer>
<answer>मङ्खुणमय</answer>

I formed this by attaching the affix त्रा directly to the stem आतिष्ठ. The stem ends in अ, so no sandhi or other change applies. I did not check which specific Pāṇinian rule licenses त्रा for this particular stem, so the form rests on simple concatenation.

<answer>आतिष्ठत्रा</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses अञ् after ग्राही, so this form comes from the general derivation rather than a confirmed sūtra.

The stem ends in the feminine ई, which is dropped before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). That leaves ग्राह्. Adding अञ् gives ग्राह + अ. The stem's first vowel is already long आ, so vṛddhi (the strengthening of the first vowel) changes nothing, and the result is ग्राह.

<answer>ग्राह</answer>

This form is a direct concatenation, with one caveat. I could not match शुश्रूषेण्य to a rule that licenses वलच् (the nearest rule I recall is 5.2.109, which lists specific bases), so I formed it mechanically from the given inputs.

The affix वलच् leaves the base वल after the markers are dropped (the च् only marks the accent). The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem is not elided by "यस्येति च". The stem and affix therefore join unchanged: शुश्रूषेण्य + वल = शुश्रूषेण्यवल.

<answer>शुश्रूषेण्यवल</answer>

Here शस् is the taddhita affix of "-wise/by many" (बहुशः type). The affix keeps its श, so it is added to क्षत्रौजस् as a whole.

1. क्षत्रौजस् + शस् gives क्षत्रौजस्शस्.
2. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem counts as a pada (1.4.17). Its final स् therefore becomes रु (8.2.66) and then visarga.
3. Before the शर् letter श, the visarga stays (8.3.35), which gives क्षत्रौजःशस्.
4. The final स् of the affix becomes रु and then visarga, so the result is क्षत्रौजःशः.

I did not verify against a derivation tool, and the visarga treatment is the least certain step. By 8.3.36 the visarga before श could optionally become श्, which would give क्षत्रौजश्शः. If the stem were not a pada, the form would be क्षत्रौजसशः. I chose the visarga form as the default.

<answer>क्षत्रौजःशः</answer>

The stem साशिरा ends in the feminine suffix आ (टाप्). The affix मयट् begins with a consonant (म), so the stem does not take the *bha* designation and its final आ is not dropped. This is the same pattern as विद्यामय. Attaching the affix (the final ट् is only a marker) gives साशिरा + मय = साशिरामय.

<answer>साशिरामय</answer>

This is a derivation from memory, not checked against the Aṣṭādhyāyī text.

The affix इष्ठन् (izWan) takes the stem करक (karaka) and forms the superlative sense (अतिशायने). Before इष्ठन्, the stem counts as *bha*, so the rule that drops the *ṭi* part (the last vowel plus any consonants after it) applies. In करक the *ṭi* part is "अक", so it is dropped, leaving कर्. Adding इष्ठ gives करिष्ठ. The stem's neuter gender plays no part in this.

<answer>करिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>विद्यावतंसस्तात्</answer>

Applying अञ् to औपसर्गिक gives the same surface form. I could not identify the specific rule that licenses अञ् for this stem, so this derivation is my best reasoning rather than a confirmed rule-based result.

- The stem already begins with the vṛddhi vowel औ, so the आदिवृद्धि required before a ञित् affix changes nothing.
- The final अ of the stem is deleted before the अ of अञ् by यस्येति च (6.4.148).
- The अ of अञ् then follows the क्, which restores the same stem.

<answer>औपसर्गिक</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses the affix कुणप्, so this form is a best guess rather than a derivation I could verify.

I assumed that in the affix कुणप् the final प् is the only marker letter. That leaves the affix as कुण, which begins with a consonant. The stem-final इ of दान्ति therefore stays, and the form is दान्ति + कुण.

<answer>दान्तिकुण</answer>
<answer>वरुणाङ्गरुहत्व</answer>
<answer>हसितवत्</answer>

The affix बहुच् (P. 5.3.68, *vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*) is added optionally to a subanta in the sense of "almost, not quite complete". Unlike most taddhita affixes, it is placed before the word, so मुण्डी keeps its feminine ending unchanged and becomes बहुमुण्डी, meaning "almost a shaven woman".

<answer>बहुमुण्डी</answer>
<answer>अच्छावाकीयपाश</answer>

The affix खञ् (KaY) is replaced by its substitute ईन (the initial ख becomes ईन, and the ञ् is only a marker). The marker ञ् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). In गृहीतार्थ the first vowel is ऋ, which becomes आर्, giving गार्हीतार्थ-. The final अ of the stem is then dropped before ईन. This gives गार्हीतार्थीन.

I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् after this particular stem. The form follows only from the general rules for the affix.

<answer>गार्हीतार्थीन</answer>

This is an application of Pāṇini 5.2.37, where मात्रच् is added in the sense of "measure". मात्रच् begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem is not elided. The affix also carries no ञित् or णित् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. Its च् is only an accent marker. The stem and affix therefore simply join as अहेध्म + मात्र. I did not check whether this particular stem is attested with this affix.

<answer>अहेध्ममात्र</answer>

This is the affix रूपप् (Pāṇini 5.3.66, "प्रशंसायां रूपप्"), which is added to a nominal word to mean "praiseworthy" or "excellent". The stem पौतुद्रुवा, taken as praised, becomes पौतुद्रुवा + रूप, meaning "an excellent पौतुद्रुवा".

The result is feminine, so it takes the feminine ending -ā (टाप्), giving रूपा.

I recall that the vowel-shortening rule 6.3.43 applies only to ī-ending (ṅī) stems, so पौतुद्रुवा keeps its long ā. I did not verify this against the sūtra text, so it is the one uncertain step.

<answer>पौतुद्रुवारूपा</answer>

I applied the affix छ (Ca), which is replaced by ईय under the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्. The final आ of the stem कपटिका drops before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च). That gives कपटिक + ईय = कपटिकीय.

<answer>कपटिकीय</answer>
<answer>तिरीचीनता</answer>

The stem न्यायिन् takes अञ् as follows:

1. Add the affix: न्यायिन् + अ.
2. The final टि of the stem (इन्) is dropped before the taddhita affix by 6.4.144 (नस्तद्धिते), leaving न्याय्.
3. The initial vowel आ of न्यायिन् is already vṛddhi, so the ञित् effect changes nothing.
4. Joining gives न्याय् + अ = न्याय.

I derived this from the general rules rather than from one specific sūtra, so the choice of meaning is left open.

<answer>न्याय</answer>
<answer>नगाटनता</answer>

<answer>साभिचरणिकतर</answer>

This follows the pattern of the affix "valac" (as in कृषीवल), where the stem's final vowel stays when the affix is added.

The affix "वलच्" leaves the stem "वल" once the indicatory "च्" is dropped. It begins with "व्", a consonant that is not "य्", so the base keeps the status of a pada (भ-संज्ञा under 1.4.18 does not apply). Because of this, the rule "यस्येति च" does not delete the final "आ" of "नवेदा". The stem therefore stays whole, as in "कृषीवल", and the result is नवेदा + वल = नवेदावल.

This is my own derivation from the rules, not checked against a source for this exact form.

<answer>नवेदावल</answer>

I could not identify a specific rule that targets सृप्त with ठक्, so I formed the derivative by the general rules for ठक्. I assumed the default ठक् sense, such as the one from 4.4.1 onward.

1. The affix ठक् has initial ठ्, which is replaced by इक (ठस्येकः, 7.3.50).
2. The affix is marked with ठ् and क्, so the stem's first vowel takes vṛddhi. Here ऋ in सृ becomes आर्, giving सार्प्त.
3. Adding the affix gives सार्प्त + इक = सार्प्तिक.

<answer>सार्प्तिक</answer>

I formed this by simply adding the affix त्रा to the stem तातल. I did not trace which Pāṇinian rule licenses the affix on this particular stem. Because त्रा begins with a consonant, the final अ of the stem is not dropped, which gives तातलत्रा.

<answer>तातलत्रा</answer>

The taddhita affix जातीयर् is added in the sense of "kind of" (Pāṇini 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्). The final ए of the ṭi-form is not involved here, so the steps are:

1. The affix begins with the consonant ज्, so it is not one of the y- or vowel-initial affixes (यचि भम्). The stem therefore keeps pada status before it (स्वादिष्वसर्वनामस्थाने).
2. The final स् of श्वेतार्चिस् becomes रु (ससजुषो रुः), which surfaces as र् before the voiced consonant ज्.
3. This gives श्वेतार्चिर्जातीय. The pattern is the same as in सर्पिर्जातीय.

<answer>श्वेतार्चिर्जातीय</answer>
<answer>रिङ्गिमत्</answer>

Applying ढक् to a feminine stem in -ā is taught by P. 4.1.120 (स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्), in the sense of "descendant of". I am recalling that rule from memory rather than checking it.

1. The affix ढक् is converted to एय, since initial ढ is replaced by एय (P. 7.1.2).
2. The final -ā of वैरागिका is dropped before the taddhita affix, giving वैरागिक + एय.
3. The first vowel is already vṛddhi (वै), so no further change is needed.

This gives वैरागिकेय, meaning "son of Vairāgikā".

<answer>वैरागिकेय</answer>

Applying ठक् (Wak) to पुरुषायुष, the affix ठ is replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50). The final अ of the stem drops before the affix. The first vowel then takes vṛddhi (ādivṛddhi, because the affix is ṭit/ṇit-type), so पु becomes पौ. This gives पौरुषायुषिक. I did not identify a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for this stem and affix, so this follows the general ठक् derivation.

<answer>पौरुषायुषिक</answer>

I could not pin down the specific rule that licenses यत् after this stem, so this form is a best judgement rather than a rule-derived result. By analogy with पितृ + यत् → पित्र्य, the final ऋ of the stem becomes a semivowel र् before the यत् affix, giving a form ending in -र्य. I kept the supplied doubled-त spelling of the stem.

<answer>कर्त्त्र्य</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a rule that licenses थाल् for it. The affix is normally added to किम्, sarvanāma words and बहु (P. 5.3.23, prakāravacane thāl, with the meaning "in the manner of"), and मूषिकाकृति is not one of these. The form below assumes the affix is added anyway.

The final ल् of थाल् is only an indicatory marker and drops out, leaving the ending -था. Because थ begins with a consonant, the final -इ of the stem is not elided. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>मूषिकाकृतिथा</answer>

<answer>विश्वाचिका</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्), the affix जातीयर् is added to the stem लान्द्रका to mean "of that kind". Because जातीयर् falls within the range of affixes covered by 6.3.35 (तसिलादिष्वाकृत्वसुचः), the feminine stem takes the masculine form (पुंवद्भाव) before it. So the final -ā of लान्द्रका drops to give लान्द्रक, and adding जातीय gives the stem below. I did not check this against a source; the pumvat step is the main judgement call.

<answer>लान्द्रकजातीय</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.66 (praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap) adds the affix रूपप् to a nominal to express praise. Added to औद्भिज्ज, it gives the stem औद्भिज्जरूप, meaning "an excellent औद्भिज्ज". I took the stem as unchanged before the affix, which I did not verify against the commentarial literature.

<answer>औद्भिज्जरूप</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् for this stem, so this form comes from applying the affix's markers in the standard way, not from a rule I checked.

In ञ्यट्, ञ् and ट् are indicatory letters (it) and the affix itself is -य. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so कर्कटक becomes कार्कटक. The final -अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च), and adding य gives कार्कटक्य.

<answer>कार्कटक्य</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rules for KaY, not a form I checked against a specific sūtra.

The affix खञ् (KaY) has its initial ख replaced by ईन, and the ञ् is only a marker. That marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem: न → ना. The final अ of नराशन drops before the vowel-initial affix.

So नराशन + ईन gives नाराशनीन. There is no णत्व, because the श between र and न blocks it.

<answer>नाराशनीन</answer>

Applying the affix ञ्यट् to मित्रयु gives the form below. I could not recall the specific Aṣṭādhyāyī rule that licenses ञ्यट् here, so the derivation rests on the general taddhita rules.

1. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the suffix ‑य. The ञ् marks vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so मि becomes मै and the stem is मैत्रयु.
2. The stem ends in उ, and before a taddhita the final उ takes guṇa (ओर्गुणः, 6.4.146), giving मैत्रयो + य.
3. Before the vowel-initial य, ओ changes to अव् (एचोऽयवायावः, 6.1.78), giving मैत्रयव्य.
4. The ट् marks the feminine in ङीप्, which does not affect the masculine stem.

<answer>मैत्रयव्य</answer>
<answer>अवह्नित्रा</answer>
<answer>दिधिषुमात्र</answer>
<answer>रूपाजीवीय</answer>

I could not tie ताड to any specific rule that licenses वलच्. The rules I recall for it, such as रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच् (5.2.112) and the one for दन्त and शिखा, name other stems, so this form rests on the general pattern only.

The affix वलच् loses its indicatory letters च् (and the ल् is kept as part of the affix), leaving the suffix -वल. Adding it to the stem ताड gives ताड + वल, which joins directly because the stem ends in -अ and the affix begins with a consonant.

<answer>ताडवल</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् here, so this form comes from applying the general taddhita rules rather than from a confirmed rule.

1. The stem एतिका loses its final feminine आ before the taddhita affix, leaving एतिक.
2. The affix ञ्यट् leaves the ending -य. Its ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel, so ए becomes ऐ.
3. The ट् marker would only matter for forming a feminine in ङीप्, which is not requested here, so I give the bare stem.

This gives ऐतिक + य = ऐतिक्य.

<answer>ऐतिक्य</answer>

I did not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ठक् on this stem, so the form below follows only the general mechanics of the affix.

The affix ठक् has the substitute इक (ठ् → इक, by "ठस्येकः"). The stem's final अ is then dropped by "यस्येति च", giving त्रैवर्षिक् + इक.

The stem already has its initial vṛddhi (त्रै-), so nothing further changes. The result is त्रैवर्षिकिक.

<answer>त्रैवर्षिकिक</answer>

Taking ईयसुन् as the comparative affix (द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ, 5.3.57), it is added to पञ्चाक्ष. Before ईयसुन्, the final टि of the stem is dropped (टेः, 6.4.155), so the stem-final अ goes: पञ्चाक्ष् + ईयस्. This gives the stem पञ्चाक्षीयस्.

वाहस् + ता gives वाहस्ता. I did not work out any further sandhi change at the junction and left the final स् unchanged, as in similar forms such as मनस्ता.

<answer>वाहस्ता</answer>

Here तल् is the affix of abstract nouns, taught in Pāṇini 5.1.119 (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ), meaning "the state or quality of that". Adding it to सेन्द्र gives सेन्द्र + ता. The final ल् is an indicatory letter and drops, and the त is retained. Words in -तल् are feminine, so the stem takes the feminine suffix टाप् (आ). That yields सेन्द्रता, "the state of being accompanied by Indra".

<answer>सेन्द्रता</answer>

I could not identify the rule that licenses जाहच्, so this form rests on the standard way Pāṇinian affix markers work rather than on a confirmed derivation.

1. In जाहच्, the initial ज् is an indicatory letter (it) by 1.3.7 (चुटू), and the final च् is an it by 1.3.3 (हलन्त्यम्). That leaves the actual affix as आह.
2. The stem शद्रि ends in -इ. Before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel, this final -इ is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). That gives शद्र्.
3. Adding आह to शद्र् gives शद्राह.

<answer>शद्राह</answer>

This is a direct application of the affix द्वयसच्, which Pāṇini 5.2.37 teaches in the sense of "measure". The final च् is only an indicatory letter (it), so the affix that remains is द्वयस.

The affix begins with a consonant and is not ḍit, so the stem सौत्रामणिक keeps its final letter and nothing is elided. The form is simply the stem followed by द्वयस. I did not check whether this stem is actually attested with this affix; I formed it mechanically from the table.

<answer>सौत्रामणिकद्वयस</answer>

This follows Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*: the affix rūpap is added to a nominal word to express praise. The p in rūpap is only a marker and drops out. Adding it to बन्धन gives बन्धनरूप, "an excellent बन्धन". I did not work through the sandhi or the treatment of the inflection on the base, since the question asks for the bare derived stem.

<answer>बन्धनरूप</answer>

This is a best-judgement derivation from memory of the rules, not a checked one.

The affix पाशप् (pASap) is taught in Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.47, "याप्ये पाशप्", and its meaning is "contemptible, inferior".

I recall no rule that shortens the final -ā of the base or applies puṃvadbhāva before पाशप्. So the stem सितांशुका keeps its long ā and takes the affix, giving सितांशुकापाश. The final अ of the affix is the usual लशक्वतद्धिते-type of marker-free vowel, so no further change applies.

The result keeps the gender of its base, so it takes the feminine ending again: सितांशुकापाशा.

<answer>सितांशुकापाशा</answer>
<answer>धारयन्तिका</answer>

Taking शाठायन्य as a vṛddha stem (its first vowel शा is vṛddhi), the affix छ is added by 4.2.114 वृद्धाच्छः. I recalled this rule from memory and did not check it. The affix छ is replaced by ईय (7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).

I treated the final -य of the stem as an apatya affix, so 6.4.151 आपत्यस्य च तद्धितेऽनाति drops it before ईय. This is the same process that gives गार्ग्य → गार्गीय. If that treatment is wrong, the form would instead be शाठायन्यीय.

शाठायन्य + ईय → शाठायन् + ईय → शाठायनीय

<answer>शाठायनीय</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses खञ् on this stem, so this form is reasoned from the general mechanics of the affix rather than checked against a rule.

Under that assumption:

1. खञ् is replaced by ईन (ख → ईन), and the final अ of the stem पारीण is dropped before it, giving पारीण् + ईन.
2. The first vowel of पारीण is already आ, so the vṛddhi triggered by the ञ् marker changes nothing.
3. The न of ईन is not changed to ण. The ण of the stem stands between the र and the न, and ण is not among the sounds that may intervene for ण-substitution, so the substitution is blocked.

This gives पारीणीन.

<answer>पारीणीन</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् (SLP1 izWan) is the superlative affix of "तिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ" (5.3.55). Before इष्ठन्, the stem's टि is deleted by 6.4.155 (टेः). The टि is the final vowel together with any consonants after it. In अस्फुटालंकार the last vowel is आ, followed by र, so the टि is "आर".

Deleting it leaves अस्फुटालंक्, and adding इष्ठ gives अस्फुटालंकिष्ठ.

<answer>अस्फुटालंकिष्ठ</answer>

Applying अण् to मनसा drops the final आ (यस्येति च) and gives vṛddhi to the first vowel, so म becomes मा. The result is मानस, for example in the sense "descendant of or belonging to मनसा".

<answer>मानस</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् on a feminine ṭāp-ending stem, so this form comes from the general rules for the affix rather than a confirmed source rule.

1. The affix खञ् becomes ईन, since ख is replaced by ईन.
2. The ञ् marker calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The stem's first vowel is already औ, so nothing changes.
3. The final -ā of the feminine stem drops before the affix, which gives सौत्सुक्य्, and then ईन is added.

<answer>सौत्सुक्यीन</answer>

I applied the affix देश्य (Pāṇini 5.3.67, "somewhat, almost") directly to the stem मेहला.

The one doubt is whether the feminine-to-masculine replacement rule (पुंवद्भाव, 6.3.42) applies before देश्य. It requires a "bhāṣitapuṃska" base, meaning the word also has a masculine form with the same sense. I recall that restriction continuing into 6.3.42, but I am not certain. Since मेहला is used only in the feminine, I assumed no such replacement and kept the ā.

<answer>मेहलादेश्य</answer>

The matup ending is added to the stem कुररावा. I derived the form from rules as I remember them, without checking them against a source text.

1. The stem ends in the long vowel आ. By 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः), the म of मतुप् becomes व after a stem ending in अ or आ, so the affix appears as वत्.
2. The long आ already in the stem remains unchanged. I did not apply any shortening, since neither of the two rules I considered fits here (6.3.63 on ṅyāp shortening, and 6.3.119 on lengthening before matup).

The result is कुररावा + वत्, giving the stem कुररावावत्.

<answer>कुररावावत्</answer>

I could not match विरट to a stem that the rules normally allow थमु on. Pāṇini 5.3.24 gives थमु after इदम्, and 5.3.25 gives it after किम्. So the form below simply attaches the affix to the given stem.

The affix is थमु, and its final उ is only a marker that drops. What remains is थम्, which begins with a consonant, so the final अ of विरट stays. The derivative is an indeclinable.

<answer>विरटथम्</answer>

The stem स्थूलोदरा ends in the feminine suffix आ, and the affix वलच् begins with the consonant व. Because it does not begin with a vowel or य, the stem does not take the भ designation, so the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not delete the final आ. The final च् of वलच् is only an indicatory letter, so what is added is व + अ (वल). That gives स्थूलोदरा + वल = स्थूलोदरावल. I derived this from the rules rather than from an attested example. In particular, I did not check whether Pāṇini actually licenses वलच् after a stem like this, so this rests on the task's instruction that any licensed meaning is acceptable.

<answer>स्थूलोदरावल</answer>

Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः) licenses मात्रच् after a nominal stem to mean "of the measure of". The final च् is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix मात्र. The stem नर्तकक ends in अ, and मात्र begins with a consonant other than य, so the stem's final vowel is not elided. The two simply join as नर्तकक + मात्र.

<answer>नर्तककमात्र</answer>

Here "रूप्य" is the affix itself, and it begins with a consonant, so the final -a of the stem चौड stays. Attaching the affix directly gives चौडरूप्य. This is a straightforward concatenation, and I did not check which sūtra licenses the affix on this base.

<answer>चौडरूप्य</answer>
<answer>यानी</answer>

The stem सागरा ends in the feminine suffix ā (टाप्), and तमप् is a "gha" affix (like तरप्). Rule 6.3.43 shortens a stem-final feminine ī or ā before a gha affix, so सागरा becomes सागर- and the affix is added to give सागरतम.

<answer>सागरतम</answer>

I read the affix as the taddhita तसि (तस्), which attaches directly to the a-ending stem and yields an indeclinable. Adding तस् to नेरेल्ल gives नेरेल्लतस्, and the final स् is written as visarga in the citation form. I did not verify the stem नेरेल्ल against any lexicon.

<answer>नेरेल्लतः</answer>
<answer>दन्त्यवत्</answer>

Adding the superlative affix तमप् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ) to the masculine stem वनीपक gives the stem वनीपकतम. The final प् of the affix is only a marker, and no sandhi or other change applies.

<answer>वनीपकतम</answer>
<answer>रत्नार्णवपाश</answer>
<answer>मानयानजातीय</answer>

This is the affix पाशप् (SLP1 pASap), taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्) with the sense of something despicable or barely sustainable. It is added directly to the stem वैभावर. The stem already ends in -a, so nothing changes at the junction, and the derived stem is वैभावरपाश.

<answer>वैभावरपाश</answer>
<answer>सुखारोहणतर</answer>

I did not derive this from a specific rule text for the stem स्फीति. The affix दघ्नच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसच्दघ्नच्मात्रचः), where it is added to a nominal stem in the sense of a measure. I applied it to स्फीति on that basis. The final च् is only a marker, so what is added is दघ्न. The result is the stem स्फीतिदघ्न. I did not check whether this form is attested.

<answer>स्फीतिदघ्न</answer>

The affix कल्पप् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः). It is added to a nominal stem to mean "slightly short of complete", here "almost a क्षेत्रिय". The stem क्षेत्रिय simply takes -कल्प with no sandhi change, giving the stem क्षेत्रियकल्प.

<answer>क्षेत्रियकल्प</answer>

I could not pin down the exact sūtra for this affix on this stem, so this form rests on the general rule for adding वलच्, not on a specific licence I checked.

The stem सिक्ता ends in the feminine long ā, and the affix वलच् adds वल after dropping its indicatory letters. The final च् of the affix is only an marker, so it disappears. Because वल begins with a consonant, the stem's final ā stays unchanged and takes no vṛddhi or other substitution. The result is the stem सिक्तावल.

<answer>सिक्तावल</answer>

I take the affix चणप् from Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ ("known by that"). I am working from memory of this sūtra and did not check it against the text.

The stem केसरिन् ends in न्. The affix चण begins with a consonant, so the stem counts as a pada before it (1.4.17). That triggers deletion of the final न् (8.2.7), giving केसरि + चण. The final प् is only a marker and drops out.

The sense would be "known by केसरिन्" (केसरिणा वित्तः), parallel to the traditional example विद्याचण.

<answer>केसरिचण</answer>

Here the affix क (ka) is added to the stem रातिन्.

1. Before a taddhita beginning with a consonant other than य, the stem counts as a *pada* (1.4.17). It is not a *bha* stem, so the टि-deletion of 6.4.144 does not apply.
2. Because it is a *pada*, the final न् of the stem is dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), which leaves रातिक. This is the same pattern that gives राजक from राजन्.

I derived this by applying the rules, not by checking a source. The one uncertain point is whether the stem counts as *pada* or *bha* before क. If it counted as *bha*, the result would be रातक instead, so रातिक rests on the *pada* reading.

<answer>रातिक</answer>

The affix थमु (SLP1 Tamu) loses its final इत् उ, leaving the ending थम्. It is added to the stem आपगेय as supplied. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped. Taddhita forms that take no case endings are indeclinable, so the result is आपगेयथम्.

Pāṇini actually teaches थमु only after इदम् (5.3.24) and किम् (5.3.25), so the table's input does not fit the usual rule. I formed the word mechanically from the given stem and affix.

<answer>आपगेयथम्</answer>
<answer>वर्णोद्धृतितः</answer>

I recalled the affix from Pāṇini 5.3.47, याप्ये पाशप्, and applied it to the stem without checking the rule text. It gives the sense "contemptible" or "deserving to be dismissed", so उपवसथीय plus पाश gives "a contemptible उपवसथीय".

The final अ of the stem is not deleted before पाश. The affix begins with a consonant, not य or a vowel, so the stem does not get the भ designation (1.4.18), and 6.4.148 does not apply. The प् of पाशप् is only a marker and drops out.

<answer>उपवसथीयपाश</answer>
<answer>साम्परायिकातः</answer>

I could not identify a specific rule for this stem, so this derivation rests on the general behaviour of मयट् and the result is somewhat uncertain.

मयट् begins with a consonant, so the stem is not treated as "bha" and the stem-final आ is not deleted. Compare विद्यामय and मायामय, where the आ is kept. Adding मयट् to शाखाम्ला therefore gives शाखाम्लामय.

<answer>शाखाम्लामय</answer>

Taking the stem नेरेल्ल as ending in short -a, the affix इनि (ini) is added in its possessive sense ("one who has नेरेल्ल"), under अत इनिठनौ (5.2.115). The final -a of the stem drops before the affix. Since इनि is not marked ṇit, there is no vṛddhi. This gives the stem नेरेल्ल + इन् → नेरेल्लिन्, parallel to दण्ड → दण्डिन्.

<answer>नेरेल्लिन्</answer>

I applied the comparative affix ईयसुन् (ईयस्) to the stem and dropped the stem's final टि before it.

1. The stem is राजान्तकरण.
2. By the rule भस्य टेर्लोपः इष्ठेमेयस्सु (6.4.155), the टि of the stem is deleted before ईयसुन्. The टि is the last vowel with any consonants after it, here the final अ of ण.
3. This leaves राजान्तकरण् + ईयस्, which gives राजान्तकरणीयस्.

<answer>राजान्तकरणीयस्</answer>
<answer>बाहीनर्य</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses फिञ् for this stem, so this derivation rests on the general behaviour of the affix.

1. In फिञ्, the initial फ् is replaced by आयन् (Pāṇini 7.1.2), and the final ञ् is only a marker. The affix therefore surfaces as -आयनि.
2. The marker ञ् calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem. The stem साहस्रान्त्य already begins with long आ, so nothing changes there.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). That gives साहस्रान्त्य् + आयनि.

The result is साहस्रान्त्यायनि, meaning a descendant of साहस्रान्त्य.

<answer>साहस्रान्त्यायनि</answer>
<answer>अचिराभिका</answer>
<answer>मुरवत्</answer>
<answer>किरकता</answer>
<answer>वीषिताता</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् (dvayasac) comes from A 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which gives a measure sense. It is added to the whole stem अरुणाश्वा. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem does not count as भ (the form that triggers यस्येति च लोपः, A 6.4.148). The final आ of the stem is therefore not deleted. The final च् of the affix is only an indicatory letter, so what remains is द्वयस. This gives the neuter stem अरुणाश्वाद्वयस. I did not check this against a source, so the retention of आ rests on this reasoning.

<answer>अरुणाश्वाद्वयस</answer>

The affix मात्रच् is added to the stem उन्मूलना. The base ends in the feminine suffix आ. Since मात्रच् begins with म, it does not trigger the elision of the final आ (यस्येति च), so the stem stays whole before the affix. The result is a neuter stem.

<answer>उन्मूलनामात्र</answer>

The affix cvi (अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः) is added to the stem प्रजोत्पादन. By the rule अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32), the final अ of the stem becomes ई, which gives प्रजोत्पादनी.

<answer>प्रजोत्पादनी</answer>

This is a mechanical derivation rather than an attested form. As far as I recall, Pāṇini prescribes थमु only after इदम् and किम् (5.3.24–25), so I could not match वैमद to a rule that licenses it.

The affix थमु drops its final इत् मु and leaves थम्. The stem वैमद already has its vṛddhi vowel in the first syllable and ends in अ. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not elided. Adding थम् gives वैमदथम्, an indeclinable (अव्यय) ending in म्.

<answer>वैमदथम्</answer>

The stem युगान्त takes the affix अञ्. The ञ् is only a marker and causes vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so यु becomes यौ. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix अ, giving यौगान्त. I did not find युगान्त in the list of words that take vṛddhi in both parts (अनुशतिकादि), but I am working from memory and did not verify the list. I also did not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses अञ् here.

<answer>यौगान्त</answer>

I am not fully certain of the sandhi here. I formed the stem by adding तमप् to पूर्वोत्थिता and then the feminine ending टाप्.

The ending ā should be shortened before a ghā-affix such as तमप् (apparently P. 6.3.43, ṅyāp-ending stems), though I could not firmly confirm that this rule covers ā-stems as well as ī-stems. Applying it gives पूर्वोत्थित + तम, and the feminine ā is then added, giving पूर्वोत्थिततमा.

If the shortening rule applied only to ī-stems, the form would instead be पूर्वोत्थितातमा.

<answer>पूर्वोत्थिततमा</answer>

The affix अण् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (ādivṛddhi), so the ब of बलाधिक takes ब → बा. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix's अ. This gives बालाधिक, which can carry any of the meanings licensed for अण्, such as "descendant of" (तस्यापत्यम्). I did not find a special rule for neuter source stems that would change this.

<answer>बालाधिक</answer>

I treated रूप्य as a whole affix added directly to the stem हनु. I did not check this against a specific Pāṇinian sūtra, since the standard rules I recall (such as 5.2.120) add यप् or रूपप्, not रूप्य.

Because रूप्य begins with the consonant र् and not with य् or a vowel, the stem is not treated as *bha* (1.4.18). It counts as a *pada* instead. So the ओर्गुणः rule (6.4.146) does not apply, and the final -u stays unchanged, with no guṇa or अव् substitution. The result is simple concatenation.

<answer>हनुरूप्य</answer>

I applied Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which attaches देश्य to a subanta in the sense of "almost, not quite complete".

The stem मैत्रायणका is feminine and ends in ā. Ordinarily it would take the masculine-like form before देश्य (pumvadbhāva, 6.3.42). Rule 6.3.37 (न कोपधायाः) blocks this when the penultimate letter is क, as it is here. The stem therefore keeps its long ā.

The ā of ṭāp is followed by a sup ending when the affix is added, so 7.3.44 (which would change the preceding a to i) does not apply. The result is मैत्रायणका + देश्य.

<answer>मैत्रायणकादेश्य</answer>

Here छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय under the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्. The final अ of जुकुट is dropped before the affix, so जुकुट + ईय gives जुकुटीय. I could not identify the specific rule that licenses छ for this stem. The answer assumes a छ-affix rule such as गहादिभ्यश्च applies, and I did not confirm that जुकुट is in that list.

<answer>जुकुटीय</answer>

Before the affix तरप् is added, the stem takes pada status, so the final न् of लापिन् drops (by नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), leaving लापि. Adding तरप् gives लापि + तर = लापितर. I treated this as the ordinary comparative sense "more of a talker."

<answer>लापितर</answer>
<answer>ध्रतम</answer>

Here the affix is the one taught in the Aṣṭādhyāyī (साति, SLP1 sAti), which is added to a nominal stem in the sense "made dependent on that" (e.g. अग्निसात्). The resulting form is an indeclinable that ends in सात्. I am recalling the exact sūtra and the loss of the final -i from memory rather than checking it, so the ending सात् rests on that recollection (the related rule 8.3.111, सात्पदाद्योः, also names the affix as सात्).

Adding it to the stem एकाक्षराभिधानकोश gives एकाक्षराभिधानकोशसात्. Because the stem ends in -a, there is no sandhi change at the join.

<answer>एकाक्षराभिधानकोशसात्</answer>

The affix बहुच् (P. 5.3.68, *vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*) is added after a complete subanta in the sense "slightly, almost". It is placed before the base, as in बहुपटु. The feminine stem शैर्ष्या therefore stays unchanged and बहु is prefixed.

<answer>बहुशैर्ष्या</answer>
<answer>हस्तादानद्वयस</answer>
<answer>मात्सरिक</answer>

I took the affix to be the measure affix *daghna* from Pāṇini 5.2.37 (*pramāṇe dvayasac-daghnañ-mātracaḥ*). This is from memory, and the stem दल्मि does not fit the usual examples of that rule, such as *ūrudaghna*. The final -c of the affix is only a marker and drops. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -i of दल्मि is not elided and the stem simply takes the affix.

<answer>दल्मिदघ्न</answer>

The affix is *rūpap* (Pāṇini 5.3.66, *praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap*), which is added to a word denoting something praised and carries the sense "praiseworthy". The final *p* is only a marker and leaves no trace. Adding the affix to मिथिलाधिपति ("lord of Mithila") gives a stem meaning "a praiseworthy lord of Mithila". I have given it as a stem ending in -a.

<answer>मिथिलाधिपतिरूप</answer>

The taddhita affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It applies in the sense of "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति, 5.3.67) and is placed before the nominal base, not after it. The final च् and the उ marker drop as indicators, leaving बहु, which is prefixed to the stem प्रश्न. I recalled the rule from memory rather than checking a source, and I took the meaning to be "almost a question".

<answer>बहुप्रश्न</answer>

Taking the affix शस् (Sas) in its distributive sense (as in P. 5.4.43), it is added to the stem शैलासनोद्भव. The final स् of the affix becomes visarga, which gives an indeclinable form.

<answer>शैलासनोद्भवशः</answer>

Here the affix is चुञ्चुप्, taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), and it means "known by that." It attaches to a word in the instrumental sense, as in विद्याचुञ्चुः, "known for learning." I am recalling that rule and its standard example from memory rather than checking a source.

The stem is the feminine ā-stem पिशुनिता. In the model form विद्याचुञ्चु the final ā of the base stays before the affix. I assume the same here, so the affix is simply added after पिशुनिता. The stem ends in the affix's vowel उ.

<answer>पिशुनिताचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix जाहच् comes from Pāṇini 5.2.24 (तस्य पाकमूले पीलुकर्णादिकुणब्जाहचौ), where it is added to words of the कर्णादि group to mean "root/base of" (मूल). The model example is कर्णजाहम्. I recalled this from memory and did not check whether आटीलक is actually listed in that group, but the table only asks for a form licensed by the affix.

The affix surfaces as -जाह. The initial ज् stays, as in कर्णजाहम्, and the final -च् is only a marker. It begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of आटीलक is not elided. The result is आटीलक + जाह = आटीलकजाह, which takes the neuter ending -म् when declined.

<answer>आटीलकजाह</answer>

I formed this by attaching the affix थाल् to the stem as given. The affix is introduced by Pāṇini 5.3.23 (प्रकारवचने थाल्, "in the sense of manner"). That rule is normally restricted to pronominal stems and similar words, so this form is a mechanical application of the affix, not a standard attested word.

The final ल् of थाल् is only a marker and drops, leaving the suffix -था. The stem तैलवक keeps its final अ because the suffix begins with a consonant. The result is तैलवक + था = तैलवकथा, an indeclinable.

<answer>तैलवकथा</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), where याप्य means "contemptible" or "inferior". I recalled this rule from memory rather than checking it.

The affix is added directly to the stem उदर्या. I found no rule that shortens the final आ before पाशप्. The shortening of feminine stems before rūpap, kalpap and similar affixes (6.3.43) does not list पाशप्. So the आ stays, and the final अ of the affix is the only vowel that remains at the end.

उदर्या + पाश → उदर्यापाश

<answer>उदर्यापाश</answer>
<answer>स्वौजस्विन्</answer>

I applied the affix अस्ताति to यमिष्ठ without checking it against the specific Pāṇinian rule for this affix. The final इ of the affix is treated as an indicatory letter (इत्) and dropped, leaving the actual affix अस्तात् (as in पुरस्तात्). When it is added, the final अ of the stem is elided, giving यमिष्ठ + अस्तात् → यमिष्ठस्तात्. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>यमिष्ठस्तात्</answer>

The affix is इञ् (iÑ), which by अत इञ् (4.1.95) is added after a stem ending in short अ to form a patronymic ("son of Tunna"). The steps are:

1. Add the affix to तुन्न. The ñ-marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (आदिवृद्धि), so तु becomes तौ.
2. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, giving तौन्न् + इ = तौन्नि.

<answer>तौन्नि</answer>
<answer>वासवोपममात्र</answer>
<answer>शमकी</answer>
<answer>कैकट</answer>

This is a formation I could only partly verify. I did not identify the specific rule that licenses शस् on this stem. I assumed the general pattern of शस् as in बह्वल्पार्थाच्छस् कारकादन्यतरस्याम् (5.4.43), where शस् added to a nominal stem gives an indeclinable adverb such as बहुशः. Applying that to सव्यापग्रहण gives सव्यापग्रहणशस्, which as a complete indeclinable word ends in a visarga.

<answer>सव्यापग्रहणशः</answer>

I applied Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), under which देश्य is added to a nominal stem to mean "slightly short of complete". The affix has no marked parts (no it-letters), so there is no vṛddhi or other stem change. It begins with a consonant, so the final -a of the stem stays, and no sandhi applies at the join. The result is ताम्राश्व + देश्य = ताम्राश्वदेश्य.

<answer>ताम्राश्वदेश्य</answer>

Here दघ्नच् is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), used for "measure", as in ऊरुदघ्नम्. The final च् is only an indicatory marker and drops, leaving the affix दघ्न.

The stem वाञ्छनीया ends in the feminine -ā. Since दघ्न begins with a consonant, the stem has pada status before it, not bha status. The rule that elides a final vowel (यस्येति च, 6.4.148) therefore does not apply, and the -ā is retained. I reasoned this through from the rules rather than checking it against an attested form.

The result is वाञ्छनीया + दघ्न = वाञ्छनीयादघ्न.

<answer>वाञ्छनीयादघ्न</answer>
<answer>मृतस्तात्</answer>

I applied P. 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), which adds कल्पप् to a stem to mean "almost, not quite complete". Before this affix, a feminine long vowel ending (here the आ of अवेक्षा) is shortened by P. 6.3.43 (ह्रस्वः), so the stem becomes अवेक्ष and the derivative is अवेक्षकल्प. The feminine -ā form would then be added separately by टाप्. I give the bare taddhita stem, which is my reading of what the table asks for rather than something it states.

<answer>अवेक्षकल्प</answer>

I did not derive this from a known example. The affix दघ्नच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नज्मात्रचः) in the sense of "measure". I assumed the form is built the same way as ऊरुदघ्न from ऊरु. The affix begins with a consonant and the stem ends in -a, so nothing is deleted. The stem अलिक्लव therefore takes दघ्न directly.

<answer>अलिक्लवदघ्न</answer>

I could not recall the specific rule that licenses जाहच्, so this form rests on applying the standard it-marker rules to the affix, not on a confirmed source.

1. The affix जाहच् has an initial ज्, which is an it-marker by the rule चुटू (1.3.7). Its final च् is also an it-marker.
2. Removing both leaves the operative affix आह.
3. Since ज् is not ञ् or ण्, no vṛddhi applies.
4. The stem अर्पिष ends in अ, which is deleted before a vowel-initial taddhita affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148). This gives अर्पिष् + आह = अर्पिषाह.

<answer>अर्पिषाह</answer>

This is a derivation from the general ठन् → इक rule; I did not trace the specific sūtra or vārttika that licenses ठन् after this stem.

The stem is प्रायोपवेश. The affix ठन् (ṭhan) has the initial ठ् replaced by इक, and the final अ of the stem is dropped before it. The first syllable प्रा already has a long ā, so the vṛddhi of the first vowel changes nothing.

प्रायोपवेश + इक → प्रायोपवेशिक

<answer>प्रायोपवेशिक</answer>
<answer>भदाकजातीय</answer>

This is a tentative derivation. I could not match रेष्टृ to any of the stems for which वलच् is taught, so I applied the affix generically.

The affix वलच् drops its final च् as an indicatory letter, leaving the suffix -वल. It begins with a consonant (व्), so the stem does not take the bha-treatment that vowel-initial or य-initial taddhita affixes trigger. The final ऋ of the stem therefore stays unchanged.

The result is रेष्टृ + वल = रेष्टृवल.

I did not apply the lengthening seen in कृषीवलः. I could not confirm that such a rule applies here, so this is the less certain point.

<answer>रेष्टृवलः</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces this affix, so this form rests on the general rules rather than a confirmed source.

The affix जाहच् begins with the consonant ज्, so it does not trigger the elision of a stem-final vowel that applies before affixes beginning with a vowel or य (1.4.17–18). The stem सप्तका therefore keeps its final आ. The चकार (च्) of जाहच् is only an indicatory letter and is dropped, leaving जाह.

Adding जाह to सप्तका gives the form below. I did not apply any shortening of the आ, since I know no rule that requires it here, but I cannot rule one out.

<answer>सप्तकाजाह</answer>

Starting from the neuter stem अपोदक, the affix कन् loses its marked consonant न् and becomes क. It is added directly to give अपोदक + क = अपोदकक.

The stem ends in -a, not in a feminine -ā, so the rule that inserts इ before the final आ (7.3.44) does not apply. The final अ is also not deleted, because the affix begins with the consonant क, not with a vowel or य.

<answer>अपोदकक</answer>

I treated झण्डू as an ordinary stem ending in long ऊ, with no feminine suffix to remove. No rule shortens the ऊ before शस्. The affix is added directly, and its शकार is only an indicatory marker (इत्). That gives झण्डू + शस् = झण्डूशः, an indeclinable taddhita form (as in बहुशः).

<answer>झण्डूशः</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (देशीय) is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः. It is added to a nominal stem in the sense of "slightly short of complete". Here, तृषार्त plus देशीय gives a stem meaning "somewhat thirst-afflicted". No sandhi change is needed, because the stem ends in a consonant and the affix begins with one.

<answer>तृषार्तदेशीय</answer>

This is a rule-based derivation; I did not check the result against an attested form.

The affix द्वयसच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, used for measure) is added to a feminine stem in ā. The affix begins with a consonant (द्), so the stem does not count as a *bha* stem. The final -ā of जघन्या is therefore not deleted by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). The stem stays whole, and the affix's marker च् drops, leaving द्वयस.

जघन्या + द्वयस = जघन्याद्वयस

<answer>जघन्याद्वयस</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.68, the affix बहुच् is added before the subanta (as in बहुपटु), in the sense of "somewhat, not fully" (ईषदसमाप्ति). Prefixing बहु to आनुवेश्य gives बहु + आनुवेश्य, and the vowel sandhi उ + आ → व्आ yields बह्वानुवेश्य.

<answer>बह्वानुवेश्य</answer>

Pāṇini 5.2.37 (pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnañ-mātrac) allows the affix मात्रच् after a nominal stem to express measure. The final च् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix added is मात्र. It begins with म्, so it does not trigger any change to the stem (the भ-designation of 1.4.18 applies only before affixes beginning with य् or a vowel). The stem ऐन्य therefore stays intact and takes मात्र directly.

<answer>ऐन्यमात्र</answer>

Here the affix तल् is the bhāva (abstract quality) suffix, introduced by "tasya bhāvas tvatalau". Its final ल् and the लित् marking drop out, leaving the suffix ता. The word is therefore त्रस्त + ता = त्रस्तता. Words formed with तल् are feminine, so the stem ends in -ā.

<answer>त्रस्तता</answer>
<answer>भुजंगदीर्घजातीय</answer>

The affix वलच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.112 (रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच्). I assumed the possessive sense ("having …") and applied it to कैदर्भ without checking whether the rule's restricted stem list actually covers this stem. After the इत् letters (the final च् and the ल-sound marker) are dropped, the affix is simply -वल. The stem's final अ is not elided, because the affix begins with व, which is neither a vowel nor य. The result is an a-stem.

<answer>कैदर्भवल</answer>
<answer>क्षौद्रसात्</answer>

चपलात्मका में स्त्रीलिंग का टाप् (आ) है। छ का आदेश "आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्" से ईय होता है। ईय परे रहने पर "यस्येति च" से अंग का अन्तिम आ लुप्त हो जाता है, इसलिए चपलात्मक + ईय बनता है। यहाँ किस सूत्र से छ लगा, यह मैंने निश्चित नहीं किया, इसलिए यह रूप-निर्माण की सामान्य प्रक्रिया पर आधारित है।

<answer>चपलात्मकीय</answer>

The affix अस्ताति is Pāṇini's अस्तात् (the final इ is an indicatory letter). It is normally added to direction words, as in पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्. I applied it to किकि anyway, since the task accepts any meaning licensed for the affix, though I did not check that किकि qualifies.

The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem counts as *bha*. By यस्येति च (6.4.148), the final इ of the stem is then dropped. This gives किक + अस्तात् = किकस्तात्, an indeclinable.

I reached this by recalling the rules, not by checking a derivation tool, so the treatment of the stem as *bha* is the part I am least sure of.

<answer>किकस्तात्</answer>

The affix सातिः (Pāṇini 5.4.52, तदधीनवचने, among others) forms indeclinables. It is added to the stem unchanged, and the final इ drops, so the result is the form ending in सात्. I am recalling this from memory and did not check the rule numbers or the treatment of the final इ against a source.

<answer>खड्गाभिहतसात्</answer>

The stem ओक्ता ends in the feminine suffix आ. Before the taddhita अण्, this final आ is dropped (अवर्णलोप, यस्येति च), leaving ओक्त्. The affix is णित्, so the first vowel takes vṛddhi, and ओ becomes औ. Adding अ gives औक्त.

I am not certain what the base word means, so I could not check the form against a specific sense.

<answer>औक्त</answer>
<answer>भाण्डारिक</answer>

The affix sāti (5.4.52, in the sense of "entirely") is added to the neuter stem कृधुक. The final -i of the affix drops, so the resulting indeclinable is कृधुकसात् (as in अग्निसात्). I worked this from memory of the Kāśikā and Pāṇini rather than checking a source, and I am not fully certain about the exact rule that drops the -i.

<answer>कृधुकसात्</answer>

The affix मात्रच् (SLP1 `mAtrac`) has the final च् as an indicatory letter, so what is actually added is मात्र. It is added in the sense of measure (प्रमाणे, Pāṇini 5.2.37). Since मात्र begins with a consonant, the final अ of आष्टकीय is not elided by यस्येति च (6.4.148). The stem therefore stays whole and the affix is simply attached.

<answer>आष्टकीयमात्र</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) is added to a noun when something becomes what it was not before, in construction with कृ, भू or अस् (अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः). The affix itself is wholly elided, but it triggers the change of final अ to ई (अस्य च्वौ). So तापिञ्छ becomes तापिञ्छी, as in तापिञ्छी भवति.

<answer>तापिञ्छी</answer>
<answer>वैनतकदघ्न</answer>
<answer>सारिणीवल</answer>

The stem धाका already ends in the feminine suffix -ā, and I found no rule that would remove or shorten that vowel before त्व, so I simply attached the affix to the full stem. This is the usual formation of an abstract noun with त्व (meaning "the state of being X"), as in खट्वात्व and मालात्व. I did not verify this against the rule texts, so the choice of धाकात्व over धाकत्व rests on that reasoning alone.

<answer>धाकात्व</answer>

The affix ढक् (Qak) is added by P. 4.1.119, *strībhyo ḍhak*, to feminine stems in the sense of "offspring", so I derive the stem on that basis.

1. The initial ढ् of ढक् is replaced by एय (P. 7.1.2, *āyaneya…*), so the affix becomes एय.
2. The final आ of बहलानुरागा is dropped before the affix.
3. The first vowel of the base takes vṛddhi (P. 7.2.117), so ब (with अ) becomes बा.

The result is बाहलानुरागेय.

<answer>बाहलानुरागेय</answer>

The stem रेपस् takes the taddhita affix कन्, which leaves the base क after the final न् drops as an indicatory letter. The stem ends in a consonant, so the affix attaches directly and the final स् stays, as in यशस्क and पयस्क. This gives the stem रेपस्क. I formed this by analogy with other s-stems rather than by finding a specific rule for रेपस्, so it is a best reconstruction.

<answer>रेपस्क</answer>
<answer>काल्माष</answer>

Before the affix ईयसुन्, the rule "टेः" (6.4.155) drops the ṭi, which is the last vowel of the stem together with any consonant after it. In मङ्गलाष्टक, the ṭi is the final -अक. That leaves मङ्गलाष्ट्, and adding the affix ईयस् (the उ and न् of ईयसुन् are indicatory letters and drop out) gives the stem below.

<answer>मङ्गलाष्टीयस्</answer>

Taking the affix इनि in the possessive sense ("having कडम्ब"), I applied Pāṇini 5.2.115 (अत इनिठनौ), which allows इनि after a stem ending in short अ. I recalled this rule from memory and did not check it against a text. The final अ of कडम्ब drops before the affix, giving कडम्ब् + इन् = कडम्बिन्.

<answer>कडम्बिन्</answer>
<answer>घूकारिद्वयस</answer>

This is a best-judgement answer, since I could not confirm the feminine handling from memory. The affix चरट् (5.3.53, भूतपूर्वे चरट्) means "formerly such", as in आढ्यचर / आढ्यचरी. It carries the marker ट्, so a feminine takes ङीप् (चरी). I assumed the feminine stem क्षेत्रिया takes the masculine-like form (पुंवद्भाव) before the affix, as in the traditional आढ्यचरी, giving क्षेत्रिय + चर + ī. I did not find a rule confirming this for taddhitas.

<answer>क्षेत्रियचरी</answer>

This is a generic application of the affix, since I could not identify a specific rule that attaches थमु to क्रौड. The affix थमु has the final उ as an indicatory letter (it-marker), so what is actually added is थम्. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of क्रौड is not dropped.
