The stem खञ्जरीटी ends in the feminine suffix ई. The affix यत् leaves the taddhita ending य after the markers त् and the initial यत् are dropped. Before a taddhita beginning with य, the final ई of the base is deleted by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). This gives खञ्जरीट् + य = खञ्जरीट्य.

<answer>खञ्जरीट्य</answer>

The stem मारक takes the affix मयट् (SLP1 mayaw), as in 5.4.21 तत्प्रकृतवचने मयट्, which gives the sense "made up abundantly of that". The affix begins with म, so 6.4.148 यस्येति च does not delete the final अ of मारक. The टकार is only a marker. It would call for the feminine ending ङीप् (मारकमयी), but the masculine/neuter stem is मारकमय.

<answer>मारकमय</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is added before the subanta, so the derived stem is बहु + प्राचीनाग्रा. I found no rule that shortens the final आ here or applies पुंवद्भाव, so the base stays unchanged. This rests on my recollection of the rules rather than a check of the text.

<answer>बहुप्राचीनाग्रा</answer>

The affix चणप् (caRap) is added by Pāṇini 5.2.26, "तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ". It follows a word in the instrumental sense and means "known by that", as in विद्याचणः "known for learning".

The ṇ and p in the affix are markers, so the affix that is actually added is चण.

Because चण begins with a consonant, the base counts as a pada, so the final ā is neither dropped nor changed. I did not check this against a Kāśikā example for this exact stem. I reasoned by analogy with विद्याचणः, where the ā of विद्या is kept.

This gives कौण्डपायिना + चण = कौण्डपायिनाचण.

<answer>कौण्डपायिनाचण</answer>

I formed this by attaching मतुप् (the affix "possessing") to निबिरीश, and checked whether the मतुप् rule that changes म to व applies.

- The rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9) changes the म of मतुप् to व only after a stem ending in म or अ/आ, or one whose penultimate letter (उपधा) is म or अ/आ. The stem here ends in श, and its penultimate letter is र, so this rule does not apply.
- The rule झयः (8.2.10) also does not apply, because श is not part of the झय् set.

So the म stays, and the derived stem keeps the final त् of मत्.

<answer>निबिरीशमत्</answer>

The affix जातीयर् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.69, *prakāravacane jātīyar*, and means "of that kind". The final र् is only an indicatory marker and drops out. Adding जातीय to नष्ट gives नष्टजातीय, "of the kind of the lost". The final -अ of नष्ट is elided before the affix by 6.4.148 (*yasyeti ca*), and the resulting stem is नष्टजातीय.

<answer>नष्टजातीय</answer>

Taking the stem मलिनास्य as given, I added the affix यत् (ya) by the general rule, since I could not tie it to a specific Pāṇinian sūtra for this stem. यत् loses its final त् as an indicatory letter, leaving य. The stem is a bha-stem before this ya-initial affix, so its final अ is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). Joining the remainder with the affix gives मलिनास्य् + य = मलिनास्य्य. No vṛddhi applies, because यत् is not ṇit or ñit.

<answer>मलिनास्य्य</answer>
<answer>पिङ्गास्यसात्</answer>

I did not trace this to a specific rule, so the form below is my best reading. The closest fit is the affix लच् (lac) added to a stem ending in आ, as in Pāṇini 5.2.96, which allows लच् in the sense "having" (matup). After the indicatory letters are removed, the affix is just ल. It begins with a consonant, so the final आ of ध्वस्ता stays. This is parallel to चूडा → चूडाल.

<answer>ध्वस्ताल</answer>

The affix फिञ् (PiY) is the one taught in 4.1.154 (तिकादिभ्यः फिञ्) and 4.1.155. I could not confirm that त्रैपुरुष actually belongs to the तिकादि list, so this derivation rests on that assumption.

1. The initial फ् of the affix is replaced by आयन् (फ → आयन्, by 7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).
2. The ञ् is only an indicatory letter (it calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel). The first vowel of त्रैपुरुष is already ऐ, so nothing further changes.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving त्रैपुरुष + आयन → त्रैपुरुषायन.
4. The न् becomes ण् by retroflexion (8.4.2, after ष् and र् in the stem), giving त्रैपुरुषायण.

The source gender (neuter) does not affect the result.

<answer>त्रैपुरुषायण</answer>

Following the usual rule, the affix दघ्नच् is added directly to the stem कूर्परा. The affix begins with a consonant and is not a सित् affix, so the stem is neither a पद nor a भ. The rule यस्येति च therefore does not delete the final आ of the feminine stem. I judged this from the general rules, not from an attested form.

कूर्परा + दघ्न gives कूर्परादघ्न.

<answer>कूर्परादघ्न</answer>
<answer>उच्चैस्तनिष्ठ</answer>

I formed this by adding अण् to the stem and applying the usual two changes.

1. The stem नर्दनीय ends in the vowel अ, which is deleted before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel (यस्येति च). This gives नर्दनीय् + अण्.
2. The affix अण् carries the marker ण्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (आदिवृद्धि): न → ना. This gives नार्दनीय्, and the affix अ joins the final य्.

I did not check which specific meaning of अण् this derivative falls under, so the form rests on the general rules above.

<answer>नार्दनीय</answer>
<answer>पुनीतशः</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), in the sense "known or famous by that". Its final प् is only an indicatory marker (it), and the ञ् is part of the affix itself, not a marker. The affix is therefore added as चुञ्चु. It is added directly to the stem with no vṛddhi and no loss of the final इ, which gives अत्रिचुञ्चु. I derived this from the rule and its standard examples (such as विद्याचुञ्चुः) rather than from an attested use with अत्रि.

<answer>अत्रिचुञ्चु</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यङ् on this stem, so the form below comes from applying the affix's general rules.

The affix ञ्यङ् leaves only the final -य, because ञ् and ङ् are markers (it). The final अ of सौवीराम्ल is dropped before it by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). The first syllable is already vṛddha, so the marker ञ् changes nothing there.

सौवीराम्ल + य → सौवीराम्ल्य

<answer>सौवीराम्ल्य</answer>

The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, with the sense "known by that" (e.g. विद्याचुञ्चुः, केशचुञ्चुः). The affix begins with a consonant, so the final -अ of the stem अवोष is not dropped. Neither the ञ् nor the प् in the affix's marker letters causes vṛddhi or any other change in the stem. The derived stem is therefore अवोष + चुञ्चु.

I could not recall a specific attested example for this stem, so the form follows from applying the rule rather than from a cited word.

<answer>अवोषचुञ्चु</answer>

The affix खञ् is replaced by its substitute ईन (the initial ख becomes ईन, and the ञ् marker only triggers vṛddhi).

1. The vṛddhi rule (तद्धितेष्वचामादेः) strengthens the first vowel of the stem. In गृहाश्रमिन्, the ऋ of गृ becomes आर्, giving गार्हाश्रमिन्.
2. Before a taddhita, the ending इन् is deleted by the rule नस्तद्धिते, leaving गार्हाश्रम.
3. Adding ईन gives गार्हाश्रमीन. The न does not become ण, because the श in between blocks the retroflexion rule.

<answer>गार्हाश्रमीन</answer>

Rule 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, adds चुञ्चुप् to a stem to mean "known by that". The affix is a pit and ñit marker, so only the part चुञ्चु is appended to the stem. This follows the traditional examples such as विद्याचुञ्चुः, where the initial च is kept. I did not check that लैङ्गचुञ्चु is itself attested; I formed it by the rule.

<answer>लैङ्गचुञ्चु</answer>

The suffix इष्ठन् is the superlative affix (अतिशयने तमबिष्ठनौ, 5.3.55). The stem जगन्नु is more than one syllable and is not monosyllabic, so the प्रकृत्यैकाच् restriction (6.4.163) does not apply.

Before इष्ठन् the stem counts as भ. The rule टेः (6.4.155) then drops its टि, which is the final vowel उ, giving जगन्न् + इष्ठ. This parallels लघु → लघिष्ठ. I assumed टेः takes precedence over the गुण rule ओर्गुणः (6.4.146), which would have given जगन्नविष्ठ. I did not check that ordering against the rules themselves; I relied on the लघिष्ठ parallel.

Joining the two parts gives जगन्निष्ठ.

<answer>जगन्निष्ठ</answer>

The affix चरट् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), which means "formerly was". Adding चरट् to आजानेय gives आजानेय + चर. Only the अ of चर remains, since ट् and the ट् of चरट् are markers. There is no sandhi at the junction, so the result is आजानेयचर, meaning "formerly an आजानेय (a well-bred horse)".

<answer>आजानेयचर</answer>
<answer>अनुस्वारागमतम</answer>
<answer>जानन्तिक</answer>

The affix मात्रच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः) in the sense of "measure". The final च् is only a marker and drops out, leaving मात्र. Adding this to शोणित gives शोणितमात्र. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final अ of शोणित is not deleted.

<answer>शोणितमात्र</answer>

This is a derivation I worked out from the affix rules, and I did not identify the specific Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses ṭhak after a feminine stem.

1. The affix ठक् (Wak) has the substitute इक in place of ठ् (ṭh → ik, by the rule ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50).
2. The stem औत्तङ्की ends in the feminine ई, so that ई is dropped before the vowel-initial taddhita affix (yasyeti ca, 6.4.148). This leaves औत्तङ्क्.
3. The first vowel औ is already vṛddhi, so no further strengthening applies.
4. Adding इक gives औत्तङ्किक.

<answer>औत्तङ्किक</answer>
<answer>अरण्यवत्</answer>
<answer>कूचीकारूप्य</answer>

I did not identify which sutra licenses कन् here, so I derived the form from the stem and affix alone.

पूर्वाशिन् takes the affix कन्, which begins with the consonant क. Before such an affix the stem counts as a pada (1.4.17), so the final न् is dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य). This gives पूर्वाशि + क, which is the stem पूर्वाशिक.

<answer>पूर्वाशिक</answer>
<answer>भूतांशी</answer>

The affix पाशप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), in the sense of "contemptible" or "barely sustained". After the final प् is dropped as an indicatory letter, the affix is पाश.

The stem कबुलि is a feminine stem ending in short इ, with no ङीप् or other feminine suffix to remove, and no rule requires its vowel to change. Since पाश begins with a consonant, the stem is a pada rather than a bha, so यस्येति च does not delete its final इ. The result is simply कबुलि + पाश.

<answer>कबुलिपाश</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ठन् on this stem, so this derivation applies only the general mechanics of the affix.

1. The affix ठन् has ठ् as its initial, and 7.3.50 (ठस्येकः) replaces ठ with इक. This gives ऐकस्वर्य + इक.
2. The stem's first vowel ऐ is already a vṛddhi vowel, so no further strengthening is needed.
3. Under 6.4.148 (यस्य च), the final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, which leaves ऐकस्वर्य्. The same rule then drops the following य्, giving ऐकस्वर् + इक.
4. Joining the two parts gives ऐकस्वरिक.

<answer>ऐकस्वरिक</answer>

I derived this from rule memory rather than a checked source. The affix त्रा is added to a nominal stem by rules such as "देये त्रा च" (5.4.55). It produces an indeclinable (avyaya). The affix begins with a consonant, so the final long आ of the stem सोमाभा is not dropped. No other change is triggered, so the form is simply the stem followed by the affix.

<answer>सोमाभात्रा</answer>

Applying the affix थमु (Tamu) to the stem क्रौञ्चा gives the form below. I applied the affix directly to the stem and did not find a specific Pāṇinian rule licensing थमु on this stem, which is why the derivation is generic.

1. The final उ of थमु is an it-marker, so the affix that is actually added is थम्.
2. The affix begins with a consonant, so the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not delete the stem-final आ. The stem क्रौञ्चा therefore stays whole.
3. A taddhita-final form with no case endings is an indeclinable (अव्यय), so no case or number endings are added.

<answer>क्रौञ्चाथम्</answer>

The affix कन् is added to कपटिक. Its initial क् is a consonant, so the final अ of the stem is not dropped by "यस्येति च", which applies only before affixes beginning with a vowel or ई. The feminine rule for ending-ka stems (7.3.44) does not apply either, because the source is neuter. Joining the two gives कपटिक + कन् → कपटिकक.

<answer>कपटिकक</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that teaches ञ्यट्, so this form comes from applying the affix's markers, not from a confirmed rule.

- The ञ् marker makes the affix ñit, which calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. In हानि the first vowel is already long ā, so nothing changes.
- The final इ of the stem is dropped before the affix beginning with य (the usual elision before a ṇit/ñit-type taddhita).
- The ट् marker only matters for the feminine, where it licenses ङीप्, giving हान्या. It does not change the stem.

This gives हान्+य = हान्य.

<answer>हान्य</answer>

This is a formation with the affix dvayasac (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure). The derivative is neuter, and the affix, once its marker letter -c drops, leaves the ending -dvayasa. The base भ्रामिता keeps its final आ, because the affix begins with a consonant (द) and so does not trigger deletion of the base's final vowel. I did not check the form against a grammatical source or an attested example; it is my best derivation from the rule.

<answer>भ्रामिताद्वयस</answer>

The affix जातीयर् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.69 (प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) and means "of that kind". Adding it to मृगाङ्क gives मृगाङ्कजातीय, "of the kind of the moon". I took the affix as attaching directly to the stem and gave the derived stem without case endings.

<answer>मृगाङ्कजातीय</answer>

The taddhita affix चुञ्चुप् (cuñcup) is taught in P. 5.2.26 *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, in the sense "known by that". It leaves the stem ending in ऊ-less -उ, so the result is a stem in -u. I am not fully sure about the treatment of the final ई, and I did not check it against the rules. Because the affix begins with a consonant, the base is a pada, so the ending of कृष्णाञ्जनी is not elided by *yasyeti ca*. I also did not apply the shortening rule for stems ending in ṅyāp, since it seems to be limited to proper names and Vedic usage. On that basis I kept the ई and added the affix: कृष्णाञ्जनी + चुञ्चु.

<answer>कृष्णाञ्जनीचुञ्चु</answer>
<answer>नृतिमय</answer>
<answer>शर्मण्यकल्प</answer>

The stem वेशन्ता is a feminine stem ending in आ. The affix त्व is added in the sense of "state or quality of" (bhāve tvatalau, 5.1.119). Before this affix the feminine आ is kept, as in खट्वा → खट्वात्व. The same pattern gives वेशन्ता + त्व = वेशन्तात्व.

<answer>वेशन्तात्व</answer>

I could not match the stem मनन्य to a specific ठन् rule, so this is the general formation only.

The affix ठन् has the initial ठ replaced by इक (ठस्येकः, 7.3.50), and the final न् drops as an indicatory letter. Since ठन् is not ञित् or णित्, there is no vṛddhi of the first vowel. The final अ of मनन्य is deleted before the affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). This gives मनन्य् + इक = मनन्यिक.

<answer>मनन्यिक</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses कुणप् with पृक्थ, so this form is a best guess rather than a derivation I could confirm.

I assumed the affix is simply added to the stem. The final अ of पृक्थ is not dropped, because the rule that deletes it (6.4.148, यस्येति च) applies only before a vowel-initial or य-initial taddhita, and कुण begins with a consonant. The ‑प् is only an indicatory marker and does not appear in the form.

<answer>पृक्थकुण</answer>

Taking the masculine stem चक्राति with the taddhita अण् in a general sense such as "descendant of":

1. The affix अण् (marked ण्) causes vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem: च → चा, giving चाक्राति.
2. The final -i of the stem is dropped before the initial अ of the affix (यस्येति च), giving चाक्रात्.
3. Adding अ gives चाक्रात.

<answer>चाक्रात</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), in the sense of measure. The final च् is only an indicatory letter and drops out, so the affix is दघ्न. Nothing else in the stem is altered, so दघ्न is simply added to the stem काठक. This gives काठकदघ्न. I could not recall a specific attested use of this form, but the question accepts any licensed meaning.

<answer>काठकदघ्न</answer>

The affix चणप् comes from Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which gives the sense "known or famous by that." The standard examples are विद्याचणः and अक्षरचणः. The final प् is only an indicatory marker, and the initial च remains in the derived stem. The feminine ending -ā is kept, as in विद्याचण, so तृणाशा becomes तृणाशाचण. This is reasoned from the rule and its standard examples, not checked against a source for this particular stem.

<answer>तृणाशाचण</answer>
<answer>सम्परीयमय</answer>

The stem अग्रा takes the comparative affix ईयसुन् (the उ and न् are indicatory letters, so the affix is ईयस्). Because the affix begins with ई, the final आ of the base is dropped by the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). So अग्र् + ईयस् gives अग्रीयस्. I derived this from the rules rather than checking an attested form.

<answer>अग्रीयस्</answer>

I could not match द्वंद्व to a rule that licenses थमु. In Pāṇini the affix is taught only for इदम् and किम् (इत्थम्, कथम्). So I applied it mechanically to द्वंद्व: the stem ends in -a and थम् begins with a consonant, so nothing is elided before it. The result is an indeclinable. I kept the anusvara spelling of the input stem, though द्वन्द्वथम् is the equivalent standard spelling.

<answer>द्वंद्वथम्</answer>

Here the affix is चरट् (caraw), taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (A. 5.3.53) with the sense "formerly such". I could not recall the rule with full confidence, so this is my best derivation.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the final ई of नीवी is not elided by "यस्येति च". I did not apply any shortening of the long ई, since I could not confirm a rule that does so here. The stem therefore stays as नीवी + चर, giving नीवीचर, which would take the feminine suffix ङीप् later because चरट् carries the marker ट्.

<answer>नीवीचर</answer>

This is a best-effort form. शूर्णा is not a direction word, so the affix does not strictly apply to it under Pāṇini 5.3.27 (which licenses अस्ताति after dik-śabdas, as in पुर + अस्ताति → पुरस्तात्). I added अस्ताति to the stem and dropped its final -ति, as in पुरस्तात्. The stem-final -ā then merges with the initial a of the affix by savarṇa-dīrgha. I did not verify these details against a source.

<answer>शूर्णास्तात्</answer>

The affix बहुच् is added before a complete word (सुबन्त) in the sense of "somewhat, not fully" (ईषदसमाप्ति). I recalled this from Pāṇini 5.3.68 without checking the text. Here the prefixed element is बहु, and the base पिप्यटा is kept unchanged. I found no rule that shortens the final आ in this case, but I did not verify that point carefully.

<answer>बहुपिप्यटा</answer>
<answer>औद्भिद्यत्व</answer>

The affix चणप् (caRap) is added by P. 5.2.26 *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, in the sense "known by …". The final प् is only an it-marker, so the affix that is actually added is चण.

1. The stem बोकडी ends in ई.
2. The affix चण begins with a consonant, so the stem is not a *bha* (P. 1.4.18 *yaci bham* does not apply). Therefore P. 6.4.148 *yasyeti ca* does not drop the ई.
3. The affix has no ञित्/णित् marker that would trigger *vṛddhi*, so the stem vowels stay unchanged.
4. This gives बोकडी + चण, which yields the stem बोकडीचण. I did not apply the shortening of a feminine ending that P. 6.3.63 allows, since it belongs to compounds and names, but I am not fully certain of that rule's scope.

<answer>बोकडीचण</answer>

I am going from recalled examples like अग्निसात्, not a checked rule, so I take the affix's final इ as dropped. The stem's final इ stays unchanged, giving सुक्कडिसात्.

I found no rule shortening the stem's final ā before पाशप् (as happens before घ, रूपप्, कल्पप् and the like), and I am only fairly sure of that. So the result is जपाख्या + पाश, with the final -a of the affix as the stem ending.

<answer>जपाख्यापाश</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them, not checked against a source. I could not identify the specific rule that licenses अञ् on this stem, so the form below rests on the sandhi alone.

The stem त्रैशङ्कव already ends in the short vowel अ. When अञ् is added, the final अ of the stem is dropped by यस्येति च. The affix अ then stands in its place, and त्रैशङ्कव् + अ gives त्रैशङ्कव again.

The initial vowel is already vṛddhi (ऐ), so तद्धितेष्वचामादेः produces no further change.

<answer>त्रैशङ्कव</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that teaches जाहच्, so this form rests on the general rules for adding a taddhita affix, not on a specific rule or attested example.

The affix has the form जाह, since the final च् is only a marker (इत्). The affix begins with a consonant (ज्), so the stem is not treated as bha. The rule that drops a final अ (यस्येति च) therefore does not apply, and the stem's final अ stays. The form is a simple concatenation of the stem नित्यानुबद्ध and the affix जाह.

<answer>नित्यानुबद्धजाह</answer>

Following the standard derivation, the affix अण् (aR) is added to सौरिक. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). Vṛddhi of the first vowel (7.2.117, "तद्धितेष्वचामादेः") is already satisfied, since the stem already begins with सौ (औ). So सौरिक + अ gives a form that is spelled the same as the input stem. I did not identify a specific sūtra that licenses अण् for this particular stem, so the result rests on the general rules above.

<answer>सौरिक</answer>

I applied the affix अस्ताति (astāti) directly to the stem हौत्र. This is a mechanical formation: the stem is not a direction word, so I did not check that it meets the affix's usual conditions.

The final -अ of हौत्र is elided before the vowel-initial affix (यस्येति च लोपः), giving हौत्र् + अस्तात्. The result is the indeclinable हौत्रस्तात्. The same spelling results if the vowel is not elided, so the form does not depend on that rule.

<answer>हौत्रस्तात्</answer>

I could not confirm that दारि is a valid base for this affix. The derivation below is my best reconstruction, not something I could check against a source.

The affix अस्ताति (5.3.27, 5.3.40) is added to the stem and yields forms ending in -स्तात्, as in पुरस्तात् and अधस्तात्. I took the final इ of the affix as an indicatory letter that drops out, leaving अस्तात्.

The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem counts as भ. The final इ of दारि is then elided by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). That gives दार् + अस्तात् = दारस्तात्.

<answer>दारस्तात्</answer>
<answer>मृचयस्तात्</answer>

I applied Pāṇini 5.3.27, where the affix अस्ताति (surface form -अस्तात्, as in पुरस्तात्) is added to the stem. The stem's final अ is dropped before the affix's initial vowel (यस्येति च). This gives गुह्यकेश्वर् + अस्तात् = गुह्यकेश्वरस्तात्. The stem is not an ordinary direction word, so this is a formal derivation from the table's inputs.

<answer>गुह्यकेश्वरस्तात्</answer>

Superlative चेटी + तमप् → चेटितम. This follows from recalled rule 6.3.43 (cited from memory and not checked): a feminine stem ending in ई and having more than one vowel takes a short final vowel before तमप्, तरप्, रूपप्, कल्पप् and similar affixes. Here चेटी has two vowels, so ई shortens to इ and तम is added. The stem is given in the masculine/neuter form, without the feminine ending -आ.

<answer>चेटितम</answer>

This form follows from the rule for the affix अस्ताति (Pāṇini 5.3.27); I did not verify every step against the text of the sūtra, and the stem is not a direction word, so I am assuming the table's input is generic.

1. The stem is चालनीया. Its final आ is a feminine suffix.
2. The affix begins with a vowel, so the stem counts as *bha* (4.1.18). By यस्येति च (6.4.148), the final आ of the stem is dropped, leaving चालनीय्.
3. The affix surfaces as अस्तात्, because the final इ of अस्ताति is only a marker.
4. Joining चालनीय् with अस्तात् gives चालनीयस्तात्.

<answer>चालनीयस्तात्</answer>

The affix सातिँ is added to the stem धृषित, with the final "ति" of the affix dropped, so the derived indeclinable ends in सात्. This is from memory of the standard pattern, as in अग्निसात्, and I have not checked the sūtra numbers.

<answer>धृषितसात्</answer>
<answer>श्लेषीयस्</answer>

I did not verify this against a source. The affix दघ्नच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसच्-दघ्नच्-मात्रचः), where it is added to a word to express measure. Because दघ्न begins with a consonant, the final अ of the stem इरण्य is not elided, so the stem and affix simply join.

<answer>इरण्यदघ्न</answer>

This is Pāṇini 5.3.68, *vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*. The affix bahuc is added after a subanta (a word with its case ending) in the sense of "somewhat, not fully", and it is placed before the word, not after it. The stem कश्मश therefore takes बहु in front of it and stays otherwise unchanged. This gives बहुकश्मश, "somewhat कश्मश". I derived the form from this rule from memory and did not check it against any source.

<answer>बहुकश्मश</answer>

Rule 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ) teaches the affix चुञ्चुप्, with the sense "known by". The final प् and ञ् are only markers, so the affix itself is चुञ्चु.

The affix begins with च, not with य or a vowel, so the stem अषाढिन् keeps the status of a pada before it. The final न् of the stem is then deleted by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), which gives अषाढि. Adding the affix gives अषाढि + चुञ्चु = अषाढिचुञ्चु.

<answer>अषाढिचुञ्चु</answer>

Taking अस्यवामीय with the affix मतुप् (matup) in the sense "that which has it", the stem ends in -a. By Pāṇini 8.2.9, the म् of मतुप् then becomes व्, and अस्यवामीय is not in the exceptional यवादि list. This gives अस्यवामीय + वत् = अस्यवामीयवत्.

<answer>अस्यवामीयवत्</answer>

The affix अञ् carries the marker ञ्, so the first vowel of the base takes vṛddhi (अञ्-type affixes, Pāṇini 7.2.117 तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). In क्षेद, the first vowel is ए, which becomes ऐ. The final अ of the base drops before the affix, which then supplies its own अ. This gives क्षैद. I could not tie क्षेद to a specific gaṇa rule for अञ्, so I applied the general derivation, which suits the patronymic sense "descendant of क्षेद".

<answer>क्षैद</answer>
<answer>सांख्याचार्यि</answer>
<answer>पाण्डुरिष्ठ</answer>

This is an application of the superlative affix इष्ठन् (5.3.55 *atiśayane tamabiṣṭhanau*), and I did not check whether the stem दलाढक itself is an attested word. Before इष्ठन्, the stem counts as a *bha* stem, and rule 6.4.155 (*ṭeḥ*) drops its *ṭi*, the last vowel together with any consonant after it. For दलाढक the *ṭi* is the final "अक", which leaves दलाढ्. Adding इष्ठ (the final न् is only a marker) gives दलाढिष्ठ.

<answer>दलाढिष्ठ</answer>

Taddhita शस् (5.4.43) forms distributive adverbs such as बहुशः. In a taddhita, श् is not an indicatory letter (1.3.8 excludes it), so the affix keeps its श् and begins with a consonant. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148), which deletes a final vowel before a vowel-initial affix, therefore does not apply. The final ā of बार्बरका stays, and the affix's final स् becomes visarga, giving the indeclinable बार्बरकाशः.

<answer>बार्बरकाशः</answer>
<answer>म्लायिशः</answer>

I did not apply pumvad-bhāva (the rule that replaces a feminine word with its masculine form before certain affixes). That rule needs a feminine word that also exists as a masculine, and I took धाना to be only feminine. So शार्करीधाना stays as it is, and जातीयर् (प्रकारवचने, "a kind of") is added directly. The resulting stem is शार्करीधानाजातीय, which takes the feminine ending when declined (शार्करीधानाजातीया).

<answer>शार्करीधानाजातीय</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.1.119 (*tasya bhāvas tvatalau*), the affix त्व is added to the stem प्रधन्य to express "the state of being" that stem. The affix begins with त्, not a vowel or य, so the stem does not take *bha* status. The final अ of -य is therefore not deleted by *yasyeti ca*, and no sandhi change occurs. The result is प्रधन्य + त्व = प्रधन्यत्व, which is a neuter noun stem.

<answer>प्रधन्यत्व</answer>

I formed this by simply adding the affix to the stem; I did not confirm that Pāṇini licenses थाल् after this particular stem. The affix is normally taught after sarvanāma-type words (5.3.23 प्रकारवचने थाल्), and कुलुङ्ग is not one of those, so the derivation below is a mechanical application.

The affix थाल् has ल् as a marker letter, so only था remains. Adding it to कुलुङ्ग gives the indeclinable कुलुङ्गथा.

<answer>कुलुङ्गथा</answer>

This derivation follows P. 5.2.37, which gives द्वयसच् in the sense of measure. Dropping the indicatory च् leaves the affix द्वयस. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of the stem मरूक is not elided, and the affix is simply added. I did not check whether मरूक is actually a measure word; the task accepts any licensed meaning.

<answer>मरूकद्वयस</answer>

The affix अण् has a final ण् marker, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi and the final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix. In शतेश, the first vowel is the अ of श, which becomes आ, giving शा. The stem-final अ is elided, and the affix's own अ is added: शातेश + अ → शातेश. This reading takes अण् in the sense "descendant of" (तस्यापत्यम्).

<answer>शातेश</answer>

I formed this by direct affixation, without checking whether a standard example exists for this particular stem. The affix द्वयसच् (A. 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to the stem शौक्र.

The final च् is only an indicatory marker and drops, leaving the suffix -द्वयस. The affix is not ṇit or kit, so it causes no vṛddhi or guṇa. It begins with द् rather than a vowel or य, so the stem-final अ of शौक्र is not elided. The result is simply the stem followed by the suffix.

<answer>शौक्रद्वयस</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ठन् on this stem, so this form is derived from the general ठन् mechanics rather than a located sūtra.

1. The affix ठन् (Wan) has its ठ replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50), so the affix becomes इक.
2. ठन् carries only the markers ṭ and n, so it does not trigger vṛddhi.
3. The stem स्तामु ends in उ and is a bha stem before a taddhita affix, so it takes guṇa (ओर्गुणः, 6.4.146). This gives स्ताम् + ओ.
4. Before the vowel of इक, ओ becomes अव्, giving स्तामविक.

<answer>स्तामविक</answer>

I derived this by rule, not from an attested example. The affix चुञ्चुप् (cuYcup) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ, in the sense "known by that". The final प् is only a marker letter, and the ञ् is part of the conjunct ञ्च, so the affix that is actually added is चुञ्चु. It begins with a consonant, so the stem वेपथु is a pada before it. It therefore keeps its final उ with no guṇa (6.4.146 applies only to bha-stems) and no vṛddhi, since the affix has no ञित् marker. This gives the stem वेपथुचुञ्चु.

<answer>वेपथुचुञ्चु</answer>

In the sense of "slightly deficient" (ईषदसमाप्ति), the affix बहुच् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.67–68 (ईषदसमाप्तौ…, विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु). It is placed before the nominal, as in बहुपटु ("somewhat clever"). The stem क्रिम्ण therefore takes बहु in front of it. The final च् only marks the accent, and no sandhi change applies. I am assuming the stem क्रिम्ण is spelled as intended.

<answer>बहुक्रिम्ण</answer>

Applying the अण् affix to the stem कारितान्त gives the same surface form, as follows.

1. The stem's final अ is deleted before the ṇit affix (यस्येति च), and the affix's own अ takes its place.
2. The initial vowel of the stem, आ in का-, is already vṛddhi, so आदिवृद्धि changes nothing.
3. The result is कारितान्त, for example in the sense "belonging to कारितान्त" (तस्येदम्).

<answer>कारितान्त</answer>
<answer>सांवेषिकादेश्य</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.4.50, the affix cvi applies to a nominal stem when something becomes what it was not before. Cvi is elided entirely (sarvāpahāra-lopa), but it still triggers the replacement of the stem's final -a/-ā by ī (7.4.32, *asya cvau*, read as covering a-varṇa). So हरिणेक्षणा becomes हरिणेक्षणी. I am recalling the sūtra and its reading from memory rather than checking a source.

<answer>हरिणेक्षणी</answer>

I applied द्वयसच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) to the stem शैशव्य. The च् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix added is द्वयस. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final -अ is not elided (as in पुरुषमात्र). I also did not apply any vṛddhi, since the affix is not ञित् or णित्. The result is the stem शैशव्य + द्वयस.

<answer>शैशव्यद्वयस</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that licenses कुणप्, so this form is my best derivation rather than a confirmed one.

The affix कुणप् has a final प् that serves only as a marker (it), so it drops. What remains is the suffix -कुण. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of ज्ञप्त is not elided. The affix has no ञ् or ण् marker, so no vṛddhi applies. Adding -कुण to ज्ञप्त gives ज्ञप्तकुण.

<answer>ज्ञप्तकुण</answer>

The derivative is formed by adding the superlative affix इष्ठन् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ) to the feminine stem. I did not check this against the rule texts; it is my own working of the sandhi.

1. The stem बोधयितव्या is बोधयितव्य plus the feminine ending टाप् (आ).
2. Before the taddhita affix इष्ठन् (the final न् is only a marker), the stem takes the bha status. The final आ is then dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148) and by "टेः" (6.4.155).
3. This leaves बोधयितव्य्, to which इष्ठ is added. The result is बोधयितव्यिष्ठ.

<answer>बोधयितव्यिष्ठ</answer>

The affix दघ्नच् (daGnac) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of "measure". The final च् is only an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the suffix दघ्न. Since दघ्न begins with a consonant, the final -अ of समीपक is not elided, so the stem and suffix simply join.

<answer>समीपकदघ्न</answer>
<answer>अनूपालुत्रा</answer>

The affix cvi (च्वि) is used when something becomes what it was not before, in construction with कृ, भू or अस्. Before cvi, a final अ of the stem is replaced by ई (अस्य च्वौ, 7.4.32). So नीलोत्पल becomes नीलोत्पली, as in नीलोत्पलीभवति. The cvi affix itself is dropped entirely, and the resulting word is indeclinable.

<answer>नीलोत्पली</answer>
<answer>जयतितर</answer>

I could not match this exact input to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The nearest rules, 5.3.24 (इदमस्थमुः) and 5.3.25 (किमश्च), apply to इदम् and किम्, not to अधरा. So I treated थमु as a generic taddhita added to अधरा.

1. The affix थमु has the form थम् once the final उ (the marker) is dropped.
2. The stem-final आ is not dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148). That rule needs the stem to be a भ-stem, and भ requires a following affix beginning with a vowel or य् (यचि भम्, 1.4.18). Here the affix begins with थ्.
3. Because थमु falls within the range of affixes from su- to kap, the stem counts as a pada (1.4.17), so the stem stays अधरा.
4. Adding the affix gives अधरा + थम् = अधराथम्. As a taddhita without case endings it is an indeclinable (1.1.38).

<answer>अधराथम्</answer>
<answer>वेल्लिक</answer>

Adding तमप् to the stem पण्याजिर gives the superlative stem पण्याजिरतम (the affix is used in the sense of "most", अतिशायने). The stem already ends in a short vowel, so the rule for shortening a neuter stem (ह्रस्वो नपुंसके) changes nothing.

<answer>पण्याजिरतम</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses खञ् after this stem, so this form rests only on the general rules for the affix.

1. The affix खञ् is replaced by its substitute ईन (ख् → ईन, by 7.1.2).
2. Because the affix carries the marker ञ्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117): the initial अ of अन्यत्रकरण becomes आ.
3. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, giving आन्यत्रकरण + ईन → आन्यत्रकरणीन.

<answer>आन्यत्रकरणीन</answer>
<answer>ललाट्यकल्प</answer>

The affix मात्रच् is added after a word that denotes measure (Pāṇini 5.2.37, as in ऊरुमात्र). The affix begins with a consonant (म), so the stem is not in the bha state. The final -अ of the stem therefore stays, and the stem is simply joined to मात्र.

<answer>अनुवत्सरीणमात्र</answer>

The affix जातीयर् (Pāṇini 5.3.69, प्रकारवचने जातीयर्) is added to the stem प्रियाल to mean "of the kind of" it. The final र् is only an indicatory letter and drops away, so the affix appears as जातीय. No sandhi change occurs at the join, which gives प्रियाल + जातीय = प्रियालजातीय.

<answer>प्रियालजातीय</answer>

This is a straightforward concatenation, not a verified application of a specific rule. The affix थाल् (Pāṇini 5.3.23, प्रकारवचने थाल्) is normally added to सर्वनाम-type words such as तथा and यथा. Here it is attached to the supplied stem पाक्षपातिक as the task instructs. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ stays. The final ल् is only a marker, so the affix surfaces as -था. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>पाक्षपातिकथा</answer>

The affix cvi (SLP1 `cvi`) is used in the sense of "becoming what one was not" (अभूततद्भावे). Before cvi, the final अ of the stem becomes ई (अस्य च्वौ, 7.4.32). The affix itself is then wholly elided, leaving the stem स्रावयितव्य with its final अ replaced by ई. This gives स्रावयितव्यी, which normally appears with कृ, भू or अस् (for example स्रावयितव्यीभवति).

<answer>स्रावयितव्यी</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यङ् on a stem like लौहा. So this derivation rests on the general taddhita rules rather than on a located rule.

1. ञ्यङ् has the markers ञ् and ङ्, so the affix that remains is -य.
2. The final -ā of लौहा (the ṭāp suffix) is dropped before a taddhita affix by यस्येति च (6.4.148), leaving लौह्.
3. Adding -य gives लौह्य. No vṛddhi is needed, since the first vowel is already औ.

I have left out the feminine suffix चाप् (यङश्चाप्, 4.1.74), which would give लौह्या, because the question asks only for the taddhita derivative.

<answer>लौह्य</answer>
<answer>गौरवेरितस्तात्</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses this affix on this stem, so this is a plain concatenation of the stem and the affix.

The affix रूप्य has no markers (it-letters) to remove, and it begins with a consonant other than य. The stem रास्नाव therefore keeps its final अ, with no vowel deletion or other change, and the affix is joined directly.

<answer>रास्नावरूप्य</answer>
<answer>सावलेपकल्प</answer>

The affix is *deśya* (देश्य), taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (*īṣad-asamāptau kalpab-deśya-deśīyaraḥ*). It is added to a finished word (subanta) to mean "nearly, almost, not quite complete".

The base *madālasā* ends in the feminine suffix ā (ṭāp). Before *deśya*, no shortening or masculine-substitution rule applies to a ṭāp stem, so the base stays as it is: *madālasā* + *deśya* gives *madālasādeśya*, "almost a Madālasā".

I gave the derived stem ending in -a, without adding the feminine ending that would turn it into *madālasādeśyā*. The question does not say which form is wanted, so this is my reading.

<answer>मदालसादेश्य</answer>

This is the affix of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, "known by that"). I recalled the sūtra and its examples from memory rather than checking a source. The usual examples are *vidyā-cuñcuḥ* and *vidyā-caṇaḥ*.

The affix is caṇap, with the final *p* as a marker, so what is added is -caṇa. It begins with a consonant, so the final -a of the base is not dropped (6.4.148 only applies before a vowel or *y*). Adding it to the base gives एकार्षेय + चण = एकार्षेयचण.

<answer>एकार्षेयचण</answer>

The affix बहुच् (Pāṇini 5.3.68, विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु) is added optionally before a subanta in the sense of "slightly less than complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It is placed in front of the stem as बहु.

Here, बहु + उषण gives बहूषण by savarṇa-dīrgha (उ + उ = ऊ). The stem ends in ण, so neuter shortening does not change it.

<answer>बहूषण</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् here, so this form is derived from the affix's markers alone and is not confirmed against a rule.

1. The stem तपा loses its final ā before the taddhita affix (by यस्येति च), leaving तप.
2. The marker ञ् makes the first vowel take vṛddhi, so तप becomes ताप.
3. Adding the affix proper, य, gives ताप्य.
4. The marker ट् only signals the feminine suffix ङीप् when a feminine is formed, so it does not change the stem asked for here.

<answer>ताप्य</answer>
<answer>हेलिकिन्</answer>

Here च्वि is added to the stem मौदमानिका to express becoming what it was not before, as in "मौदमानिकी भवति". The affix is then dropped entirely, but it still triggers the change of the stem's final vowel. By "अस्य च्वौ" (7.4.32), a stem-final अवर्ण (here the long ā of the feminine suffix) becomes ई before च्वि. So मौदमानिका → मौदमानिकी. I am recalling this rule from memory and have not checked its wording or its application to ā-stems against the source text.

<answer>मौदमानिकी</answer>

Applying अण् to the stem त्रैंशिक: the final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च). The first vowel ऐ is already vṛddhi, so no further change occurs. The result is त्रैंशिक् + अ = त्रैंशिक.

<answer>त्रैंशिक</answer>

Adding the affix तसि to the stem तडाग (as in the sense of "from the pond") gives the indeclinable तडागतः.

<answer>तडागतः</answer>

Under the rule for cvi (5.4.50), the affix is added to शातित, and the final -a of the stem becomes -ī before cvi (7.4.32, अस्य च्वौ). The affix itself then disappears, so शातित becomes शातीत.

<answer>शातीत</answer>

I derived this from memory of Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), which adds चणप् to a nominal stem. I did not check a commentary.

1. The affix चणप् leaves the base चण, because the प् is only an accent marker.
2. The stem शूद्राणी ends in the feminine ई. The shortening rule ङ्यापोः संज्ञाछन्दसोर्बहुलम् (6.3.63) applies only to names and Vedic usage, so the ई stays long.
3. The ई-deletion rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) applies only before a taddhita beginning with a vowel or य. चण begins with च, so the ई is kept.
4. The result is शूद्राणी + चण = शूद्राणीचण.

<answer>शूद्राणीचण</answer>

The affix चरट् is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, भूतपूर्वे चरट्, which means "formerly such-and-such". It is added directly to the nominal stem, giving forms like आढ्यचर, "formerly rich". The ट् marker only matters for the feminine, where it calls for ङीप्, so the masculine stem takes no other change.

Adding चर to सयन gives सयनचर, "formerly सयन".

<answer>सयनचर</answer>

I formed the stem with the affix ठक् (ṭhak), whose substitute is इक (ik).

1. The affix initial ठ् is replaced by इक (ṭhasyekaḥ, 7.3.50).
2. The final अ of the stem शोभनाचरित is dropped before the affix.
3. The first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi because the affix is ṇit/ñit/kit-type in effect for ādi-vṛddhi: शो (ओ) becomes शौ (औ).
4. The result is शौभनाचरित + इक = शौभनाचरितिक.

I have not identified which specific sense rule licenses ṭhak for this stem. The form follows the general ṭhak pattern.

<answer>शौभनाचरितिक</answer>

I could not recall the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses the affix कुणप् here, so this form is built from the affix's marker structure rather than from a located sūtra.

The final प् of कुणप् is only an indicatory marker (it-letter), so the affix that actually attaches is कुण. It begins with a consonant, so there is no elision of the stem-final इ. Adding it to अष्ठि gives अष्ठि + कुण = अष्ठिकुण.

<answer>अष्ठिकुण</answer>
<answer>चैत्रान्निक</answer>

This is an application of the affix त्रा to the stem भावानुग. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final अ is not dropped and no other change applies. Joining them gives भावानुगत्रा. I did not check whether the rule licensing त्रा (5.4.56, which lists देव, मनुष्य, पुरुष, पुरु and मर्त्य) extends to this stem; I assumed it does.

<answer>भावानुगत्रा</answer>

The input is the feminine stem धानुष्का, and the affix मतुप् (matup) applies in the sense "he has this" (तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति). After a stem ending in आ, the म of मतुप् becomes व by the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9). This is the same pattern as खट्वा → खट्वावत्. The result is the stem धानुष्कावत्, with no case ending added.

<answer>धानुष्कावत्</answer>

This form is built by applying the affix to the stem, with one adjustment for the feminine ending. I assumed the table intends the pumvat rule.

The affix थाल् is added to a stem to give the sense of "manner". The final ल् is only a marker and drops out, leaving था. Taddhita forms ending in such affixes are indeclinable.

The stem गाणेशा is feminine and ends in the feminine suffix -ā. Rule 6.3.35 makes a feminine stem behave like its masculine base before affixes from तसिल् onward, and थाल् falls in that range. So the final -ā is replaced and the base becomes गाणेश.

Adding the affix: गाणेश + था = गाणेशथा.

This is my best reading of the table's feminine note. थाल् is normally taught only after pronoun-type stems, so the input is somewhat artificial.

<answer>गाणेशथा</answer>
<answer>पूर्वोपार्जितसात्</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses यत् on this stem, so this form comes from the general derivation rather than a confirmed source. The stem कृतापकृता ends in the feminine suffix आ (ṭāp). When the taddhita affix य (from यत्) is added, the final आ of the stem is dropped by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). That gives कृतापकृत् + य, which joins as कृतापकृत्य.

<answer>कृतापकृत्य</answer>

The stem अंहती ends in the feminine long ī, and the affix क (ka) is added to it.

1. Before the affix ka, the final long ई of the stem is shortened by "ke 'ṇaḥ" (7.4.13), giving अंहति + क = अंहतिक.
2. Because the source stem is feminine, the stem अंहतिक takes the feminine suffix टाप् (ṭāp). This gives अंहतिका.

I assumed the expected answer includes the feminine ending आ. The bare stem अंहतिक would be the alternative if it does not.

<answer>अंहतिका</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces this affix, so the form below is derived from the affix's technical shape alone and is not checked against the rule.

1. In जाहच्, the initial ज् drops as an indicatory letter (it) by 1.3.7 (चुटू), and the final च् drops by 1.3.3 (हलन्त्यम्). That leaves the operative affix आह.
2. Adding आह to व्रतक, the stem's final अ is elided by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), giving व्रत्क् + आह.
3. This yields व्रतकाह.

<answer>व्रतकाह</answer>

I derived this by attaching ईयसुन् to the stem and dropping the feminine ending. This is my own reconstruction of the rule application, not a form checked against a source.

The stem मथ्रा ends in the feminine long ā. Before the taddhita ईयसुन्, which begins with ई, the stem-final आ is deleted by यस्येति च (6.4.148). That leaves मथ्र् + ईयस्, which gives मथ्रीयस्.

<answer>मथ्रीयस्</answer>

I'm assuming the sense "good in/at सारूप्य" (तत्र साधुः, A. 4.4.98), which takes यत्. I didn't confirm this against the sūtra text.

1. Start with सारूप्य + यत्. The यत् affix loses its marker त्, leaving य.
2. The stem सारूप्य ends in the vowel अ (the final -a of -ya). Under यस्येति च (A. 6.4.148), this अ is deleted before a taddhita affix beginning with य. That leaves सारूप्य्.
3. Adding य gives सारूप्य्य. No vṛddhi applies, because यत् is not ṇit and the first vowel is already long ā.

<answer>सारूप्य्य</answer>
<answer>ग्लेयत्रा</answer>
<answer>अन्वयागतसात्</answer>

Applying अण् to द्राह्यायणीय gives a form identical to the input stem. This derivation is my own reasoning from the rules, and I did not identify which specific sūtra licenses the affix here.

- The stem ends in the अ of ईय. Before the taddhita affix, यस्येति च (6.4.148) drops that final अ.
- The affix अण् then supplies its own अ, restoring the same ending.
- अण् is ञित्/णित, so आदिवृद्धि applies to the first vowel. That vowel is already आ in द्रा, so nothing changes.

<answer>द्राह्यायणीय</answer>

The affix बहुच् is added by P. 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु), and it goes before the subanta as a prefix. It is used in the sense of "slightly less than complete" (ईषदसमाप्ति) or "a kind of".

So बहु is placed in front of मौलभारिका, and the stem itself stays unchanged. I did not apply पुंवद्भाव (the masculine-like replacement of a feminine stem), because I am not certain it applies when the affix is prefixed. If it does apply, the form would be बहुमौलभारिक instead.

<answer>बहुमौलभारिका</answer>

This is a derivative formed with the affix देश्य (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः, 5.3.67), which means "slightly less than complete". I recall this sūtra from memory rather than checking a source.

The affix attaches directly to the stem कनक्नका. The pumvadbhāva rule (6.3.35) lists जातीय and देशीय but not देश्य, so the feminine long ā stays. I also found no rule that shortens it before देश्य. This gives कनक्नकादेश्य.

I could not tell whether the ka in कनक्नका counts as a pratyaya, so I did not apply 7.3.44, which would turn the ā into i. The result rests on that assumption.

<answer>कनक्नकादेश्य</answer>

The affix चरट् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53, भूतपूर्वे चरट्, and means "formerly so-and-so". It is added directly to the nominal stem मन्दन. Since चर begins with a consonant, the final -a of मन्दन is not elided under 6.4.148. The ṭ is only a marker, which later gives the feminine in -ī. The derived stem is therefore मन्दनचर.

<answer>मन्दनचर</answer>

Taking the affix चरट् as the one taught in "भूतपूर्वे चरट्" (Pāṇini 5.3.53), meaning "formerly so-and-so", it is added to वर्तक.

The final ट् of चरट् is only an indicatory letter (it matters for feminine formation), so the affix itself is चर. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of वर्तक is not elided. The result is वर्तक + चर = वर्तकचर, "formerly a वर्तक".

<answer>वर्तकचर</answer>

I could not place कुणप् in a specific Aṣṭādhyāyī rule, so this is derived from the affix's markers alone, and I am not certain it is the attested form.

The affix is कुण with the marker ण् (so it is ṇit) and the marker प्. Before a taddhita affix, the final टि of the stem (the final vowel plus any consonant after it) is dropped by 6.4.144 नस्तद्धिते. That rule applies to a stem ending in न्, so न्यायिन् becomes न्याय्.

The ṇit marker calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel, but the आ in न्या is already vṛddhi, so nothing changes.

Adding the affix gives न्याय् + कुण = न्यायकुण.

<answer>न्यायकुण</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.68 (*vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt tu*), the affix बहुच् is placed before the nominal word in the sense "slightly incomplete" (ईषदसमाप्ति). It therefore comes before पत्वन् rather than after it, giving बहु + पत्वन्. The stem is masculine with no nyap suffix, so nothing else changes.

<answer>बहुपत्वन्</answer>

This is an application of the taddhita affix देश्य, taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), with the sense "slightly short of complete". I derived the form from memory of the rules rather than checking a source.

The rule that makes a feminine stem take masculine form (पुंवत्, 6.3.42) names only देशीय and जातीय. It does not name देश्य, so the feminine stem क्ष्मायिता keeps its long ā.

The form is therefore क्ष्मायिता + देश्य = क्ष्मायितादेश्य. I am less sure of this last point than of the rest, because the alternative क्ष्मायितदेश्य would follow if पुंवत् were extended to देश्य.

<answer>क्ष्मायितादेश्य</answer>

The affix ईयसुन् is the comparative affix (meaning "more…"). The stem बृंहण ends in the vowel अ. Before ईयसुन् the stem is a bha-aṅga, so its ṭi, here the final अ, is deleted by "टेः" (Pāṇini 6.4.155). This gives बृंहण् + ईयस्, which joins to बृंहणीयस्. The ending -स् remains in the stem form, because case endings are not added.

<answer>बृंहणीयस्</answer>

This is a derivation from the standard rules for adding the affix यत् (ya); I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses यत् after इन्द्रानुज, so the meaning is left unspecified.

1. The stem इन्द्रानुज takes यत्. Its final त् is only an indicatory marker and is dropped, leaving the affix ya.
2. Before the affix ya, the stem-final अ is deleted by the rule यस्येति च. This gives इन्द्रानुज् + य.
3. The combination joins as इन्द्रानुज्य. No vṛddhi applies, because यत् is not marked ñit or ṇit. The replacement of ज by a velar (चजोः कु) applies only before ṇyat and ghiṇ, so it does not apply here.

<answer>इन्द्रानुज्य</answer>
<answer>दाधृविमात्र</answer>

Here इञ् (4.1.95 अत इञ्) is added to an a-ending stem, and I took it in the sense of "descendant". This derivation is my own reasoning rather than checked against a source.

1. The stem is आनुसीर्य, which ends in short अ.
2. Before the ञित् affix, the initial vowel takes vṛddhi. It is already आ, so nothing changes.
3. The final अ drops before the affix under 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), giving आनुसीर्य् + इ.
4. The result is आनुसीर्यि.

One doubt remains: the final य might be an apatya affix. If it were, 6.4.151 could drop it after a consonant. The stem's origin is unclear to me, so I kept the य.

<answer>आनुसीर्यि</answer>

The affix त्रा (trA) is added to the stem ताडकायन. The rule I have in mind is Pāṇini 5.4.56, देवमनुष्यपुरुषपुरुमर्त्येभ्यो द्वितीयासप्तम्योर्बहुलम्, though I am recalling its number from memory and am not certain of it. That rule lists only a few stems, so I am applying the affix to ताडकायन on the strength of "बहुलम्" (the rule's allowance for wide variation). Following the pattern of देवत्रा, the final -a of the stem is kept before the affix, so the form is simply the stem plus त्रा.

<answer>ताडकायनत्रा</answer>
<answer>चातुराश्रम्यिन्</answer>
<answer>बीभत्सुमय</answer>
<answer>क्रकणक</answer>
<answer>अश्वत्थिलवत्</answer>

This is the superlative affix इष्ठन् (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, 5.3.55). I assumed it applies here, and I did not check whether सोमाभिषिक्त meets any further condition on its base.

1. Before इष्ठन्, the stem's टि (its final vowel, here the अ of त) is dropped by टेः (6.4.155). यस्येति च (6.4.148) gives the same result for a final अ before a taddhita beginning with इ.
2. This leaves सोमाभिषिक्त्, to which इष्ठ is added.
3. The result is सोमाभिषिक्त् + इष्ठ = सोमाभिषिक्तिष्ठ.

<answer>सोमाभिषिक्तिष्ठ</answer>

Applying the cvi affix (kṛ/bhū/as-yoga, in the sense of becoming what one was not) to the a-ending stem थक्रिय, the affix itself disappears entirely (only its trace remains as a marker). By the rule "asya cvau" (7.4.32), the final अ of the stem becomes ई. This gives थक्रियी, which would then be used with kṛ, bhū or as.

<answer>थक्रियी</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them; I did not identify which taddhita rule licenses यत् for this particular stem. The stem चटकका ends in the feminine suffix -ā (टाप्). Before the taddhita affix यत्, whose initial is य, the stem-final आ is deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). This gives चटकक् + य = चटकक्य. यत् is not marked ञित् or णित्, so there is no vṛddhi.

<answer>चटकक्य</answer>
<answer>सहावस्थितत्व</answer>

I could not identify the Pāṇinian rule that licenses चरट् on this stem, so this form rests on the general rules of affixation rather than on a located sūtra.

The stem is the a-ending चर्म, as the table specifies. The affix चरट् loses its marker ट् and leaves चर. The affix begins with the consonant च, so the stem does not take भ-saṃjñā (यचि भम्, 1.4.18). The final अ of चर्म therefore stays unelided, since यस्येति च (6.4.148) does not apply. This gives चर्म + चर = चर्मचर.

<answer>चर्मचर</answer>
<answer>अल्पास्थित्व</answer>

The affix च्वि (cvi) is used with the verbs कृ, भू and अस् for the sense "becoming what one was not before". Its taddhita form replaces the stem-final अ with ई (अस्य च्वौ, 7.4.32), and the affix itself leaves nothing else behind. The stem कुचित ends in अ (कुचित् + अ), so the final अ becomes ई and the result is कुचिती. This is the stem used in forms such as कुचितीभवति or कुचितीकरोति.

<answer>कुचिती</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् (dvayasac), taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (*pramāṇe dvayasaj-daghnaj-mātrac*), is added in the sense of "measure". The affix itself is द्वयस, since the final च् is only an indicatory letter. Because द्वयस begins with a consonant, the stem-final अ of ऋतव्य is not deleted, so ऋतव्य + द्वयस gives ऋतव्यद्वयस. This follows the pattern of ऊरुद्वयस. I did not check the stem ऋतव्य against attested usage.

<answer>ऋतव्यद्वयस</answer>

I applied the taddhita affix वलच् to the stem सामृता directly, without trying to match a specific Pāṇinian rule.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem-final आ of सामृता is not dropped before it. This is the same pattern as खट्वावत् and मालावत्. The result is सामृता + वल = सामृतावल. The feminine form would be सामृतावला.

<answer>सामृतावल</answer>

I could not recall the specific Pāṇinian rule that licenses ञ्यट् after मधूल, so this derivation rests on the general rules for the affix's markers.

1. The initial ञ् of ञ्यट् is an indicatory marker (it makes the affix ञित्). It triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem, so मधूल becomes माधूल.
2. The final ट् is also an indicatory marker. It only matters for forming the feminine, so it does not affect the stem asked for here.
3. The final अ of मधूल is dropped before the affix by "यस्येति च", leaving माधूल + य.

The result is माधूल्य.

<answer>माधूल्य</answer>

The affix इष्ठन् is added in the sense of "most" (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, 5.3.55). Before इष्ठन्, the final vowel (ṭi) of the stem is dropped (टेः, 6.4.155). So तुण्डि becomes तुण्ड्, and adding इष्ठ gives तुण्डिष्ठ. I worked this out from memory of the rules rather than checking a source.

<answer>तुण्डिष्ठ</answer>

I could not confirm the exact sandhi treatment of the final स्, so the choice of स् over visarga is a best guess.

The affix कल्पप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67 (ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः), with the sense "slightly short of complete". It is added to a subanta stem, giving a derived stem ending in -कल्प. Adding it to स्वर्यस् gives स्वर्यस्कल्प.

<answer>स्वर्यस्कल्प</answer>

Using Pāṇini 5.4.43 (संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायाम्), the affix शस् can be added to a singular noun to express distribution ("one by one"). Applied to मारारि ("enemy of Kāma", i.e. Śiva), it gives the indeclinable मारारिशस्, meaning "each Śiva in turn".

I gave the form ending in स् rather than the visarga form मारारिशः, since the question asks for the derived stem without further endings.

<answer>मारारिशस्</answer>

I applied the affix deśya (Pāṇini 5.3.67, in the sense "nearly, not quite complete") to the feminine stem प्रावृषिका. Before this affix the final feminine ā of the stem is shortened (puṃvadbhāva), giving प्रावृषिक. Adding देश्य gives प्रावृषिकदेश्य. I derived this from memory of the rules and did not check the exact sūtra numbers for the shortening.

<answer>प्रावृषिकदेश्य</answer>

The stem बुधान ends in न, and its penultimate letter is the long vowel आ. Under the rule मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (8.2.9), the म of मतुप् becomes व after a stem whose upadha is म or अ/आ. बुधान is not in the यवादि list, so the rule applies. The derivative is therefore बुधान + वत् = बुधानवत्.

<answer>बुधानवत्</answer>

I could not pin down which sūtra licenses ka here, so I used the general kutsita-type "ka" extension (5.3.70 ff.). I added ka to the stem as an ordinary taddhita suffix. Because ka is not a bha-triggering suffix (no yañ or ac initial), the final -a of the stem is not elided. The ṇ-final shortening rule (7.4.13) also does not apply, since the stem is neuter and ends in ṭhak-derived -ika. So औत्तरार्धिक + क gives औत्तरार्धिकक.

<answer>औत्तरार्धिकक</answer>

The stem त्रीरावतीका ends in the feminine suffix -ā. The affix थाल् has the final ल् as an indicatory letter (it), so only थ is added to the stem.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem does not take the भ designation. The rule यस्येति च (6.4.148) therefore does not delete its final आ. The stem stays as it is and takes थ. Words in -थाल् are indeclinable (तद्धितश्चासर्वविभक्तिः).

<answer>त्रीरावतीकाथा</answer>
<answer>तार्क्ष्यासनजातीय</answer>

This derivation is from memory and I did not verify it against the sūtra text. The affix दघ्नच् (daghnac) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), in the sense of "measure". The final च् is only a marker and drops, leaving the stem ending in -दघ्न. The pattern is the same as ऊरुदघ्न and जानुदघ्न. Adding it to द्रु gives द्रुदघ्न.

<answer>द्रुदघ्न</answer>
<answer>पिप्पलाशनजातीय</answer>

Stem and affix combine as डौण्डुभा + शस्. I did not check this against a specific example in the commentaries.

The stem ends in the feminine ā, and शस् begins with a consonant. So the stem counts as a pada before this affix, and the rule that drops a stem-final अ/आ (यस्येति च, which needs an affix beginning with a vowel or y, or ईकार) does not apply. The final ā therefore stays. The derived form is an indeclinable, so the final स् becomes visarga.

<answer>डौण्डुभाशः</answer>

I could not match this exact pairing to a specific Pāṇinian rule. The affix वलच् is taught in "रजःकृष्यासुतिपरिषदो वलच्" (5.2.112) with the sense "possessing", as in रजस्वला and कृषीवलः. I assumed the same sense and simply attached the affix to शायक.

The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops. वल is not marked ñit or ṇit, so the stem takes no vṛddhi or other internal change. The result is शायक + वल = शायकवल, meaning "one who has a शायक".

<answer>शायकवल</answer>

I formed this by attaching the taddhita affix पाशप् (याप्ये पाशप्, A. 5.3.47) to the stem आम्लीका. The final प् of the affix is only an indicatory marker, so the affix itself is पाश. Since पाश begins with a consonant, the final आ of the stem is not elided. I found no rule that shortens it here, so the stem is kept whole. This is a reasoned derivation rather than a checked attested form.

<answer>आम्लीकापाश</answer>

I could not match this exact stem to a rule for the affix थमु. Pāṇini licenses it only for इदम् (इत्थम्) and किम् (कथम्). So I formed the word by the general rule: the stem takes the affix थम् (the उ is a marker and drops), and the final अ of the stem stays because थ begins with a consonant. The result is an indeclinable.

<answer>गुणालाभथम्</answer>

I could not recall the rule that introduces jAhac, so this form is a best guess rather than a verified derivation. I treated jAhac as an affix like जातीयर्, adding "-जाह" to the stem, with the final "च्" as an indicatory letter that drops. I assumed the stem's final long ā stays unshortened before the affix. I could not confirm that against a specific shortening rule.

<answer>जोष्याजाह</answer>

The affix ढक् applies to feminine stems in the sense of "descendant" (Pāṇini 4.1.120, स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्). I derived this from memory of the rule and did not check the stem तुटि against a source list.

1. ढक् becomes एय, because the initial ढ् is replaced by एय (ढ् → एय, 7.1.2) and the final क् drops as an indicatory letter.
2. The final इ of तुटि is dropped before the vowel-initial affix.
3. The first vowel is lengthened by vṛddhi (उ → औ) because the affix is marked as ञ्णित्/कित्-type taddhita, giving तौट + एय.

This gives तौटेय.

<answer>तौटेय</answer>

Applying मतुप् to the stem सौवर्चल, which ends in अ, the मतुप् element म् becomes व् by 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः). I am not fully certain this rule covers a stem ending in ल, but the pattern matches वृक्ष → वृक्षवत्, so I take the result to be the stem सौवर्चलवत्, meaning "possessing सौवर्चल".

<answer>सौवर्चलवत्</answer>

I derived this from rule 5.2.37, which adds द्वयसच् to a noun of measure, and I could not confirm the result against a source. The final च् of the affix is only a marker and drops. The stem दर्विदा ends in long ā. The affix begins with a consonant, so the ā is not elided by rule 6.4.148. This gives दर्विदा + द्वयस = दर्विदाद्वयस. The word is neuter, so its nominative singular would be दर्विदाद्वयसम्.

<answer>दर्विदाद्वयस</answer>

This is my best reading of the table, and I did not check it against a source. Because the stem न्यायावक्राक्रमणा ends in the long vowel आ, rule 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः) changes the initial म of मतुप् to व. This gives the stem ending in -वत्. The derived stem is therefore न्यायावक्राक्रमणा + वत्.

<answer>न्यायावक्राक्रमणावत्</answer>

I could not identify the exact Pāṇinian sūtra that licenses छ on फलाग्र. I am relying on the general rule that छ (Ca) is replaced by ईय (अ-ending stem, 7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). Adding ईय to फलाग्र, the final अ of the stem drops before the affix, giving फलाग्र + ईय = फलाग्रीय.

<answer>फलाग्रीय</answer>

Adding the affix क (ka) to भासुरक gives भासुरकक. The stem already ends in a short अ, so ke 'ṇaḥ (7.4.13) changes nothing. The masculine stem also has no feminine आ that would take इ before the affix (7.3.44–46), so the affix is simply appended. I did not pin down a specific sūtra licensing क here (for example one of the senses such as kutsita or anukampā).

<answer>भासुरकक</answer>

Applying मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) to आनव्य: the final च् is only an indicatory marker (it), so the affix that remains is मात्र. मात्र begins with a consonant, so the stem does not take the bha designation and its final अ is not deleted. The stem and affix simply join as आनव्य + मात्र.

<answer>आनव्यमात्र</answer>
<answer>स्कन्दकस्तात्</answer>

Since the stem धीरोदात्त ends in short -a, the rule अत इनिठनौ (Pāṇini 5.2.115) allows the possessive affix इनि after it, meaning "having धीरोदात्त". The final -a of the stem drops before the affix, giving धीरोदात्त + इनि → धीरोदात्तिन्.

<answer>धीरोदात्तिन्</answer>

The stem दित्स्य ends in short अ, so the apatya affix इञ् applies (अत इञ्, 4.1.95). The steps are:

1. The affix इञ् is marked ञ्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (ञ्णिति, 7.2.117): दि → दै, giving दैत्स्य + इ.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix (यस्येति च, 6.4.148), giving दैत्स्य् + इ = दैत्स्यि.

<answer>दैत्स्यि</answer>

The affix बहुच् (5.3.68, विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु) is added before the subanta in the sense of "somewhat" (ईषदसमाप्ति, 5.3.67). Here the stem is यज्ञावकीर्ण, so the form is बहु + यज्ञावकीर्ण. No sandhi arises. This follows the pattern of the standard example बहुपटु.

<answer>बहुयज्ञावकीर्ण</answer>
<answer>गावीता</answer>

- तरलित → तारलित्
- तारलित् + अ → तारलित

The result is spelled the same as the original stem except for the long ā.

1. By analogy with जातीयर्, I treated the initial ज् as part of the affix rather than as an इत्. Only the final च् is dropped as an इत्, which leaves the affix जाह.
2. Because जाह begins with a consonant, the stem is not a भ-अङ्ग. The final अ of गोप्यक therefore stays, since यस्येति च does not apply.

<answer>गोप्यकजाह</answer>

I could not identify the rule that gives the affix रूप्य, so this answer rests on a recalled rule I could not confirm.

<answer>दीपितीय</answer>

I did not derive this from a rule I could pin down. थाल् is taught in a few places, such as 5.3.23 (after सर्वनाम words) and 5.3.111 (Vedic, after प्रत्न, पूर्व, विश्व and इम). रेभ fits neither list, so I formed the word by simply adding the affix, as the table asks.

The final ल् of थाल् is only a marker and drops, leaving the affix as था. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of रेभ stays. This gives रेभ + था = रेभथा. A taddhita ending in थाल् is indeclinable, so no case endings are added.

I could not identify the specific rule that applies थमु (Tamu) to शराली. In Pāṇini's grammar थमु is normally prescribed only after इदम् and किम्, so the ending below is my best inference rather than a derivation I could confirm.

Here थमु reduces to the affix थम्, since the final उ is only a marker. Because थ begins with a consonant, the stem शराली stays unchanged and takes the affix directly. This gives शरालीथम्.

<answer>शरालीथम्</answer>

I could not match the affix रूप्य to a Pāṇinian rule that applies to the stem कुलभ. Rule 5.2.120 gives -य to the stem रूप, and 5.3.66 gives रूपप्, which is a different affix. <answer>कुलभरूप्य</answer>

I could not derive this with full certainty. The affix is द्वयसच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, used for measure). Its final च् is only a marker, so what is attached is द्वयस. Taking इञ् in the sense of descendant (अपत्य) by "अत इञ्" (4.1.95), the stem मरणान्त ends in short अ. The final अ drops before the affix, and the first vowel takes vṛddhi (म → मा). This gives मारणान्ति.

This form is built from the stem अभीप्सिता plus the affix साति, and I am not fully certain of the final shape. The affix is taught in Pāṇini 5.4.52–54 and gives indeclinables such as अग्निसात्. Adding the affix कन् (which leaves the stem ending in -क) to the stem युगलायित, for example in a diminutive or contemptuous sense, gives युगलायित + क. I could not recall the specific sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् after पालल, so I derived the form from the affix itself, and the result rests on that derivation rather than on a cited rule.

- Before य, the final अ of पालल is dropped by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148).

So पालल + य gives पालल्य.

<answer>पोट्टलीजातीय</answer>

Adding the affix मयट् to the stem माख gives माखमय.
