The affix मयट् (SLP1 mayaw) is added to वनाग्नि. The final ट् is only an indicatory letter and drops. Because the affix is ṭit rather than ñit or ṇit, there is no vṛddhi of the stem vowels. So वनाग्नि + मय gives the a-stem वनाग्निमय, a stem meaning something like "consisting of or abounding in forest fire".

<answer>वनाग्निमय</answer>

Adding the taddhita affix मयट् to पाञ्चाल्य gives पाञ्चाल्य + मय. The affix begins with म, so the rule that drops a final अ before an affix beginning with a vowel or य (यस्येति च) does not apply. The stem stays intact. The final ट् is only a marker, and it would matter only for forming the feminine (ङीप्), which is not requested here.

<answer>पाञ्चाल्यमय</answer>

I could not recall the exact sūtra that licenses ञ्यट् after हलिक, so the form below rests on the general rules for the affix's markers rather than on a confirmed source.

1. The stem is हलिक and the affix is ञ्यट्, which leaves the suffix य after the markers are dropped.
2. The marker ञ् makes the affix ञित्, so the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi: ह → हा, giving हालिक.
3. The marker ट् is dropped as an indicatory letter. It would only matter for forming the feminine, which is not asked for here.
4. The final अ of the stem is deleted before the taddhita affix by यस्येति च, giving हालिक्.
5. Adding य gives हालिक्य.

<answer>हालिक्य</answer>
<answer>फलितव्यकल्प</answer>

The affix कल्पप् is added by the rule ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः (5.3.67) and means "almost, not quite". Adding it to तृणाङ्कु gives तृणाङ्कुकल्प, meaning "almost a grass-sprout". The final प् is only an accent marker and drops out, and no other change applies to the stem.

<answer>तृणाङ्कुकल्प</answer>

The affix शस् (Sas) is added to a number-word stem in a distributive sense, as in एकैकशः and द्विशः (Pāṇini 5.4.43). The stem तति ("that many") is formed with डति, which makes it count as a number word (संख्या). So शस् applies to it and gives a distributive indeclinable, "that many each". I have not checked this against a source. I gave the form ending in स्, before its pausal change to ः (ततिशः).

<answer>ततिशस्</answer>

This is a best-effort formation, not a checked derivation. The affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, where a form like विद्याचुञ्चु means "known by that". I added it directly to the stem दोडी without changes. The affix begins with a consonant, so the final ई of the stem is not elided, and I found no rule that shortens it here.

<answer>दोडीचुञ्चु</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that teaches ञ्यट्, so this form comes from applying the general rules and may be wrong.

1. The input stem is वैलक्ष्या, which ends in the feminine suffix आ.
2. The affix ञ्यट् reduces to ्य after dropping the markers ञ् and ट्.
3. The stem's final आ is deleted before an affix beginning with य, by यस्येति च (6.4.148), giving वैलक्ष्य्.
4. Adding ्य gives वैलक्ष्य्य.
5. Vṛddhi from the ञ् marker has no further effect, since the first vowel is already ऐ.
6. The marker ट् would normally call for the feminine ṅīp in the full paradigm. I leave that out because you asked for the derived stem only.

<answer>वैलक्ष्य्य</answer>

Taking the affix तल् in the sense of "state of being" (भावे त्वतलौ, 5.1.119), the stem औपसदा gets तल्, and the result takes the feminine ā-ending (टाप्), giving …ता. I did not find a rule that makes the feminine stem revert to its masculine form before तल्; the closest candidates (6.3.34–35) do not cover it, and I did not check this against a reference. So the final आ of औपसदा stays and joins the ता: औपसदा + ता gives औपसदाता. This follows the pattern of forms like खट्वाता.

<answer>औपसदाता</answer>

I could not recall the sūtra that introduces जाहच् with confidence, so this form is a best reconstruction rather than a verified one. The final च् of जाहच् is an indicatory letter, so the affix added is जाह. Because जाह begins with ज, the stem क्षपक does not take the bha designation. That means the final अ of the stem is not elided, and the affix is simply added to the stem.

<answer>क्षपकजाह</answer>

I could not identify which specific rule licenses अञ् here, so this derivation assumes a general application of the affix.

The affix अञ् carries the markers ञ् and ञ्, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem. The stem is कुलायन, ending in अ. The vowel उ of कु becomes औ, and the final अ of the stem drops before the affix अ (by "यस्येति च"). This gives कौलायन.

<answer>कौलायन</answer>

This is a derivation by Pāṇini 5.3.53, *bhūtapūrve caraṭ*, which adds चरट् to a word to mean "formerly such". I could not confirm from memory whether a feminine base like एता takes a पुंवद्भाव (masculine-like) substitution before चरट्. I assumed it does not and simply joined the base and the affix, so this answer rests on that assumption.

The ट् of चरट् is an indicatory letter and drops, leaving the affix as -चर. Joining it to एता gives एताचर. The feminine ङीप् (which would give एताचरी) is a further step that applies only when a feminine word is wanted, so I did not add it.

<answer>एताचर</answer>

I could not pin down the exact rule for this affix, so this derivation is partly inferred.

The affix छ (Ca) becomes ईय by the substitution of ईय for छ (7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The stem सैंहली is vṛddha, since its first vowel is ऐ. It can therefore take छ, which I take to be the rule वृद्धाच्छः (4.2.114), in a sense such as "belonging to".

Before the initial ई of the affix, the final ई of the stem is dropped (6.4.148, यस्येति च). That leaves सैंहल्, and adding ईय gives सैंहलीय.

<answer>सैंहलीय</answer>

The affix चरट् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), in the sense "formerly was". It is added to the nominal stem लौमकीय. The final ट् is only an indicatory letter, so the affix leaves the form चर. No sandhi applies at the join, giving "one who was formerly a लौमकीय".

<answer>लौमकीयचर</answer>

I applied Pāṇini 4.1.95, "अत इञ्", which adds इञ् to a stem ending in short अ to form a descendant (patronymic) word. This is the only rule I recalled that fits इञ् with तुन्द; I did not verify it against a source.

1. The stem is तुन्द, which ends in अ.
2. The ञित् marker of इञ् triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel (Pāṇini 7.2.117), so उ becomes औ, giving तौन्द.
3. The final अ is dropped before the vowel of the affix, and इ is added.
4. The result is तौन्दि, meaning "descendant of Tunda".

<answer>तौन्दि</answer>

I could not identify the sūtra that teaches this affix, so this form rests on general rules rather than a confirmed rule.

The affix कुणप् ends in प्, which is an indicatory letter (it-marker) and drops out. The initial क् is not dropped, because the rule that removes initial क् (लशक्वतद्धिते, 1.3.8) does not apply to taddhita affixes. The ण् is not final, so it also stays. The affix therefore reduces to कुण.

It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of निक्ष is not elided. The affix has no ञ् or ण् marker at the end, so there is no vṛddhi. The result is निक्ष + कुण.

<answer>निक्षकुण</answer>
<answer>वेधनीतः</answer>

This is a rule-based derivation; I have not checked it against any source text. The affix द्वयसच् is added after a word denoting measure (प्रमाणे, Pāṇini 5.2.37). The final च् is only an indicatory marker, so the suffix that actually joins the stem is द्वयस.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem चिप्य is not treated as a *bha* stem (1.4.18). Its final अ is therefore not deleted by "यस्येति च" (6.4.148). The result is simply चिप्य + द्वयस.

<answer>चिप्यद्वयस</answer>

The affix देश्य is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.67, together with कल्पप् and देशीयर्. It is added to a subanta in the sense "slightly incomplete", so it forms "almost मीनाक्षा". The long ā of मीनाक्षा stays, because the shortening rule 6.3.42 lists कल्पप् but not देश्य, so it does not apply here. I did not check this against a commentary. Adding देश्य directly gives the taddhita stem मीनाक्षादेश्य. Its feminine form would be मीनाक्षादेश्या.

<answer>मीनाक्षादेश्य</answer>
<answer>रोषाणतः</answer>
<answer>कूटतम</answer>

Applying the taddhita affix छ (Ca) to the stem सारसेय gives सारसेयीय.

1. The affix छ is added by Pāṇini 4.2.113 (वृद्धाच्छः), which applies to a stem that is vṛddha, meaning its first vowel is a vṛddhi vowel. I recalled this rule number from memory and did not check it.
2. The stem सारसेय begins with सा, whose vowel ā is a vṛddhi vowel, so the stem qualifies.
3. The affix छ is replaced by ईय (Pāṇini 7.1.2, आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्).
4. The final -a of सारसेय is dropped before the affix (Pāṇini 6.4.148, यस्येति च). This gives सारसेय् + ईय = सारसेयीय.

<answer>सारसेयीय</answer>

The affix caṇap (चणप्) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप्चणपौ), where it means "known/famed by that". I am recalling this sūtra from memory rather than checking it.

Here ṇ is not a marker, and only the final p is dropped, so the affix surfaces as चण. Because चण begins with a consonant, the final -a of the stem is not elided (यस्येति च 6.4.148 needs a following vowel or y). The derivative is therefore the stem अषतर plus चण, in the pattern of examples like विद्याचण.

<answer>अषतरचण</answer>

Adding च्वि (cvi) to वृद्ध gives the "becoming what one was not" sense (as in वृद्धीभवति or वृद्धीकरोति). The affix's वि is elided entirely (सर्वापहारी लोपः), and a final -अ of the stem becomes ई before च्वि by अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32). So वृद्ध becomes वृद्धी. The neuter gender of the source stem does not change this.

<answer>वृद्धी</answer>
<answer>त्रययाय्यथा</answer>

Applying the affix अण् (aṇ) to रासन gives the same spelling, with only the stem-final अ replaced.

1. The final अ of रासन is dropped before the अ of अण् (यस्येति च).
2. The initial vowel is already आ, so आदिवृद्धि (the vowel strengthening of the first syllable) changes nothing.
3. The affix अ is then added, so the stem is again रासन.
4. The स् blocks ण-substitution after र्, so the न् stays dental.

<answer>रासन</answer>

I could not identify the specific Pāṇinian rule that introduces ञ्यट्, so this form is derived from the affix markers alone and is not checked against a rule.

The ञ् marker makes the affix ñit, which triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem: भवान्तर becomes भावान्तर. The affix ञ्यट् leaves य after dropping the markers ञ् and ट्. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the affix, so भावान्तर्+य gives भावान्तर्य.

<answer>भावान्तर्य</answer>

Following the superlative rule (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, A. 5.3.55), the affix तमप् is added to the stem शकुन. The final प् is only a marker (it drops out), and no other sandhi or stem change applies, so the result is the stem शकुनतम.

<answer>शकुनतम</answer>

I could not tie this stem and affix to a specific Pāṇinian rule, so this derivation is partly inferred rather than confirmed.

The affix लच् is "अल" once the marker letters are dropped. It begins with a vowel, so the final आ of the feminine stem प्राघूर्णिका is elided under the rule यस्येति च (6.4.148). That gives प्राघूर्णिक + अल = प्राघूर्णिकल. I gave the default masculine stem, not the feminine प्राघूर्णिकला.

<answer>प्राघूर्णिकल</answer>

Pāṇini 5.3.68–69 allows बहुच् to be placed before a subanta in the sense of "somewhat, almost" (ईषदसमाप्ति). I am working from memory of these sūtras and did not check them. Applied to हरणाहरण, the affix comes in front of the stem and leaves it unchanged, which gives बहुहरणाहरण.

<answer>बहुहरणाहरण</answer>
<answer>घटिलाचण</answer>
<answer>उरलीय</answer>

I applied the affix अस्तात् to the stem. I did not check whether लवनीय meets the usual condition of being a direction word, since the task accepts any meaning licensed for the affix.

The affix is Pāṇini's अस्ताति (5.3.27), which yields forms like पुरस्तात्. Its final इ is only a technical marker, so what is added is अस्तात्. The stem-final अ is dropped before the affix's initial अ (यस्येति च), so लवनीय् + अस्तात् gives लवनीयस्तात्.

<answer>लवनीयस्तात्</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.47 (याप्ये पाशप्), the affix पाश attaches to a nominal stem to mean "something despicable or defective" of that kind. The affix begins with a consonant other than य, so देवन् takes pada status (1.4.17). The final न् is then dropped by 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य), giving देव + पाश = देवपाश. I derived this from the rules as I recall them and did not check it against a source.

<answer>देवपाश</answer>

Adding ईयसुन् (comparative) to देशाख्य gives a stem that ends in -ईयस्.

1. The affix is ईयसुन्. Its उ and न् are markers (it), so only ईयस् is added.
2. The stem देशाख्य ends in अ, which is deleted before the affix, by 6.4.154 (the टि of the stem drops before इष्ठन्, इमनिच् and ईयसुन्) and also by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च).
3. This leaves देशाख्य् + ईयस्, which joins to देशाख्यीयस्.

I did not check whether देशाख्य counts as a guṇavacana (a quality word), which 5.3.55 requires; the question says any licensed meaning is acceptable.

<answer>देशाख्यीयस्</answer>

I derived this from memory of the Pāṇinian rules. I could not confirm whether the shortening rule 6.3.43 applies to ā-stems, so the result is uncertain.

The affix रूपप् (rūpap) is added after a word that denotes praise (प्रशंसायां रूपप्, 5.3.66). The affix reduces to -रूप, which is added to the stem घोराकारा. I took the shortening rule 6.3.43 to apply only to ङी-stems, so the final -ā of the stem stays long. This gives the masculine-form stem घोराकारारूप, to which the feminine suffix ṭāp can be added later (घोराकारारूपा).

<answer>घोराकारारूप</answer>

Applying यत् to पाक्षी, a stem ending in the feminine suffix ई, gives पाक्ष्य. I derived this from the general rules rather than from a specific sūtra for this affix, and I did not pin down which meaning of यत् applies, which the prompt allows.

1. Start with पाक्षी + यत्. The affix यत् loses its final त् as an indicatory letter and leaves य.
2. Rule 6.4.148 (यस्येति च) deletes the final ई of the base before a taddhita affix beginning with य. This leaves पाक्ष् + य.
3. यत् is not marked with ण्, so no vṛddhi is triggered. The initial आ in पाक्ष् is already long, so nothing further changes.

<answer>पाक्ष्य</answer>

Under Pāṇini 5.3.53 (भूतपूर्वे चरट्), the affix चरट् is added to a nominal stem to mean "formerly that". The ट् is only a marker, and the final अट् leaves the stem ending in -अ. Adding it to हीर gives हीरचर, "formerly a हीर".

<answer>हीरचर</answer>

This is a best-effort derivation, not a confirmed one, because I could not pin down the exact Pāṇinian rule that licenses त्रा on a feminine stem.

The affix त्रा is added to the stem तारणी as a taddhita and yields an indeclinable. Nothing in the stem changes. The rule that shortens a final long vowel (1.2.48) applies only to a subordinate member of a compound, so it does not apply here. The final ई therefore stays long, and the form is तारणी + त्रा = तारणीत्रा.

<answer>तारणीत्रा</answer>

The affix बहुच् is taught in Pāṇini 5.3.68 (विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात्तु), in the sense of ईषदसमाप्ति ("slightly deficient"). It is placed before the base, as in बहुपटु ("somewhat clever"). Adding it before चित्तार्पित gives बहुचित्तार्पित. The neuter shortening rule (1.2.47) does not change anything here, because the stem already ends in the short vowel -अ.

<answer>बहुचित्तार्पित</answer>

I derived this by applying the standard sandhi rules, without checking a reference text.

The affix इष्ठन् (izWan) is the superlative affix from the rule for expressing a higher degree of a quality (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ).

1. The base is कौटवी, which ends in the feminine ई, and the affix begins with the vowel इ.
2. Before a taddhita affix beginning with a vowel, the final ई of the base is dropped (यस्येति च). This leaves कौटव्.
3. Before इष्ठन्, the base's final vowel is also dropped (टेः), so the अ of कौटव is removed. This is the same step that applies to the base's final vowel before ईयसुन् and इमनिच्.
4. इष्ठन् is not marked with ञ् or ण्, so the first vowel does not undergo vṛddhi. The result is कौटव् + इष्ठ = कौटविष्ठ.

<answer>कौटविष्ठ</answer>

The stem सांतानिक takes the affix कन् (in senses such as कुत्सित, अज्ञात or अनुकम्पा). The final -a of the stem is not elided, because कन् begins with a consonant, so the यस्येति च deletion does not apply. The affix कन् reduces to the suffix -क, and the derived stem is सांतानिक + क = सांतानिकक. I did not trace the specific sūtra in detail.

<answer>सांतानिकक</answer>

Following the usual derivation, the affix क is added to the stem अनहा. The rule "के ऽणः" (7.4.13) then shortens the final आ before क, giving अनहक. I did not add the feminine suffix again, which would change the form to अनहका (or अनहिका by 7.3.44).

<answer>अनहक</answer>

The affix caṇap (चण, with the indicatory p) is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26, *tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*, with the sense "known by that". Kāśikā examples are *vidyācuñcuḥ* and *vidyācaṇaḥ*.

The affix begins with a consonant other than y, so the stem counts as a pada and the final ī of मासिकी stays. The ṇ is a real letter of the affix, not an indicatory one, so there is no vṛddhi. I found no rule that shortens the ī here, so the affix is simply added.

The derived stem is मासिकी + चण = मासिकीचण. I derived this from the rules rather than from an attested example, so the treatment of the ī is the least certain step.

<answer>मासिकीचण</answer>

I could not trace the affix जाहच् to a specific Pāṇinian rule, so this form comes from applying the general taddhita rules mechanically, not from a rule I could cite for this affix.

1. The initial ज् of जाहच् is an it-letter by 1.3.7 (चुटू), and the final च् is an it-letter by 1.3.3. The affix that remains is आह.
2. Because the affix is जित्, 7.2.117 (तद्धितेषु अचामादेः) calls for vṛddhi of the first vowel. The first vowel of साम्राज्य is already आ, so nothing changes.
3. The stem साम्राज्य ends in short अ (from ya). Under 6.4.148 (यस्येति च), this अ is deleted before a taddhita affix, giving साम्राज्य् + आह.
4. Joining the two gives साम्राज्याह.

<answer>साम्राज्याह</answer>
<answer>राजत्व</answer>

The taddhita affix त्व (tva) is added to the stem मोदनीय under Pāṇini 5.1.119, *tasya bhāvas tvatalau*, to express the abstract sense "state of being". The stem takes no change before the affix. The resulting neuter stem is मोदनीयत्व.

<answer>मोदनीयत्व</answer>

श्रुता में इष्ठन् (अतिशायन अर्थ में) जोड़ने पर "टेः" (6.4.155) से अन्तिम अच् सहित भाग, यहाँ आकार, का लोप होता है। तब श्रुत् + इष्ठ = श्रुतिष्ठ बनता है।

<answer>श्रुतिष्ठ</answer>

I could not identify the Aṣṭādhyāyī rule that introduces ञ्यट्, so this form comes from applying the affix's markers to the stem, not from a confirmed rule.

1. The stem कटुकित ends in -a, and the affix begins with य. By "यस्येति च" (6.4.148), the final अ of the stem is dropped, giving कटुकित् + य.
2. The ञ् in ञ्यट् is an it-marker, so it triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem (ज्ञित् rule 7.2.117). The first क becomes का, giving काटुकित्य.
3. The ट् marker only affects feminine formation and does not change this form.

<answer>काटुकित्य</answer>

I applied the affix अस्ताति (SLP1 astAti), which attaches to direction words. The final इ of the affix is a marker letter and drops away, leaving अस्तात्. This is the same pattern as पुरस्तात्. The stem लडह ends in अ, and that अ is elided before the affix's initial vowel. This gives लडह + अस्तात् = लडहस्तात्, an indeclinable.

I did not check लडह against any list of direction words, so this assumes the affix may be added to it as given.

<answer>लडहस्तात्</answer>
<answer>मलनतर</answer>

Here the affix ईयसुन् is added to दंसु. The final उ of the stem is dropped before ईयस् by the rule that elides the stem's final vowel (ṭi) before इष्ठ, इमन् and ईयस् (Pāṇini 6.4.155, टेः). This is the same process that gives लघु → लघीयस्. So दंसु becomes दंस्, and adding ईयस् gives दंसीयस्. I did not find a specific rule that licenses ईयसुन् after दंसु, so I took the formation to follow the ordinary comparative pattern.

<answer>दंसीयस्</answer>

The affix रूपप् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्), which applies after a subanta to express praise. The final प् is only a marker and drops out. Adding रूप to भाल्लेय causes no sandhi or other change, so the stem is "praiseworthy BhāllEya".

<answer>भाल्लेयरूप</answer>

This is a derivation from the rules as I recall them; I did not check the stem against a gaṇa list.

The affix फिञ् has an initial फ्, which is replaced by आयन् (7.1.2). That gives the ending -आयनि. Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi, and शैरीषिक already begins with ऐ, so nothing changes there. The final अ of the stem drops before the affix, so शैरीषिक + आयनि gives शैरीषिकायनि.

<answer>शैरीषिकायनि</answer>

This derivation rests on a guess, not on an identified Pāṇinian rule. I could not find a sūtra that applies खञ् specifically to दारिका, so I applied the affix by its general rules, and the result may not match a rule-licensed form.

1. The affix खञ् (KaY) has the initial ख, which is replaced by ईन (7.1.2 आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The ञ् is only an indicatory marker.
2. Because of the ञ् marker, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi (7.2.117). The first vowel of दारिका is already long, so it does not change.
3. The final आ of the feminine stem is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (6.4.148 यस्येति च), giving दारिक + ईन.

The result is दारिकीन.

<answer>दारिकीन</answer>

The stem सुख्या is feminine and ends in a feminine suffix, and जातीयर् (P. 5.3.69, in the sense of "kind, sort") is added to it. Before जातीय, the feminine stem takes the masculine form by पुंवद्भाव (P. 6.3.35, पुंवत्कर्मधारयजातीयदेशीयेषु), so the feminine ending drops and सुख्या becomes सुख्य. Adding जातीय to this gives सुख्यजातीय. I am applying पुंवद्भाव from memory of the rule, so treat that step as my best reading of the table rather than a checked derivation.

<answer>सुख्यजातीय</answer>

The affix तमप् is added to the feminine stem एकायना. I did not verify the shortening rule against the Aṣṭādhyāyī and chose it from memory of the rule for feminine stems before घ-affixes (तरप्/तमप्). On that recollection, the final long vowel of a polysyllabic feminine stem is shortened before तमप्, so एकायना becomes एकायन. Adding तमप् then gives the stem एकायनतम. The feminine ending ā would be added in a separate step, so I give the stem without it.

<answer>एकायनतम</answer>

Applying अण् (for example in the sense तस्येदम्) to कौमारहारित, the stem-final अ is dropped by यस्येति च. The affix's अ is then added. The first vowel is already vṛddhi (कौ), so आदिवृद्धि changes nothing. The resulting stem is therefore spelled the same as the input.

<answer>कौमारहारित</answer>

Here the affix च्वि (cvi) is added under the rule अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः (5.4.50). The whole affix is then elided (सर्वापहारी लोपः), leaving only its effect on the stem. By अस्य च्वौ (7.4.32), the final अ of तडाग becomes ई, which gives तडागी. This is the form that appears in compounds such as तडागीभवति.

<answer>तडागी</answer>
<answer>चम्पोपलक्षितमय</answer>

Adding the affix मात्रच् (the final च् is only a marker and drops) to the stem एत leaves the stem unchanged. This gives एत + मात्र = एतमात्र. This is based on the affix's general rule (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of "extent") rather than a form I have found attested for this particular stem.

<answer>एतमात्र</answer>

Applying the affix क (ka) to the masculine stem धन्य gives धन्यक. The affix is added under the senses of contempt, smallness or unspecified reference (as in P. 5.3.73–74 and 5.3.85). I did not check the exact sūtra, so the rule citation is from memory. The masculine stem takes no feminine-suffix change, so the result is simply धन्य + क.

<answer>धन्यक</answer>
<answer>वल्गाङ्कतम</answer>
<answer>भूतोड्डामरिक</answer>

The affix थाल् (TAl) has its final ल् as an indicatory letter (it), so only the part था is added to the stem मौल. Since था begins with a consonant and the affix is not marked to cause vṛddhi, the stem's final अ stays. The result is the indeclinable मौलथा.

<answer>मौलथा</answer>

Following the superlative rule (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ), the affix इष्ठन् is added to वर्षिक. Before इष्ठन्, the final टि part of the stem, here the final अ, is dropped (टेः). That gives वर्षिक् + इष्ठ = वर्षिकिष्ठ.

<answer>वर्षिकिष्ठ</answer>
<answer>मन्दोत्साहत्रा</answer>

This is a derivation from memory of the rules, not checked against a text. Adding matup to the feminine stem क्नूता gives क्नूतामत्. By the rule "मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः" (8.2.9), the म of matup becomes व after a stem ending in आ, as in शालावत् and द्राक्षावत्. The result is क्नूतावत्.

<answer>क्नूतावत्</answer>
<answer>सौश्रोमतेयदेश्य</answer>

Applying मयट् to श्रुतार्था: the final -ā of the stem is dropped by यस्येति च (6.4.148), and the affix then attaches as -मय. This gives श्रुतार्थमय. I did not add the feminine ending (-ई), which would apply if the derived word were used in the feminine.

<answer>श्रुतार्थमय</answer>

This is a derivation by rule recall; I did not check the form against a reference text.

The affix ईयसुन् begins with ई, so the final ई of the stem चपलाक्षी is dropped before it (यस्येति च, 6.4.148). The remaining stem चपलाक्ष् then joins with ईयस्, which gives चपलाक्षीयस्. Simple concatenation of ई + ई would give the same form, so the result does not depend on that rule.

<answer>चपलाक्षीयस्</answer>

I could not pin down the exact sūtra that licenses this combination. This is a best-effort formation: I attached the affix त्रा directly to the stem विस्रा, keeping its final long आ, as in देव → देवत्रा.

<answer>विस्रात्रा</answer>

I took जार्य as a basic stem ending in short अ and added मतुप् (matup) to it.

Rule 8.2.9 (मादुपधायाश्चमतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः) changes the म of मतुप् to व after a stem with a final or penultimate म or अवर्ण (a/ā). The stem जार्य ends in अ and is not in the यवादि exception group, so the म becomes व. This is the same pattern as वृक्ष → वृक्षवत्.

The result is जार्य + वत् = जार्यवत्.

<answer>जार्यवत्</answer>
<answer>भालयानन्दाचार्यतम</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (P. 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः) is added to a word meaning "slightly incomplete". Before it, a stem ending in a ṅyāp-type feminine suffix is shortened (P. 6.3.43). So वनिका becomes वनिक, and adding देशीय gives वनिकदेशीय. I am recalling the shortening rule from memory and am not fully certain of its exact number or wording.

<answer>वनिकदेशीय</answer>

Here the affix क (ka) is added to a stem that already ends in the feminine -ā (āp), so I derived the form from the rules I recall for this situation, without checking them against the text.

1. Before ka, the final long -ā of the stem is shortened: विवन्दिषा + क → विवन्दिष + क (7.4.13 *ke 'ṇaḥ*, as I recall it).
2. The feminine ending -ā is added again after the new stem: विवन्दिषक + आ.
3. When ka stands in the affix position and an āp ending follows, the a before ka becomes i (7.3.44 *pratyayasthāt kāt pūrvasyāta ity āpi supaḥ*). This gives विवन्दिषिका.

The same pattern gives खट्वा → खट्विका. I did not pin down which ka-rule supplies the meaning here, but the form is the same for the meanings I considered (such as small or contemptible).

<answer>विवन्दिषिका</answer>
<answer>पूर्वोचितथा</answer>

This is a best-effort answer: I could not identify a Pāṇinian rule that teaches an affix spelled exactly "rUpya" after this stem, so I attached the affix mechanically.

The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem शिरोपस्थायिन् counts as a pada before it (1.4.17). The final न् is therefore dropped (8.2.7), giving शिरोपस्थायि. Adding the affix रूप्य gives:

<answer>शिरोपस्थायिरूप्य</answer>

I could not pin this to a specific sūtra, so this is my best derivation.

The feminine stem मगधा takes the affix कन्. Before a affix with क, the final long vowel of the stem is shortened (7.4.13 के अणः). That gives मगध + क = मगधक.

Since the base is feminine, the feminine suffix टाप् is added after the affix, giving मगधक + आ. Before आ, the आ-preceding अ of a pratyaya-internal क becomes इ (7.3.44 प्रत्ययस्थात्कात्पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः). This gives मगधिका.

<answer>मगधिका</answer>

The affix तल् (भावे, "state of being") is added to रूक्षित. The ल् is only an indicatory letter, so the ending is -ता. The result is a feminine abstract noun, and the feminine -आ is added by टाप्. This gives रूक्षित + ता = रूक्षितता.

<answer>रूक्षितता</answer>

I formed this with the affix फिञ् (the "-āyani" type). I am recalling the sūtra from memory (4.1.157, उदीचां वृद्धादगोत्रात् फिञ्), so I have not checked it against a text.

The stem दार्ढच्युत begins with a vṛddhi vowel (दा), so it counts as vṛddha, and it is not a gotra name, which meets the condition of the rule.

In फिञ्, the initial फ् is replaced by आयन्, and the final ञ् is only a marker and drops. The final -अ of the stem is deleted before the affix.

दार्ढच्युत + आयन् + इ → दार्ढच्युतायनि

<answer>दार्ढच्युतायनि</answer>
<answer>वार्मणदेशीय</answer>

I could not tie this stem to a specific sūtra, so this is a best-fit answer rather than a verified derivation. I took the affix क (ka) as the usual one added to the whole stem, as in अश्व + क = अश्वक. Since क begins with a consonant, the final अ of the stem is not elided, so अङ्काङ्क + क gives अङ्काङ्कक.

<answer>अङ्काङ्कक</answer>

The affix इञ् (iY) is the one taught in A 4.1.95, अत इञ्, which applies to stems ending in short अ. It gives the sense "descendant".

1. The stem पौरूरवस ends in अ, so इञ् can be added.
2. The final अ of the stem is dropped before the vowel-initial affix (A 6.4.148, यस्येति च), giving पौरूरव् + इ.
3. The affix is marked ञित्, so the first vowel would normally take vṛddhi. Here it is already पौ, so nothing changes.
4. The result is the stem पौरूरवि.

<answer>पौरूरवि</answer>
<answer>त्वायुवल</answer>

I could not match this exact word to a specific rule, so this form rests on general principles rather than a cited sūtra.

The affix तसि is added to the feminine stem सामित्या, which ends in the feminine suffix आप्. Because तसि begins with a consonant, the stem takes pada status before it. This means the final आ of the stem stays unchanged, and no vowel-elision rule applies. The result is the indeclinable सामित्यातः.

<answer>सामित्यातः</answer>
<answer>वृद्धायुमत्</answer>

Reading the table, I took "रूप्य" as an affix added directly to the stem आपत्य. I did not derive it as the affix यप् added to रूप, which is how Pāṇini 5.2.120 yields रूप्य. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem ending in अ undergoes no change. Joining the two gives आपत्यरूप्य. This follows the table's wording rather than a rule I could confirm, so it is the least certain part of the answer.

<answer>आपत्यरूप्य</answer>

I did not find a specific rule in the वलच् sutras that applies to पृतन्यु, so I simply attached the affix by the general method. The affix वलच् loses its indicatory च् and leaves the stem-forming अ, giving -वल. Adding this to पृतन्यु needs no sandhi, because the stem's final उ stands before व.

<answer>पृतन्युवल</answer>

The affix रूप्य is added directly to the stem. It begins with a consonant and carries no marker that would trigger vṛddhi or deletion of the stem's final अ, so the stem is unchanged and the two simply join. I could not tie रूप्य to a specific Pāṇinian rule for this stem, so the form comes from straightforward concatenation.

<answer>कानीयसरूप्य</answer>

I formed this with the affix कल्पप् (Pāṇini 5.3.67, "ईषदसमाप्तौ कल्पब्देश्यदेशीयरः"), which means "almost, nearly (but not quite)". The stem is the feminine वचस्या, so the result takes the feminine ending -ā again: वचस्याकल्पा, "almost a वचस्या". I did not shorten the stem's final ā. I recalled the shortening rule (6.3.43) as applying to ङी-ending stems and was unsure whether it also covers an आप् ending. That leaves the alternative form वचस्यकल्पा as a possible but unconfirmed variant.

<answer>वचस्याकल्पा</answer>

Here the affix पाशप् (pASap) is the one taught in Pāṇini 5.3.47, याप्ये पाशप्, which expresses something bad or defective (याप्य). It attaches to a nominal stem, and the final प् is only a marker that drops. The affix begins with a consonant, so the stem's final अ stays unchanged. Joining अमिन and पाश gives the stem अमिनपाश.

<answer>अमिनपाश</answer>

I could not identify the specific rule that licenses खञ् on this stem, so the form below comes from applying the affix's general mechanics.

1. खञ् leaves the affix ईन, because ख is replaced by ईन (ख् → ईन, rule 7.1.2). The ञ् is only a marker: it makes the affix ञित्, which triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel of the stem.
2. The stem पतरु takes vṛddhi on its first vowel, giving पातरु (प → पा).
3. The final उ of the stem takes guṇa before the vowel-initial ञित् affix ईन, by the rule ओर्गुणः (6.4.146). This gives पातरो + ईन, and ओ becomes अव् before the vowel, so the stem becomes पातरव् + ईन.

The result is पातरवीन.

<answer>पातरवीन</answer>
<answer>क्षयथुकल्प</answer>

The affix रूपप् is added by Pāṇini 5.3.66 (प्रशंसायां रूपप्) to express praise, so it is simply attached to the stem. The rule is applied here without any change to the stem, which ends in -a, and the result is "नानोल्बरूप" (praiseworthy नानोल्ब).

<answer>नानोल्बरूप</answer>

This is the affix दघ्नच् taught in Pāṇini 5.2.37 (प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः), which is added to a noun to express measure. A typical example is ऊरुदघ्न, "thigh-deep." The final च् is only an accent marker and drops out. Since तृम्पण already ends in -अ, the affix attaches directly with no further change. This gives तृम्पणदघ्न. I did not find a standard attested example with तृम्पण, so the form is built by applying the rule.

<answer>तृम्पणदघ्न</answer>

Here the affix चुञ्चुप् is taught in Pāṇini 5.2.26 (*tena vittaś cuñcup-caṇapau*), with the sense "known by that". The final प् is only a marker, and the ञ् is the nasal before च, so the affix that remains is चुञ्चु. It begins with a consonant, so the final अ of चक्राट is not dropped. The affix carries no ञ्/ण् marker, so there is no vṛddhi. Adding चुञ्चु directly to चक्राट gives the stem below. I derived this by applying the rule, not by finding the form in a source.

<answer>चक्राटचुञ्चु</answer>

I formed this by applying मात्रच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) to the stem निगु. The affix is neither ञित् nor णित्, so the stem takes no vṛddhi and stays as it is. The result is a stem ending in -a. I have not checked this against a particular source for this stem.

<answer>निगुमात्र</answer>
<answer>सेनाधिपतितम</answer>

I did not find a specific rule licensing वलच् after this stem, so this form follows the general pattern of the affix. The stem मधुरानिरुद्ध ends in -a, which drops before the affix. The affix's final च् is only an indicatory marker and also drops, leaving -वल.

<answer>मधुरानिरुद्धवल</answer>

The affix देशीयर् (P. 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ, "almost, but not quite") attaches to a subanta, so the stem keeps its pada status. Because of that, the final न् of उपवासिन् drops by P. 8.2.7 (नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य). Adding देशीय to the remaining उपवासि gives उपवासिदेशीय, meaning "almost an उपवासिन्".

<answer>उपवासिदेशीय</answer>

Applying अण् to पौण्ड्रक drops the final अ of the stem (यस्येति च). The initial vowel औ is already vṛddhi, so adding अण् leaves the form unchanged. This assumes a meaning such as "relating to पौण्ड्रक" (तस्येदम्), which I did not check against a specific sūtra.

<answer>पौण्ड्रक</answer>

I could not identify the specific sūtra that licenses KaY after this stem, so this derivation applies the general affix rules only.

The affix खञ् is formed from ख + ञ्. Under the rule आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्, the initial ख् becomes ईन. The ञ् is only an indicatory letter (it marks vṛddhi of the first vowel).

1. Start with केशाद + ईन.
2. The final अ of the stem drops before the vowel-initial affix, giving केशाद् + ईन.
3. The ञ् marker triggers vṛddhi of the first vowel. The ए of केश becomes ऐ, giving कैशाद् + ईन.
4. Joining the parts gives कैशादीन.

<answer>कैशादीन</answer>

I identified ञ्यट् as the affix of Pāṇini 5.3.114 and applied its markers to गमनार्ह. I did not find a rule that tells me which sense of "गमनार्ह" the affix would carry, so this derivation is based on the affix's markers alone, and the task accepts any licensed meaning.

- The ञ् and ट् are markers and drop, leaving the affix -य.
- Because the affix is ञित्, the first vowel of the stem takes vṛddhi, so ग becomes गा.
- The final अ of गमनार्ह drops before the affix (6.4.148).

This gives गामनार्ह्य.

<answer>गामनार्ह्य</answer>

I could not pin down the sūtra behind जाहच् with confidence, so this form is a best derivation rather than a verified one.

The affix जाहच् has its final च् as an indicatory letter (it), leaving the operative suffix जाह. The suffix begins with a consonant, so the rule that deletes a stem-final "a" before a vowel-initial suffix (यस्येति च) does not apply. The stem-final long आ of बार्बरा therefore stays. I also found no rule that would shorten it or replace it with the masculine stem (the पुंवद्भाव rule I checked lists जातीय and देशीय, not जाह). Adding जाह directly gives बार्बराजाह.

<answer>बार्बराजाह</answer>

खादिका (a stem in -ā) + देशीयर् (the suffix of P. 5.3.67, ईषदसमाप्तौ, "almost, not quite complete") gives the stem खादिकादेशीय, meaning "almost a खादिका". I did not check the rule on shortening the final -ā before certain suffixes against a source. As I recall it, that rule does not list देशीयर्, so the -ā stays. The rest follows from the suffix rule above: the suffix is added to the whole word and the र् of देशीयर् is only a marker, so it drops out.

<answer>खादिकादेशीय</answer>
<answer>चारणतम</answer>

The affix द्वयसच् (Pāṇini 5.2.37, in the sense of measure) is added to the stem पेरोज. The final च् only marks accent and is dropped, so the affix surfaces as द्वयस. The stem's final अ is elided before the affix by 6.4.148 (यस्येति च). This gives पेरोज + द्वयस = पेरोजद्वयस.
